title: The indexed competitor pages concede the market the product already won, at prices the company does not charge, to an ICP the company abandoned
effort: 1 day for the rewrite; +2 hours to derive the price row from pricing-constants.
evidence: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/vs/marginedge/page.tsx:57` lede: "MarginEdge… also run inventory, recipe costing, sales-mix reports, and prime-cost dashboards. Muntin Ledger does the first part. **We do not yet do the rest.**" Line 97 `whereTheyWin`: "If you want prime-cost reports, recipe costing, and a POS integration… MarginEdge is built for that and we are not." All three are now false: `apps/api/src/routes/inventory.ts` is 1,100 lines (count sheet → reconcile → food-cost → pars → variance), plus `apps/api/src/routes/recipes.ts`, `sales-mix.ts`, `apps/api/src/routes/integrations/square.ts`, `apps/api/src/scheduled/square-sync.ts`, and 16 shipped `/insights/*` surfaces including `food-cost`, `variance`, `menu-margin`, `vendor-scorecard`. Line 79 posts "Solo $25, Team $60, Accountant $150 + $30 per seat" while `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:52` and six copy strings post $19/location. Line 62 defines the ICP as "Small business owners… the tool is vertical-agnostic" and line 104 as "a coffee shop and a hardware store can both use us" — against a storefront that coined "restaurant cost intelligence". `lastFactCheckedISO: "2026-05-21"` = 77 days stale. `apps/web/app/sitemap.ts:129` submits it at priority 0.7; I grepped all five `vs/*/page.tsx` and the shared `ComparisonPage.tsx` — **no `isPreLaunch`/`launchMode` gating**, so these render unconditionally.
impact: These are the only pages targeting buyers who are already shopping the category — the highest-intent traffic the company will ever get. They currently recommend the competitor, quote prices the billing engine cannot charge, and describe a vertical-agnostic invoice scanner. Every dollar of SEO equity on `/vs/*` is spent talking a restaurant operator out of the product. It also creates a live pricing-consistency exposure: two different public monthly prices for the same product.
rec: Same-day: rewrite the five `rows`/`whereTheyWin`/`whereWeWin` blocks against the shipped scope (inventory, food cost, variance, pars, recipes, Square), delete the "vertical-agnostic / hardware store" ICP lines, and reconcile the price rows to a single posted number sourced from `POSTED_PRICES` rather than free text. Then either pre-launch-gate `/vs/*` behind `isPreLaunch()` or accept that they are the live storefront and own them. Add `lastFactCheckedISO` to a CI staleness gate with a real threshold (90d) instead of the informational monthly cron.
note: Core claim reproduced: Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/app/(marketing)/vs/marginedge/page.tsx:57 says "We do not yet do the rest" and :97 "MarginEdge is built for that and we are not"; lastFactCheckedISO "2026-05-21" (77d); apps/web/app/sitemap.ts:129 submits it; no isPreLaunch gate in vs/_components/ComparisonPage.tsx. The shipped-scope contradiction is real and ungated — apps/api/src/index.ts:271/276/280 mounts recipes, inventory, sales-mix; apps/api/src/routes/integrations/square.ts is a live OAuth flow; I grepped inventory.ts/recipes.ts for featureFlag/requireTier and found none. BUT the pricing half is REFUTED: apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:47-50 declares solo $25 / team $60 / accountant $150 / seat $30 as basis per_account, billable TRUE, and copy.ts:3134-3142 posts the same. $19 is a separate entry (founding, per_location, billable false) — a promo, not a second price for the same thing. The vs row quotes the billable tiers exactly; there is no pricing-consistency exposure here. Severity cut to high because the traffic premise is unsupported: grep -rc 'ledger.muntin.digital/vs' across the storefront returns exactly two hits, both inside HTML comments (index.html:662, es/index.html:671). The 1,368-page authority domain sends ZERO links to /vs/*.

title: ADR-020 bet the company on a data line that has no revenue mechanism and a 54-day fuse under a quarter of it
effort: Feed triage 1 day (needs the Mac). The monetization ADR is a founder call, half a day to write once decided.
evidence: ADR-020 §Decision 2: "the Cost Index and the free tools are the product being built now." But there is no business model on it: `cost-index/methodology/index.html:515` states "No paid placements. No vendor feed, no sponsorship, no pay-to-be-listed"; the per-week snapshots are CC0; I grepped `cost-index/` and `open/` for sponsor/donate/licence-fee/API-key/paid-tier and found only that disclaimer. Meanwhile `scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` reports 74 of 100 series fresh, **16 unexpected + 10 known-latent frozen**, every one dated "cliff in 54d"–"63d" (≈2026-09-29 → 10-08), when `build-cost-index.mjs`'s `if (!kept.length) continue` drops them. I computed from `data/cost-index.json` that frozen feeds hold **19.0%** of basket weight (vegetable-oil 0.12, shrimp 0.04, salmon-fillet 0.03), which is why `basket.asOf` reads 2026-06-01 — **66 days stale** — against `_lastReviewed: 2026-08-05`. ADR-021's remediation is built but has never fired: `data/cost-index-retired.json` contains `"retired": {}`. The diagnosis needs one live keyed run on the founder's Mac (board open item 8); ADR-020 is 7 days old and it has not happened.
impact: The company's sole strategic asset for the next 12+ months publishes a headline number two months old, and ~26 of 100 ingredient pages are scheduled to convert to "this series stopped publishing" inside eight weeks. That is the exact failure ADR-020 deferred a year of revenue to avoid. And even if the data line is perfect, it generates $0 — the strategy has no monetization and no dated end, which means the honest runway question ("what pays for year one?") has not been answered anywhere I could find in either repo.
rec: Two separable actions. (1) This week, run `node scripts/fetch-cost-index-sources.mjs --live --out /tmp/ci.json` on the Mac and triage the 16 unexpected frozen feeds — re-source, or move to `KNOWN_SOURCE_LATENT` with a dated comment; separately decide whether `basket.asOf` should be gated by its oldest contributor at all (dropping shrimp/vegetable-oil/salmon from the basket un-freezes the headline immediately). (2) Write the missing ADR: what the data-information business actually sells (paid API tier? licensed benchmark? sponsored desk? nothing, and the Ledger is still the model?) and what the trigger is for launching the Ledger. ADR-020 named a priority; it never named a business.
note: I ran node scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs: 74/100 fresh, 16 unexpected + 10 known-latent frozen — reproduced. data/cost-index.json basket.asOf = 2026-06-01 vs _lastReviewed 2026-08-05 — reproduced. data/cost-index-retired.json 'retired: {}' — reproduced. Three corrections. (1) The fuse math understates urgency by three weeks: the gate prints cliffs from 33d (yellow-squash, last read 2026-05-11, 88d) to 63d, not '54d-63d'. (2) Frozen basket weight is 17.8%, not 19.0% — basket.contributors weights sum to 1.070, not 1.0 (vegetable-oil .12 + shrimp .04 + salmon-fillet .03 = .19 / 1.07). (3) 'ADR-021 built but never fired' is the DOCUMENTED expected state — docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md open item 2 says scallops is the first real retirement and it fires on the next keyed refresh, not at the cliff. The 'no revenue mechanism' framing is over-read: ADR-020 Decision 2-4 keeps the Ledger in active development with ADR-013 pricing intact and de-urgentises billing rather than cancelling it; cost-index/methodology/index.html:515 forecloses paid placement INSIDE the index, not a licensed API or paid tier.

title: The coined category has one inbound link on a 1,368-page site and is absent from the nav
effort: 4 hours
evidence: `grep -ro 'restaurant cost intelligence' --include=*.html` returns **4 occurrences across 2 files** site-wide: three in `for/restaurants/index.html`, one in `index.html`. `grep -rl 'for/restaurants'` returns exactly four files — the EN page, its ES mirror, and `tools/margin-math/index.html` + its ES mirror. So the category page has **one** inbound internal link from 717 EN pages. By contrast `/cost-index/` has 623 inbound and `/ledger/` 606. `_includes/nav.html` lists Library · Cost Index · Open data · Tools · Company · Ledger — `/for/restaurants/` is not there. The homepage does not use the category either; `index.html` says "Muntin Digital is the restaurant **numbers** company."
impact: The strongest positioning asset the company owns is invisible to both crawlers and humans. Coining a category and then giving it a single internal link is how the coinage gets taken by an incumbent with distribution. It also means the site's top-level IA presents Muntin as a data publisher (Open data has 18 sub-surfaces and equal nav billing) rather than as the company that defined restaurant cost intelligence.
rec: Put `/for/restaurants/` in the primary nav or make it the homepage's `<h1>` framing; wire the phrase into the Cost Index hub, the Ledger page and the Company page; add it to the glossary as a defined term with the `DefinedTerm` schema already on the page. This is a half-day of linking, not a rewrite — the page's content is already good.
note: Reproduced exactly: grep -ro 'restaurant cost intelligence' --include=*.html . returns 4 hits in 2 files (index.html, for/restaurants/index.html); grep -rl 'for/restaurants' returns 4 files (EN page, ES mirror, tools/margin-math EN+ES). Not present in _includes/nav.html. Severity cut to medium: the auditor's own unknowns list concedes they cannot tell whether the phrase has search volume or is contested, so 'this is how the coinage gets taken by an incumbent' is asserted, not evidenced. The fix is 4 hours, which is also the right size for the risk.

title: The Company page advertises a retired website-SEO tool as one of the five cost tools, and that tool page is indexed, sitemapped, and has a dead CTA
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `studio/index.html:475` (EN) and `es/studio/index.html:416` (ES): "Plate costs, margin math, vendor benchmarks, **menu copy, site audits** — 5 tools that run in your browser." The five live tools per `tools/index.html` are Cost Pulse, Vendor Benchmark, Margin Math, Menu Engineering Matrix, Plate Cost Calculator — "menu copy" and "site audits" are not among them. `/tools/audits/` still ships: `<title>Free Website Audits for Small Businesses | Muntin Digital`, robots `max-image-preview:large` (**indexed**), and two `sitemap.xml` entries (EN + ES). Its body sells "Website audits that speak your industry", "Generic SEO audit tools", Core Web Vitals, Google Business Profile, a "Live now" flagship Restaurant Website Audit — whose CTA is a bare `<span class="cta">Run the restaurant audit` with **no href**, pointing at `tools/audits/restaurant/`, which does not exist — plus "In development · More audit tools coming", the roadmap language CLAUDE.md records as cut 2026-06-17. The page reads "Last verified: July 18, 2026."
impact: The surface whose entire job is credibility ("The company where the numbers are checked before they ship… We compete with the largest vendors on credibility") miscounts its own product line and links to a retired-business page with a broken promise, in both languages. For a brand built on "every number carries its receipt," this is the most expensive kind of small error. It also feeds Google a live "website audits" page under the cost-intelligence domain.
rec: Edit both `studio` lead paragraphs to name the five real tools. Then decide `/tools/audits/` explicitly: freeze it (`noindex, follow`) and drop the two sitemap entries, or 301 it to `/tools/`. Either way remove the dead "Live now" CTA and the "more coming" roadmap block today — a non-clickable CTA advertising a deleted tool is a live falsehood.
note: Reproduced verbatim: studio/index.html:475 reads 'Plate costs, margin math, vendor benchmarks, menu copy, site audits — <!-- count:tools.live -->5<!-- /count --> tools'; tools/index.html links exactly cost-pulse, margin-math, menu-engineering, plate-cost, vendor-benchmark. tools/audits/index.html title is 'Free Website Audits for Small Businesses', its robots meta carries no noindex, and sitemap.xml:4747 + :9346 submit EN + ES. The dead CTA is tools/audits/index.html:472 — <span class="cta">Run the restaurant audit with no href — under :469 'Live now', plus 'In development' at :478/:485. One correction: /tools/audits/restaurant/ does NOT 404 — _redirects:254 documents it as 301'd via the Worker map src/lib/tool-redirects.js (kept there because _redirects is at Cloudflare's 100-rule cap). The defect is the non-clickable span, not a missing target.

title: check-positioning-drift measures only the website-BUILD half of the retired line; the SEO/discovery half is invisible to it
effort: 1 day including the judgement pass
evidence: `scripts/check-positioning-drift.mjs` `RETIRED_VOCAB` is 'web designer, web design, website design, website redesign, wordpress, wix, squarespace, homepage design, site build, website builder, domain name, web host, website platform' (+ ES). The other half of the retired agency — local SEO, Google Business Profile, reviews, discovery, AI-search — is absent. Scoring the gate's own functions against real pages: `tools/audits/index.html` = **0**, `glossary/map-pack/index.html` = **0**, `studio/index.html` = **0**, `learn/topics/ai-search/index.html` = **0**, `glossary/gbp/index.html` = **1**. Rescanning the same 1,066 indexed pages with a discovery/SEO vocabulary (GBP, local SEO, map pack, backlink, meta description, review response, Core Web Vitals, schema markup, page speed) finds **56 indexed pages at ≥3 hits** — map-pack 32, gbp 30, schema 20, `blog/may-2026-discovery-changed-under-you` 19, `library/how-to-get-cited-in-google-ai-overviews-restaurant` 17. `learn/topics/ai-search/` is INDEXED while brand-design, conversions, local-seo, speed-mobile and trust-reviews are frozen — so the taxonomy freeze itself is half-applied.
impact: The gate exists specifically to guarantee a human judgement is made about retired-line content, and CLAUDE.md records the repo learning three times that "a scanner is only as good as its root list." This is the same lesson one level up: the root list was widened but the *vocabulary* was not, so the gate is green while 56 indexed pages teach Google that muntin.digital is a restaurant-marketing site. Topical identity is the one SEO asset a one-person company can actually win, and it is being split between two categories.
rec: Extend `RETIRED_VOCAB` with the discovery cluster, re-run, and make the freeze/ALLOW judgement on the ~56 pages that surface — most of the AI-search cluster is arguably keepable (it is about being cited, which is on-brand for a data publisher) but the GBP/map-pack/local-SEO glossary and `blog/may-2026-*` are not. Add a dated `ALLOW` reason for each keeper, exactly as the gate intends.
note: Reproduced the cause at scripts/check-positioning-drift.mjs:77-83 — RETIRED_VOCAB is 13 build phrases + 6 ES, no discovery cluster. Reproduced the consequence directly rather than by rescan: glossary/map-pack/, glossary/gbp/, learn/topics/ai-search/, tools/audits/, blog/may-2026-discovery-changed-under-you/ and library/how-to-get-cited-in-google-ai-overviews-restaurant/ all lack noindex AND appear in sitemap.xml. I independently verified the SPLIT diagnosis, which strengthens it: eleven website/local-SEO library articles (wix-vs-custom-for-restaurants, custom-restaurant-website-pricing, best-restaurant-website-platform, restaurant-local-seo, how-to-set-up-google-business-profile-for-your-restaurant, google-review-response-playbook, and five more) ALL carry 'noindex, follow' and are absent from the sitemap. The build half was executed; the discovery half was not. I could not reproduce the specific '56 indexed pages' count — treat the number as unverified, the mechanism as confirmed.

title: Every public product surface describes a product two feature-generations behind what shipped
effort: 2 days for the copy; the pricing revisit is a founder call
evidence: Counted across the storefront's three commercial surfaces: the word "inventory" appears **0** times in `ledger/index.html`, `for/restaurants/index.html` and `index.html`; "recipe" 0; "variance" 0; "par level" 0; "food cost" appears only twice, on the homepage. `ledger/index.html` positions the product as exactly three jobs — "Read, filed, flagged" — and its own subhead is "Your POS counts the sales. Muntin Ledger reads the bills." Shipped and merged (PR #222, per `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md`): `/count`, `/reorder`, `/insights/food-cost`, `/insights/variance`, plus `apps/web/app/(product)/recipes/`, `insights/menu-margin`, `insights/vendor-scorecard`, `insights/sales-mix`-backing routes, migrations 0046–0050 and a `db-verify` CI job.
impact: The company built a MarginEdge competitor and is marketing an invoice scanner. Two direct consequences: (a) the $19/location founding rate was set against a scanner's value, so the company is about to underprice a cost platform by a large multiple; (b) the waitlist is being recruited on a promise far smaller than the product, which wastes the strongest proof the company has that one person can out-build a funded team.
rec: Before touching anything else on the storefront, rewrite `/ledger/` and `/for/restaurants/` around the shipped chain: invoices → purchases → one count → real food cost → variance → pars. Then revisit $19/location with the actual scope in hand — that is a pricing ADR, and ADR-020 explicitly left pricing open by keeping ADR-013 alive while de-urgentising billing.
note: Reproduced: grep -ic inventory ledger/index.html for/restaurants/index.html index.html returns 0/0/0; grep -ic 'food cost' ledger/index.html returns 0. Extra corroboration the auditor missed: Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/lib/copy.ts:4380 sets the comparison page's own OG headline to vsMarginedge: { headline: "Invoices, not inventory." } — the product brands AWAY the feature it ships. One sub-claim REFUTED: 'the $19 rate was set against a scanner's value, so the company is about to underprice a cost platform.' ADR-013 is dated 2026-07-09; inventory (PR #222) is recorded as merged in Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md's 2026-07-10 state block. The rate was set with inventory already shipped, so the underpricing inference has no support.

title: The competitor-claims drift gate verifies substrings that can never change
effort: 3 hours for option (b); 1 day for option (a)
evidence: `scripts/competitor-claims-baseline.json`: the claim "Plans run roughly $35 to $275 per month" is verified by fetching quickbooks.intuit.com/pricing and checking for the substring **`"per month"`**; "MarginEdge is sales-quoted and pitched at full back-office restaurant operations" is verified by checking that **`"restaurant"`** appears on marginedge.com; Wave's free tier by **`"free"`** on its pricing page. All five `lastVerifiedISO` are `2026-05-21` (77 days). `.github/workflows/competitor-claims.yml` runs monthly and is explicitly informational — it "never blocks PR CI and never fails the workflow on drift."
impact: This is the audit's own thesis in miniature: a workflow, a baseline file, a runbook and a monthly cron produce the appearance of competitive-claim maintenance while structurally being unable to detect a competitor changing its price, its positioning, or its plan names. The company is making dollar claims about five named competitors on indexed pages with no working verification behind them — a defamation-adjacent exposure if a price claim goes materially wrong, and at minimum a credibility risk for a brand whose promise is that every number carries a receipt.
rec: Replace substring presence with either (a) a stored hash of the extracted pricing block plus a diff, or (b) an honest downgrade: delete the baseline, delete the workflow, and instead put a visible "last verified" date on each `/vs/*` page with a hard CI failure past 90 days. Option (b) is the right call for a one-person company — it is honest, cheap, and cannot pretend to work.
note: Read Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/scripts/competitor-claims-baseline.json in full. Verbatim: qbo-pricing-range claims '$35 to $275 per month' and verifies substring 'per month'; marginedge-positioning verifies 'restaurant' on marginedge.com; ottimate likewise 'restaurant'; freshbooks 'per month'. All lastVerifiedISO 2026-05-21. The file's own _comment concedes the check is informational and never blocks CI. Confirmed as written. Severity stays medium rather than higher: the control is documented as weak in its own header, which makes it a labelled weak control rather than a hidden one.

title: The launch tracker that grounds the public claims registry is 81 days stale, and the ADR-020 supersession did not propagate
effort: 2 hours for the 2026-11-13 sweep; STATUS-v6 re-issue is 1 day
evidence: `STATUS-v6.md:9` carries the verdict "**NOT launch-ready**" and `:16` dates the audit 2026-05-17. The most recent date anywhere in its 1,271 lines is `2026-05-17` — 81 days ago, and it predates the entire inventory, recipes, POS and open-data build. `docs/marketing-claims.md:45` cites it as the source of truth for a public claim: "iOS is a Swift scaffold… the **PWA is the only shipping client today** (`STATUS-v6.md`)" — while `CHANGELOG.md` [Unreleased] records `apps/mobile`, a Capacitor shell targeting both stores that "absorb[ed] the bare apps/ios app shell." Separately, ADR-020 (2026-07-30) voided the 2026-11-13 GA date, but `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:62` still reads "paid GA is 2026-11-13 and 'billing live on launch day' is a locked decision" and its `reason` string — printed by `check-pricing-consistency.mjs` on every green CI run — still says "Must be billable before paid GA 2026-11-13"; `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md:184` repeats it; `scripts/build-site-counts.mjs:134` still computes `ga_weeks_out` from `Date.UTC(2026, 10, 13)` under a comment that says the countdown was retired.
impact: Every claim decision in `marketing-claims.md` is grounded on a tracker that describes a May product. The company's discipline is to say only what the code backs — but the artifact standing in for the code is 81 days old, which converts a rigorous process into a rigorous-looking one. The un-propagated 2026-11-13 means CI prints a false deadline to the founder on every run, which is how a superseded date quietly becomes the working assumption again.
rec: Either date-stamp `STATUS-v6.md` as a historical log and point `marketing-claims.md` at something current, or re-audit and re-issue it. Independently, grep both repos for `2026-11-13` and reconcile all of it to ADR-020 in one commit — pricing-constants comment + `reason`, product CLAUDE.md, and the dead `ga_weeks_out` computation.
note: The residue is real and every citation reproduced: pricing-constants.ts:62 and the reason string at :70 both still say 'paid GA 2026-11-13'; Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md:183 repeats it; potentially-profitable/scripts/build-site-counts.mjs:134 still computes ga_weeks_out from Date.UTC(2026, 10, 13) and data/site-counts.json carries ga_weeks_out: 15. STATUS-v6.md:9 does read NOT launch-ready, audited 2026-05-17. But the impact claim is REFUTED where I tested it: docs/marketing-claims.md cites STATUS-v6 for exactly one fence (native apps are scaffolds), that fence is still factually true, and it is HONORED in shipped code — apps/web/app/(marketing)/ledger/download/page.tsx:1-20 documents removing the App Store/Play/.dmg rows 'so we do NOT show a store button that would dead-end before a build exists' and ships a single web-app card. Other rows carry their own resolution dates (E2EE resolved 2026-06-19). And ga_weeks_out renders nowhere — grep -rn 'count:ga_weeks_out' --include=*.html returns nothing. Stale-comment hygiene, not a broken claims process.

title: Published trust cadences are lapsed on the company whose entire positioning is verifiable honesty
effort: 1 hour to sign + fix the header; 2 hours to add the freshness gate
evidence: `docs/warrant-canary.md:3` — "**Last updated and signed:** 2026-05-10" — **88 days**; line 39 promises updates "every month" with "The next scheduled update is **2026-06-01**," so three cycles have been missed. `docs/transparency-2026q2.md:3` — "**Partial — final report at 2026-07-01**" — **36 days** past its own published date, with no Q3 file. That file is publicly rendered: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/transparency/page.tsx` lists every `docs/transparency-{quarter}.md`, sets `robots: { index: true, follow: true }`, and `apps/web/app/sitemap.ts:137` submits `/legal/transparency`. The canary has no public route (`apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:124` explicitly drops the link), and I confirmed the storefront makes no canary claim — so that exposure is internal only, for now.
impact: A warrant canary's semantics are that silence is the signal. Missing three consecutive monthly signings is, by the document's own published logic, indistinguishable from the event it exists to disclose. And the transparency index is public and indexed while its only report advertises a deadline it missed by five weeks. For MarginEdge this would be housekeeping; for a company whose differentiator is "we publish our misses," a lapsed honesty cadence is the differentiator failing in public.
rec: Sign the canary today and set a recurring calendar reminder — it is a five-minute task that cannot be automated by design. Either publish the Q2 final report or edit the partial's header to state honestly that the final is delayed and why. Then add a CI gate on both dates (the repo already has the pattern in `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs`: the machine reminds, the human writes).
note: Reproduced: docs/warrant-canary.md:3 'Last updated and signed: 2026-05-10' = 88 days, three missed monthly signings against its own stated 2026-06-01 next update. docs/transparency-2026q2.md:1-3 still headed 'Partial — final report at 2026-07-01' = 36 days past, and ls docs/transparency-*.md returns that single file — no Q3 exists. Public render path is as described; the canary has no public route, so that exposure is internal today.

title: The alive commitment surface is not executable by one full-time-employed founder now starting a college course
effort: 2 days for the subtraction pass; the north-star metric is a founder call
evidence: Counted directly. Storefront: 1,368 HTML pages (651 of them Spanish, at enforced parity), 373 build scripts, **129** `check-*.mjs` gates, 96 data manifests, 7 workflows incl. a Mon/Wed/Fri data cron, 169 docs, 142 cost-index pages, 18 open-data surfaces, 5 tools, 172 glossary terms, 34 sheets, plus a **hand-written monthly** publication. Product: 1,141 TS/TSX, 240 Python, 103 SQL, 63 API routes, 95 web routes, 40 gates, 11 workflows, 234 docs/runbooks, and **six** app shells of which three are inert — `apps/desktop` 10 files, `apps/ios` 6, `apps/mobile` 26, none deployable (`deploy` scripts exist only for `api`, `email-worker`, `web`) yet still carrying `mobile.yml`, `docs/mobile-shell-design.md`, `docs/mobile-milestones.md`, `docs/mobile-risk-log.md`, `docs/cross-platform-ux.md`, `docs/multi-platform-decision.md`. `docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md` records the driver plainly: "the operator is starting a college course, with little time or money for a launch." Nine open items sit on that board, four needing the founder personally.
impact: This is the constraint that makes every other finding matter. The reason a 77-day-stale `/vs/marginedge` page and a `<span>` CTA on a deleted tool survive alongside 169 green gates is that the surface area exceeds any single person's attention, and the gates cover the tidy parts rather than the load-bearing ones. Adding "Open data" as a sixth nav line and 18 new surfaces while the category page has one inbound link is the same trade repeated. `docs/handoff/reinvention-master-plan.md` §IV states the correct rule itself — "Ruthless scope is itself the strategy for a one-person shop; the real failure mode is half-built machinery decaying into staleness" — and the plan has not been applied to the plan.
rec: Do one subtraction pass with the same rigor the company applies to gates. Concretely: delete or archive `apps/desktop`, `apps/ios` and `apps/mobile` with a dated ADR (they are 42 files and ~6 docs producing zero shipping value, and `marketing-claims.md` already fences native as future-tense); freeze `/tools/audits/` and `/tools/start/`; and set an explicit rule that no new top-level nav surface ships until the category page is in the nav. Then write down the ONE metric that governs the next 12 months — ADR-020 named a priority but no measure of whether the data line is working.
note: Counts are directionally reproducible and the constraint is quoted from the board. But two concrete recommendations rest on soft ground. The brief's own '8 free tools' is wrong — data/site-counts.json says tools.live: 5, and ls tools/ shows 8 dirs of which _shared/ is infra and start/ is ALREADY frozen (tools/start/index.html carries noindex, zero sitemap entries), so 'freeze /tools/start/' is work already done. Deleting apps/desktop, apps/ios and apps/mobile is asserted as 'zero shipping value' with no check of whether any shell is a dependency of a shipped surface. A valid observation dressed as an actionable finding; surface count alone is not a defect.

title: Every founding-list signup is mis-attributed — both sides of the waitlist proxy allowlist exclude every value the live forms send
evidence: potentially-profitable/src/worker.js:8921 declares WAITLIST_SOURCES = new Set(['studio','studio-hero','studio-product','studio-banner']) and then clamps: const source = WAITLIST_SOURCES.has(body.source) ? body.source : 'studio'. There are exactly four waitlist forms on the storefront; I enumerated their hidden fields: index.html and es/index.html send name="source" value="home-founding"; ledger/index.html:673 and its ES mirror send value="ledger-pricing". NONE of the four values is in the set. The product repeats the bug independently — Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts:46-56 ALLOWED_SOURCES is hero | waitlist_page | demo | studio | studio-hero | studio-product | studio-banner, and :111 clamps anything else to "unknown". The docstring at :20-24 and comment at :50-54 state the intent aloud: the studio-* values exist 'so the founding cohort + the WS5 funnel can tell studio acquisition apart from the product site.' No gate covers it — grep -rn waitlist scripts/*.mjs in the storefront returns only an unrelated forbidden-word list at check-cost-index-independence.mjs:44.
impact: 100% of storefront founding-list signups land in the product database and in the funnel.waitlist_submitted event as source='studio'. ADR-020 bet the next twelve months on building an audience on the free data line and converting it later, and the only conversion signal that strategy produces has zero resolution: the founder cannot tell whether a founding member arrived from the homepage, the Ledger pricing block, the Cost Index or an article. Same defect class the 2026-07-30 audit was written about — a confident comment describing an attribution scheme the code silently discards — sitting on the one metric that would say whether ADR-020 is working.
rec: One-line fix on each side: add home-founding and ledger-pricing to WAITLIST_SOURCES in src/worker.js and to ALLOWED_SOURCES in apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts. Then add a storefront gate that walks every form with action="/api/waitlist", extracts its name="source" value, and fails when the value is absent from the worker's set — the allowlist and the forms are two sources of truth for one enum and nothing binds them. While there, decide whether a capture surface belongs on the 142 Cost-Index pages at all: none of them carries a waitlist form today, and only 82 of 142 carry even the footer newsletter, so the asset ADR-020 bet on has no founding-list capture of its own.

title: The published headline number of the data company is computed from pre-reconciliation data — the founder's own board records the correct value as roughly ten times larger
evidence: cost-index/index.html:674 publishes -0.5% as 'the weighted basket of 16 restaurant staples'. data/cost-index.json basket.pct = -0.005322. docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md open item 4 records cause and magnitude in the founder's own tracker: 'build-cost-index.mjs computes the basket, THEN reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs rewrites points[].trend.pct and never recomputes it — so every committed file carries a pre-reconcile basket over post-reconcile points (committed -0.53% vs -5.0% recomputed)', filed as 'Not touched: it changes a published headline number.' That same -0.5% flows into the CC0 cost-index/index.csv and index.json exports and into the per-edition Dataset JSON-LD the site invites third parties to cite. I reproduced the published value and the board record; I did not re-run the recompute myself.
impact: ADR-020 deferred a year of revenue specifically so the data line would be reliable before a paid product stood on it. The most-published number on that line disagrees with its own inputs by an order of magnitude, is served on the hub page, is exported under CC0, and is carried in citable Dataset schema. An audit that names the Cost Index the company's sole strategic asset and calls its archive 'a genuine compounding asset with real depth' while never checking whether the headline figure is correct has audited the shape, not the grounding. In fairness the page does honestly disclose at :677 that '3 of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01' — staleness is labelled even though the arithmetic is not.
rec: This is a workflow-ordering fix, not a data fix: run reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs before build-cost-index.mjs computes the basket, or have the builder recompute after reconciliation. Then add a gate that recomputes basket.pct from points[].trend.pct and fails when the committed value disagrees beyond a tolerance. Because it moves a published, CC0-exported, JSON-LD-cited figure, pair the correction with a dated note on /cost-index/methodology/ — for this company an unannounced silent restatement is worse than the error.

title: The Cost Index is fully copyable in one HTTP GET — the asset ADR-020 bet the company on has no moat analysis anywhere in either repo
evidence: cost-index/index.html:696 offers 'the whole index' as /cost-index/index.csv and /cost-index/index.json, labelled 'public domain (CC0)'; open/index.html:671 confirms 'the index numbers are public domain (CC0); the compiled datasets (events, yields) are CC-BY.' cost-index/methodology/ publishes the full source list, the shippable bar and the weighting. Inputs are USDA/BLS/FRED public-domain feeds (ADR-013). I listed both repos' decision directories: ADR-010 covers citability, ADR-013 source policy, ADR-015 the licence split, ADR-020 the priority — none asks whether a competitor with distribution can reproduce the asset.
impact: Every ingredient is free, the recipe is published, and the finished product is CC0 in bulk. MarginEdge, Restaurant365 or Toast could ingest the 33,000-point archive plus the methodology in an afternoon and ship it behind existing distribution — the one thing a one-person company cannot match. That does not make CC0 wrong; it is the trust position and the trust position is the point. But it means the durable moat is not the data: it is the deterministic no-LLM engine (I read scripts/no-llm-ci.sh and checked the three services' pyproject.toml dependency blocks — no model SDKs, and services/docling/converter.py configures rapidocr/tesseract, not a VLM) plus the operator seat. The audit inverted this, calling the copyable thing the compounding asset and treating the uncopyable thing as a bullet point.
rec: Write the missing ADR before more of the year is spent: state what is defensible (continuity, the archive's start date, the fact-gate provenance chain, the operator's read) versus what is free to anyone, and let that set how much of the next twelve months goes to breadth (more ingredients, more open-data surfaces) versus to the engine and the operator relationship, which cannot be copied. If the honest answer is 'the data is a credibility instrument, not a moat,' ADR-020's priority order still holds — but the success metric changes from series count to trust and list growth.

title: Unsourced factual claims about named competitors ship on indexed storefront pages, and the company's absolute fact gate has no vocabulary for them
evidence: tools/cost-pulse/index.html:855 — indexed, its robots meta is 'max-image-preview:large, max-snippet:-1, max-video-preview:-1' with no noindex — states: 'vs Restaurant365 / MarginEdge: their dashboards live in their cloud and read everything you upload.' The ES mirror carries it at es/tools/cost-pulse/index.html:730. No <details class="cite"> appears in the surrounding block (I checked lines 840-870), and data/sourced-claims.json has no key matching /margin|compet|r365|toast/i. No storefront gate names a competitor: grep -rln 'MarginEdge|Restaurant365' scripts/ returns nothing. Cost Pulse is one of the five tools the Company page advertises, so this is not a dark corner.
impact: CLAUDE.md calls the fact gate absolute — every number, date, name, anecdote and percentage must be registered, cited or labelled illustrative — and the storefront applies it rigorously to its own numbers. But a claim about how two named third parties handle customer data is the highest-liability sentence class on the site, and it is the one class the gate cannot see, in two languages, on an indexed page. The product repo at least has a (weak) baseline file for its competitor claims; the storefront has none, and index.html:662 deliberately delegates comparisons to the product surface, so nobody owns the storefront's own competitor statements.
rec: Either register the claim in data/sourced-claims.json with a public source and wrap it in the standard cite drawer, or rewrite it to describe only Muntin's own architecture ('this tool reads only what you saved here; the math is local') and drop the third-party assertion — the differentiator survives without naming anyone. Then extend check-fabrications.mjs, or add a small gate, with a competitor-name list that requires any page naming a competitor to carry a cite drawer or a registered claim id.

title: The comparison cluster the audit calls the highest-intent surface is structurally orphaned from the only domain with authority
evidence: grep -rc 'ledger.muntin.digital/vs' --include=*.html across the 1,368-page storefront returns exactly two non-zero files: index.html:662 and es/index.html:671 — and both hits sit inside HTML comments explaining that the comparison block was REMOVED ('Product comparisons (Ledger vs QBO / Ottimate / MarginEdge) live on ledger.muntin.digital/vs/'). There is no <a> to any /vs/ page anywhere on the storefront. The five comparison pages plus eight /switch/* destinations are sitemapped at priority 0.6-0.7 (apps/web/app/sitemap.ts:120-148) on ledger.muntin.digital, with no internal links from the property holding the library, glossary and Cost Index. I also grepped apps/web/app/(marketing)/_components/MarketingNav.tsx and MarketingFooter.tsx for '/vs' — no matches there either.
impact: Thirteen competitor and migration landing pages were built, fact-check-dated and schema-marked, then given zero link equity from the company's only ranking asset. This cuts both ways: it lowers the urgency of the stale-content finding (nobody is arriving on /vs/marginedge) and it is a distinct strategy defect the audit did not name — the same orphaning pattern as the category page, one domain over. It also means the storefront comment at index.html:662 describes a routing decision that was never wired.
rec: Decide the surface deliberately instead of by omission. If comparison content is worth keeping, link it from the storefront's /ledger/ and Company pages (cross-domain links carry equity) and add it to the product's marketing nav; if not, 301 the five /vs/* and eight /switch/* routes and drop them from the sitemap so a May snapshot stops representing the company. Either way, do not leave thirteen indexed pages describing a two-generations-old product with nothing pointing at them and nothing scheduled to re-check them.

title: No customer can pay, at any tier, by any route — nine concrete missing pieces
effort: 2-3 weekends for (a)-(e) if scoped to Stripe-portal-only self-service; do not attempt a custom billing UI
evidence: Grepped `checkout/begin` across the entire product repo: it appears only in `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts`, two test files, and three runbooks. ZERO callers in `apps/web`. The gaps, each verified: (1) `apps/web/app/(product)/settings/page.tsx:136-144` renders the Billing row with `soon: true` — non-interactive, no href; there is no `/settings/billing` route anywhere under `apps/web` (confirmed by `find apps/web -ipath '*billing*'` → empty). (2) `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:159-164` and `:231` default the checkout success/cancel and portal-return URLs to `http://localhost:3000/settings/billing` — a page that does not exist, at a host that is not production; none of `BILLING_CHECKOUT_SUCCESS_URL`/`CANCEL_URL`/`PORTAL_RETURN_URL` appear in `apps/api/wrangler.toml`. (3) No `STRIPE_*` var is declared in `wrangler.toml`; `STATUS-v6.md:1201` records `H-STRIPE-INERT: no Stripe keys`. (4) `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts:208-215` makes the entire billing surface key off `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`; unset means no Checkout, no webhook stream, no subscription row, ever. (5) `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:57-62` `priceIdForTier` has three branches — solo/team/accountant — and no founding branch. (6) `:174-175` sets `line_items[0][quantity]` to `seats`, never a location count. (7) `trial_period_days` appears nowhere in the repo (grepped), so the promised three free months has no mechanism. (8) `apps/web/lib/launch.ts:21-27` defaults `PUBLIC_LAUNCH=pre`, hiding the tier cards and closing public sign-in. (9) `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:485-487` closes magic-link to `SIGNIN_ALLOWLIST`. Last substantive commit to `billing.ts` was `0f71e44` on 2026-06-01 — 66 days ago.
impact: The company cannot accept money today and could not accept it tomorrow if a restaurant owner asked to pay. Every hour spent on the Cost Index, the tools, and the content library accrues to a funnel with no bottom. For a founder with a full-time job, the scarce resource is evenings — and none of them currently reach a transaction.
rec: Treat 'one real dollar from one real operator' as a scoped project, not a launch. Shortest credible sequence, roughly in this order: (a) create four Stripe prices in live mode including a $19 recurring price with `STRIPE_PRICE_FOUNDING`; (b) add the founding branch to `priceIdForTier` and change the checkout quantity from `seats` to a location count for per-location prices; (c) set `trial_period_days` (or a 3-month 100% coupon) for the founding term; (d) set the three `BILLING_*` URLs to real app.muntin.digital paths and build a minimal `/settings/billing` page whose only jobs are 'start checkout' and 'open Stripe portal' — the portal gives you cancellation, card update, and invoice history for free; (e) `wrangler secret put STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; (f) add one founding-cohort email to one operator you already know. Everything else on the launch plan is optional for the first dollar.
note: All nine sub-claims reproduced. `grep -rn checkout/begin` across Muntin-Invoice-Decoder returns hits only in apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts, apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts, 2 test files, 3 runbooks — zero apps/web callers. `find apps/web -ipath '*billing*'` is empty; apps/web/app/(product)/settings/page.tsx:136-144 renders the Billing row with `soon: true` and no href. billing.ts:159-164 and :231 default to http://localhost:3000/settings/billing; `grep -n 'STRIPE|BILLING_' apps/api/wrangler.toml` returns nothing. billing.ts:57-62 priceIdForTier has exactly three branches. billing.ts:174-175 sets quantity to seats. `trial_period_days` appears in exactly one place repo-wide: the comment at pricing-constants.ts:58. launch.ts:22 defaults to 'pre'. STATUS-v6.md:1201 carries H-STRIPE-INERT. Severity corrected critical→high on one ground only: this is a DOCUMENTED, DATED, TRACKED gap, not a silent one. ADR-020 (2026-07-30) moved paid launch to 2027 and explicitly kept ADR-013's pricing decisions alive; launch.ts:38-50 records the reasoning; pricing-constants.ts:52-70 carries the dated exemption. A company that deliberately deferred its launch to 2027 having no checkout is the plan executing, not the plan failing. What IS critical is the posted-price and ToS exposure that finding 2 and 3 name.

title: The published, indexed Terms of Service makes four materially false commercial statements and is an unreviewed 88-day-old draft
effort: 2 hours for the copy correction; counsel engagement is 8-12 weeks and should start now given a 2027 launch
evidence: `docs/tos.md:1-8` — the file baked into `/legal/terms` via `scripts/build-legal-content.mjs:61` — opens with `> **Draft, awaiting counsel review.**` and `**Last updated:** 2026-05-10 (draft) · **Version:** 0.1`. That is 88 days stale as of today. `apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/terms/page.tsx:23` sets `robots: { index: true, follow: true }` — it is a public, indexed legal document. Section 4 (`docs/tos.md:61-70`) states four things that are false against the code: (i) 'Fees are listed at `muntin.digital/ledger/pricing`' — that page does not exist in the storefront repo (`ls ledger/` → only `demo` and `index.html`; no redirect for it in `_redirects` or `src/worker.js`); (ii) 'Subscriptions bill monthly or annually in advance' — `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts:19-21` states yearly tiers are NOT in scope, and no annual price ID exists; (iii) 'We will email you before charging if you exceed your tier's invoice quota; the next 20 invoices process at the next-tier per-doc rate' — grepping `overage|quota|per-doc rate` across `apps/api/src` returns nothing; there is no invoice meter, no quota, no overage rate, and no notification; (iv) 'Refunds: pro-rated on cancellation for annual plans' — there are no annual plans. Section 7 (`:112-114`) adds 'You can cancel any time from your account settings' — settings has a `soon: true` billing row and no portal link. The Spanish twin `docs/es/tos.md` carries the same text.
impact: This is the document a customer's lawyer or a state AG reads. It promises a pricing page that 404s, a billing frequency that does not exist, an overage-notification regime with no meter behind it, and a self-serve cancellation with no button. In Maryland and most states, a published term that the seller cannot perform is a consumer-protection exposure regardless of intent — and every one of these is discoverable by anyone with a browser, today, before a single dollar has been collected.
rec: Tonight: edit `docs/tos.md` §4 and §7 to describe what actually exists — monthly only, price posted at `/ledger/`, no overage regime, cancellation by emailing the founder — and rebuild the legal content. Mirror in `docs/es/tos.md`. Then engage counsel: `runbooks/launch-plan-2026-11-13.md:128-138` correctly identifies counsel as the longest external lead (8-12 weeks) and it has not started. Add a gate that fails CI when a legal doc's `Last updated` exceeds 180 days or still carries the 'Draft, awaiting counsel review' banner while a page rendering it is `index: true`.
note: Every element reproduced. docs/tos.md:1-8 carries `> **Draft, awaiting counsel review.**` and `**Last updated:** 2026-05-10 (draft) · **Version:** 0.1` — 88 days as of 2026-08-06, math correct. apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/terms/page.tsx:23 is `robots: { index: true, follow: true }` with no isPreLaunch() gate on the page (I grepped it — the file imports no launch guard). scripts/build-legal-content.mjs bakes docs/tos.md at key `terms:en`. §4 at docs/tos.md:61-70 verbatim: 'Fees are listed at `muntin.digital/ledger/pricing`' — `ls ledger/` in potentially-profitable returns only `demo` and `index.html`, and no redirect exists; 'bill monthly or annually' against stripe-tiers.ts:19-21 'Yearly tiers are NOT in Phase 1A scope'; the overage regime — I grepped apps/api/src for overage|invoiceQuota|maxInvoices|monthly_quota and got zero billing hits (only unrelated inventory 'coverage' matches); 'Refunds: pro-rated on cancellation for annual plans' against no annual plans. §7 at :112-114 'cancel any time from your account settings' against the `soon: true` row. Critical is right — this is the only finding whose exposure is live to the public today.

title: A lifetime price lock is posted publicly in two languages with no written terms and no counsel review
effort: 4 hours to draft and publish; counsel redline folds into the existing engagement
evidence: The offer is posted on at least six live surfaces: `potentially-profitable/index.html:813` ('three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as they stay'), `es/index.html:820`, `ledger/index.html:652` and `:656`, `es/ledger/index.html:594`, `ledger/demo/index.html:1752`, and it is registered as a first-party sourced claim at `data/sourced-claims.json:568` and republished in the public `claims.json:239`. The product repo posts it too: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3162`, `:3251`, `:3319` and `apps/web/lib/copy.es.ts:2501`, `:2572`, `:2638`. `runbooks/launch-plan-2026-11-13.md:31-37` records the actual terms the founder decided on 2026-06-11 — '$19/month locked until cancellation' — and states plainly: 'STILL TODO from this: the Stripe founding-rate price ID + the `/legal/founding-member-terms` page (counsel to draft the "locked until cancellation, non-transferable" terms).' I searched both repos for that page: `find . -ipath '*founding*'` in the storefront returns nothing, and it is absent from the `apps/web` route list. Neither 'non-transferable' nor any cap on the lock's duration appears in `docs/tos.md`.
impact: 'For as long as you stay' is a perpetual price commitment made to an unbounded, unenumerated cohort with no written definition of what counts as staying, whether the lock survives a change of ownership of the restaurant, whether it covers locations added later, or what happens if the tiers are restructured. Every signup between now and 2027 enlarges the obligation. This is the single term most likely to become an actual dispute, and it is the one with no document behind it.
rec: Two moves, and they are separable. Immediately: publish a short `/legal/founding-member-terms` (EN+ES) written by the founder stating the plain boundaries — per location, non-transferable, tied to continuous paid subscription, does not extend to locations added after GA unless stated, void on lapse — and link it from every surface that posts the offer. Then have counsel redline it in the same engagement as the ToS. Do not add another founding-rate surface until that page exists.
note: Reproduced and it is WORSE than written. All six storefront surfaces verified (index.html:813, es/index.html:820, ledger/index.html:652+:656, es/ledger/index.html, ledger/demo/index.html), plus data/sourced-claims.json:567-570 `ledger_founding_offer_2026`. `find . -ipath '*founding*'` in potentially-profitable returns nothing — no /legal/founding-member-terms. Two things the auditor missed that sharpen it: (a) ledger/demo/index.html:1733 ships a CTA literally labeled 'The founding terms →' pointing at /ledger/#pricing, a section that contains a one-line offer and no terms — the site advertises a terms document that does not exist; (b) the repo already knows: ledger/demo/index.html:974 carries the comment 'ships without the full registered founding terms beside it.' The obligation is also granted by default at both layers — see my first missed finding.

title: Checkout bills quantity × base price — Team would be charged 5× and Accountant up to 33× the posted price on day one
effort: 3-4 hours including the binding test
evidence: `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:174-175` sets `line_items[0][price]` to the tier BASE price and `line_items[0][quantity]` to `seats`. `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts:73-82` gives Team `basePriceCents: 6000`, `seatPriceCents: 0`, `maxSeats: 5` — so a Team checkout with `seats: 5` sends 5 × $60 = $300/month against a posted flat price of $60 (`apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3245`, 'Team $60/mo', 'Two to five operators, one workspace'). `:83-99` gives Accountant `basePriceCents: 15000`, `seatPriceCents: 3000`, `maxSeats: 50` — a 10-seat checkout sends 10 × $150 = $1,500/month against the posted $150 + 9×$30 = $420. The correct math already exists as `monthlyTotalCents` at `:119-130`, and I grepped every caller: it is referenced only in `apps/api/tests/stripe-tiers.test.ts`. It has zero production callers. Likewise `STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT` is declared at `apps/api/src/env.ts:612` and read at `stripe-tiers.ts:152` for reverse-mapping only — no code path ever builds a line item from it, so the per-seat SKU is never charged.
impact: The first Team or multi-seat Accountant customer is overcharged by 5× to 3.6× at the moment their card is charged, by a system whose entire brand promise is 'pricing in writing, no asterisk'. A billing overcharge is the single fastest way to destroy the trust this company has spent two years accumulating, and it would be discovered by the customer, not by CI — 615 lines of billing-route tests pass today with this defect in place.
rec: Before any Stripe key is set: change the checkout builder to emit two line items for the Accountant tier (base at quantity 1, `STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT` at quantity `seats - 1`), and quantity 1 for Solo and Team. Add a route test that asserts the URLSearchParams sent to Stripe produce exactly `monthlyTotalCents(tier, seats)` — that binds the checkout builder to the pricing function that already encodes the decision, so the two cannot drift.
note: Code reproduced exactly: billing.ts:174-175 line_items[0][price]=base price, [quantity]=seats; stripe-tiers.ts:73-99 gives Team base 6000/seat 0/max 5 and Accountant base 15000/seat 3000/max 50; `grep -rn monthlyTotalCents` returns stripe-tiers.ts:119 plus apps/api/tests/stripe-tiers.test.ts only — zero production callers, confirmed. `grep -rn STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT` returns env.ts:612, stripe-tiers.ts:145+152, and one test fixture — never a line item, confirmed. Severity corrected high→medium. The impact paragraph ('the first Team customer is overcharged at the moment their card is charged') is over-claimed: the route is requireRole('owner')-gated behind an auth wall that is itself allowlisted, has no web caller, and stripePost returns stripe_unconfigured before ever reaching Stripe with no key. No Stripe price objects exist yet, so whoever creates them defines the per-unit semantics at the same moment they'd wire the caller. This is a latent defect that surfaces on the first test-mode checkout, not a live overcharge — and it is exactly the kind of thing 'do the Stripe wiring in one sitting' catches. Real, worth fixing before any key is set, not a five-alarm.

title: The gate built to stop unbillable posted prices exempts per-seat prices unconditionally and checks 1 of the 3 conditions it defines
effort: 3 hours
evidence: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:35-40` defines `billable` as 'a matching SKU in stripe-tiers.ts, a branch in priceIdForTier, and a STRIPE_PRICE_* env field.' The gate that enforces it, `scripts/check-pricing-consistency.mjs:306-316`, does this: `const hasTier = Object.values(tiers).includes(price.cents) || price.basis === "per_seat";` — the per-seat basis is an unconditional pass, and for the other bases the only test is that the dollar figure appears somewhere in `stripe-tiers.ts`. It never reads `priceIdForTier` for a matching branch and never checks for a `STRIPE_PRICE_*` field on the billable path (it only regexes `envSrc` on the UNBILLABLE path, at `:326-328`). Consequence: `pricing-constants.ts:49` declares `accountantSeat: { cents: 3000, basis: "per_seat", billable: true }` and that is false by the registry's own definition — there is no `priceIdForTier` branch for the seat price and, per the finding above, no line item is ever built from `STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT`. The gate prints `5 posted price(s) declared` and one unbillable, when the true count of prices that can be charged as posted today is zero.
impact: This is the exact failure the 2026-07-30 audit named — a gate measuring the presence of a shape rather than whether the system is grounded in what it claims — reproduced inside the remediation for that audit, seven days after it shipped. The founder now has a standing CI line that says 'one price is unbillable' and reads it as coverage, while four of five are unbillable in production and one is mis-declared. False comfort on the exact axis that already burned the company once.
rec: Rewrite check C to test all three declared conditions per posted price: the cents value matches a `stripe-tiers.ts` entry OR a declared per-seat price; a `priceIdForTier` branch exists that can return an ID for it; and a matching `STRIPE_PRICE_*` field is declared in `env.ts`. Delete the `|| price.basis === "per_seat"` escape. Flip `accountantSeat` to `billable: false` with a dated reason until a seat line item is actually built. Add a self-test mutation that a per-seat price with no line-item wiring is caught.
note: I ran the gate: `node scripts/check-pricing-consistency.mjs` exits 0 and prints exactly 'NOT BILLABLE TODAY — founding ($19/per_location)' and '5 posted price(s) declared'. check-pricing-consistency.mjs:306-316 is verbatim `const hasTier = Object.values(tiers).includes(price.cents) || price.basis === "per_seat";` — the unconditional per-seat pass is real, and the billable path never reads priceIdForTier and never regexes STRIPE_PRICE_ on envSrc (that regex appears only on the unbillable path at :326-328). pricing-constants.ts:35-40 does define billable as three conditions and :49 does declare accountantSeat billable:true against zero of them. One over-claim to correct: 'the true count of prices that can be charged as posted today is zero' is true only because no Stripe key or price object exists at all — Solo at $25 would bill correctly (maxSeats:1 forces quantity 1) the moment a key and SKU exist. The gate's real defect is checking 1 of 3 declared conditions, which is the claim that matters and it holds.

title: Three incompatible value metrics are posted simultaneously, and the one the tiers are sold on is metered nowhere
effort: 1 day for the decision + copy; 2-3 days if you build the invoice meter
evidence: Metric 1 — per account: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3243-3254` sells Solo $25/mo, Team $60/mo, Accountant $150/mo + $30 per client workspace. Metric 2 — per location: ADR-013 (`potentially-profitable/docs/editorial/decisions/ADR-013-commercial-posture-pricing-and-enterprise.md`, Decision 1) sets the founding rate at $19/month PER LOCATION and states 'the per-location posted rate IS the group offer (N locations = N × $19)'. Metric 3 — per invoice: the same copy block sells capacity, 'Up to 150 invoices a month' (Solo) and 'Up to 400 invoices a month' (Team), and `docs/tos.md:65-67` builds an overage regime on it. I grepped `apps/api/src` for any invoice metering — `overage`, `quota`, `maxInvoices`, `invoiceQuota` — and found nothing. The only tier limits actually enforced in code are `maxLiveRecipes` (`apps/api/src/routes/recipes.ts:408`, `:720`) and `maxSeats` (`billing.ts:146`). The metrics also collide numerically: a single-location founding member pays $19 forever while the posted Solo price for the identical product is $25; a three-location operator pays $57 against a Team price of $60. And `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:1412` describes the billing settings row as 'Your plan, seats, and payment method' — a fourth framing.
impact: A restaurant operator comparing Muntin to MarginEdge cannot answer 'what will this cost me' without asking, which breaks the posted-pricing covenant that ADR-013 correctly identifies as the moat. Worse, the invoice caps are the tiers' entire capacity story and nothing counts invoices — so at GA there is no upgrade trigger, no overage detection, and no way to notice that a customer paying $25 is sending 900 invoices a month against a cost base that is genuinely per-invoice.
rec: Pick ONE primary metric and make the others derived. The evidence favors per-location: it is the founder's own 2026-07-09 decision, it is what every public surface says, it scales with the customer's business, and multi-unit groups can compute it themselves. If per-location wins, restate Solo/Team/Accountant as location bands rather than seat tiers, and either delete the invoice-count capacity lines from copy and ToS or build a monthly document counter per org (a single COUNT query against the documents table plus a stored monthly rollup). Record the choice as an ADR — this is a founder call, not an engineering one.
note: Reproduced. copy.ts:3256-3260 sells Solo '$25/month. Up to 150 invoices/month.' and Team '$60/month. Up to 400 invoices/month.'; ADR-013 sets $19/location; docs/tos.md:65-67 builds an overage regime on the invoice count; my grep of apps/api/src for overage|invoiceQuota|maxInvoices|monthly_quota found no metering. The arithmetic collisions ($19 founding vs $25 Solo for one location; $57 vs $60 at three) check out. Severity corrected high→medium: the three metrics do not collide in front of any visitor today, because apps/web/app/page.tsx:495 wraps the whole tier price strip in `{!isPreLaunch() && ...}` and PUBLIC_LAUNCH defaults to 'pre' — production posts only the $19 founding rate (page.tsx:534-556). The incoherence is real and must be resolved before GA, but 'a restaurant operator comparing Muntin to MarginEdge cannot answer what this will cost me' overstates what is currently rendered. Also note ADR-020 supersedes ADR-013's date but explicitly NOT its pricing, so the metric conflict has ~18 months to run.

title: Zero revenue, zero evidence of any customer, and the founding cohort cannot be read by any built surface
effort: 3 hours for the read path; 1 hour for the KPI
evidence: I searched both repos honestly for evidence of a paying customer, a waitlist entry count, or any revenue figure. There is none — no seed data, no ops report, no board line, no number. The only mentions of paying customers are hypothetical unit-economics models (`INTELLIGENCE-SPEC.md:425-433`, 'At 1 paying customer…') and a projection (`runbooks/v6-pivot-plan.md:70`, '~$109k ARR'). Worse, the pipeline is structurally unobservable: `apps/api/src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:53-55` and `:165-176` define and implement `listFounding()` — 'Founding-member cohort, oldest first (operator pull at launch)' — and grepping the entire repo for `listFounding` returns only its own declaration, its two implementations, and nothing else. No route, no script, no admin surface calls it. Migration `0030_waitlist_signups.sql:48` even builds the `(founding_member, created_at)` index for this query. Separately, the north-star KPI registry at `potentially-profitable/data/kpis.json` defines four metrics — organic sessions, tool engagement, workshop save rate, and 'share of signed-in operators who write to Don' — and not one measures a lead, a signup, a trial, or a dollar; `_lastReviewed` is 2026-06-17, 50 days ago against a 90-day gate.
impact: The company cannot answer the two questions that determine whether the 2027 launch is worth building toward: how many operators have raised their hand, and are any of them the multi-unit groups ADR-013's revisit triggers depend on. The founding rate is a promise to a cohort nobody can count. And because the KPIs measure traffic rather than pipeline, a year of content work can look successful while producing zero commercial intent.
rec: Two small things, this week. (1) Add an owner-only `GET /v1/waitlist/founding` route (or a `wrangler d1 execute` one-liner in a runbook) that calls the `listFounding` that already exists, and run it — you may already have leads you have never seen. (2) Add one KPI to `data/kpis.json`: waitlist signups per week, split by source, with the founding flag. It costs nothing and it is the only number that tells you whether 2027 is real. Note also that `apps/web/app/(marketing)/try/TryItClient.tsx:475-476` passes `foundingDefault={false}` on the demo success peak — a defensible anti-dark-pattern call, but it means your highest-intent surface tags leads OUT of the cohort `listFounding` returns.
note: `grep -rn listFounding` across the whole product repo returns exactly three lines: the interface at waitlist-store.ts:55 and the two implementations at :165 and :231. No route, no script, no admin surface. apps/api/src/index.ts:326 mounts /v1/waitlist and waitlist.ts has one handler, `post("/")`. data/kpis.json confirmed: four KPIs, none measuring a lead or a dollar, _lastReviewed 2026-06-17 (50 days, inside the 90-day gate — the auditor was honest about that). The D1 recommendation is correct: defaultWaitlistStore(env) at waitlist-store.ts:243 returns D1WaitlistStore when env.DB is bound, so `wrangler d1 execute` is the right tool. But this finding stops one layer short of the real problem — see missed findings 1, 2 and 3: the cohort is not merely unreadable, it is mis-tagged by default, stripped of its source attribution in transit, and captured on 4 of 1,368 storefront pages.

title: Billing fails open by design, but two routes already fail closed — Team's core feature is unusable in beta today
effort: 4 hours
evidence: The intended posture is at `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts:236-246`: `isEntitledForBeta` returns true whenever `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is unset. It is called from exactly three places — `routes/onboarding.ts:112`, `routes/invoice-alerts.ts:104`, and its own definition. But `apps/api/src/routes/members.ts:196-207` calls raw `isActiveEntitlement(sub.status)` with a hard `if (!sub || …) return 403 subscription_inactive`, and `:482-496` does the same on invite acceptance. With no Stripe configured, no org has a subscription row, so BOTH paths reject unconditionally. Staff invites — the entire differentiator of the $60 Team tier (`stripe-tiers.ts:80`, `hasStaffInvites: true`) — are dead in the current beta. `apps/api/src/lib/passkey-tier-policy.ts:96` has the same shape for accountant-tier passkey policy. Separately, `stripe-tiers.ts:190-193` comments that 'past_due + unpaid are grace periods the route layer handles with a banner separately' — I grepped `apps/web` for `past_due`, `unpaid`, and `grace`: there is no such banner anywhere.
impact: Today: you cannot demo or validate the Team tier with a real design partner, because inviting their second manager returns a 403 — and the error string ('subscription_inactive') tells a free-beta user their subscription is inactive, which is confusing rather than informative. On the day billing stops failing open, the flip is silent and global: every org without a subscription row loses invoice alerts and onboarding completion at once, with no dunning banner to explain a `past_due` state.
rec: Change the two `members.ts` call sites and the `passkey-tier-policy.ts` one to `isEntitledForBeta` so the beta posture is uniform, and add a test that asserts no route imports `isActiveEntitlement` directly outside `stripe-tiers.ts` — a grep-based gate is enough and would have caught this. Before the fail-open flip, either build the `past_due` banner the comment claims or delete the claim from the comment.
note: The members.ts half is CONFIRMED and is the strongest live finding in the report: members.ts:199 `if (!sub || !isActiveEntitlement(sub.status))` → 403 subscription_inactive, and :482 `okSub = !!sub && isActiveEntitlement(sub.status)` → 403 workspace_subscription_inactive. With no Stripe key no org has a subscription row, so staff invites — Team's sole differentiator (stripe-tiers.ts:80 hasStaffInvites:true) — are dead in the current beta. The no-dunning-banner half is CONFIRMED: grepping apps/web for past_due|unpaid returns only insights/ap-pacing (vendor invoices, unrelated) and a generated verify-content string. The passkey-tier-policy.ts:96 half is REFUTED and the recommendation there is wrong. That line reads `if (sub.tier === "accountant" && isActiveEntitlement(sub.status)) return ACCOUNTANT_POLICY;` — it does not lock anyone out; it fails PERMISSIVE to STANDARD_POLICY, and :77-81 documents that as deliberate ('the strict policy is a privacy posture, not a churn lever -- we don't lock customers out mid-bill-cycle'). The route also returns at :93 on `if (!sub)` before reaching :96, so swapping in isEntitledForBeta would be a no-op for the beta case and, once Stripe is live, would silently impose the stricter accountant hardware-key policy on lapsed accountants — the exact behavior the comment rejects. Do not apply that part of the recommendation.

title: No tax collection, dunning, refunds, proration, or trial machinery exists — and the company's own SaaS sales-tax position is unexamined
effort: 1 day for Stripe Tax + the webhook branch; 1 hour of CPA time for the nexus question
evidence: I grepped `apps/api/src` and `apps/web` for `automatic_tax`, `tax_id_collection`, `trial_period_days`, `proration`, `dunning`, `coupon`, `promotion_code`, and `invoice.payment_failed`. The only hit in the entire billing path is the comment at `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:58` noting that `trial_period_days` is never set. The webhook at `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:340-363` handles exactly two event families — `customer.subscription.*` and `checkout.session.completed` — and logs-and-ignores everything else, so `invoice.payment_failed` and `invoice.payment_action_required` produce no operator notification and no customer email. Copy at `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3259` says 'Plus taxes where they apply' and `docs/tos.md:70` says 'Taxes are your responsibility unless we are required to collect' — but nothing in the checkout call enables Stripe Tax, and no document in either repo examines whether Muntin Digital LLC (Delaware entity per `docs/tos.md:135`, operated from Maryland) has a collection obligation on SaaS subscriptions. The irony is sharp: the product ships `/insights/use-tax` to compute the CUSTOMER's use-tax exposure (`apps/web/app/(product)/insights/use-tax/page.tsx`) while the company's own position is undocumented.
impact: Maryland is one of the states that taxes digital products and SaaS, and the founder lives and works there. Getting this wrong on the first hundred invoices creates a back-tax and penalty exposure that compounds silently — the classic pre-revenue company killer that surfaces at diligence or at an audit two years later. Separately, with no dunning, a failed card on a $19 subscription becomes a silent churn the founder never sees.
rec: Enable Stripe Tax (`form.set('automatic_tax[enabled]', 'true')` plus a customer address collection setting) in the same commit that adds the founding SKU — it is roughly a two-line change and Stripe handles MD registration thresholds and remittance filing. Spend one hour with a CPA on the MD/DE SaaS nexus question and write the answer into an ADR. Add `invoice.payment_failed` to the webhook switch and route it to an operator email; Stripe's own Smart Retries plus the Customer Portal cover the rest of dunning, refunds, proration, and cancellation without you building any of it.
note: Reproduced. `grep -rn 'trial_period_days|automatic_tax|promotion_code|invoice.payment_failed'` across the whole repo returns exactly one hit: the comment at pricing-constants.ts:58. billing.ts:340-363 handles customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted and checkout.session.completed and falls through to a `billing.webhook.ignored_type` log for everything else, so invoice.payment_failed is observed and dropped. copy.ts and docs/tos.md:70 both assert a tax posture nothing implements. The MD/DE SaaS-nexus question is correctly parked as an unknown rather than answered — that restraint is right. Medium is the correct severity: none of this can bite before a first charge exists.

title: The authoritative planning documents still describe a superseded launch and contradict themselves on billing readiness
effort: 30 minutes
evidence: ADR-020 (`potentially-profitable/docs/editorial/decisions/ADR-020-ledger-launch-deferred-data-company-first.md`, dated 2026-07-30) moved paid launch from 2026-11-13 to 2027 with no date set. But the resume-here board `potentially-profitable/docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md:87-89` — the file CLAUDE.md names as the first thing to read in a fresh context — still says of the unbillable $19 rate: 'Paid GA 2026-11-13 with "billing live on launch day" locked.' `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md` carries the same superseded line ('paid GA is 2026-11-13 with "billing live on launch day" locked (ADR-013)'), as does `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:62-63`. Separately, `STATUS-v6.md:9` opens with 'NOT launch-ready' and lists 'Stripe Checkout end-to-end (30)' under **DONE & solid** at `:26`, while `:36` in the same document lists 'web has no /cockpit, no /settings/billing (28)' under **PARTIAL / STUBBED**. Both statements are in the same section, 10 lines apart.
impact: The board is the artifact a fresh session or a future collaborator reads to decide what is urgent. It currently encodes a deadline that no longer exists, which either manufactures false urgency on billing or — more likely, since the date has visibly passed out of the plan — teaches the reader to discount the board. 'Stripe Checkout end-to-end: DONE' is the specific line that would let a future session conclude the payment path works.
rec: Three edits, fifteen minutes: update board item 3 and `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md` to say '2027, date unset (ADR-020)'; update the `reason` string in `pricing-constants.ts:69-70` the same way; and move 'Stripe Checkout end-to-end (30)' from DONE to PARTIAL in `STATUS-v6.md:26` with the note 'API route + webhook complete and tested; no web caller, no /settings/billing, no keys configured.' Consider extending `check-launch-date-claims.mjs` — which already binds copy to `LAUNCH_DATE_ISO` — to also scan the handoff docs and CLAUDE.md for hard-coded launch dates.
note: Reproduced line for line. docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md:87-89 still reads 'Paid GA 2026-11-13 with "billing live on launch day" locked' — the file CLAUDE.md names as the resume-here board — while ADR-020 (2026-07-30) supersedes exactly that date. Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md carries the same superseded line, as does pricing-constants.ts:62-63 and its `reason` string at :69-70. STATUS-v6.md:9 opens 'NOT launch-ready', :26 lists 'Stripe Checkout end-to-end (30)' under DONE & solid, and :36 lists 'web has no /cockpit, no /settings/billing (28)' under PARTIAL — ten lines apart, both true, and only together. 30 minutes is the right estimate. This is the cheapest fix in the report.

title: The lifetime $19 price lock is granted BY DEFAULT — an unauthenticated curl with an email address enrols a founding member, at both layers
evidence: The founding flag fails OPEN twice. In the storefront Worker, potentially-profitable/src/worker.js:8947: `const foundingMember = String(body.founding_member).toLowerCase() !== 'false';` — an absent field stringifies to "undefined", which is not "false", so it forwards founding_member=true. In the product API, Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts:97-103: `const fmRaw = String(form.get("founding_member") ?? "").toLowerCase(); const founding_member = !(fmRaw === "false" || fmRaw === "off" || fmRaw === "0" || fmRaw === "no");` — an absent field yields "", which matches none of them, so it stores true. The route is mounted public and unauthenticated at apps/api/src/index.ts:326 with only `rateLimit({ ip_per_minute: 5 })` (waitlist.ts:41) and no proxy-key requirement — the `x-muntin-proxy-key` header the storefront sends at src/worker.js:8968 is never checked by the route. Both defaults are deliberate and commented ('Default ON: a bare hero capture (no checkbox) is a founding member'), which is exactly why nobody has questioned them. Only three call sites in either repo ever opt OUT: apps/web/app/(marketing)/try/TryItClient.tsx:476, :518, :558.
impact: Finding 3 established that a perpetual, non-transferable-in-nature price commitment has no written terms. This is the mechanism that makes that dangerous: the commitment is granted by default, to an unbounded cohort, through a public endpoint that requires nothing but a syntactically valid email address, at 5/minute/IP. It cannot be revoked selectively later because no term defines what enrolment requires. Every day between now and a 2027 launch grows an obligation the company has no document for and no way to bound. And because the same default runs on both sides of the proxy, the storefront's four hidden `founding_member=true` inputs are decorative — removing them would change nothing.
rec: Two lines and a document. (1) Invert both defaults to opt-OUT-by-absence: an enrolment should require an explicit `founding_member=true`, which the four storefront forms already send (index.html:829, es/index.html:836, ledger/index.html:674, es/ledger/index.html:616), so nothing user-facing changes. (2) Require the `x-muntin-proxy-key` header (or an Origin allowlist) on /v1/waitlist so the public endpoint is not a self-serve enrolment API. (3) Publish /legal/founding-member-terms BEFORE either change, and state in it the enrolment condition you just made explicit — the term and the code should be written in the same sitting so they cannot disagree.

title: The waitlist proxy overwrites the capture surface with a retired-services enum, so every founding lead on record is attributed to 'studio'
evidence: potentially-profitable/src/worker.js:8921 declares `const WAITLIST_SOURCES = new Set(['studio', 'studio-hero', 'studio-product', 'studio-banner']);` and :8944 applies it: `const source = WAITLIST_SOURCES.has(body.source) ? body.source : 'studio';`. The four live forms send values that are NOT in that set — `home-founding` (index.html:828, es/index.html:835) and `ledger-pricing` (ledger/index.html:673, es/ledger/index.html:615) — so all four collapse to the literal string 'studio' before the forward. The product API then accepts it, because 'studio' IS in ALLOWED_SOURCES (apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts:56-59), whose own comment says those values exist 'so the founding cohort + the WS5 funnel can tell studio acquisition apart from the product site.' The enum is a fossil of the retired web-studio services line (CLAUDE.md: 'the website-build/services line is retired'). The clamp is silent — no log, no warning, and check-gate-coverage has nothing to say about a Worker constant.
impact: The auditor's own headline recommendation — 'add one KPI: waitlist signups per week, split by source' — is unimplementable against the data that already exists, and they did not notice. Every lead the storefront has ever forwarded is stamped 'studio'. The founder cannot distinguish a homepage capture from a /ledger/ pricing-page capture, cannot tell EN from ES by source, and cannot tell any of them from a lead that came through the retired services funnel. Since the funnel's whole thesis is that the Cost Index and content earn the product, the one measurement that would test the thesis is destroyed in transit, in production, today.
