rec: Replace WAITLIST_SOURCES in src/worker.js with the four values the forms actually send plus any future ones, and add the same values to ALLOWED_SOURCES in apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts — the two lists must be edited together or the API clamps to 'unknown' instead, which is a different silent loss. Then make the clamp loud: log a `waitlist.source_clamped` event with the rejected value so the next drift shows up in the logs rather than in an audit. Add a storefront check script that walks every `action="/api/waitlist"` form and asserts its hidden `source` value is a member of WAITLIST_SOURCES — this is precisely the 'declare your roots' gate class the storefront CLAUDE.md already teaches.

title: The funnel has no mouth: 0 of 628 content pages carry a founding-list capture — the entire top of funnel feeds a newsletter in KV with no bridge to the cohort
evidence: I counted `action="/api/waitlist"` across the storefront: 4 files site-wide — index.html, es/index.html, ledger/index.html, es/ledger/index.html. Two of them are Spanish, so EN has exactly two founding-capture surfaces. By section the count is zero everywhere the content actually lives: cost-index 0/142 pages, library 0/221, glossary 0/172, sheets 0/40, tools 0/8, blog 0/20, learn 0/25. Meanwhile 777 pages carry `action="/api/subscribe"`, whose handler (src/worker.js:8821+) writes the subscriber into the AUTH_SESSIONS KV namespace (`env.AUTH_SESSIONS.put(subKey, ...)` at the handler's line ~70) — a different store, in a different account, with no founding flag, no source, and no code path anywhere in either repo that reads it into the waitlist. Even ledger/demo/index.html — the highest-intent storefront surface, which posts the $19 rate at :1733 — carries zero capture forms; its only CTA is a cross-page link.
impact: This is the structural answer to the auditor's 'zero pipeline' finding, and it is more actionable than 'the KPIs measure the wrong thing.' The company has spent two years building 1,368 pages of cost intelligence and then asks for the product lead on two of them. An operator who reads a Cost Index ingredient page, runs a free tool, and downloads a sheet is offered a newsletter subscription that lands in a KV bucket the founding cohort cannot see. The 405 pages that do route to the product (see next finding) hand the visitor off cross-domain, which is the highest-friction possible conversion. For a founder whose scarcest resource is evenings, adding a capture block to the templates that already build these pages is the highest-leverage hour in this domain.
rec: One injector, run once. The storefront already has ~70 build/inject scripts and a sentinel convention — the founding form is already delimited by `<!-- founding-capture:start (ledger) -->` / `<!-- founding-capture:end -->` at ledger/index.html:661-683, which is exactly the shape an injector consumes. Write `inject-founding-capture.mjs`, give it a declared root list per the CLAUDE.md rule, and land the block on the cost-index ingredient pages, the tool result surfaces, and the sheet pages first — the three places where the visitor has just received value. Give each root its own `source` value (and add them to both allowlists per the previous finding) so the first week of data answers which surface converts. Separately, decide what the 777 newsletter captures are for: either bridge them to the waitlist with an explicit opt-in, or stop treating them as pipeline.

title: Host split-brain: 405 storefront pages send every conversion CTA to ledger.muntin.digital, and the only route the web app deploys to is app.muntin.digital
evidence: `grep -rc ledger.muntin.digital --include=*.html` in potentially-profitable matches 405 files; `grep -rl app.muntin.digital --include=*.html` matches 0. Every 'See Muntin Ledger' button (library/restaurant-prime-cost/index.html:1057, library/loyalty-program-roi/index.html:804, all ten menu-design-cuisines pages, ledger/index.html:660) points at https://ledger.muntin.digital/. But Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:26-31 declares exactly one route: `{ "pattern": "app.muntin.digital/*", "zone_name": "muntin.digital" }`, and its own vars set `APP_ORIGIN: "https://app.muntin.digital"` (:52). Worse, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is never set anywhere in the repo — not in wrangler.jsonc vars, not in .github/workflows, and scripts/guard-web-deploy-env.mjs (91 lines) does not mention it — so all five consumers fall back to their hardcoded default: apps/web/lib/canonical.ts:28, app/robots.ts:16, app/sitemap.ts:27, lib/seo-schema.ts:19, app/.well-known/security.txt/route.ts:14 all emit `https://ledger.muntin.digital`. The storefront's own fact gate cites the host too — data/sourced-claims.json:569 gives `source_url: "https://ledger.muntin.digital/"` for the $19 claim. A third name appears in Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md ('the operator app at app.muntin.digital'). I cannot see Cloudflare's dashboard from this container, so a redirect rule or a second route may exist out-of-band — but nothing in either repo evidences one, and the deploy config actively contradicts it.
impact: If ledger.muntin.digital does not resolve, the funnel's only exit is broken on 405 pages and the audit's other findings are moot — nobody reaches the product at all. If it does resolve via an out-of-repo redirect, the defect is quieter but still real: a Worker serving from app.muntin.digital emits canonical tags, a sitemap, a robots.txt and a security.txt all declaring a different host, which is a self-inflicted SEO split for a company whose entire acquisition strategy is organic search, and it means the security.txt the founder-todos runbook (F18) tells you to curl at ledger.muntin.digital is served by a host that does not claim it. Either way, three names for two surfaces across two repos is a seam nobody owns.
rec: Settle the naming in one commit, in this order: (1) `curl -I https://ledger.muntin.digital/` from the founder's Mac — five seconds, and it decides which branch you are on. (2) Whichever host wins, set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL explicitly in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc vars and add it to the required list in scripts/guard-web-deploy-env.mjs, so the default in canonical.ts can never silently ship again. (3) If app.muntin.digital is the answer, add a redirect route for ledger.* rather than rewriting 405 storefront files — slugs are final-forever in this company and so, effectively, are outbound links in published articles. (4) Update data/sourced-claims.json:569 to match, since the fact gate currently cites the loser.

title: The Team tier's posted differentiator — 'phone support (Tuesday SMS group + a real number)' — is copy lifted from the retired web-studio line and has no mechanism
evidence: apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3259 sells Team as '$60/month. Up to 400 invoices/month. Includes phone support (Tuesday SMS group + a real number).' The phrase traces to runbooks/proposals/landing-refresh/lens-10-competitive-positioning.md:287, a retired-services positioning doc: 'The Workshop tier ($59) includes Tuesday SMS group + a real phone number.' There is no phone number anywhere in the product — the only phone-shaped string in copy.ts is the placeholder `callbackPhonePlaceholder: "+1 555 123 4567"` at :3202 — no SMS provider in apps/api, and no support-hours document in runbooks/. The support row in settings is a `mailto:hello@muntin.digital` link (settings/page.tsx, groupHelp). The founder works full time at Tacombi; a weekly SMS group is a staffing commitment nothing in either repo plans for.
impact: This is a paid-tier feature promise with no implementation, no staffing model, and provenance in a business line the company retired — the exact class of defect the storefront built check-positioning-drift.mjs to catch, and apps/web has no equivalent gate. It is currently latent because page.tsx:495 hides the tier strip pre-launch. At GA it becomes the difference between two tiers a customer pays $35/month extra for, which makes it a specific, arguable misrepresentation rather than a vague one — and it is the sort of thing a $60 customer tests in week one.
rec: Delete the phone-support clause from copy.ts:3259 and its ES twin, or replace it with what you will actually do ('email, answered by the founder'). Then port the storefront's positioning-drift idea across: a check script over apps/web/lib/copy.ts that fails on retired-services vocabulary and on any support/SLA promise not backed by a named mechanism. The storefront learned this lesson three times on 2026-07-28 and wrote it into CLAUDE.md; the product repo has not learned it once.

title: The /never/ page promises "it never learns from your corrections" — the product's entire learning surface does exactly that
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `never/index.html:436` (guarantee two, "I will never resell your data"): "The model that reads an invoice is fixed; it never learns from your corrections, so the same invoice gives the same numbers and your data trains nothing." The product's own documentation opens with the opposite: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/community-templates.md:3-7` — "Muntin Ledger learns the layout of each vendor's invoice over time. When you correct a field, we promote a rule for that vendor so the next invoice from them lands closer to right." The mechanism is shipped and reachable: `services/extract/engine_pkg/harvest.py` applies ACTIVE template rules as the first harvest path; `apps/api/src/routes/learning.ts:9` is literally "the 'ask me what I learned' surface", reading `template.rule_promoted` events; there is a customer-visible page at `apps/web/app/(product)/insights/learning/page.tsx` and a per-vendor page at `insights/learning/[vendor]`. There is also an opt-in CROSS-TENANT pool — `apps/api/src/routes/community-templates.ts:19` "the opt-in cross-tenant template pool" — that sends redacted rule fingerprints derived from your corrections to other customers' orgs.
impact: This is on the one page whose entire premise is "guarantees you can check instead of trust," under the heading about not reselling data. A journalist, a competitor, or a security-minded operator who reads `/never/` and then the product's own `docs/community-templates.md` finds the company contradicting itself on a privacy claim in under five minutes. That is worse than never having made the claim: it converts the site's strongest asset — verifiable honesty — into evidence of the opposite. The underlying behavior is defensible and even a selling point (per-org rules, opt-in pooling, no ML training); only the sentence is wrong.
rec: Rewrite `never/index.html:436` (and its ES mirror) today to say what is actually true: no language model reads your invoices; nothing you upload trains a model; per-vendor layout RULES are learned inside your own organisation from your corrections, and sharing a redacted slice of them with other shops is opt-in and off by default. Keep "the same invoice gives the same numbers" — that one is backed by the determinism gate. Then add the claim to the registry in `docs/marketing-claims.md` so it is governed rather than free-floating.
note: Reproduced. never/index.html:436 says "it never learns from your corrections"; the loop is real and durable: apps/api/src/routes/templates.ts:596 forwards operator corrections to the extract service's /v1/learn, services/extract/main.py:878 and :1021 call template_store.record_observation, and main.py:94 selects make_template_store(database_url=os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL")) — PostgresTemplateStore's own docstring (template_store.py:1079-1081) says it "closes the silent-data-loss bug where the production process was constructing InMemoryTemplateStore(), so every learned template evaporated on Fly machine restart." harvest.py:211 _apply_template_rules is the first harvest path. So corrections persist and steer future reads. Severity corrected from critical to high: this is a copy defect on a pre-revenue site with no customers, and the surrounding sentence ("no language model", "your data trains nothing") is accurate — the fix is one clause, not a product change.

title: /security/integrity.txt publishes 6 SHA-256 digests and all 6 are wrong — the page tells readers to verify, and verification fails
effort: 3 hours
evidence: `security/integrity.txt` says "Recomputed on every deploy. If you can hash the same file on disk and the digests match below, you're running the same code we shipped" and is stamped `# Generated: 2026-05-02T16:08:42Z` — 96 days ago. I recomputed all six against the working tree: `/assets/site.css`, `/assets/site.js`, `/assets/workbench-save.js`, `/_includes/nav.html`, `/_includes/footer.html`, `/src/worker.js` — 6 MISMATCH, 0 MATCH (e.g. site.js published `2dbb027b…` vs actual `361384ad…`). The `/security/` page points readers straight at it: "Hash the file yourself, or compare against the SHA-256 digests published at /security/integrity.txt (regenerated on each deploy; the file lists exactly which paths were hashed)." There is no generator script and no gate — `ls scripts/ | grep -i integrity` returns only `expected-integrity.json`, and `integrity` appears nowhere in `scripts/check-all.mjs`, `wrangler.jsonc`, or `.github/workflows/`.
impact: A security-conscious reader — exactly the audience this page is written for — runs the published `curl … | shasum -a 256` and gets six mismatches. The honest reading of that result is "the site is serving code that does not match its published hashes," i.e. a tampering signal. On the page whose entire argument is "you don't have to take any of it on faith," a self-inflicted integrity failure is the single most damaging thing that can be there. It also silently voids the one supply-chain control the storefront claims.
rec: Either (a) write `scripts/build-integrity.mjs`, wire it into the Cloudflare `build.command` alongside `check-all.mjs`, and add a check that fails CI when any published digest does not match the file on disk — the same pattern the repo already uses for count sentinels; or (b) if per-deploy regeneration is not going to happen reliably, delete `integrity.txt` and the paragraph on `/security/` that points at it. A removed claim costs nothing; a false verification instruction costs the whole page.
note: Reproduced 6/6 mismatch by hand (e.g. assets/site.js published 2dbb027b… vs actual 361384ad…; _includes/footer.html published bb22b901… vs actual 8b6c59e4…). No generator exists; 'integrity' appears nowhere in scripts/check-all.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, or .github/workflows/. Two corrections that make it worse, not better: (1) the reach is larger than reported — the file is linked from index.html:647 AND es/index.html:655, receipts/index.html:482, es/receipts/index.html:425, learn/topics/information-security/index.html:426, its ES twin, and library/how-to-tell-if-a-restaurant-tool-is-safe/index.html:769, whose EN+ES audio narration speaks the instruction aloud; (2) the article and topic pages both say it carries "SHA-256 hashes of every shipped JS file" — it hashes 3 of the 5 files in assets/*.js and none of assets/vendor/*. Also note the header stamp reads 2026-05-02 but git log says the file was last committed 2026-07-05: it was touched without regeneration. Severity corrected to high on the same pre-revenue reasoning.

title: "Flags price hikes against your own six-month history" — the engine uses a 90-day window, in body copy and in four JSON-LD blocks
effort: 3 hours (copy) or 1 day (engine + goldens)
evidence: Claimed: `ledger/index.html:622` "A vendor raises a price and Ledger marks it against your own six-month history", plus `ledger/index.html:8` (meta description) and `:42` and `:58` (two JSON-LD `description` fields), and the Spanish mirror `es/ledger/index.html:564`, `:39`, `:55` ("tu propio historial de seis meses"). Actual: the price-anomaly producer defaults to a 90-day trailing median — `services/extract/price_anomaly.py:159` `window_days: int = 90` and `apps/api/src/lib/verdict-compute.ts:241` `const windowDays = opts.windowDays ?? 90`. I grepped every `windowDays` reference in `apps/api/src`: no caller passes 180 or any six-month value. The generated verdict text itself says `trailing-${windowDays}d median` (`verdict-compute.ts:286`), so the product will literally print "trailing-90d" to a customer who was sold six months.
impact: A prospect who signs up and reads their first price-hike verdict sees "trailing-90d median" against a homepage that promised six months. It is a small number but it is the specific mechanism the product is sold on, it is duplicated into structured data that Google and AI answer engines quote verbatim, and it is bilingual — so the correction is a six-file fix, not a one-line one. Discovering that the flagship mechanism was described at 2x its real window is the kind of thing that makes an operator stop trusting the rest of the page.
rec: Pick one and make the other match. Either change `windowDays ?? 90` → `?? 180` in `verdict-compute.ts:241` and `price_anomaly.py:159` (and re-baseline the golden tests), or change all seven strings to "your own 90-day history" / "tu propio historial de 90 días". Then register the window as a claim in `docs/marketing-claims.md` keyed to the constant, so the copy cannot drift from the parameter again.
note: The copy half is confirmed (ledger/index.html:8,42,58,622 and es/ledger/index.html:39,55,564). The mechanism half is wrong and the recommendation would fix nothing. The shipped price-hike verdict is computePriceHike, not computeRollingAnomaly: verdicts-store.ts:1490 calls computePriceHike(g.obs) and inserts the verdict at :1505; computeRollingAnomaly is invoked at :1494 only when this.shadowLog is true (env.LENS11_SHADOW_LOG === "on", verdicts-store.ts:1952), and only its null-ness is captured into shadowFire — its "trailing-90d median" reason string (verdict-compute.ts:286) is never read, never persisted, never rendered. Worse, computePriceHike (verdict-compute.ts:58-89) takes NO window at all, and the feeding SQL (verdicts-store.ts:1368-1423) bounds observations by key/canonical/currency/provisional with no date predicate — so the shipped baseline is the median of every observation ever recorded for that item. The real gap is not '180 claimed vs 90 shipped' but 'a bounded window claimed vs an unbounded lifetime median shipped', which also means a two-year-old price still anchors 'typical'. Changing windowDays ?? 90 → 180 in verdict-compute.ts:241 would change nothing a customer sees.

title: Two claims the company catalogued as live exposures on 2026-06-15 are still shipped verbatim 52 days later, and both are false for the default user
effort: 4 hours
evidence: `docs/marketing-claims.md` §🔴 lists exposure 2 (`residencyBodyTemplate` "Files auto-delete after {retention}") and exposure 3 (demo `privacyHeading` "We cannot read your invoices" + "locked with a key only you hold") as needing rewording. Files auto-delete after {retention}." and `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3747-3749` "We cannot read your invoices" / "Your files are locked with a key only you hold." `copy.ts` was last committed 2026-07-31 — the file has been edited since the exposure was catalogued; the exposures just were not fixed. Both are false by default: the retention reaper is off unless an operator sets an env flag (`apps/api/src/index.ts:668-670` — `RETENTION_REAPER_ENABLED === "true"` and `RETENTION_REAPER_DRYRUN`, neither present in `apps/api/wrangler.toml [vars]`), and E2EE requires enrollment (`apps/api/src/lib/finish-encrypt.ts` returns `skip_no_identity_key` and falls through to the legacy path when the owner has no identity key — "E2EE is opt-in" in its own docstring). "Files auto-delete after N" is a data-protection representation; making it while the deleter is switched off is the kind of statement that becomes a problem in a DPA review, a security questionnaire, or a regulator's reading. rec: Fix the two strings this week: scope the demo privacy step to "we don't use a language model to read them" plus "you can lock your originals with a key only you hold — here's how," and change `residencyBodyTemplate` to match `promises-data.ts`'s already-correct "delete on request; automatic deletion is being switched on." note: Split verdict. Retention half CONFIRMED and stronger than reported: copy.ts:1968-1969 residencyBodyTemplate is rendered — PostureSheetIsland.tsx:60 passes it and the island is mounted site-wide at apps/web/app/(product)/layout.tsx:178, with use-posture.ts STATIC_FALLBACK retentionSeconds 86400 — so every signed-in operator can open a sheet that says 'Files auto-delete after 24 hours' while index.ts:668-670 keeps the reaper off. Demo half REFUTED: copy.ts:3747-3749 sits inside the landing.tour block (opens at 3474), and demo/page.tsx:99 renders only <DemoTour copy={t.reveal}>; DemoTour.tsx never reads privacyHeading/privacyBody, and the only renderer of those key names (BookkeeperBody.tsx:70-73) binds to landing.bookkeeper (copy.ts:4096), whose heading is the honest 'What we read and what we never read'. 'The demo is the first thing a prospect touches, and it tells them the company cannot read their invoices' is not reproducible — that string is dead. The registry entry citing it is stale, which is a registry finding, not a shipped-copy finding.

title: The $150/mo accountant tier is marked billable and sells a multi-client cockpit that has no web page

evidence: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:48-49` declares `accountant: {cents: 15000, basis: "per_account", billable: true}` and `accountantSeat: {cents: 3000, basis: "per_seat", billable: true}`. `apps/api/src/lib/stripe-tiers.ts:83-99` defines the tier with `hasCockpit: true`, documented as "the accountant cockpit (the multi-client switcher + the workspace-switcher header). The web half does not: I enumerated every `page.tsx` under `apps/web/app` — there is no `/cockpit` route and no workspace-switcher component; the only occurrence of the word "cockpit" anywhere in `apps/web` is the error-code string `tier_no_cockpit` at `apps/web/app/(product)/settings/members/members-client.tsx:35`. title: The market-price check covers 24 of 100 Cost-Index ingredients, zero seafood, and its snapshot is 9–19 days into a 30-day fail-closed window with a manual-only refresh
