note: Verified by parsing both files: apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json carries _asOfRange 2026-07-18..2026-07-28 and exactly 24 ingredients, no seafood; oldest points (butter, cheddar-cheese) are 2026-07-18 = 19 days, against STALE_AFTER_DAYS = 30 at cost-index-valuation.ts:73 (checked :111, :169) → cliff 2026-08-17. Upstream, data/cost-index.json has exactly 18 of 100 ingredients past 30 days: 17 at 2026-06-01 (66 days, all seafood plus vegetable-oil and pork-belly) and ground-beef at 2026-06-10 (57 days). One fairness correction the auditor should have made: the storefront itself does NOT misrepresent this — cost-index/salmon-fillet/index.html titles itself 'Salmon fillet wholesale price — coverage in progress' and prints no price. The single overreach is ledger/index.html:625's 'prices wholesale proteins, produce, and dairy'.

title: The two-person production-deploy approval workflow deploys nothing — every step is an echo TODO
effort: 1 hour
evidence: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` documents itself as the gate for production deploys ("a gated `environment: production` job", reviewer pool, prevent-self-review ON, "this is what makes it two-person"). Its actual steps: line 76 `echo "TODO(B-priv-6): wire wrangler deploy after cosign signing pipeline lands"`, line 84 same for flyctl docling, line 90 same for flyctl extract, line 96 same for vercel web, line 103 `echo "TODO: POST /v1/audit/deploys after the route lands"`. Real deploys go through `scripts/deploy-api.sh` and `pnpm --filter @muntin/web deploy:cf` from a laptop, per `CLAUDE.md` — outside the approval gate entirely.
impact: Lower business severity than the copy findings because a one-person company cannot do two-person review anyway — but it matters for what gets said out loud. If "two-person production-deploy approval" ever appears in a security questionnaire, a DPA, an enterprise sales conversation, or the transparency doc, it is not a control that exists; it is a YAML file that prints TODO. It also means no deploy is recorded in the audit chain, which weakens the "every change is logged" story at exactly the change that matters most.
rec: Rename the workflow to what it is (`deploy-plan.yml`, or a comment header saying NOT WIRED — real deploys are manual) so nobody cites it as a control, and grep both repos plus `docs/security/posture-scorecard.md` and `docs/transparency*.md` for any claim of two-person deploy approval. Wiring it for real is not the right move for a solo founder; being accurate about it is free.
note: Reproduced: .github/workflows/deploy.yml:76,84,90,96,103 are all echo TODOs (and :96 still names Vercel, though the repo deploys apps/web via OpenNext to Cloudflare). Severity RAISED from medium, because the auditor's hedge — 'if two-person production-deploy approval ever appears in a security questionnaire, a DPA...' — was left unchecked and the answer is yes, already, in published documents. See the missed finding; the recommendation to 'grep both repos for any claim of two-person deploy approval' was the right instinct abandoned one command short.

title: Post-deferral leftovers still anchor work to the retired 2026-11-13 date
effort: 45 minutes
evidence: ADR-020 (`potentially-profitable/docs/editorial/decisions/ADR-020-…md`, 2026-07-30) moved paid launch to 2027 and explicitly supersedes ADR-013's date. Still pointing at the old date: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:62-71` — "paid GA is 2026-11-13 and 'billing live on launch day' is a locked decision, so this must be resolved before then"; `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3155` comment — "human string per lib/launch.ts (LAUNCH_DATE_ISO = 2026-11-13)" while `launch.ts:52` is `null`; `potentially-profitable/scripts/build-site-counts.mjs:134` still computes `ga_weeks_out` from `Date.UTC(2026, 10, 13)` into `data/site-counts.json` (currently 15, from a 2026-07-28 build). ADR-020 itself lives only in the storefront repo, while the gate that cites it (`Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/scripts/check-launch-date-claims.mjs:296,306`) is in the product repo with no local copy.
impact: No customer sees any of this — `ga_weeks_out` is computed but never injected into any HTML (grep finds no `count:ledger` sentinel). The cost is to the founder: the billing gap's stated deadline is now a date that does not exist, which removes the urgency signal without replacing it, and a future reader of `pricing-constants.ts` will believe there is a November deadline. The cross-repo ADR is a smaller version of the same problem — the product repo's gate cites a decision record it cannot show you.
rec: Update the `founding` reason string in `pricing-constants.ts` to cite ADR-020 and a 2027 window; fix or delete the stale `LAUNCH_DATE_ISO` comment in `copy.ts:3155`; delete `ga_weeks_out` from `build-site-counts.mjs` since nothing renders it. Add a one-line ADR-020 stub in `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/ux/decisions/` pointing at the storefront file, so the gate's citation resolves in the repo where the gate lives.
note: All four anchors reproduced: pricing-constants.ts:62-71 still cites 'paid GA is 2026-11-13'; launch.ts documents LAUNCH_DATE_ISO null under ADR-020 at lines 35-45; scripts/build-site-counts.mjs:134 computes ga_weeks_out from Date.UTC(2026, 10, 13); data/site-counts.json:17 holds 15. Confirmed that no HTML carries a count:ga_weeks_out sentinel, so nothing renders it. ADR-020 exists at docs/editorial/decisions/ADR-020-ledger-launch-deferred-data-company-first.md and explicitly supersedes only ADR-013's date, not its pricing — so the $19 per-location basis in pricing-constants.ts is correct; only the deadline sentence is stale. Low is right.

title: Stripe checkout multiplies the BASE tier price by seat count — a 5-seat Team is billed $300 against a posted $60, a 5-seat Accountant $750 against a posted $270 — and both tiers are declared billable:true
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:175 sets `line_items[0][quantity]` to `seats` against the single price returned by `priceIdForTier` (billing.ts:57-61), which for accountant returns `STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_BASE` — the $150 base. There is no second line item. `STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT` is declared at apps/api/src/env.ts:612 and read only by a webhook tier-resolver (stripe-tiers.ts:152) and one test; billing.ts never references it. The tier shapes disagree with the checkout: stripe-tiers.ts:83-99 accountant = basePriceCents 15000 + seatPriceCents 3000, maxSeats 50; team (:73-81) = basePriceCents 6000 + seatPriceCents 0, maxSeats 5. So a Team org that invites 4 staff is charged 5 × $6000 = $300/mo for a tier whose own seat price is zero, and a 10-seat firm is charged $1,500/mo against a posted $150 + 9×$30 = $420. apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:46-49 declares solo/team/accountant/accountantSeat all `billable: true`, and scripts/check-pricing-consistency.mjs only parses basePriceCents and matches dollar literals in copy — it never reads billing.ts and has no assertion about quantity or seat math (grep for 'quantity' in that file returns nothing).
impact: This is the exact failure class the 2026-07-30 audit named — a gate measuring the presence of a shape (a declared SKU) rather than whether the seam is grounded. `billable: true` is defined in pricing-constants.ts:35-38 as 'a customer can actually be charged this today', and for Team and Accountant that is false in the worst direction: they can be charged, incorrectly, at up to 5x and 3.5x the posted price. The founding-rate gap the gate does print is latent and self-inflicted; this one produces a wrong Stripe subscription the moment any multi-seat org checks out, on the two tiers with seats. The auditor looked at the accountant tier and stopped at the missing cockpit UI.
rec: Today, in pricing-constants.ts, flip `team` and `accountant`/`accountantSeat` to billable:false with a dated reason naming billing.ts:175, so the standing green-run line prints all four gaps instead of one. Then fix the checkout: emit two line items for accountant (base qty 1 + STRIPE_PRICE_ACCOUNTANT_SEAT qty seats-1) and pin Team quantity to 1 while seatPriceCents is 0. Add an assertion to check-pricing-consistency.mjs that every tier with seatPriceCents !== basePriceCents has a second line item in billing.ts — the gate's own charter is 'stripe-tiers.ts is what Stripe actually bills', and right now it isn't.

title: The public /verify/no-llm-ci page describes the flagship gate as scanning dependencies — it cannot see any dependency manifest, and its import matcher is line-anchored
evidence: apps/web/lib/verify-registry.ts:60 describes scripts/no-llm-ci.sh as: "Scans new dependencies for LLM, transformer, or AI packages on every pull request." That string is rendered as body copy at apps/web/app/(marketing)/verify/[slug]/page.tsx:261 AND as the page's `<meta name=description>` at :92/:184 — so it is the sentence search engines and answer engines quote. The gate does not do that. no-llm-ci.sh builds its file list from `git ls-files -z -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.py' '*.toml' '*.ipynb' '*.yaml' '*.yml'` and then explicitly filters `pnpm-lock.yaml` out; `*.json` is not in the glob at all, so all 15 tracked package.json files are invisible to it. Its three matchers are line-anchored `^[[:space:]]*import|from` statements, bare LLM hostnames, and six env-var names — `require("openai")`, `await import(x)`, `importlib.import_module(name)`, and any host built from a variable all pass. Its vendor list (anthropic|openai|instructor|cohere|together|vertexai|google.generativeai) omits Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Ollama, and HuggingFace inference. I ran it: `no-LLM gate: OK.`
impact: The auditor called this "the rare case where the marketing claim, the gate, and the code all agree" and listed it as the report's first strength — after reading the script. The claim and the gate do not agree: the published description promises dependency scanning that the script structurally cannot perform. This is the load-bearing differentiator of the entire company (never/index.html:436, ledger/index.html:612 and :633, the /promises page), and the one gate a hostile reader will actually open, because the site hands them the path. The invariant itself holds today — no LLM dependency is present — so this is a description defect plus a coverage hole, not a live breach; but a page whose whole argument is 'don't trust, verify' cannot afford a description that fails on inspection.
rec: Two lines of work. Rewrite the verify-registry.ts:60 description to what the script does: 'scans every tracked source file for LLM SDK imports, LLM vendor hostnames, and LLM API-key env vars, and fails the build on a hit.' Then actually add manifests: drop `pnpm-lock.yaml` from the exclusion, add `package.json` to the glob, and match on dependency-name keys — a lockfile is the cheapest place to catch the thing the promise is about. Widen the vendor list to the current market (bedrock-runtime, azure openai, mistral, groq, ollama, huggingface inference) while there, and add a `require(`/dynamic-import matcher.

title: "Two-person approval" for production access is a published legal representation of a one-person company — in the privacy policy and ROPA that render on the public web, and in the DPA
evidence: docs/privacy-policy.md:538-540: "Production access requires a named-customer ticket, two-person approval, and time-boxed credentials." docs/ropa.md:48 lists "two-person production-access controls" among the Art. 30 security measures. docs/dpa.md:207-209 repeats it as a contractual measure. docs/threat-model.md:132 relies on it. Both the privacy policy and the ROPA are shipped to the public web: apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/privacy/page.tsx:7,14 and legal/ropa/page.tsx:8 render docs/privacy-policy.md and docs/ropa.md through apps/web/lib/legal-content.generated.ts. The company is one employed person (CLAUDE.md, both repos), real deploys run from that person's Mac (Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/CLAUDE.md branch-and-deploy section), and the only workflow that even models a second approver is .github/workflows/deploy.yml, every step of which is an echo TODO. Separately, docs/dpa.md:212 promises "signed container images (cosign), SBOMs per release" — SBOMs do exist (ci.yml:807-829, syft), but cosign appears nowhere in either repo except as the TODO text blocking deploy.yml:68-96 and a comment in scripts/deploy-docling-ephemeral.sh:98.
impact: The auditor found the echo-TODO workflow and then explicitly hedged: 'if two-person production-deploy approval ever appears in a security questionnaire, a DPA, an enterprise sales conversation, or the transparency doc, it is not a control that exists.' It already appears in all three of the documents that matter, two of them served at public URLs, one of them the Art. 30 record a regulator reads. Unlike every other finding in this domain, this one is not a marketing sentence — it is a data-protection representation, and it is the single claim in either repo that a solo founder can never satisfy no matter how much code ships. Cosign is the same shape, in the same contract, one section down.
rec: Rewrite all four to what a one-person company can honestly assert and actually enforce: no standing production credentials, time-boxed credentials issued per named ticket, every access written into the customer's own audit log, and — if the founder wants a second party — a hardware-key requirement or a delayed-reveal break-glass, not a second human. Change the cosign line to 'SBOMs emitted per release (CI); image signing planned' until deploy.yml:68 is untrue. Then rename deploy.yml to deploy-plan.yml so nobody re-derives the claim from the file, and add both sentences to docs/marketing-claims.md, which today governs marketing copy but not legal copy — the gap that let this sit.

title: The Cost Index methodology statement — the company's citability spine — asserts six-language narration that was retired 50 days ago
evidence: cost-index/methodology/index.html:498, inside the page that declares itself methodology version 1.3.0 effective 2026-06-18 with a machine-readable twin at /cost-index/methodology.json: "The narration of this index is read aloud verbatim in six languages, so a fabrication would be spoken aloud — which is precisely why the gate has no soft edge." No fr/it/pt/zh audio exists anywhere in the repo (find for audio.fr.mp3 / audio.zh.mp3 returns nothing), and potentially-profitable/CLAUDE.md records the cause: "Cut 2026-06-17: fr/it/pt/zh article audio (EN + ES only now)" — the day before this methodology version took effect. learn/index.html:638 carries the same claim ('Audio narration in six languages'), as does blog/may-2026-wave-publishing-for-citation/index.html:829.
impact: This is not the same as the /system/ page the auditor found. /system/ is a build-story page; /cost-index/methodology/ is the document the company points citing journalists, researchers, and AI answer engines at, versioned and change-logged precisely so it can be trusted as of-record. The sentence is also self-defeating in a specific way: it uses the six-language narration as the *justification* for the absoluteness of the fact gate ('a fabrication would be spoken aloud'), so the one false statement on the page is the one propping up the page's claim to be free of false statements. A reader who checks the cheapest claim on a methodology document and finds it false discounts everything above it.
rec: Fix cost-index/methodology/index.html:498 and learn/index.html:638 to 'English and Spanish' today, and bump the methodology to 1.3.1 with a changelog line — the page's own machinery exists for exactly this and using it turns the correction into evidence of discipline. Then close the class: the language list and the sheet/article counts should be `<!-- count:KEY -->` sentinels sourced from data/article-audio.json and data/site-counts.json, and check-positioning-drift-style scanning should cover /system/, /security/, /never/, /receipts/ and /cost-index/methodology/ — the trust pages sit outside every content gate, which is why all four of these survived.

title: GET /v1/templates — the customer-facing 'what did it learn' surface — throws in any environment where DATABASE_URL is set, which is exactly the environment where learning is durable
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/templates-store.ts:181-183: `defaultTemplatesStore` returns `new NeonTemplatesStore(env.DATABASE_URL)` when DATABASE_URL is set, else the Stub. Every NeonTemplatesStore method is unimplemented and throws: :144 `throw new Error("NeonTemplatesStore.listForOrg not yet wired (needs @neondatabase/serverless install)")`, :152 getByIdForOrg, :175 retire. The route calls it unconditionally — apps/api/src/routes/templates.ts:179-180, :198-199, :227-228 — and is mounted at apps/api/src/index.ts:380. The Stub's own docstring (templates-store.ts:64-72) says it exists so 'the Worker route can render the "no templates yet" state without any data source', and warns that 'a deploy that sets DATABASE_URL without the driver installed flips to the Neon path which throws on every call'. Meanwhile the Python side has the opposite posture: services/extract/main.py:94 selects the Postgres template store precisely when DATABASE_URL is present, and template_store.py:1079-1081 documents that as the fix for templates evaporating on restart.
impact: Two sources of truth on the same feature, wired in opposite directions by the same env var. Turning on durable learning in the engine is exactly what breaks the API surface that shows the operator what was learned — a 500, not the graceful empty state the Stub was written to give. This sits directly under the /never/ finding: the page says the product never learns, the docs say it learns, and the route built to show you what it learned cannot answer. I could not confirm DATABASE_URL's live value (Worker secret, not in wrangler.toml), so this is conditional — but the condition is the intended production configuration, and the failure is a hard throw with a message naming an uninstalled driver.
rec: Make NeonTemplatesStore degrade instead of throw, or invert the factory so an unwired Neon path falls back to the Stub with a logged warning — a 'no templates yet' page is honest, a 500 is not. Add a one-line integration assertion that defaultTemplatesStore(env).listForOrg resolves for both env shapes; the store's own docstring predicted this bug in 2026 and nothing tests the prediction. While there, decide whether /v1/templates should read the Python-side tables at all, or whether the learning surface at /v1/learning (which reads audit events and does work) is the one to keep.

title: The storefront's 'absolute' fact gate registers the unbillable $19 price as a sourced claim citing the company's own product page, then propagates it to 25+ article surfaces and the public claims.json
evidence: data/sourced-claims.json `ledger_founding_offer_2026` registers: 'three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as they stay', with `source_url: "https://ledger.muntin.digital/"` and `source_name` 'Muntin Ledger — posted pricing (first-party, founder-confirmed…)'. Its `used_in` array lists ~25 surfaces — ledger/, es/ledger/, ledger/demo/, index.html, es/index.html and twenty-odd library articles — and scripts/build-claims-json.mjs republishes the registry to the public /claims.json. The price it certifies is the one apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts declares `billable: false` with a dated reason. Structurally, the claim's source is the assertion: a first-party marketing page is accepted as the primary source, which is why no product-capability claim in this domain — 'six-month history', 'post it to QuickBooks Online', 'it never learns from your corrections' — is registered at all. Grep of sourced-claims.json for 'six-month', 'quickbooks' returns nothing product-related.
impact: CLAUDE.md calls the fact gate absolute and says every number must be registered, cited, or labeled illustrative. It is absolute about USDA report numbers and the operator bio, and blind to the product. The one product claim it does hold is circular — the site cites itself — and it is a price with no billing path, now embedded in 25 pages and a machine-readable ledger that AI answer engines are explicitly courted to read. That is how four unbacked product sentences survived 129 gates: they were never in scope. The auditor's recommendation to 'add the claim to docs/marketing-claims.md' names the wrong registry — that file lives in the product repo and governs app copy; the storefront sentences are governed by this one.
rec: Add a claim class for product capability to data/sourced-claims.json whose `source_url` must be a repo path plus a line anchor (verify-registry.ts already proves the pattern works), and register the four live ones — no-LLM path, price-hike baseline, QuickBooks posting state, per-vendor rule learning — each pointed at the file that decides it. Extend check-fabrications.mjs or a new check-product-claims.mjs to fail when a storefront page states a capability with no registered claim. And mark ledger_founding_offer_2026 with its billability state so the storefront's own ledger stops certifying a price the billing engine cannot charge.

title: 294 test files, ~72% coverage, and not one line of production SQL ever runs in CI
effort: 3 days for the documents/extractions verify script; 1 more day for the RLS + reaper role
evidence: apps/api/vitest.config.ts sets `environment: "node"` with no Workers pool and no miniflare binding — so D1, KV, R2, Queues and Neon are all fakes. I counted 40 `class Stub*`, 22 `class Neon*` and 24 `class D1*` implementations in apps/api/src/lib, and 644 SQL statements across those files. The tests hit the Stub side: 47 test files inject fakes through the `__test_*_store` env seam documented at apps/api/src/lib/extractions-store.ts:1716-1726. Real-SQL verification is only scripts/db-verify.sh, which applies migrations then runs exactly 3 files totalling 393 lines (infra/postgres/verify/{coverage-persist,reorder-rate,tier2-theoretical}-verify.sql) — all inventory/POS. Zero grep hits for `documents` or `extractions` anywhere in infra/postgres/verify/. Separately: `documents` is NOT among the 28 tables receiving FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and runbooks/neon-data-plane.md line 86 states plainly that documents-RLS was "Deferred with documented rationale" and that "the explicit org_id predicate remains the actual boundary." I read those predicates (documents-store.ts:575-576, :799-801) and they are correct — but they are the sole tenant boundary for invoice records and they are exercised only against in-memory stubs. The company already knows: STATUS-v6.md:9 lists "ledger persistence is unverified against a live Neon." Also unexecuted: apps/desktop's Rust parity test — no `cargo` job exists in any of the 11 workflows.
impact: The first paying restaurant is the integration test for the layer holding their invoices. A drifted WHERE clause, a wrong ON CONFLICT, or a missing org_id in any of 644 statements ships green and is discovered by a customer seeing another restaurant's purchase data. Because documents has no database-level RLS, there is no backstop underneath the application predicate — a single bug is a cross-tenant data breach with breach-notification exposure, against the privacy positioning that is the entire competitive story versus MarginEdge and Restaurant365.
rec: Extend scripts/db-verify.sh with a documents/extractions tenant-isolation verify script modelled on the existing three: seed two orgs, set app.org_id to one, assert the other's rows are invisible through each real store query. Then add FORCE RLS on `documents` with the BYPASSRLS reaper role the runbook already specifies — that decision has been open since the note was written. Highest leverage per hour in the whole codebase.
note: Reproduced the core claim. apps/api/vitest.config.ts:6 is `environment: "node"` with no Workers pool; infra/postgres/verify/ holds exactly 3 files (coverage-persist, reorder-rate, tier2-theoretical) and `grep -rl documents infra/postgres/verify/` returns nothing. The documents-RLS deferral is real and DOCUMENTED at infra/postgres/migrations/0015_rls_data_plane.sql:33-55 ('SCOPE — why these four tables and not documents / line_item_keys'), so it is a recorded tradeoff. STATUS-v6.md:9 verbatim contains 'ledger persistence is unverified against a live Neon'. Two corrections: (a) severity — launch is deferred to 2027 with zero customers, so breach impact is prospective; 'critical' is inflated for a pre-revenue side-venture; (b) the 3-day effort estimate is wrong because the auditor never opened infra/postgres/tests/, which already holds 554 lines of cross-tenant RLS contract tests (see missed finding).

title: No migration runner, no applied-version ledger, and four migrations the code calls HARD pre-deploy gates that nothing checks
effort: 2 days including renumbering and a first reconciliation run against prod
evidence: infra/postgres/README.md states "In production, migrations run via the deploy pipeline... Do not run them by hand against production once that pipeline exists; let CI own the ordering." That pipeline does not exist: .github/workflows/deploy.yml contains no migration step, and grep for schema_migrations across scripts/, infra/postgres/ and apps/api/src returns nothing. The only application record is STATUS-v6.md:1077 — "Neon provisioned; Postgres 0001–0018 applied" — against a repo now shipping 59 files up to 0057. Three migration numbers are duplicated (0046, 0047, 0052 — e.g. 0052_catalog_family_key.sql and 0052_org_yield_overrides.sql), so ordering is decided by alphabetical tiebreak. infra/postgres/migrations/inventory_p1_bundle.sql is explicitly a copy-paste-into-the-Neon-SQL-editor convenience, confirming the manual workflow. Meanwhile apps/api/src/lib/documents-store.ts declares four separate hard preconditions — lines 454, 461, 469 and 642 each name a migration (0017/0018/0025/0026) whose absence makes every documents read and insert error. scripts/deploy-api.sh verifies branch, git freshness, clean tree, typecheck, copy-grade, verboten phrases, email templates, prettier and vitest — and nothing about schema.
impact: Nobody, including the founder, can state which schema version production is on. Deploying apps/api before hand-applying a migration errors every document read and write — total product outage, discovered by customers. The reverse (a migration applied without the code) is equally unguarded. For a founder who deploys in gaps between restaurant shifts, this is the failure most likely to happen on the worst possible evening.
rec: Add a `schema_migrations` table and a 30-line applier (filename, checksum, applied_at) run from deploy-api.sh before `wrangler deploy`; have it refuse to deploy when a migration file is unapplied. Renumber the three duplicate pairs first. This also gives you the version number no one can currently state.
note: All four evidence legs reproduce. `grep -rn schema_migrations scripts infra apps/api/src` → zero hits. .github/workflows/deploy.yml has no migration step. Duplicate numbering verified: 0046_inventory_stations / 0046_vendor_header_profile, 0047_inventory_counts / 0047_vendor_profile_contribution, 0052_catalog_family_key / 0052_org_yield_overrides. STATUS-v6.md:1077 reads 'Postgres `0001–0018` applied' and I found no later applied-version record in runbooks/ or docs/; the repo ships through 0057. Mitigation the auditor omitted: scripts/db-verify.sh:41-45 applies every numbered migration to a fresh PG16 in the ci.yml `db-verify` job on every push, so the migration SET is proven appliable in order — what is unknown is only which subset prod has. That makes this a deploy-sequencing hazard, not an unknown-correctness one; high, not critical.

title: The storefront deploy gate is red right now — no content change can ship, and the fix is two commands
effort: 2 hours for the deploy unblock; half a day to prune the baseline and wire the builder
evidence: I ran the gate. `node scripts/check-all.mjs --baseline scripts/check-all-baseline.json` reports: "✗ NEW regressions (2) — NOT in the baseline: Cost-index picker — grapefruit: dollarRef false != recomputed true; Ingredient state record (idem) — DRIFT: cost-index/ingredient-state-record.csv is stale." The plain-flag form is what wrangler.jsonc:159 runs as the Cloudflare build command, and check-all.mjs exits 1 on any failure in that mode (`process.exit(failed > 0 ? 1 : 0)`). Running `node scripts/build-ingredient-state-record.mjs --check` directly gives exit 1 with three drifted outputs. That builder is registered as OPERATOR_DATA/MANUAL at scripts/check-idem-coverage.mjs:74, appears zero times in wrangler.jsonc, zero times in .github/workflows/, and is not in check-all-baseline.json — so nothing heals it. It is deterministic by design (its header at line 23 reads "Deterministic (no build clock)"), reading only committed data files, so the drift reproduces identically inside Cloudflare's build container. Same run also shows the baseline has rotted: 19 of its 25 entries now PASS and are flagged "prune from baseline", leaving only 6 of 25 legitimate.
impact: The Cost Index and free tools are the entire top of funnel and the whole reason the storefront exists. While this is red, no article, price update, or copy fix reaches muntin.digital — and the failure is silent from the founder's side unless he watches Cloudflare build logs. The second regression (grapefruit dollarRef) is a data-honesty check the baseline doc explicitly refuses to ever baseline, so it is signalling real drift in published readings, not build noise.
rec: Run `node scripts/build-ingredient-state-record.mjs`, then investigate the grapefruit dollarRef mismatch (it is a semantic data drift, not a regeneration). Commit both. Then prune the 19 stale baseline entries so the list stays trustworthy, and add the ingredient-state-record builder to the cost-index-refresh workflow so operator-data drift self-heals like its siblings.
note: The headline reproduces exactly. `node scripts/check-all.mjs --baseline scripts/check-all-baseline.json` → '312 of 320 passed', '✗ NEW regressions (2)': grapefruit dollarRef and the ingredient-state-record CSV drift; 19 of 25 baseline entries flagged 'prune from baseline'. `node scripts/build-ingredient-state-record.mjs --check` exits 1. wrangler.jsonc:159 runs the strict no-flag form. Tree is clean, so the deploy is red at HEAD. REFUTED sub-claim: the auditor called grapefruit 'a semantic data drift, not a regeneration' and told the founder to investigate it. I ran `node scripts/build-cost-index-picker.mjs`; the check goes green and the ONLY change is dollarRefCount 19→20 with grapefruit flipping true — a plain stale derived artifact, identical in kind to the other regression. Following that recommendation burns an evening on a non-problem. The auditor also misdiagnosed the cause as manual-builder neglect; the real cause is an automated workflow staging bug (missed finding #1).

title: Four TypeScript source files contain literal NUL bytes and are silently invisible to every grep-based CI gate, including the no-LLM and secret-scanning gates
effort: 2 hours
evidence: Empirically confirmed, not inferred. `grep -EnH 'async' apps/api/src/lib/recipes-store.ts` returns 0 lines on stdout; the same command against catalog-store.ts returns 28. GNU grep classifies the file as binary and its notice does not reach stdout, so any pipeline consuming grep's stdout sees nothing. I reproduced the exact failure with a seeded secret: a file containing `sk-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ012345` plus one NUL byte produces zero output through the privacy-ci.sh pipeline shape. Four tracked source files are affected: apps/api/src/lib/org-settings-store.ts (1 NUL, a composite-key separator at byte 6825), apps/api/src/lib/recipes-store.ts (3 NULs), apps/api/src/lib/pos/sales-store.ts, and apps/api/src/routes/hablanos.ts (a raw control char inside a filename-sanitiser regex character class). The affected gates all use `xargs -0 -r grep -EnH` over `git ls-files`: scripts/privacy-ci.sh:71 (the sk-/AKIA/ghp_ secret scan), :86 (DO-NOT-COMMIT scan), :120 (console.log/print leak scan), and scripts/no-llm-ci.sh:58, :76, :94 — the last being the build gate behind the company's flagship "no LLM in the read path" claim.
impact: Six privacy and supply-chain gates have four blind spots, one of them a route file. A committed API key in any of these files would pass secret scanning; an LLM call added to hablanos.ts would pass the no-LLM gate that the marketing site sells as a structural guarantee. That turns a public, differentiating privacy claim into one that is unverified for part of the codebase — exactly the class of gap a pen-test or a customer's security questionnaire is designed to surface.
rec: Replace each literal NUL with the two-character escape `�` (functionally identical in a TS string and in a regex class) so the files become plain text again. Then add `grep -Il` binary-detection to privacy-ci.sh and no-llm-ci.sh that FAILS on any tracked non-binary-extension file grep considers binary, so this can never silently recur.
note: Independently reproduced end to end; the strongest finding in the report. Python byte counts: org-settings-store.ts 1 NUL, recipes-store.ts 3, pos/sales-store.ts 2 (auditor implied fewer), routes/hablanos.ts 1 (auditor called it 'a raw control char'; it is a NUL). `grep -EnH 'async' apps/api/src/lib/recipes-store.ts 2>/dev/null` produces ZERO stdout lines — the 'binary file matches' notice goes to stderr, which scripts/privacy-ci.sh:71 and scripts/no-llm-ci.sh:58 both discard with 2>/dev/null; the same command on catalog-store.ts returns 28 matches. Seeded-secret repro: two files each containing `sk-ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ012345`, one with a trailing NUL, piped through the gates' exact `xargs -0 -r grep -EnH` shape — only the clean file is reported. Six privacy/supply-chain scans are blind in four tracked source files, one a route.

title: One unset env var on the Fly extract app silently disables six subsystems while /health still returns ok
effort: 1 day, plus 10 minutes to check the live secret
evidence: services/extract/main.py:95-142 constructs six components from a single `os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL")`: template_store, community_pool, vendor_profile_store, sku_history, price_history, and the vendor-trust path. Every factory falls back silently — template_store.py:1704-1711 returns InMemoryTemplateStore when database_url is falsy, and the docstring at :1692-1698 acknowledges the failure mode was "templates evaporating on restart" while claiming it is "no longer silent." It is still silent: HealthResponse (main.py:387-394) is `extra="forbid"` and exposes only status, version, engine, synonyms_loaded and vendor_catalog_loaded — no store backend. services/extract/fly.toml:31 sets `auto_stop_machines = true` with the health check at :43-48 hitting that same /health, so an idle-stopped machine restarts, reports perfectly healthy, and has lost every learned template. No CI gate, no startup assertion, and no /health field would reveal it. Note the scale of what depends on it: VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md projects the trust path lifting first-pass straight-through extraction from 24% to ~62%.
impact: This is the cost-index snapshot lapse (dormant 42 days, found only by audit) repeated six-fold on the extraction engine — the product's core value. If DATABASE_URL is not set on muntin-extract-iad, auto-confirm never matures, every invoice keeps landing in needs_review, and the operator experiences it as "the product just doesn't learn" with no error anywhere to explain why. Unverifiable from this container, which is precisely the problem.
rec: Add the store backend to HealthResponse (`template_store: "postgres"|"memory"`, plus the same for community_pool and vendor_profile) and have the Fly health check fail when MUNTIN_ENV is production and any reads "memory". A degraded service should not report healthy. Then verify the live value with `flyctl secrets list -a muntin-extract-iad` today.
note: The code reading is accurate: services/extract/main.py:95-142 derives template_store, community_pool, vendor_profile_store, sku_history_store and price_history_store from one `os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL")`, each falling back silently, and HealthResponse (main.py:387-394) is `extra="forbid"` with no backend field. But the impact is overstated on its own evidence: main.py:118-120 sets `self.vendor_trust_active = os.environ.get("EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE") == "1"` and the adjacent comment says the path defaults to SHADOW — 'compute + surface the decision for telemetry, but do NOT auto-confirm on it'. The 24%→62% straight-through unlock the auditor attaches to this finding is therefore off by design today regardless of DATABASE_URL. With zero production invoices flowing, medium is honest.

title: The production deploy workflow deploys nothing — every step is an echo, and its documented two-person approval gates an empty job
effort: Half a day to correct the file honestly; 2 days to actually wire it
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy.yml carries 33 lines of header describing a two-person `environment: production` approval control ("Prevent self-review: ON — this is what makes it two-person", CODEOWNERS-protected so "a PR that strips the gate cannot land"). Every actual step is a stub: `echo "TODO(B-priv-6): wire wrangler deploy after cosign signing pipeline lands"` for api, docling and extract, and the same for web. The audit step is `echo "TODO: POST /v1/audit/deploys after the route lands"`. It is also stale in two ways that prove nobody has run it: it deploys web via `vercel deploy --prod`, while apps/web/package.json:18 deploys through OpenNext to Cloudflare (`opennextjs-cloudflare build && wrangler deploy`); and it references `infra/fly/extract.toml`, which does not exist — the file is at services/extract/fly.toml (infra/fly/ holds only docling-ephemeral.toml and pdfa-render-ephemeral.toml). Real deploys run from scripts/deploy-api.sh on the founder's Mac, which is well-guarded but records only to a gitignored `.deploy-history`.
impact: A control described in detail — and referenced in docs/pen-test-prep.md as part of the packet handed to a third-party assessor — does not exist. Any security questionnaire, SOC2 pre-assessment, or pen-test answered from this file would be answered incorrectly. Operationally there is also no durable deploy audit trail: what shipped to production and when lives only in one untracked local file on one laptop.
rec: Either wire the three deploy targets to their real commands (correcting the Vercel and infra/fly path errors) or rewrite the header to say honestly that production deploys are single-operator via scripts/deploy-*.sh and that two-person approval is not in force for a solo company. Then make deploy-api.sh append its record to a committed file, not a gitignored one. Do not leave a document that describes a control you do not have.
note: Every claim reproduces. .github/workflows/deploy.yml carries the 33-line two-person-approval header and all five job steps are `echo "TODO(B-priv-6): ..."` / `echo "TODO: POST /v1/audit/deploys ..."`. The web branch comments `pnpm dlx vercel deploy --prod` while apps/web deploys via OpenNext to Cloudflare. `ls infra/fly/` returns only README.md, docling-ephemeral.toml and pdfa-render-ephemeral.toml — the referenced infra/fly/extract.toml does not exist (real path services/extract/fly.toml). Nothing to correct; the 'rewrite the header honestly for a solo company' recommendation is right and cheap.

title: The storefront deploy installs two unpinned @latest packages from the network on every build
effort: 1 hour
evidence: wrangler.jsonc:159 is a single ~80-command `&&` chain. After the tar it runs `npm install --no-save --no-fund --no-audit --silent lightningcss@latest`, then `node scripts/minify-css.mjs`, then `node scripts/vendor-pin.mjs`, then `npx -y pagefind@latest --site dist`. Both are floating to whatever npm serves at build time, with no lockfile and no integrity pin — inside the same command that also runs a script literally named vendor-pin. The contrast with the product repo is stark: there, .github/workflows/ci.yml:753 enforces `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` as a hard gate, installs are `--frozen-lockfile`, and ci.yml:807 emits SPDX SBOMs via syft. I also verified the one dependency worth checking by hand — pdfjs-dist resolves to 4.10.38 in pnpm-lock.yaml, safely past the 4.2.67 fix for the CVE-2024-4367 PDF script-execution issue, and it renders customer invoices, so that one is genuinely fine.
impact: Two unpinned third-party packages execute with full filesystem access during every production build of the public site. A breaking release halts all deploys until diagnosed; a compromised release injects into 1,368 pages serving the free tools that are the entire top of funnel. The blast radius is the brand's credibility on exactly the axis it competes on. It is also the weakest link in an otherwise strong supply-chain posture, which makes it easy to miss.
rec: Pin both to exact versions (`lightningcss@1.x.y`, `pagefind@1.x.y`) and bump deliberately. One line each, zero downside.
note: wrangler.jsonc:159 verbatim contains `npm install --no-save --no-fund --no-audit --silent lightningcss@latest` and `npx -y pagefind@latest --site dist`, both inside the same `&&` chain that runs scripts/vendor-pin.mjs. Medium is right for a pre-revenue static site — real supply-chain hole, but the realistic failure is a breaking release halting deploys, and the fix is one line each.

title: Cross-repo parity contracts are declared in comments and enforced by nothing — the exact shape that produced the 42-day snapshot lapse
effort: 1 day for both gates
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/yield-table.ts:1-4 reads: "AUTO-EXTRACTED VERBATIM from storefront tools/plate-cost/plate-cost.js YIELD_TABLE... DO NOT hand-edit — re-extract from the storefront source so Ledger and the free tool never disagree (parity contract)." I diffed the two tables mechanically: 314 keys each, 0 keys unique to either side, 0 value disagreements — the contract currently HOLDS. But nothing enforces it. scripts/check-cross-repo-seams.mjs (its own header, lines 10-17) checks only three things: ?source=ledger attribution on /window links, the parentOrganization @id, and the hello@muntin.digital contact string. Same pattern on the crypto vectors: apps/desktop/.../parity-vectors.json's own `_comment` says "DO NOT mutate without coordinating across all four files; the byte-level outputs are the contract" — four copies (apps/api/src/lib/parity-vectors.ts, services/docling/parity_vectors.py, plus the Rust and Swift fixtures) and grep for parity-vectors across scripts/ and .github/workflows/ returns nothing. This is structurally identical to the cost-index snapshot seam that sat dormant 42 days; that one now has scripts/check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs, but its siblings do not.
impact: If the yield table drifts, the free Plate Cost tool and the paid Ledger return different food costs for the same ingredient — a visible contradiction between the funnel and the product, on the number the product exists to compute, and a quiet falsification of the stated parity guarantee. The crypto-vector copies are worse in kind: silent divergence there means a recovery phrase generated on one platform may not restore on another, which is unrecoverable customer data loss.
rec: Write one gate that hashes the four parity-vector files' parsed content (ignoring comments) and fails on mismatch — cheap and fully local. For the yield table, add a `--check` mode to the extraction script and run it in the same cross-repo job that already handles the cost-index snapshot, since that job already assumes both checkouts.
note: Confirmed and UNDERSTATED. scripts/check-cross-repo-seams.mjs does check only the three cosmetic seams named; `grep -rn parity-vectors scripts .github/workflows` returns nothing. But the auditor's framing — 'that one now has scripts/check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs, but its siblings do not' — is falsely reassuring. I ran the siblings: `node scripts/check-cost-pressure-snapshot-fresh.mjs` EXITS 1 today ('STALE SOON — asOf 2026-07-20 is 17d old and the resolver stops answering past 21d'), and ci.yml:208-209 runs it in the privacy-gates job on every push and PR. The cross-repo vendoring seam is not a latent risk; it is failing now. Raised to high.

title: The extraction engine's regression net is 24 hand-authored synthetic cases; the 919-document real corpus its key decisions cite is not in the repo
effort: 3 days, mostly anonymization
evidence: services/extract/tests/golden/cases.py is 1,795 lines defining 24 GoldenCase entries whose `docling_doc` fields are hand-written dicts. services/extract/tests/golden/MISSES.md states the reframing directly: "the synthetic golden set is now the canonical regression corpus." Real anonymized fixtures number 7 (tests/golden/real_fixtures/: baldor, chefs_warehouse, cintas ×2, fresco ×2, ihalper). Meanwhile VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md bases its central promotion decision — the 0.7 header-overlap knee, projecting 24%→62% straight-through — on "a 919-doc real-corpus run" via cli/vendor_flywheel.py; that corpus is nowhere in the tree, so the measurement cannot be reproduced or re-run in CI. MISSES.md also notes the harness uses 28 seeded synonyms and 5 vendor catalog entries while production loads ~225 synonyms and 44 vendors. The determinism gate (ci.yml:561-584) runs `pytest tests/test_golden.py -k determinism` under PYTHONHASHSEED=0, which proves run-twice-equal within one process — not stability across engine versions.
impact: The engine is validated mostly against invoices its own author wrote, which cannot contain the layouts he did not think of. Real-world first-pass accuracy is therefore an estimate, and 87%/62% numbers that appear in planning (and could plausibly reach marketing) trace to a corpus no gate can re-verify. For a product whose promise is "it does not guess," the accuracy claim is the one number that must never be soft.
rec: Commit an anonymized slice of the 919-doc corpus (or its docling JSON, which carries no images) as fixtures so vendor_flywheel numbers become reproducible in CI. If licensing forbids that, record the measured numbers plus corpus hash in a dated file and add a gate that fails when the claim is cited without a matching run — the same discipline the storefront's sourced-claims gate already applies to prose.
note: services/extract/tests/golden/cases.py is 1,795 lines with exactly 24 `GoldenCase(` constructions; real_fixtures/ holds exactly 7 JSON files (baldor, chefs_warehouse, cintas ×2, fresco ×2, ihalper); VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:14 and :203 cite the '919-doc real-corpus run' / 'Measured findings (2026-06-18, 919-doc corpus)' and that corpus is absent from the tree. Nothing to correct; medium is right for a pre-launch engine.

title: 82,050 lines of build tooling for a static site — 6× the product repo's — with a 74-script serial deploy chain and one person to maintain it
effort: 1 week to split the deploy stages; the freeze is a decision, not work
evidence: The storefront's scripts/ holds 383 files totalling 82,050 LOC of .mjs, of which 129 are check-*.mjs at 18,867 LOC; `node scripts/check-all.mjs` runs 320 checks. The product repo's entire scripts/ directory is 12,808 LOC. wrangler.jsonc:159 chains 74 distinct `node scripts/*.mjs` invocations with `&&` before check-all, the tar, and the two @latest installs — any one failing blocks every deploy, which is how finding #3 happens. The rot is already visible in the artifacts meant to keep this honest: 19 of 25 entries in check-all-baseline.json now pass and are flagged for pruning, and CLAUDE.md records 21 manual idem builders (8 rendering operator-fetched data) whose drift only surfaces as a red deploy. Corroborating small drift in the product repo: the coverage floor is stated as three different numbers — the ci.yml job name says "apps/api >= 63%", check-coverage-floor.mjs:9's docstring says 80, and the actual constant at :42 is 67.
impact: This is the single largest claim on the scarcest resource in the company — the evenings of a full-time front-of-house manager. Every hour maintaining 320 checks over a pre-revenue marketing site is an hour not spent on the persistence gap in finding #1 or the migration pipeline in #2, which are what actually stand between the product and a paying customer. The tooling is high quality; the allocation is the problem, and its brittleness now actively blocks shipping.
rec: Freeze the storefront gate count — no new check-*.mjs there until the product's db-verify covers documents/extractions. Split the deploy chain so content builds and the 320-check audit are separate stages, letting a content fix ship while a data-drift check is amber. Then retire or fold the checks whose subject was already retired, using the same evidence standard the repo applies elsewhere.
note: Numbers are directionally right but loose: 373 .mjs in storefront scripts/ totalling 78,783 lines (auditor: 383 / 82,050), 129 check-*.mjs, and the run printed 320 checks — those hold. Product scripts/ is 13,185 lines (auditor: 12,808). The coverage-floor triple-disagreement reproduces exactly: ci.yml:670 job name 'apps/api >= 63%', check-coverage-floor.mjs:9 docstring 'default 80', :42 `APPS_API_FLOOR ?? "67"`. PARTIAL because the central causal claim — that build burden is what blocks shipping — is not what I found: the deploy is red because an automated bot discards derived artifacts it rebuilt (missed #1) and because no storefront gate runs pre-merge (missed #2). Freezing the gate count prevents neither.

title: The daily Cost-Index bot reds the storefront deploy on a schedule: it rebuilds derived artifacts, then stages an allowlist that omits them and reverts the rest
evidence: .github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml:99 runs `node scripts/build-cost-index-picker.mjs`. Its `git add` allowlist at lines 302-309 does NOT include data/cost-index-picker.js (nor cost-index-events.json, cost-index-context.json/.js, cost-index-labels.json, cost-index-sources.json). Line 313 then runs `git checkout -- . 2>/dev/null || true`, discarding every unstaged rebuild the job just performed. The workflow's own comment at line 291 records that this exact mechanism already destroyed a rebuild once ('then the `git checkout -- .` below discarded the freshly-rolled prev') and the fix was applied to that ONE file, not to the staging list as a class. The consequence is live at HEAD: bot commit 7808827cc ('data(cost-index): measured read 2026-08-05', author muntin-cost-index-bot) shipped a seed where grapefruit gained a firm dollar reference, without the regenerated picker. `node scripts/check-cost-index-picker.mjs` fails with 'grapefruit: dollarRef false != recomputed true'; running the builder changes exactly dollarRefCount 19→20 and the check goes green. It recurs: git log on data/cost-index-picker.js shows dea46ad34 'fix(ci): regenerate lockfloat + picker stale after the main merge' and 0eb001af4 'chore(cost-index): reconcile picker + revisions derived data to unblock deploy'.
impact: The primary auditor diagnosed this red deploy as an operator who forgot a manual builder and told the founder to investigate grapefruit as semantic data drift. Both are wrong, and wrongly is expensive: he chases a data-honesty ghost, hand-runs a builder, and the same bot reds the deploy again on the next Mon/Wed/Fri run. Every push-triggered Cloudflare deploy of muntin.digital — the entire top of funnel — is blocked until a human hand-reconciles a file the automation deliberately threw away.
rec: Replace the `git add <allowlist>` + `git checkout -- .` pair with an explicit deny-list revert, or `git add -A` scoped to the paths the job may touch. Then run `node scripts/check-all.mjs` inside the refresh job before the push, so the bot can never commit a state its own deploy gate rejects. One workflow edit; it retires the recurring 'unblock deploy' commits permanently.

title: Nothing runs the storefront's 320-check suite before merge — 129 gates are a post-merge deploy blocker, never a merge blocker
evidence: `grep -ln check-all .github/workflows/*.yml` in potentially-profitable returns only cost-index-refresh.yml and freshness-heartbeat.yml. The three PR-triggered workflows are lighthouse-ci.yml, playwright.yml and window-a11y.yml; none invokes check-all. freshness-heartbeat.yml:12-15 states it in the repo's own words: 'They already run inside check-all.mjs. But check-all runs in the Cloudflare Workers build, which runs on PUSH,' and :17-21 says it deliberately runs ONLY the time-decay gates, not the full suite, because the (idem) injector checks need the ~75-step build chain first. So the only place the full suite meets a merge candidate is wrangler.jsonc:159 — after the merge, inside Cloudflare's builder, where the sole notification channel is a build log someone must think to open.
impact: This is the structural reason the deploy has been red repeatedly and why 'to unblock deploy' commits exist in history. A one-person company gets its content pipeline broken by merges it cannot see failing, and finds out when it notices the site did not update. It also explains the 19-of-25 rotted baseline entries: nothing forces anyone to read check-all output on a cadence tied to change.
rec: Add a `pull_request` + `push: main` workflow that runs the wrangler build.command's builder chain followed by `node scripts/check-all.mjs` in the same STRICT form Cloudflare runs. It needs no secrets (the chain is all local node) and converts 129 gates from post-hoc deploy blockers into pre-merge signal. Highest-leverage change in the storefront repo; cost is one YAML file.

title: The product repo's CI is failing right now on a vendored-snapshot gate — the 2026-07-30 lesson recurring on the sibling seam the auditor called solved
evidence: I executed the gates instead of reading about them. `node scripts/check-cost-pressure-snapshot-fresh.mjs` exits 1: 'FAIL (STALE-SOON) — asOf 2026-07-20 is 17d old and the resolver stops answering past 21d.' ci.yml:206-209 runs it (with --self-test) in the privacy-gates job, which fires on push to main and claude/**, and on every pull_request — so CI is red on every branch today. The fresh data already exists on the other side: potentially-profitable/data/cost-pressure.json carries asOf 2026-08-03 (commit ed3cc1704). Only the cross-repo `node apps/api/scripts/vendor-cost-pressure.mjs` step is missing, and no workflow in either repo checks out the other. Its sibling check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs passes (freshest 9d, oldest 19d of a 30d window), which is presumably why the auditor assumed the class was handled.
impact: The primary report asserts 'the meta-gate works and is currently clean' and offers check-gate-coverage's empty UNWIRED as a strength — a statement about SHAPE (every gate is wired) presented as evidence about GROUNDING (the system is healthy). That is precisely the error the 2026-07-30 audit was written to prevent, committed inside the report that cites that audit as its method. Concretely: CI is red on every push, and in four days the supply-pressure band silently stops answering in the product — the same way the 42-day market-prior lapse began.
rec: Re-vendor today (`node apps/api/scripts/vendor-cost-pressure.mjs` with both repos checked out) and commit. Then treat both vendored snapshots as one problem: either accept the cross-repo PAT as an explicit founder call and cron both re-vendors, or have the resolvers fetch the public storefront JSON at runtime so no human step stands between fresh public data and the product.

title: 554 lines of cross-tenant RLS contract tests exist, are cited by the threat model and pre-launch checklist as running in CI, and are executed by nothing
evidence: infra/postgres/tests/ contains 0004_rls_cross_tenant.sql (146 lines), 0034_org_recipes_rls.sql (58), 0038_pos_sales_rls.sql (179), 0039_pos_views_rls.sql (109), 0041_pos_location_map_rls.sql (62). scripts/db-verify.sh:31 sets `VER="$ROOT/infra/postgres/verify"` and line 51 loops `for v in "$VER"/*.sql` — the tests/ directory is never referenced by db-verify.sh, ci.yml, or any workflow (`grep -rn 'postgres/tests' --include=*.sh --include=*.yml` returns zero hits under scripts/ and .github/). Meanwhile docs/threat-model.md:91-93 states 0004_rls_cross_tenant.sql 'is a runnable script that asserts org_A's role cannot SELECT or INSERT against org_B's rows. Runs against any Postgres in CI' — the last sentence is false. runbooks/pre-launch-checklist.md:33 lists it as a GO gate ('Cross-tenant pgTAP RLS test green'). The only other references are copy-paste psql instructions in runbooks/square-pos-activation.md:40 and ledger-spec/README.md:103.
impact: Two compounding harms. The threat model — the document handed to a pen-tester or attached to a customer security questionnaire — attests to a running control that does not run; that is a false attestation, not a gap. And it makes the primary auditor's headline finding both more true and far cheaper to fix than estimated: they budgeted 3 days to WRITE a tenant-isolation verify script, unaware the hardest one already exists and needs a second glob plus the two test roles its own header documents.
rec: Extend scripts/db-verify.sh to run infra/postgres/tests/*.sql after the verify/ set, creating tenant_role_a / tenant_role_b as the 0004 header specifies. Expect real failures on the first run — that is the finding. Then correct docs/threat-model.md:93 to say what actually runs. Half a day, and it moves the largest unproven layer from 'unknown' to 'measured'.

title: The storefront's ability to deploy is coupled to one laptop: 21 manual builders are hard deploy gates, and the meta-gate certifies the coupling rather than removing it
evidence: scripts/check-idem-coverage.mjs:8-16 states the arrangement plainly — check-all `--check`s the (idem) builders and runs at the END of the Cloudflare build.command, so 'a builder that check-all verifies but nothing re-runs turns any drift into a RED DEPLOY that no automation can clear.' Running it: '83 (idem) builder(s) — 56 run by the deploy, 6 by a workflow, 21 documented as manual. 0 unhealed.' It reports green because MANUAL is one of three ACCEPTED states (:25-31), and eight of the 21 carry the OPERATOR_DATA entry (:62-66) whose `who` field reads 'the operator, on the Mac that holds the API keys'. build-ingredient-state-record.mjs is entry one on that list — and it is what is reding the deploy today. The gate says 0 unhealed while one of its healers is unavailable and the deploy is down.
impact: For a one-person company where the person is a full-time FOH manager, 21 latent deploy blockers clearable only from his own machine — 8 needing API keys and network he only has there — means the site cannot be fixed from anywhere else, by anyone else, or by any automation. The primary audit inspected this gate and reported its green as a strength; green here means 'the dependency is written down', not 'the dependency is safe'.
rec: Split the 21 into two classes. Add the 13 content-linked builders to the wrangler build chain — they read only committed data, so they genuinely self-heal. Downgrade the 8 operator-data entries in check-all from hard-fail to warn: they cannot be healed inside the deploy container by construction, so failing the deploy on their drift is a category error. Let freshness-heartbeat carry that alarm instead.

title: The storefront production deploy is RED today — the site cannot ship anything
effort: 45 minutes to clear; 2 hours to make it not recur
evidence: I ran `node scripts/check-all.mjs` on HEAD `7808827cc` (== `origin/main`). title: The storefront has no blocking pre-merge CI at all — 129 gates run only after merge
effort: 3 hours including one shakeout cycle
evidence: `grep -rn "check-all" .github/workflows/` returns only comments — no workflow invokes it. impact: The company's entire quality methodology is its gates, and none of them can stop a bad merge. The only enforcement point is the deploy — so a violation does not get blocked, it gets the whole site blocked. This is exactly the pattern in board open item 6: PR #536 was merged with three reds under founder approval, and two of the three were structurally incapable of blocking anything in the first place.
rec: Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to `potentially-profitable`: Node 22, `on: [pull_request, push]`, running the deploy's injector chain then `node scripts/check-all.mjs`. It needs no secrets and no network — I ran the whole thing in this container in ~9 minutes. Do this AFTER clearing the current red, or it reds every PR on day one (the repo's own rule).
note: Reproduced. `.github/workflows/` holds exactly 7 files; no workflow invokes check-all. lighthouse-ci.yml:41, playwright.yml:48, window-a11y.yml:56 (+124/131/138) all carry `continue-on-error: true`, and all three headers say so deliberately ('continue-on-error initially ... remove when baseline is locked'). I am downgrading severity: for a one-person repo where the founder is the only committer, the deploy IS the enforcement point and it does block (finding 1 proves it). The real cost is the blast radius the auditor names in passing — a violation freezes the whole site rather than one PR — plus the fact that the deploy gate cannot be consulted before merging. That is high, not critical.

title: The Mon/Wed/Fri refresh rebuilds the picker manifest and then throws it away — an oscillating deploy blocker
effort: 20 minutes
evidence: `.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml` line 99 runs `node scripts/build-cost-index-picker.mjs`, writing `data/cost-index-picker.js`. The commit step's `git add` list (lines 305-313) does not include that path, and line 314 is `git checkout -- . 2>/dev/null || true`, which discards it. `git log --format=%an -- data/cost-index-picker.js` returns four commits, all authored by `Claude` — `muntin-cost-index-bot` has NEVER committed it. I replayed grapefruit's `dollarRef` across the last 15 refresh commits of `data/cost-index.js` using the gate's own rule: it oscillates with confidence (`low`→false / `medium`→true) — 07-29 false, 07-31 true, 08-03 false, 08-05 true. The committed manifest has said `false` since 2026-07-28, so roughly every other refresh reds the deploy and the next one accidentally clears it. The very comment block above that `git add` (lines 290-294) documents this identical bug being fixed for `data/cost-index-readings.prev.json`.
impact: About half of all data-refresh deploys fail for a reason unrelated to the data, and the failure clears itself, which trains the founder to treat a red deploy as noise. That is how a real red gets ignored — the exact dynamic the repo's own idem-coverage gate was written to prevent.
rec: Add `data/cost-index-picker.js` to the `git add` list in `cost-index-refresh.yml` (line ~305). While there, audit the other builders that step runs against the staged set — `build-cost-index-events.mjs` writes `data/cost-index-events.json` and `build-cost-index-context.mjs` writes `data/cost-index-context.{json,js}`, none of which are staged either; they pass today but sit on the same fuse.
note: Fully reproduced, and it is the sharpest finding in the report. cost-index-refresh.yml:99 runs build-cost-index-picker.mjs under a comment that explicitly states it 'must be rewritten here or it trips check-cost-index-picker on the next PR'; the `git add` list at lines 303-311 omits data/cost-index-picker.js and line 312 is `git checkout -- . 2>/dev/null || true`. `git log --format=%an -- data/cost-index-picker.js` returns 4 commits, all `Claude`, none by muntin-cost-index-bot. I independently reproduced the oscillation the auditor inferred, using confidence rather than their replay: grapefruit's point confidence across the last six refresh commits is low(07-24) / low(07-27) / low(07-29) / medium(07-31) / low(08-03) / medium(08-05). The picker's dollarRef keys off that, the committed manifest was built on a `low` day, so alternating refreshes red and green the deploy. The comment block at lines 288-292 documents this exact bug being fixed for cost-index-readings.prev.json — the lesson was written down and not generalized.

title: The three gates that claim to enforce currency compare frozen artifact pairs, never today's date
effort: 1 day for the gate work; the 16-feed triage is a separate founder call
evidence: `node scripts/check-staleness-honesty.mjs` prints `93 shippable point(s) · max overdue ratio 0.00× cadence · 0 overdue · ✓ no point wears a confidence its freshness can't support` — while `check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` reports 26 of 100 series frozen 58–88 days. The mechanism is in `tools/_shared/cost-staleness.js`: `stalenessOf()` computes `daysBetween(point.asOf, freshestLevelSource(point).date)`, both frozen in the vendored data, and its own header calls this "deterministic by construction". So `salmon-fillet` (asOf 2026-06-01, provenance 2026-06-01) scores 0 stale days forever, and `butter-lettuce` (asOf 2026-08-04, provenance mixing 2026-08-04 with 2026-05-22) scores 0 because `freshestLevelSource` takes the MAX. `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` line 76+108 is `lag = days(dataAsOf, latestDispatch)` — if the data pipeline dies, `asOf` freezes and the gate goes permanently green. `check-cost-index-editors-note.mjs` contains no `Date` reference at all. Mechanically: only 13 of 128 storefront gates and 4 of 39 product gates touch `Date.now()`/`new Date()`/`spawnSync`; ~89% are pure text-and-structure inspection.
impact: The published Cost Index — the company's credibility asset and its whole top of funnel — carries `medium`/`high` confidence labels on prices last measured in May, and the gate written specifically to prevent that reports zero violations. Two of these three sit in `freshness-heartbeat.yml`'s roster (lines 66-72) as "time-decay gates", so the weekly alarm that exists for absence is partly made of gates that absence cannot trip.
rec: Two changes, both small. (1) In `cost-staleness.js`, add a wall-clock arm: staleness is `max(asOf − freshestProvenance, today − asOf)`, so a frozen point ages in real time; keep the frozen arm for page rendering determinism and use the wall-clock arm in the gate. (2) Add `check-cost-index-series-freshness` to the `GATES` list in `freshness-heartbeat.yml` — it is the only gate that can see a dead feed and it is the one gate missing from the roster. Then triage the 16 UNEXPECTED feeds (8 of them new since the board was written on 2026-07-31) and promote it to `--strict`.
note: Mechanism CONFIRMED, impact REFUTED, severity inflated. Confirmed: tools/_shared/cost-staleness.js:49-58 `freshestLevelSource` takes the MAX provenance date and :72 `staleDays = daysBetween(asOf, src.date)` — both frozen, and check-staleness-honesty.mjs:10-11 documents this as intentional ('never today, so this never churns between rebuilds'). check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh is indeed lag(dataAsOf, dispatch). Only 10 storefront gates reference Date.now()/new Date(), close to the auditor's 13. REFUTED: the impact paragraph. I evaluated all 93 shippable points in data/cost-index.json against 2026-08-06 — ZERO carry medium or high confidence on data older than 45 days; all 11 such points are labeled `directional`, the lowest rung (overall split: 11 directional / 62 low / 20 medium, no `high` anywhere). salmon-fillet (asOf 2026-06-01) is `directional`; butter-lettuce is `low` and has six 2026-08-04 provenance legs against one 2026-05-22 leg, so 'prices last measured in May' misdescribes it. The gate's stated job — no label above its freshness ceiling — is being met in substance, not just shape. Also REFUTED as a hidden gap: check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs:12-16 explicitly documents that check-staleness-honesty cannot see an absent source ('a source that stops publishing entirely is not overdue, it is absent'), and that gate is wired into check-all and named all 26 frozen feeds in my run. This is a known, documented, already-mitigated gap. The one durable residual is the auditor's rec #2: series-freshness is absent from freshness-heartbeat.yml's roster.

title: `deploy.yml` deploys nothing — every branch is an echoed TODO, and no deploy record exists anywhere
effort: 3 hours
evidence: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` carries a 30-line header about two-person `environment: production` approval, then all four targets are `echo "TODO(B-priv-6): wire ... after cosign signing pipeline lands"` (lines 71, 79, 87, 95) and the audit step is `echo "TODO: POST /v1/audit/deploys after the route lands"` (line 100). The web branch says "Deploy web (Vercel)" while the actual path is `apps/web/package.json` line 18: `deploy:cf` → `opennextjs-cloudflare build && wrangler deploy` — the stub names the wrong platform. The only real deploy record mechanism is `deploy-api.sh` line 84 appending to `.deploy-history`, which is gitignored (`.gitignore:60`), plus a manual paste into `runbooks/deploy.md` — which contains zero deploy entries.
impact: Nothing in either repo can tell you what commit is live at api.muntin.digital or app.muntin.digital. "Merged" is structurally indistinguishable from "shipped" — CLAUDE.md warns about this in prose ("A pushed branch is not live", "merged is not shipped") precisely because there is no artifact that answers the question. The two-person-approval control that CODEOWNERS protects is protecting a no-op.
rec: Either un-stub the workflow or delete it and stop implying a control exists. Cheapest honest step for a solo founder: make `deploy-api.sh` and `deploy:cf` append a line to a COMMITTED `runbooks/deploy-log.md` and refuse to deploy if the previous entry is malformed. That gives you one grep-able answer to "what is live?".
note: Facts reproduced, framing over-claimed. deploy.yml lines 71/79/87/95 are all `echo "TODO(B-priv-6): wire ... after cosign signing pipeline lands"`, line 100 is the audit-log TODO, and line 91 does say 'Deploy web (Vercel)' against the real OpenNext/Cloudflare path. `.gitignore:60` is `.deploy-history` and runbooks/deploy.md carries no entries. But the stub is not a silent lie: lines 66-70 name the blocker (B-priv-6 cosign image signing) in the file itself, and the workflow does not stand between the founder and a deploy — the real path is deploy-api.sh, which the auditor themselves credit as a genuine control (HEAD==origin/main, clean tree, 5 gates + vitest). Calling it 'a control protecting a no-op' overstates it. The durable and correct point is narrower: no committed artifact anywhere answers 'what commit is live?'. That is medium.

title: 8 of 21 MANUAL builders are falsely documented as needing the operator's Mac — one is blocking the deploy right now
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `check-idem-coverage.mjs` files 8 builders under `OPERATOR_DATA` with the justification "the operator, on the Mac that holds the API keys ... this container has neither [keys nor network]". I checked all eight: `grep -cE "await fetch\(|process\.env\.[A-Z_]*KEY"` returns **0** for every one of `build-ingredient-state-record`, `build-eia-energy-backdrop`, `build-crop-condition-backdrop`, `build-noaa-landings`, `build-ers-availability`, `build-ers-meat-chain`, `build-ers-food-dollar`, `build-open-data-catalog`. `build-ingredient-state-record.mjs`'s own docstring says "Inputs (all in-repo)" and "Deterministic (no build clock)". I ran all eight with `--check` here: seven CLEAN, and `build-ingredient-state-record` DRIFT — it is one of the five failures blocking today's deploy. The keys/network caveat is true of the upstream FETCH, not of these renderers.
impact: A gate whose entire purpose is to force honest documentation of manual dependencies carries eight entries with a wrong reason, and the wrong reason is what keeps a pure, deploy-safe builder out of the deploy — turning a 3x/week data refresh into a recurring hand-cleared deploy block on a CC-BY public download.
rec: Move all eight `build-*` calls into `wrangler.jsonc` `build.command` immediately before `check-all.mjs` (they are pure and fast), delete their `MANUAL` entries, and let `staleManual` confirm the registry shrank. Same for the three theme/cuisine builders — or, better, retire those 47 menu-design page-sets outright since they are off-funnel by the company's own CLAUDE.md and are the reason the deploy is red.
note: Numbers reproduced, characterization wrong. `grep -cE 'await fetch\(|process\.env\.[A-Z_]*KEY'` returns 0 for all eight OPERATOR_DATA builders, and build-ingredient-state-record.mjs:11 says 'Inputs (all in-repo)' and :22 'Deterministic (no build clock)'. But the registry is not falsely documented: check-idem-coverage.mjs:64 `drifts` reads 'when its SOURCE JSON is refreshed by a live fetch ... the builder is re-run and committed alongside the data it renders' — an accurate description of a pure renderer over operator-fetched inputs. The `who` field names who triggers the run, not what the script needs. So 'eight entries with a wrong reason' is unfair to the gate. The substantive residual is real and worth the medium: build-ingredient-state-record is pure over in-repo inputs that the Mon/Wed/Fri refresh rewrites, so it belongs in build.command or in the refresh's builder chain, and its absence is blocking the deploy today — a hand-clear that already happened once on 2026-07-31 ('rebuild the ingredient state record, which nothing else does').

title: check-idem-coverage only sees labels containing "(idem)" — 14 drift-gated builders are outside the registry entirely
effort: 4 hours including working the orphan list
evidence: `check-idem-coverage.mjs`'s `idemEntries()` regex is `/\[\s*'([^']*\(idem\)[^']*)'\s*,\s*'([\w.-]+\.mjs)'/`. `check-all.mjs` contains 178 entries invoked with `--check`; only 83 carry an `(idem)` label. I cross-referenced the other 95 against `build.command` and all seven workflows: 14 are BUILDERS with no healer anywhere — `build-conformal-vectors`, `build-recalls-open-data`, `build-qcew-open-data`, `build-marts-open-data`, `build-open-recalls-page`, `build-open-labor-page`, `build-open-demand-page`, `inject-open-cards`, `build-study-dataset`, `build-cost-plate-drift`, `build-cost-index-proxies`, `build-cost-index-methodology`, `inject-event-exposure`, `inject-study-cite`. `check-cost-index-picker.mjs` is worse — it takes no `--check` flag at all, so it is invisible to both the regex and my sweep, and its healer is the one the refresh discards. This is the repo's own documented lesson ("a scanner is only as good as its root list") reappearing in the scanner written to enforce that lesson.
impact: The gate reports "0 unhealed" and is wrong by at least 15. Each of those 15 is a latent red deploy no automation can clear — the precise failure the gate exists to prevent, and the thing that has the site frozen today.
rec: Change `idemEntries()` to collect every `[label, script, '--check']` row whose script matches `^(build|inject|wire|sync|reconcile|migrate)-`, regardless of label, plus every gate whose failure text says "run: node scripts/build-*". Then work the resulting orphan list. Add a `--self-test` case pinning that a non-`(idem)`-labelled builder is still collected.
note: Verified the load-bearing half, did not verify the list. Confirmed: check-cost-index-picker.mjs's usage block (lines 26-27) offers only bare invocation and `--self-test` — it takes no `--check`, so it is invisible to idemEntries()'s regex, and its only healer is the one cost-index-refresh.yml discards (finding 3). That single case is enough to prove the gate reports '0 unhealed' while a builder with no working healer reds the deploy. I did NOT independently confirm the count of 14 orphaned non-(idem) builders or cross-reference each against build.command and all 7 workflows, so treat that number as unverified. Medium is right.

title: The production build installs two dependencies at `@latest` with no lockfile
effort: 15 minutes to pin; 2 hours to add a build lockfile
evidence: `wrangler.jsonc` `build.command` ends with `npm install --no-save --no-fund --no-audit --silent lightningcss@latest && node scripts/minify-css.mjs && node scripts/vendor-pin.mjs && npx -y pagefind@latest --site dist`. rec: Pin both to exact versions (`lightningcss@1.x.y`, `pagefind@1.x.y`) in `build.command` today — a one-line edit. If you later want reproducibility, commit a minimal `package.json` + lockfile for build-time deps only; the "package.json is gitignored by convention" rule was written for contributor tooling, not for the production build path.
note: Reproduced verbatim from wrangler.jsonc build.command, which ends `... && npm install --no-save --no-fund --no-audit --silent lightningcss@latest && node scripts/minify-css.mjs && node scripts/vendor-pin.mjs && npx -y pagefind@latest --site dist`. No package.json and no lockfile in the repo (gitignored by convention per CLAUDE.md). The contrast with deploy-api.sh's pinned `prettier@3.4.2` is real. Medium is the right call for a static site whose build holds no secrets.

title: The flake tracker detects only flapping tests, never persistently failing ones, and its quarantine half was never built
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `.github/workflows/flake-tracker.yml` line 18-21: `TODO(H-qa-8 part 3): the auto-PR step is left as a TODO; this batch ships only the detection + issue-opening half`, repeated at line ~330 in the inline JS. The diff logic (`if (statusToday !== statusPrior) flaps.push(...)`) fires only on a status CHANGE, and `if (!statusPrior) continue` skips anything new — so a test that fails every single night is never reported. Both suites run under `|| true` (lines 78, 84) so the job is green regardless. On the storefront side, board open item 6 lists three inherited reds from PR #536; two of them (a Playwright hub baseline, an lhci accessibility check) come from workflows that are `continue-on-error: true`, so they were never merge-blocking and the "probably flakes" inference in the board is untestable from CI status.
impact: The company believes it has flake detection. What it has is change detection on a nightly job that cannot fail, with no quarantine. A test that rots to permanently-failing is invisible; a test that flaps generates an issue nobody is obliged to close. For a solo operator this is the difference between a signal and a second inbox.
rec: Add one line to the diff: also report any test whose status is `failed` in BOTH runs, labelled `persistently-failing` rather than `flaky-test` — that is 5 lines of JS and turns the nightly into a real regression detector. Leave the quarantine PR unbuilt; it is not worth founder time at this scale. Separately, decide about the three PR #536 reds: reproduce them or close them, but do not carry them as open items against non-blocking workflows.
note: Reproduced. flake-tracker.yml lines 14-20 carry the quarantine TODO ('this batch ships only the detection + issue-opening half'); line 223 is `if (!statusPrior) continue;` and line 224 `if (statusToday !== statusPrior)`, so a test failing on every run is structurally invisible; lines 75 and 80 run pytest and vitest under `|| true`, so the job cannot go red. All four mechanism claims hold.

title: The cost-index refresh reports success when the fetch returns nothing, so a source outage is indistinguishable from a quiet week
effort: 3 hours for the gate; the source triage needs one live run on the operator's machine
