Not declared anywhere in it: the founding-member waitlist (apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts, fed by potentially-profitable/src/worker.js:8949-8966 which forwards email + name + business + the visitor's real `cf-connecting-ip` server-to-server to api.muntin.digital — a cross-service PII transfer the storefront's own privacy.html does not mention either); Square POS sales ingest (routes/integrations/square.ts — a read-only third-party data SOURCE, a different shape from A3's outbound posting); push notifications (routes/push.ts with APNs and VAPID configuration live in wrangler.toml [vars] — device tokens are personal data); accountant handoffs and the weekly accountant digest (routes/accountant-handoffs.ts, scheduled/accountant-digest.ts, cron '0 15 * * 1' — discloses org financial data to a third party's inbox); inventory counts, pars and locations; the community-template pool (cross-org sharing, opt-in). Stripe appears in the sub-processor table (:71) and in no ROPA activity at all. The ROPA's own Maintenance clause requires review 'on every material change to a processing activity' including 'expanding the categories of personal data processed'.
impact: An Art. 30 record's value is completeness — a regulator or an enterprise buyer's security review reads it as the map of the system, and gaps read as either sloppiness or concealment. The waitlist gap is the sharpest: it is the only processing activity with live real-person data today (the storefront collects it now), it crosses a service boundary carrying an IP, and it is documented in neither the ROPA nor the storefront privacy policy.
rec: Add A5 waitlist/prospect data (Controller role, Art. 6(1)(a) or (f), the IP forward, retention per privacy-policy.md:184's '90 days of launch'), A6 POS sales ingest (Square), A7 push notification addressing, A8 accountant handoff disclosure, and fold inventory/counts into A2's data categories. Name Stripe's activity. Add a paragraph on the waitlist to potentially-profitable/privacy.html. Then add a gate: enumerate apps/api/src/routes/*.ts and fail when a route file is not named in ropa.md or in an explicit skip list with a reason — the same 'declare roots, justify omissions' rule the storefront already enforces on its scanners.
note: docs/ropa.md scopes to A1-A4; the uncovered activities the auditor lists all exist as routes (waitlist.ts, integrations/square.ts, push.ts, accountant-handoffs.ts, scheduled/accountant-digest.ts) and src/worker.js:8949-8966 does forward email+name+business+cf-connecting-ip server-to-server via x-muntin-client-ip. Add one the auditor did not reach, which is the sharpest of the set: src/lib/window.js:1086-1126 detectCrisisTier runs a suicide/self-harm/eviction/domestic-violence keyword scan over every Window message, and the resulting crisisTier is persisted on the thread (window.js:379-385). That is an inference about a data subject's mental and physical health — Art. 9 special-category data and 'sensitive data' under MODPA/CPA/CTDPA — generated and stored by a processing activity declared in no record and disclosed in no policy.

title: GPC is declared on the surface that has no trackers and absent from the one that does
effort: 3 hours
evidence: docs/ropa.md:106 uses GPC honoring as part of the Art. 6(1)(f) balancing test that justifies running analytics without a consent banner: 'honours Global Privacy Control (/.well-known/gpc)'. That route exists only at apps/web/app/.well-known/gpc/route.ts — on app.muntin.digital, whose analytics proxy points at an unreachable placeholder — and its own header says 'No behavioural code change lives here; this route only declares support' with a TO-VERIFY-ON-DEPLOY note that has not been executed (lastUpdate 2026-05-21, 77 days). On muntin.digital, /.well-known/ contains only security.txt. `grep -rn 'Sec-GPC'` across both repos returns two comment lines and zero code: nothing anywhere reads the header. handlePlausibleEvent (potentially-profitable/src/worker.js:8700) forwards to plausible.io unconditionally.
impact: The one place a beacon actually leaves to a third party ignores the signal, and the declaration sits where there is nothing to opt out of. Legally this is thin — Muntin sells no data, so GPC-as-opt-out-of-sale has little bite, and the company is under every state-law applicability threshold. But the ROPA leans on it as a stated reason for having no consent banner, which makes it a load-bearing claim in a published compliance record rather than a nice-to-have.
rec: Add a five-line check in handlePlausibleEvent: if `request.headers.get('sec-gpc') === '1'`, return 204 without forwarding. Add /.well-known/gpc.json to the storefront (static file, same JSON shape as the product route). Then the ROPA sentence becomes true and can cite the code line. If you would rather not, delete the GPC clause from ropa.md:106 and re-argue the balancing test on cookielessness alone — which is the stronger argument anyway.
note: Reproduced: `grep -rn 'Sec-GPC'` across both repos returns only two comment lines in apps/web/app/.well-known/gpc/route.ts:7,12; the storefront's /.well-known has only security.txt; handlePlausibleEvent forwards unconditionally. But the legal weight is close to nil — GPC is an opt-out-of-sale/share signal, Muntin sells nothing, and the ROPA's own balancing test at :106 leads with cookielessness and lists GPC as one clause among several. Downgraded to low: this is a five-line honesty tidy-up, not a compliance exposure, and the auditor's own impact paragraph concedes as much before rating it medium.

title: An unqualified WCAG 2.2 AA conformance claim, an empty Known Limitations section, retired-services copy, and one non-blocking axe run on one surface
effort: 4 hours for the statement; 2 days to widen the axe coverage
evidence: potentially-profitable/accessibility.html: 'Conformance target: WCAG 2.2 AA' and 'Where 2.2 introduces new success criteria over 2.1 (focus appearance, dragging movements, target size, accessible authentication), this site meets them too.' Its 'Known Limitations' section names no actual limitation, only a generic third-party-vendor caveat. It also still says 'This commitment applies to our website, all client work we produce, and the services we provide' and carries a 'What We Build for Clients' section — the web-studio services line was retired (potentially-profitable/CLAUDE.md). Last reviewed 2026-05-01, 97 days ago. Automation behind the claim: .github/workflows/window-a11y.yml is the storefront's only a11y job — axe-core scoped to /window/ and /es/window/, path-filtered, `continue-on-error`, with a header noting 'Promote to required-check ... once three consecutive PRs land green' (not done). That is 2 of 1,368 pages, non-blocking. On the product side, docs/accessibility.md claims 'axe-core runs in CI on every push'; .github/workflows/e2e-informational.yml triggers on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` (not push), runs `continue-on-error: true`, and emits a `::warning::` — it is named 'informational' and behaves that way.
impact: For a US commercial website, an unqualified public conformance assertion is the exposure, not the underlying defects: ADA Title III demand letters routinely quote the site's own accessibility statement back at it, and a statement claiming full 2.2 AA conformance with zero listed limitations and no audit is the worst posture — worse than an honest 'partially conformant, here is our list'. The retired-services paragraphs additionally advertise a business line that no longer exists.
rec: Rewrite accessibility.html this week to the honest shape the product's own docs/accessibility.md already models: state 'partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 AA', delete the 'meets them too' sentence, delete the client-services sections, and populate Known Limitations with what is actually untested (no formal third-party audit; automated coverage limited to /window/; no screen-reader pass on the 1,300+ generated Cost-Index pages; no voice-control or Windows high-contrast testing). Keep the feedback commitment and the 2-business-day response — that part is genuinely good. Separately, either flip window-a11y.yml to blocking and widen its path filter, or say in the statement that a11y checking is advisory today. Also fix docs/accessibility.md's 'on every push' to match the workflow's real triggers.
note: Reproduced every element: accessibility.html carries 'Conformance target: WCAG 2.2 AA' and 'we meet them too'; the Known Limitations section at :437-439 names only a generic third-party caveat; 'client work we produce, and the services we provide' plus a 'What We Build for Clients' section survive from the retired services line; Last reviewed 2026-05-01 (97 days). .github/workflows/window-a11y.yml:56 continue-on-error: true with path filters, and it is the only a11y job among 7 storefront workflows. Adding evidence the auditor missed: I ran check-positioning-drift.mjs — it scans 1066 indexed pages and returns 0 violations, so the gate written to catch retired-services copy walks straight past the page that still advertises the retired services line. The gate is threshold-shaped, not grounded.

title: The surface built to prove the privacy promises renders no proof and cannot show that it failed
effort: 4 hours for (a); 1 hour for (b)
evidence: runbooks/promises-last-verified.md states the design contract: 'When a promise's gate runs clean in CI, the deploy pipeline updates the timestamp. When a gate fails, the timestamp stops updating — the page truthfully shows the stale date. This means a regression in a privacy guarantee produces a visibly-stale page, not a quietly-broken contract.' The implementation: apps/web/app/(marketing)/promises/page.tsx:163-165 `const LAST_VERIFIED: Record<string, string> = { // Format: <anchor>: "YYYY-MM-DD" };` — empty. :320 `const verifiedDate = p.anchor && LAST_VERIFIED[p.anchor];` and the render is conditional, so all 20 promise entries in promises-data.ts display with no date at all and no error. No workflow writes the constant; grepping .github/workflows for LAST_VERIFIED returns nothing.
impact: This is the exact failure mode the 2026-07-30 audit named — the page has the shape of a verification surface with no grounding behind it. The company's differentiation against MarginEdge and Restaurant365 is 'you can check us', and the page built to make that checkable ships with the checkable part blank, degrading silently rather than loudly. It is also a missed early-warning system: had it worked, the retention-reaper and Cost-Index-snapshot lapses would both have surfaced as stale dates on a public page.
rec: Either (a) populate LAST_VERIFIED by hand today with the dates the gates last ran green and add a CI step that rewrites it from the workflow run timestamp — a 15-line node script in the prebuild, same pattern as build-legal-content.mjs; or (b) if per-promise timestamps are more machinery than a one-person company can sustain, delete the LAST_VERIFIED plumbing and the runbook's claim, and instead link each promise to its gate file so a reader can check the gate themselves. Do not leave the empty object: it is a promise about promises that is itself unkept.
note: Reproduced: apps/web/app/(marketing)/promises/page.tsx:163-165 LAST_VERIFIED is an empty Record with only a format comment, and the file's own docstring at :160-162 says it is a "'not yet captured' fallback until the CI/deploy pipeline writes real ISO timestamps via a codemod after each green CI run" — a pipeline step that grep shows does not exist in any workflow. The render is conditional so 20 promises display with no date and no error. Medium is right.

title: The reaper being off does not just falsify a sentence — plaintext invoice PDFs are retained indefinitely, and the only two backstops are also unbuilt
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/ingest.ts:884-898 writes the uploaded file to R2 as PLAINTEXT via r2PutForOrg. Encryption is post-hoc and OPT-IN: apps/api/src/lib/finish-encrypt.ts:96-101 returns 'skip_no_identity_key' when the owner has no enrolled X25519 key, with the comment 'No enrolled identity key => owner is NOT opted in to E2EE => the legacy 24h delete is the correct, intended behaviour.' That 'legacy 24h delete' is apps/api/src/scheduled/retention-reaper.ts, which STATUS-v6.md:1099-1100 records as double-locked off. The bucket-level backstop was never applied either: runbooks/r2-lifecycle.md's own status table reads 'Last applied: Not yet executed', and :20-26 explains there is no object-expiry lifecycle rule because 'reaper wins on flexibility'. So for any non-enrolled uploader there is no deleter at all — not at 24 hours, not ever.
impact: The auditor treated the reaper as a documentation problem ('the policy says 24 hours and it doesn't'). The grounded version is worse: unencrypted restaurant invoice PDFs — vendor names, prices, addresses, sometimes signatures — accumulate in R2 with no expiry, and the code that decided not to encrypt them did so on the explicit assumption that a disabled process would delete them. Two independent safety properties (deletion AND the plaintext window) hang off one flag nobody has armed, plus a bucket policy whose runbook says it has never been run. This also means the R2 object count is the real measure of exposure, which no one has looked at.
rec: Before touching any prose: run `aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration` per runbooks/r2-lifecycle.md to find out whether ANY expiry exists, and list the bucket to count surviving plaintext objects. Then either arm the reaper (stage 1 dry-run, then RETENTION_REAPER_ENABLED=true) or apply a bucket-wide lifecycle expiry as the fail-safe floor — a bucket rule is coarser than per-document retention_until but it is unconditional, which is the property that matters when the conditional path is off. Only then correct privacy-policy.md:164/:296/:559/:591.

title: Every Window message is scanned for suicide and crisis keywords, the verdict is stored, and an 80-character excerpt is SMS'd to a personal phone through a vendor named in no policy
evidence: src/lib/window.js:1086-1126 detectCrisisTier() keyword-matches every message body against a tier-1 list ('kill myself', 'suicide', 'suicidio', 'quitarme la vida', …) and a tier-2 list ('eviction', 'bankruptcy', 'domestic violence', 'violencia doméstica', …). The verdict is persisted on the thread and rendered in the admin queue (window.js:379-385). src/worker.js:6747 and :6892 then call sendCrisisSms(env, label, sanitized) on tier-1, and src/lib/sms.js:105-109 buildCrisisSmsBody puts the first 80 characters of the visitor's message into an SMS delivered by api.twilio.com (sms.js:66). It is live-capable on both the signed-in and the anonymous path (wrangler.jsonc:226/:235 both "true"); the only thing holding it back is whether four Twilio secrets are set, which is not visible from the repo. 'Twilio' appears in zero legal, privacy or vendor page in either repo. privacy.html:427 says of the Window: 'No third-party chat or scheduler sees your message.'
impact: This is the single most sensitive processing either company performs — an automated inference about a person's suicidality, housing loss, bankruptcy or domestic-abuse situation, attached to a device-persistent identifier (md_anon_thread_id) for anonymous senders who believed they were writing an unauthenticated note. It is special-category data under GDPR Art. 9 and 'sensitive data' under MODPA (Muntin's home-state law, effective 2026-10-01, which requires consent for sensitive-data processing and bans its sale outright), CPA and CTDPA — and unlike the CCPA analysis, sensitive-data duties in several of those regimes are not purely threshold-gated. None of it appears in the ROPA, the DPIA, privacy.html, cookies.html, or the sub-processor register, and the vendor-disclosure sentence that does exist affirmatively denies it.
rec: Decide first whether the crisis path stays. If it does: add Twilio to privacy.html's vendor list with exactly what it receives (an 80-char excerpt of your message plus an 8-char pseudonymous label); add a Window paragraph disclosing that message bodies are keyword-scanned for crisis signals, that the result is stored, and why; delete or qualify 'No third-party chat or scheduler sees your message'; add a ROPA activity and a screening DPIA note (Art. 9 processing is the one case where the A4-style 'not required' shortcut does not apply); and put a TTL on crisisTier. If it does not: delete detectCrisisTier and sms.js. What is not tenable is a suicide-keyword classifier that no published document admits exists.

title: The marketing-claims registry — the document that governs what may be said — orders present-tense E2EE copy that the launch tracker says was retracted as false
evidence: docs/marketing-claims.md, ✅ Verified table, last row: 'Your scan is locked; a key only you hold / end-to-end encrypted — **Founder-confirmed live + verified 2026-06-19.** … Keep the present-tense E2EE copy ("a key only you hold") everywhere — do not soften it.' STATUS-v6.md:40-45 says the opposite: 'NOT STARTED: … end-to-end encryption of scanned documents — DEK/UMK uncalled, R2 stores plaintext, recovery-crypto parked off-tree', and :51-54 lists as launch-blocker #1 'Privacy/legal copy claimed E2EE the code does not implement. Corrected across web + docs/privacy-policy.md + docs/dpa.md … on 2026-05-17.' STATUS-v6.md:840 marks sprint 1A.10's E2EE framing '⚠️ superseded — FALSE and retracted'. The code sits between the two and matches neither: finish-encrypt.ts:109-113 has the SERVER mint the DEK and wrap it to the user's public key, only for owners who enrolled an identity key, only after extraction. apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3749 ships the unqualified sentence today: 'Your files are locked with a key only you hold. We keep the locked bytes, never the key.'
impact: The auditor filed the deployed-copy question under 'unknowns' and moved on. It is not an unknown — it is two committed governance documents giving opposite instructions about the company's most load-bearing privacy claim, with the more recent one (2026-06-19) instructing writers not to soften it. For an unenrolled operator the sentence in copy.ts is simply false: the server minted the key, held it in memory, and wrote plaintext to R2 first. This is the same class of failure as the retention reaper, one layer up: the process that is supposed to prevent false claims is itself asserting one.
rec: Reconcile in marketing-claims.md today, since it is the file every future copy change consults. The honest row is scoped, not deleted: 'For an operator who has enrolled a recovery phrase, the retained document image is encrypted to a key only they hold; before enrolment, and for the extracted ledger, the server can read it.' Then qualify copy.ts:3749 + copy.es.ts to the enrolled case, and add the claim to check-claims.mjs so the unscoped form cannot come back. Note that check-verboten-phrases.mjs and check-claims.mjs both run green today — neither gate reads marketing-claims.md's verdict column, so the registry can be wrong forever without CI noticing.

title: No commercial email from either repo carries a valid physical postal address — a black-letter CAN-SPAM defect on a path that is sending today
evidence: src/lib/templates.js:346-376 htmlShell() is the single wrapper for every storefront email. Its footer at :369 is 'Muntin Digital · Silver Spring, MD · muntin.digital' — a city and state, no street address and no PO box. The ES wrapper repeats it (src/lib/templates.es.js:56, :184, :344, :445, :566). This footer wraps the Cost Index broadcast (templates.js:183-235, sent by handleCostIndexBroadcast on the monthly dispatch), the lifecycle drip (lifecycleWelcomeEmail / lifecycleSavedNoReturnEmail / lifecycleMonthlyDigestEmail), and the subscriber confirmations. Unsubscribe handling is genuinely good — a stable token, /sub/unsubscribe, a hard cap of 4 per quarter — which is what makes the omission conspicuous.
impact: 15 U.S.C. §7704(a)(5) and 16 CFR §316 require every commercial email to include the sender's valid physical postal address; FTC guidance is explicit that this means a street address, a registered PO box, or a registered private mailbox. A city and state is not one. Penalties are per-message. This is the clearest black-letter US statutory violation in either repository, it applies to a code path that actually sends mail today (unlike every GDPR/CCPA item in the report, all of which are threshold-gated to near-zero), and the auditor — who devoted a paragraph to Global Privacy Control, which has no bite here — did not look at an email template. A home-address-averse one-person company also has a real reason not to have fixed it, which is exactly why it needs a decision rather than a silent gap.
rec: Get a registered PMB or PO box in Silver Spring (a CMRA box satisfies the statute and keeps the home address private), then add it to htmlShell's footer in templates.js and templates.es.js — one line, both files. Do the same audit on apps/email-worker before the product sends its first marketing message. Consider a check-*.mjs that greps the email templates for a street-address pattern; it is the cheapest possible shape gate and here the shape genuinely is the requirement.

title: The customer-facing privacy posture sheet is a hardcoded array that cannot track the flags it claims to reflect
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/posture.ts:26-30 states 'the docs/sub-processors.md row set is the source of truth, and this route mirrors the active rows so the UI does not have to fetch the markdown', then hardcodes the vendor list. apps/api/src/routes/data-map.ts:43-48 says the same and hardcodes its own copy at :109-139 (AWS, Cloudflare, Fly.io, Neon, Stripe, Resend — six rows), with the comment 'Intuit + Xero stay omitted while the integration env flags are off'. But nothing reads a flag: the array is a literal. Square is enabled in apps/api/wrangler.toml:139 and appears in neither array. So there are three registers — the markdown (11 rows), posture.ts, data-map.ts — and scripts/check-subprocessor-freshness.mjs reads only the first (I ran it: '94 IaC files, 14 vendors named, 6 active rows').
impact: The auditor treated the Square/QBO/Xero drift as documentation hygiene. It is worse: the drift is baked into the two surfaces a customer actually reads inside the product, and those surfaces are the ones docs/dpa.md §6 makes contractually load-bearing. A comment that says 'X stays omitted while the flag is off' is a promise about a conditional that the code does not evaluate — the exact 'shape without grounding' pattern the 2026-07-30 audit named. The moment a flag flips, three registers disagree and only one of them will be noticed.
rec: Make one of the three the actual source and derive the others. Cheapest honest version: keep docs/sub-processors.md canonical, generate a sub-processors.generated.ts at build time (the build-legal-content.mjs pattern already exists in this repo and solves the identical Worker-filesystem problem), and have posture.ts and data-map.ts import it. Then extend check-subprocessor-freshness.mjs to parse INTEGRATIONS_*_ENABLED out of wrangler.toml and fail when a row's stated status contradicts the deployed flag — the gate already reads the IaC, so this is the ~30 lines the auditor described, pointed at the right target.

title: The storefront ships 129 check-*.mjs gates and not one of them touches privacy, cookies, vendors or legal text — while the ES mirrors of the false statements go unchecked too
evidence: `ls scripts/check-*.mjs | wc -l` = 129 in potentially-profitable; filtering that list for privacy|cookie|vendor|consent|legal|gdpr returns only vendor-pin.mjs and vendor-tokens.mjs, both npm-dependency gates. There is no gate tying cookies.html's cookie table to the Set-Cookie names in src/worker.js (which is how md_anon_thread_id survived), none tying privacy.html's vendor list to the fetch hostnames in src/worker.js (which is how Google survived), and none checking the review dates — privacy.html says 'Last reviewed 2026-05-02' (96 days) and accessibility.html 2026-05-01 (97 days) with no freshness gate anywhere. The ES mirrors carry the same defects untested: es/privacy.html repeats the four-vendor list, and on the product side docs/es/privacy-policy.md:503 repeats the 24-hour assertion while :173 carries the hedge — and the ES policy is still Versión 0.1 against the EN's Version 0.2 (docs/privacy-policy.md:9 vs docs/es/privacy-policy.md:11), so a Spanish reader is served a differently-versioned legal document at the same route.
impact: The auditor named this structural cause in the posture paragraph but never verified the counts or the ES half, and never noticed the version skew between the EN and ES policies that are both baked into LEGAL_DOCS and both served. For a company whose CLAUDE.md documents having learned the 'declare your roots' lesson three separate times in one day, the compliance surface is the one place where the root list was never declared at all — and it is a bilingual surface, so every uncaught defect is caught twice or not at all.
rec: Write two cheap storefront gates in the same commit as the copy fixes, because a corrected sentence with no gate regresses the next time the Worker grows a route: (1) check-cookie-disclosure.mjs — regex every Set-Cookie name out of src/**.js and fail when one is absent from cookies.html and es/cookies.html; (2) check-vendor-disclosure.mjs — extract every external fetch() hostname from src/**.js and fail when its vendor is absent from privacy.html's Vendors list, with an explicit skip list where each entry says why. Add a third that fails when privacy/cookies/accessibility EN and ES disagree on their review date or version stamp. Each is under 60 lines and each would have caught a live finding in this report.

title: Tacombi's and its vendors' real invoice data is committed to the product repo, under an MIT grant, with no gate watching
effort: 1 day to redact and gate; needs counsel for the employment question
evidence: `services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/fresco_lineitems.json:390` contains the literal string "TacombiBethesda 4749 Bethesda Ave, Bethesda, MD 20814" (four occurrences), plus real invoice numbers 121397 and 396552, dates 8/7/2024 and 01/15/2024, "Net 45" terms, a 9/21/2024 due date, and negotiated line prices ("Tortilla 5' Mi Famila Cs | 48.00 | 336.00"; "AvocadoHass 48cnt Ripe"). `git ls-files` confirms all 7 fixtures are tracked. `chefs_warehouse_stacked_header.json` carries real Chefs' Warehouse item numbers and unit prices (10743422FRO, 96.94; 10720394FRO, 84.31); `baldor_collapse.json` and `cintas_{fail_total,pricezero_2}.json` carry Cintas SKUs and rates. Two siblings in the same directory — `fresco_merged_header.json` and `ihalper_metadata_header.json` — ARE shape-redacted to "Xxxxxx Xxxxxxxx / ####", proving the redaction practice exists and was applied to some files and not others. Repo root `LICENSE:1-8` is MIT: "Copyright (c) 2026 Muntin Digital LLC ... to deal in the Software without restriction, including ... publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or sell." Separately, 20+ shipped CLIs document the employer's books as their canonical invocation (`services/extract/cli/vendor_flywheel.py:65`, `corpus_seed.py:28`, `total_gap.py:25`, and 17 more: `--buyer "Tacombi Bethesda" --buyer "Tacombi"`), and the engine's entire measurement basis is that corpus (`services/extract/VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:14` "a 919-doc real-corpus run"; `services/extract/README.md:138` "the 782-doc corpus"; `docs/plans/first-try-reliability-roadmap.md:126,240` "the single-operator Tacombi corpus"). `ls scripts/ | grep -i pii` returns only `check-funnel-no-pii.mjs`, which scans the funnel — nothing scans `tests/golden/real_fixtures/`.
impact: This is the exposure that can end the venture and the day job in one move. The fixtures are Tacombi's confidential commercial records and its distributors' pricing — the exact categories of information restaurant employment agreements and distributor invoice legends protect. Whether Don's Tacombi agreement contains an IP-assignment or confidentiality clause is unknowable from here, but Maryland's employee-invention statute (Lab. & Empl. §3-716) only shields inventions developed WITHOUT the employer's trade-secret information, so a product tuned on the employer's own invoice corpus is arguably outside the shield rather than inside it. Layer on the MIT grant, which purports to give the world the right to publish and sell that content, and any future contractor, acquirer, or diligence reviewer receives it with a license attached. Nothing about this is theoretical: the data is on disk, tracked, and licensed away.
rec: Tomorrow morning, in this order. (1) Run the same shape-redaction already used in `fresco_merged_header.json` across `fresco_lineitems.json`, `chefs_warehouse_stacked_header.json`, `baldor_collapse.json` and both `cintas_*.json` — the golden tests key on layout geometry, not values, so redaction should not change behavior. (2) Purge the pre-redaction blobs from git history (`git-filter-repo`) and force-push; a tracked blob survives a delete commit. (3) Write `scripts/check-fixture-redaction.mjs` that fails CI on any real buyer name, street address, or invoice number under `services/extract/tests/` — the missing gate. (4) Replace root `LICENSE` per the separate finding. (5) Take Don's Tacombi employment agreement, offer letter, and handbook to counsel with these file paths and ask three specific questions: does the agreement assign inventions relating to the employer's business; does it define his access to vendor invoices as confidential information; and does building on that corpus create a duty-of-loyalty or trade-secret claim independent of the contract. Do not attempt to answer these yourself.
note: Reproduced: `services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/fresco_lineitems.json:390` carries "TacombiBethesda 4749 Bethesda Ave, Bethesda, MD 20814" (4 occurrences); `git ls-files` shows all 7 fixtures tracked; root `LICENSE:1-8` is unmodified MIT. `services/extract/VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:14,34` independently confirms the measurement basis is that corpus ("919-doc real-corpus run"; i_halper 99 invoices, chefs_warehouse 248, fresco 91). BUT the auditor's central supporting claim is WRONG and its remediation would not work: the two "properly shape-redacted" siblings are only cosmetically masked. I parsed both — `fresco_merged_header.json` masks the `text` field but its `orig` fields still read "TacombiBethesda", "4749 Bethesda Ave,", "Bethesda, MD 20814", "Phone#929-222-5392", "Net 45", "$839.50"; `ihalper_metadata_header.json` `orig` holds "TACOMBI BETHESDA 4749 BETHESDAAVENUE BETHESDA,MD 20814" (twice), "CSFP-TACOMBI-L788", "NET 60" and 14 line-level dollar amounts. Worse, those two are the ONLY fixtures that also leak the source PDF filename (`name`/`origin.filename` = "FRESCO10.10.22.pdf", "Bethesda Invoice 11.06.23.pdf") — the five "unredacted" ones are anonymized to `tmp*.bin`. So the redaction practice does not exist as described; it was applied to one field and missed the field that carries the same string. Recommendation step (1) as written would leave every PII value on disk.

title: The legal entity behind every contract, license and GDPR record is unconfirmed — and two published documents place it in different states
effort: 2 hours to verify; 1 week if formation is needed
evidence: `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:353-356` — the founder's own checklist, box UNCHECKED: "[ ] Entity facts: legal entity name, type, state of formation, registered agent, EIN; confirmation an entity EXISTS (if the product is currently operated as a sole proprietorship, counsel should advise on entity formation FIRST — it gates everything)." Every one of the 8 boxes in that §A7 checklist is unchecked. Meanwhile four documents assert the entity as fact: `potentially-profitable/terms.html:423` — "Muntin Digital™ is a Maryland LLC operated by Don Goldstein ... registered in Silver Spring, MD; the LLC's registered agent is on file with the Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation"; `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/tos.md:134-137` — "the laws of the United States and the State of Delaware (Muntin Digital LLC's home state) ... Disputes are resolved in the state or federal courts located in Delaware" (mirrored in `docs/es/tos.md:124-126`); `LICENSE:3` — "Copyright (c) 2026 Muntin Digital LLC"; `docs/ropa.md:4` — "Article 30 GDPR record kept by Muntin Digital LLC as a Processor." `runbooks/launch-plan-2026-11-13.md:203` scheduled "Counsel engaged day 1" for Weeks 1–2 (June); `grep -rn -i "counsel engaged|retained counsel|law firm|reviewed by counsel"` across `docs/` and `runbooks/` returns only that plan line and the kickoff brief's own framing.
impact: If the LLC does not exist, or exists only in Maryland, then terms.html §1's registered-agent sentence is a false statement of fact inside a consumer-facing contract, the Delaware governing-law and forum clause is unenforceable and points customers at the wrong courthouse, the GDPR Art. 30 record names a non-existent processor, the MIT copyright line vests in the wrong party, and — the part that actually matters for a solo founder — every liability limitation in both documents runs against Don personally with no veil whatsoever. The company is about to invite operators to hand over their vendor pricing under a contract whose counterparty may not be a legal person.
rec: Pull the Maryland SDAT business entity search and the Delaware Division of Corporations search for "Muntin Digital" this week; both are free and take minutes. If an LLC exists in Maryland only, change `docs/tos.md:134-137` and `docs/es/tos.md:124-126` to Maryland law and Maryland forum so both repos agree — do not keep a Delaware clause for a Maryland entity. If nothing exists, form it before any further public contract text ships, then reconcile all four documents to the formed entity's exact registered name and state. Either way, tick or strike `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:353` — an unchecked box on the gating question is the loudest signal in either repo.
note: Reproduced verbatim: `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:353-356` unchecked (all 8 boxes in §A7 unchecked); `terms.html:423` "Muntin Digital™ is a Maryland LLC ... registered agent is on file with the Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation"; `docs/tos.md:134-137` "the laws of the United States and the State of Delaware (Muntin Digital LLC's home state) ... Disputes are resolved in ... Delaware"; `LICENSE:3`; `docs/ropa.md:4`. Severity corrected down from critical: no customer has signed anything, billing fails open, `pricing-constants.ts` marks the only posted price non-billable, and ADR-020 defers launch to 2027 — the contradiction is live text but not yet a live contract. Also note the two documents are not merely inconsistent about state, they are inconsistent about the ENTITY TYPE'S existence while `terms.html:475` and `docs/tos.md:134` pick opposite forums, so whichever is wrong is wrong in a document the other repo publishes.

title: The root MIT LICENSE open-sources the entire commercial product, and the ToS points customers straight at it
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `LICENSE` at the monorepo root is unmodified MIT covering the whole tree — `apps/api` (the Worker API), `apps/web` (the operator app), `services/extract` (the extraction engine that is the product's moat), `packages/*`, and the fixtures from finding #1. There is no scope carve-out and no second license file (`ls LICENSE*` returns one file). `README.md:115` restates it: "Code: [MIT](./LICENSE)." `CONTRIBUTING.md:130-132` restates it again. This directly contradicts `docs/tos.md:120-123` §8: "Parts of the system are open source under the MIT license, including docling (IBM Research) and tools/pii-scrubber ... **The Muntin Ledger SaaS orchestration layer is not open source.**" And `docs/tos.md:52-53` §3 tells the customer their prohibition on reselling applies "except as the open-source license terms permit (see Section 8)" — so the contract itself routes a reader to the license file to learn what they may resell.
impact: MIT is an irrevocable grant to anyone who lawfully received a copy. The ToS asserts a proprietary orchestration layer that the LICENSE gives away, and then invites the customer to check. A contractor, a future employee, an acquirer's diligence team, or anyone who ever gets repo access can copy, rebrand and sell the product — including the fixtures containing his employer's invoices. Even if the GitHub repo is private today (`apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:62` says "the source repo is private"), this is the kind of unresolved rights question that stalls or reprices an acquisition, and it is currently the ONLY written statement of what customers may do with the code.
rec: Replace root `LICENSE` with a proprietary "All rights reserved" notice this week, and place a separate `LICENSE` (MIT) inside `tools/pii-scrubber/` only — the one component ToS §8 actually intends to open-source. Update `README.md:113-115` and `CONTRIBUTING.md:130-132` to match, and add the same carve-out language to `docs/tos.md` §8 so contract and repo say one thing. Note for counsel: past copies distributed under the current LICENSE cannot be clawed back, so ask whether any third party has ever had repo access.
note: The root-scope problem is real: `LICENSE` is unmodified MIT with no carve-out and `README.md:115` + `CONTRIBUTING.md:130-132` restate it against `docs/tos.md:120-125` §8. But two load-bearing pieces of evidence are false. `ls LICENSE*` at root returning one file is not the same as "there is no second license file" — `find . -name 'LICENSE*'` returns `./LICENSE` AND `./tools/pii-scrubber/LICENSE`, which is exactly the component ToS §8 names. So recommendation step 2 ("place a separate LICENSE (MIT) inside tools/pii-scrubber/ only") is already done and the auditor did not check. Severity corrected to high: the grant is latent (private repo per `apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:62`), so this is a diligence/contradiction defect, not a live giveaway.

title: A perpetual price-lock is publicly offered on 51+ surfaces in two languages, with no terms page and no ability to bill it
effort: 1 day for the page; counsel review before GA
evidence: The offer: "Founding rate — three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as you stay" (`apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3161-3162`), and on the storefront `ledger/index.html:652,656` plus its JSON-LD `Offer` description at `ledger/index.html:72`. `data/sourced-claims.json` claim `ledger_founding_offer_2026` lists a `used_in` array of **51 surfaces** across EN and ES. The terms that would qualify it do not exist: `runbooks/launch-plan-2026-11-13.md:35-37` — "STILL TODO from this: the Stripe founding-rate price ID + the `/legal/founding-member-terms` page (counsel to draft the 'locked until cancellation, non-transferable' terms)." `find apps/web/app -ipath "*founding*"` returns nothing; `grep -rn "non-transferable"` across the whole repo returns exactly one hit — that runbook line. And it cannot be charged: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:66-70` declares `founding: { cents: 1900, basis: "per_location", billable: false }` with the dated reason "no $19 SKU, no per-location quantity, and no trial exist in the billing engine."
impact: "For as long as you stay" with no written qualification is a perpetual, unconditional pricing commitment to every operator who signs up — the exact language counsel was supposed to bound with "locked until cancellation, non-transferable" and never did. A solo, pre-revenue founder is offering an unbounded-duration price to an unbounded number of accounts, in Spanish as well as English (which draws extra state UDAP scrutiny), while ADR-020 has moved launch to 2027 with no date, so the founding list will be waiting far longer than anyone was told. The company can also literally not honor it: there is no $19 SKU, no per-location quantity, and no three-month trial, so the first person who tries to pay $19 for two locations is a broken promise plus a support incident.
rec: Ship `/legal/founding-member-terms` before the next signup — it does not need counsel to say the four things that matter: (1) the rate applies to the account that claimed it and is non-transferable on sale or assignment of the business; (2) it is per location, priced on locations active at claim time; (3) it survives continuous subscription and ends on cancellation, non-reinstatable; (4) taxes and any statutory increase are excluded. Link it from every surface listing the offer and add the URL to the `ledger_founding_offer_2026` claim record. Separately, either build the $19 per-location SKU or add one qualifying sentence — "founding pricing opens when Muntin Ledger begins billing" — so the posted price is not represented as currently available.
note: Reproduced: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3161-3162` verbatim, still RENDERED at `apps/web/app/page.tsx:547` (I traced the caller — it survived commit c191888 which retired the launch date but left the perpetual-lock sentence); `ledger/index.html:652,656` and the JSON-LD `Offer` at `:72`; `pricing-constants.ts:66-70` `billable: false`. `find apps/web/app -ipath '*founding*'` returns nothing and the only `non-transferable` hit in the repo is `runbooks/launch-plan-2026-11-13.md:36`. One correction: the `ledger_founding_offer_2026` claim's `used_in` array has 48 entries, not 51 — I counted it. Immateriality noted, but it is the kind of number that should be counted before it is published.

title: Comparative claims about named competitors are uncited, 77 days unverified, and the drift gate is structurally incapable of catching drift
effort: 2 hours to pull the claim; 2 days for a real baseline
evidence: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/vs/marginedge/page.tsx:81-82` publishes, about a named competitor: "Sales-quoted. Public reviews report several hundred per location per month" — no citation on the page, no source, no link, mirrored in Spanish at line ~137. The page carries `lastFactCheckedISO: "2026-05-21"` (line 56) = **77 days** stale as of today, as do all 10 `lastFactCheckedISO` values across the five `/vs/*` pages. title: The live Terms and Privacy Policy are published with a "Draft, awaiting counsel review" banner, and the Privacy Policy names a superseding URL that does not exist

title: The site's only binding public terms govern a business that no longer exists, and contradict the open-data licenses the company actually grants
effort: 2 days
evidence: `potentially-profitable/terms.html` (last reviewed 2026-06-12, 55 days) is still the web-studio's contract. §5 (lines ~449-455) prices "Full builds (Essentials $2,500–$4,000, Full Service $5,000–$9,000, Group $8,000–$15,000+)", the "$499 audit", the "$1,500 menu drop-in", "$99/mo Light" and "$225/mo full" Care Plans, and sets "1.5%/mo or the Maryland statutory maximum" late interest. §6 governs client deliverable ownership and portfolio display rights. Nothing in 12 sections addresses the Cost Index, the 23 open datasets, or the data company Muntin now is. §4 instead blankets all content as CC BY-NC 4.0 — "you ... don't use the work for commercial purposes without my written permission" — while `open/index.html:671` publicly grants the opposite: "the index numbers are public domain (CC0); the compiled datasets (events, yields) are CC-BY — use them, credit 'Muntin Digital'", backed by CC0 `license` fields inside `cost-index/index.json`, `week-*.json`, `sources.json` and 4 more, plus `Link: rel="license"` headers in `_headers:144,150`. §2 also routes the paid product's terms to `https://ledger.muntin.digital/legal/terms`, a host no Worker route serves (`apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:28` binds only `app.muntin.digital/*`), though 405 storefront pages link to that hostname so a DNS alias may exist — I cannot resolve it from here.
impact: Two concrete harms. First, the terms page is the document a prospective operator, a journalist, or an acquirer reads to understand what this company is, and it describes a retired web studio — the same positioning-drift problem `check-positioning-drift.mjs` was written to catch, in the one page that is legally operative and not covered by it. Second, the NC clause and the CC0 grant contradict each other for exactly the audience the data company is courting: a researcher or a commercial reuser gets "non-commercial only" from Terms and "public domain, use it" from `/open/`. CC0 is irrevocable, so the NC clause reads as an attempted clawback of a grant already made — the worst possible posture for a company whose strategy is being the citable open source of restaurant cost data.
rec: Rewrite `terms.html` this week around three surfaces that actually exist: the free site and tools, the published open data, and a pointer to the Ledger's own terms. Move §5 and §6 into a dated "engagements signed before 2026-06-12" appendix. Add an explicit §4 carve-out: "Datasets published at /open/ and /cost-index/ are licensed per the `license` field inside each file and the notice on /open/ — CC0 for US-government recomputes, CC BY 4.0 for Muntin compilations. The CC BY-NC term in this section does not apply to them." Verify `ledger.muntin.digital` resolves; if it does not, repoint §2 and the 405 pages to `app.muntin.digital`.
note: Severity and framing are both inflated. `terms.html` §5 opens "**Retired 2026-06-12.** Muntin Digital no longer takes website-build, audit, menu drop-in, or care-plan engagements. This section stays as the record governing engagements signed before that date; nothing here is an offer." — which IS the auditor's own recommendation ("Move §5 and §6 into a dated 'engagements signed before 2026-06-12' appendix"), already shipped. §2 likewise labels paid engagements "(retired 2026-06-12 — not offered to new clients)" and routes the paid product to its own terms. So "governs a business that no longer exists" is refuted; the prices are a dated historical record, a documented decision. The CC0-clawback framing is also overstated: §4 scopes CC BY-NC to "articles, research notes, glossary terms, checklists, and topic essays" — prose, not datasets — so it does not on its face reach the CC0 files, whose `license` fields and `_headers:144,150` `Link: rel="license"` I verified independently. What survives is real but smaller: 12 sections and none of them names the Cost Index or the 23 published datasets, so a commercial reuser has to infer the carve-out. Medium.

title: The landing page claims shipped templates for five named distributors that do not exist in the codebase, and the shipped disclaimer is weaker than the one the fair-use analysis relies on
effort: 3 hours
evidence: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:4219-4220` renders under the SYSCO · US FOODS · PFG · CHEFS' WAREHOUSE · RESTAURANT DEPOT strip on the landing page (`apps/web/app/page.tsx:563`): "**We ship templates for these vendors out of the box.** Any other vendor learns after three confirms." The only seed artifact in the tree is `services/extract/fixtures/community_seed.example.json`, whose own `_comment` says: "Example shape only ... the EXAMPLE_* placeholders below will be rejected/ignored until replaced" — its single `sysco` entry has `"layout_hash": "EXAMPLE_replace_with_real_layout_hash"` and four `EXAMPLE_replace_with_real_fpv2` rules. `find services/extract -path "*template*" -name "*.json"` returns that one file. An operator arriving because "they ship a Sysco template" experiences the first upload as a cold start. On the trademark side, the fair-use memo is now a legal analysis of a page that no longer exists: "None of them work for us" does not say "not an endorsement" and can even be misread as a statement about employment. Every vendor's layout learns after three confirms" — or seed real templates for the five and replace the placeholder file. Add the resulting claim as a row in `docs/marketing-claims.md` with its backing code path. note: Confirmed and materially understated. `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:4220` "We ship templates for these vendors out of the box" is real, and no extraction templates ship — `find services/extract -iname '*template*' -name '*.json'` returns only `fixtures/community_seed.example.json` whose sole `sysco` entry is `"layout_hash": "EXAMPLE_replace_with_real_layout_hash"` + four `EXAMPLE_replace_with_real_fpv2` rules; `seed.py` and `infra/postgres/seed/vendor_catalog.sql` are the identity CATALOG, a different artifact per `VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md`. But the auditor read the strip off the legal memo instead of the code. `apps/web/lib/distributors.ts` ships TEN wordmarks — SYSCO, US FOODS, PFG, REINHART, GORDON FOOD SERVICE, BEN E. KEITH, CHEFS' WAREHOUSE, FRESHPOINT, RESTAURANT DEPOT, COSTCO BUSINESS — expanded from five on 2026-05-25 with the in-file justification "The template library has shipped with day-one support for a much wider set since the engine refresh," which the code does not support. `runbooks/legal/distributor-logo-use.md:56` still analyses only the original five, so five real companies' marks now appear on the primary conversion surface with NO nominative-fair-use analysis and outside the memo's own disclaimer sentence. title: The ToS omits four standard solo-founder protections, and neither repo has any third-party license inventory
effort: 2 days plus counsel; 4 hours for the OSS inventory
evidence: `docs/tos.md` (144 lines, all 11 sections read) contains no arbitration clause, no class-action waiver, no customer indemnity for uploaded content, and no explicit exclusion of indirect/consequential/special damages — §6 caps liability at "the amount you have paid us in the 12 months immediately preceding the claim" and stops there. §3 requires customers not to "Upload content you do not have the right to process" but attaches no indemnity to that promise, even though the product's entire input is third-party commercial documents. §10 sets a Delaware forum for a founder in Silver Spring, MD. By contrast `potentially-profitable/terms.html:471-475` does exclude consequential damages and does choose Maryland — the storefront's retired-business terms are the better-drafted document. On OSS: `find . -iname "*sbom*" -o -iname "*.spdx*" -o -iname "THIRD-PARTY*" -o -iname "NOTICE*"` returns nothing in either repo, and `grep -rn -i "license-check|licensee|license-checker|pip-licenses" .github/ scripts/ package.json` returns nothing — no license tooling in 11 workflows and 40 gates. The docling image pulls `opencv-python-headless` (Apache-2.0, whose §4(d) requires carrying attribution notices) and `pillow-heif>=0.16,<2`, which bundles libheif (LGPL-3.0) and its codecs; `apps/desktop` (Tauri) and `apps/ios`/`apps/mobile` are distribution surfaces where copyleft obligations differ from hosted SaaS.
impact: The four missing ToS provisions are the ones that decide whether a single unhappy operator becomes a $5,000 problem or a $150,000 one. Without a class waiver, a pricing or privacy claim can be aggregated; without an indemnity, a customer who uploads a document they had no right to process leaves Muntin holding it; without a consequential-damages exclusion, the "amount paid" cap may not reach lost-profits theories at all — and during free beta "amount paid" is $0, which is protective for money claims but does nothing for injunctive or statutory ones. The Delaware forum means a Maryland solo founder must defend or sue out of state. The OSS gap is smaller and I found no AGPL, but a NOTICE file is a 30-minute obligation the company is simply not meeting, and it is a standard diligence checklist item.
rec: Give counsel a scoped, flat-fee brief on the ToS only: add a consequential-damages exclusion, a customer indemnity tied to §3's upload representation, and a decision on arbitration plus class waiver (note that `terms.html:475` currently advertises "No mandatory arbitration. No class-action waiver" as a virtue, so this is a positioning call, not just a legal one). Align the forum to wherever the entity actually is. Separately, and without counsel: add `NOTICE` files carrying Apache-2.0 attributions for opencv and any other Apache dependency, and wire `pip-licenses` plus `pnpm licenses list` into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to produce a checked-in inventory — then confirm whether the pillow-heif/libheif LGPL chain reaches any distributed shell.
note: The factual half checks out: I read all 144 lines of `docs/tos.md` — no arbitration, no class waiver, no upload indemnity, §6 caps at amounts paid with no consequential-damages exclusion; and `find . \( -iname 'NOTICE*' -o -iname '*.spdx*' -o -iname '*sbom*' \)` returns nothing in either repo. But the recommendation collides with a documented positioning decision the auditor noticed and then argued against anyway: `terms.html:475` publishes "**No mandatory arbitration.** No class-action waiver ... it happens in a real courtroom in front of a real Maryland judge" as a customer-facing promise. Recommending a class waiver is recommending the company break a published commitment; that is a founder call, not a defect. Severity corrected to low: pre-revenue, billing fails open, $0 paid means the cap is already $0, and the transitive OSS chain was explicitly not resolved (the auditor says so). This is diligence hygiene, not exposure.

title: /never/ promise #2 says the engine "never learns from your corrections" while the landing page sells the opposite and the code ships it
evidence: `never/index.html:436`, on the storefront's absolute-promise page: "The model that reads an invoice is fixed; it never learns from your corrections, so the same invoice gives the same numbers and your data trains nothing." The product ships per-org learning from corrections on two seams. (1) `services/extract/vendor_overrides.py:11-16,47` — "Every correction on vendor.name lands in `org_vendor_overrides` ... After 2 corrections within a 90-day rolling window the override is promoted to `is_promoted=True`" and "the vendor_resolver consults `lookup_override(org_id, ...)` BEFORE the global catalog return path; a promoted override wins." (2) Template promotion after three operator confirms — `services/extract/VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md` defines a template as what earns auto-confirm, `cli/vendor_flywheel.py` is run at `--threshold 3`, and `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:4220` ADVERTISES it on the same landing page: "Any other vendor learns after three confirms." Two live surfaces of the same company, in the same sentence-space, assert opposite facts about whether operator corrections change future extractions.
impact: This is a privacy/data-use representation, not a feature description, and it sits under the heading "I will never resell your data" next to "the proof is on the wall" — the paragraph invites verification. The true, defensible claim (no language model, no cross-customer training, deterministic per document version) is available and is what `no-llm-ci.sh` actually gates; the sentence as written overshoots into "your corrections change nothing," which is false and which the company's own marketing contradicts one page over. An operator who reads /never/ #2 and then reads the landing strip has been told two different things about what happens to their data. Under FTC §5 the exposure is the privacy-adjacent absolute, not the marketing puff.
rec: Rewrite `never/index.html:436` to the claim the code supports: "No language model reads your invoices, and nothing you upload trains a model or crosses to another customer. Your own corrections do teach the reader — a vendor name you fix twice, or a layout you confirm three times, sticks for your account only." Then add that sentence pair as a row in `docs/marketing-claims.md` with `vendor_overrides.py` and `VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md` as its backing paths, and mirror to `es/never/`. The per-org-only scoping is the strong claim; do not give it away by over-promising determinism the engine deliberately abandoned.

title: The Cookie Policy's absolute "no third-party cookie set by an embedded widget" ships on 781 pages that embed Cloudflare Turnstile, which the policy never names
evidence: `cookies.html:450`: "Three cookies. That's the entire list. There is no fourth, no advertising cookie, no third-party cookie set by an embedded widget." The cookie table (`:432-448`) lists only `md_locale`, `lang_hint_dismissed`, `md_session`. Yet `cookies.html:592` itself contains `<div class="cf-turnstile" data-sitekey="0x4AAAAAADIgoGh56MvqeE8L" ...>` and `:750` loads `https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js`. `grep -rl "cf-turnstile"` returns **781 HTML pages**. The load is not user-initiated: `:767-768` fires `loadTurnstile()` 1500ms after `load` when the form is already in view. "Turnstile" appears nowhere in the cookie policy's prose (lines 412-481) — the 15 hits are all in the page's own footer script. `privacy.html:458` lists Cloudflare only as "hosting (Pages), Workers, KV namespace, R2 backups. Standard log retention; no analytics" — Turnstile, a bot-detection service that receives the visitor's IP, UA and behavioral signals, is not disclosed as a processing activity anywhere.
impact: Cloudflare documents Turnstile as capable of setting a `cf_clearance` cookie and it is unambiguously a third-party embedded widget transmitting visitor data to a third-party origin. The policy's claim is absolute and self-refuting on the very page that makes it, which is the worst possible construction — it is not a stale omission, it is a negative assertion contradicted by the same file. For a company whose entire differentiator is verifiable privacy claims, a demonstrably false cookie disclosure on 781 pages is the finding that discredits the true ones, and under GDPR/ePrivacy and CCPA it is a disclosure defect with the contradiction visible in the shipped source.
rec: Add a fourth row to the `cookies.html` table (and `es/cookies.html`) naming Turnstile: what it is, that it loads from `challenges.cloudflare.com` on pages carrying the newsletter form, what it receives, and what state it may set — then replace the absolute sentence with "Three first-party cookies. The only third-party code any page loads is Cloudflare Turnstile on the newsletter form; here is what it does." Add Turnstile as a named row in `privacy.html`'s vendor list alongside Resend and Cloudflare hosting. Then write the gate that makes it stick: a check that fails if any HTML file references a host other than `muntin.digital` in a `<script src>` without that host appearing in `cookies.html`'s disclosed list.

title: /security/ claim 5 tells readers to open DevTools and check — and the check fails on 33 of 33 operator sheets, one tool page, and /security/ itself
evidence: `security/index.html:600-603`: "**No third-party scripts touch the inputs.** Every tool page loads only first-party JS plus one privacy-first analytics script (Plausible)... *Inspect this:* DevTools → Network → filter JS. Reload. **Every script should be plausible.io or muntin.digital — nothing else.**" I ran the reader's test statically: `challenges.cloudflare.com` is loaded by 33 of 33 `sheets/*/index.html`, by `tools/audits/index.html`, and by `security/index.html` itself (1 hit). Claim 10 at `:651` compounds it: "Anonymous visitors trigger zero network calls from the sheet itself" — an anonymous visitor on any sheet page fetches a 28KB bundle from a Cloudflare origin 1.5s after load. The gate that is supposed to protect this, `scripts/check-security-claims.mjs`, passes: I ran it and it reports "10 claims × 2 locales, 5 audit tests × 2, 4 tiers × 2 — all rendered + schema'd." It counts that the claims are PRESENT and mirrored; it never executes the verification the claims publish.
impact: This is the company's own diagnosed failure mode landing on the single page whose purpose is to be verified. The page does not merely make a claim — it hands the reader the exact procedure to falsify it, on pages where it is false, and a green CI gate stands behind it. A journalist, a competitor, or the operator audience the /security/ page courts can disprove the site's flagship privacy claim in fifteen seconds using the site's own instructions. Every other true claim on that page loses its warrant at the same moment.
rec: Fix the claim to the truth and then make the gate test the truth. (1) Narrow claim 5 to "the tool's own code and one cookieless analytics script; the newsletter form at the bottom of some pages loads Cloudflare Turnstile, which never sees your inputs" — and say the same in claim 10 for sheets. (2) Rewrite `check-security-claims.mjs` so that for each claim carrying an "Inspect this" instruction it executes the corresponding static assertion: for claim 5, walk every page under `tools/` and `sheets/` and fail on any `<script src>` host outside an explicit allowlist that the claim text itself names. A claim that publishes its own test must be gated by that test, not by its presence.

title: Two of the three "known live exposures" the company catalogued for itself on 2026-06-15 are still shipping, in EN and ES, 52 days later
evidence: `docs/marketing-claims.md:50-59` is the founder's own red list. Item 1 (native apps) was resolved 2026-06-19. Items 2 and 3 were not, and I verified both still ship. Item 2 — `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:1968-1969` still reads "Your files live in {region}. **Files auto-delete after {retention}.** Your audit log keeps for seven years," rendered by `apps/web/app/_components/PostureSheetIsland.tsx:60`, with the ES mirror at `copy.es.ts:1614-1615` ("Se borran solos después de {retention}"). The retention reaper that would make it true is off: `apps/api/src/lib/retention-reaper-disabled-event.ts:38` gates on `env.RETENTION_REAPER_ENABLED === "true"`, and `RETENTION_REAPER_ENABLED` appears in `apps/api/src/env.ts:240` as an optional field and NOWHERE in `apps/api/wrangler.toml` `[vars]` or any workflow — so in production automatic deletion does not run. The registry's own instruction ("Reword to match `promises-data.ts` ... until the reaper is armed") was never carried out. Item 3 — `copy.ts:3747,3749` still reads "We cannot read your invoices" / "Your files are locked with a key only you hold" on the demo.
impact: A data-deletion promise is not marketing puff; "files auto-delete after N" is a retention representation of the kind state AGs and the FTC treat as material, and it is made in Spanish as well, which draws additional state UDAP attention. The aggravating fact is the paper trail: the company diagnosed both exposures itself, wrote the correct replacement wording into a registry, and then let 52 days pass with the false text live — that record converts a drafting error into documented knowledge. The registry's closing line ("when a fenced claim ships, move its row up to ✅") shows the maintenance loop was designed; nothing enforces it.
rec: Today: change `residencyBodyTemplate` in both `copy.ts` and `copy.es.ts` to the wording `promises-data.ts` already uses — "delete on request; automatic deletion is being switched on" — and scope the demo's `privacyHeading` to the enrolled/opt-in case or recast it on the verified no-language-model claim. This week: give the registry teeth. `docs/marketing-claims.md`'s red list is a markdown table nothing parses; add a `scripts/check-claim-exposures.mjs` that reads the 🔴 rows, and for each unresolved row greps the named file for the named string and FAILS. An exposure list that cannot fail is the same shape as a baseline whose substring cannot change.

title: The app's canonical origin defaults to ledger.muntin.digital, the Worker routes only app.muntin.digital, and the deploy guard checks the other variable
evidence: `apps/web/lib/canonical.ts:27-29` and `apps/web/lib/seo-schema.ts:19` both resolve `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "https://ledger.muntin.digital"` — that value becomes every canonical link, hreflang, JSON-LD `@id`, and the `Offer` URL on the pricing surfaces. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is set nowhere: not in `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc`, not in any `.github/workflows/*`, not in any env example — I grepped all of them. `scripts/guard-web-deploy-env.mjs:40` guards exactly one variable, `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL`, and its header explains the inlining hazard that applies identically to `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`. Meanwhile `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:26-31` binds the Worker to `app.muntin.digital/*` only. Three legal artifacts rest on that hostname resolving: `terms.html:436` routes the paid product's governing terms to `https://ledger.muntin.digital/legal/terms`; `never/index.html:440` grounds promise #3 ("I will never hide pricing behind a call") in "tiers are posted in writing at ledger.muntin.digital"; and `data/sourced-claims.json` `ledger_founding_offer_2026.source_url` is `https://ledger.muntin.digital/` — the sole substantiation for the founding-rate claim on 48 surfaces.
impact: The company's pricing-transparency promise and the registered claim behind its $19 offer both cite a URL the repo never configures and the Worker never routes. If the alias does not exist, the storefront's most-repeated promise resolves to nothing and the founding offer has no source; if it does exist, an unguarded build-time default is the only thing keeping the app's canonical, hreflang and Offer URLs pointed at it, and a single deploy without the variable would silently repoint them. Either way, a guard written for precisely this failure class covers the sibling variable and not this one — the same gate-shape gap this audit was commissioned over.
rec: Two lines and a curl. Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to `scripts/guard-web-deploy-env.mjs` beside `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` and set it explicitly in the deploy path so the fallback is never load-bearing. Then curl `https://ledger.muntin.digital/legal/terms` and `https://ledger.muntin.digital/` from a networked machine. If they 404, repoint `terms.html:436`, `never/index.html:440`, the `ledger_founding_offer_2026` `source_url`, and the 405 storefront links to `app.muntin.digital` in one commit; if they resolve, add the alias to `wrangler.jsonc` routes so the config says what production does.

title: The "absolute fact gate" is 47 registered claims plus a five-pattern blocklist across 1,368 pages, and the articles that name competitors' prices are among the eight with no citation drawer at all
evidence: CLAUDE.md calls `docs/fact-check.md` + `data/sourced-claims.json` "the absolute fact gate. Every number, date, name, anecdote, percentage must be (a) registered ... (b) cited inline ... or (c) labeled illustrative." Nothing enforces that sentence. `scripts/check-fabrications.mjs:22-38` is explicit about its own scope — five historical patterns from the May-2026 round (the two-restaurants bio, invented cohorts, the AI-Overview percentages, the $4,000 margin swing) — and `check-claim-usage.mjs` runs the inverse direction. `data/sourced-claims.json` holds **47** claims for 1,368 pages. I walked the library: 8 of 40 articles contain zero `<details class="cite">`, and two of the eight are the delivery-economics pair. `library/third-party-delivery-comparison/index.html` publishes 32 instances of "30%" including "DoorDash commission (Marketplace Plus, 30%)" at :512 and "Grubhub commission (Premium, 30%)" at :640, and at :741 and :795 makes an unsourced comparative superlative about three named companies: "Uber Eats has the **highest first-order conversion to a return customer in this market**, and the in-app cross-pollination with Uber rides means the platform brings discovery volume that the other two don't." No source, no citation drawer anywhere on the page, no registered claim covering it — the five delivery-platform claims in the registry cover published commission tiers only, and were last verified 2026-05-14 (84 days).
impact: The auditor found the comparative-advertising problem in the product repo's `/vs/` pages, where at least a baseline file and a monthly cron exist. The storefront version is worse and completely ungated: an indexed article asserting a market-share superlative about Uber Eats relative to DoorDash and Grubhub, with commission percentages for all three, and no substantiation mechanism of any kind pointed at it. Lanham Act §43(a)(1)(B) and FTC comparative-advertising substantiation attach at publication and do not care which repo the page lives in. This also means the company's most-cited governance claim — an absolute fact gate — is itself the presence of a shape.
rec: Pull or source the superlative at `library/third-party-delivery-comparison/index.html:741` and `:795` today; it is one sentence and it is the sharpest exposure on the storefront. Then close the gate gap in the direction that matters: write the forward check CLAUDE.md already promises — walk every reader-facing page (declared roots, explicit skip list, per this repo's own hard-learned rule), find each percentage or dollar figure attributed to a NAMED third party, and fail unless it is inside a `<details class="cite">`, registered in `sourced-claims.json`, or labeled illustrative. Scope it to third-party-attributed figures first so the finding count stays actionable, and add a staleness arm that reds any registered competitor-pricing claim older than 90 days.

title: Every product CTA on the storefront points at a hostname the product repo never routes
effort: 2 hours to verify and decide; 1 day to sweep both repos and add the gate
evidence: 405 storefront HTML files contain `ledger.muntin.digital` (496 link instances: 496x `https://ledger.muntin.digital/`, 10x `/promises`, 4x `/#app`, 2x `/legal/terms`); ZERO storefront files contain `app.muntin.digital`. The product routes only app: /home/user/Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:26-31 `"pattern": "app.muntin.digital/*"`, and runbooks/web-deploy.md:24-27 gives the DNS + route instructions for app.muntin.digital only. I grepped every .toml/.jsonc/.yml/.yaml in the product repo for `ledger.muntin.digital` — no route, no redirect, no DNS note. Meanwhile the product's own canonical helper defaults to the OTHER host: apps/web/lib/canonical.ts:28 `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "https://ledger.muntin.digital"`, same at app/robots.ts:16, app/sitemap.ts:27, app/layout.tsx:51, app/page.tsx:23. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is set nowhere in the repo — not in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc vars (which sets only APP_ORIGIN=https://app.muntin.digital), not in .github/workflows, not in guard-web-deploy-env.mjs.
impact: Two mutually exclusive failure modes, both bad. If ledger.muntin.digital no longer resolves, the entire storefront-to-product funnel is a dead link on 405 pages and has been for an unknown period — and because analytics is absent on 79% of those pages (see next finding), nothing would have surfaced it. If it does resolve, the product's marketing site self-canonicalizes to a host different from the one Cloudflare serves, which is the classic way to get an entire marketing site dropped from the index. Either way the company's only paid-product acquisition path is built on an unverified hostname, and the two repos disagree about the company's own product URL.
rec: Ten-minute check tomorrow: `curl -sI https://ledger.muntin.digital/` and `curl -sI https://app.muntin.digital/`. Then pick ONE canonical product host. If app: set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=https://app.muntin.digital as a runtime var in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc, add a 301 from ledger to app in Cloudflare, and sweep the storefront (496 link instances, mostly injected by the shared nav/footer partial plus the ledger-cta injector — fix _includes/footer.html, _includes/es/footer.html, and the injector, then rebuild). Add a storefront gate that asserts every outbound product link uses the one canonical host.
note: Reproduced exactly and then strengthened. 405 storefront HTML files reference ledger.muntin.digital; `grep -rl app.muntin.digital --include=*.html` in the storefront returns 0. apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:26-31 routes only `app.muntin.digital/*` and it is the ONLY route pattern in any .jsonc/.toml in the product repo. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL appears in 19 code sites (canonical.ts:28, robots.ts:16, sitemap.ts:27, layout.tsx:51/257/262/267/274/350/370/375/383/390, page.tsx:23, seo-schema.ts:19, MarketingBreadcrumb.tsx:29, verify/page.tsx:121, verify/[slug]/page.tsx:177, .well-known/security.txt/route.ts:14) and is SET NOWHERE — every one falls back to ledger.muntin.digital. What the auditor missed makes it worse: the product's own docs contradict the code. docs/multi-platform-decision.md:38 and docs/cross-platform-ux.md:124 both name app.muntin.digital 'the canonical surface'; docs/shell-bridge-protocol.md:65 says 'https://app.muntin.digital (canonical production)'. Meanwhile PlausibleAnalytics.tsx:52 HARDCODES data-domain="ledger.muntin.digital" with no env fallback, so even product analytics reports under the disputed host. The auditor's FIX is wrong, however: setting NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL as a wrangler `vars` entry has zero effect — runbooks/web-deploy.md:36-44 states plainly that NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined by Next at BUILD time and 'a runtime Worker vars entry has zero effect'; it must go in the build environment alongside NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL.

title: 79% of the site emits no analytics, including every glossary term and 142 of 143 Cost-Index pages
effort: 1 day
evidence: I walked every HTML file outside assets/docs/scripts/tests/_includes/src (1,329 files) and tested for the `plausible.init` bootstrap block. 274 pages have it; 1,055 do not. By section, pages WITHOUT any tracker: es 518 (of 651), library 183, glossary 171 (of 172 — only the hub), cost-index 142 (of 143), open 18, learn 11, tools 2. Verified by hand: glossary/food-cost/index.html and cost-index/eggs/index.html both contain 0 occurrences of `assets/p.js` and 0 of `plausible.init`, while library/restaurant-prime-cost/index.html has both. Worse, those pages DO load assets/js/first-touch.js (893 pages do), whose newsletter handler at first-touch.js:277-282 fires the conversion event behind `if (typeof window.plausible === 'function')` — on a page with no init block that guard is false and the event is silently discarded. Cross-tabulated: 891 pages carry a signup form; 649 of them have no analytics init. Nothing fixes this at deploy time — scripts/inject-lazy-script-loader.mjs only REWRITES existing p.js/site.js tags (its header, lines 20-31), it never adds one, and no other script in the wrangler.jsonc build.command chain injects the init block.
impact: The company cannot answer the only questions that matter: does the 1,368-page corpus bring anyone, does the Cost Index (the stated flagship acquisition asset) get traffic, do the 651 Spanish pages get read, and does any of it convert. The entire content investment is being made blind. This is the same failure class as the 42-day-dormant market prior: the shape is present (a tracker exists, a gate guards it, a KPI file names metrics) while the system is not grounded in what it claims.
rec: Add the 3-line Plausible bootstrap to the page-generating builders that omit it — build-cost-index-pages.mjs, the glossary builder, build-library.mjs, and the ES mirror path — or write a single `inject-analytics-bootstrap.mjs` that stamps it into every non-admin HTML page and wire it into check-all with a --check mode. Then verify one glossary and one cost-index page in DevTools. Until then treat every traffic or conversion number you have as covering one fifth of the site.
note: Reproduced independently: 1,329 HTML files outside assets/docs/scripts/tests/_includes/src; 274 contain `plausible.init`, 275 contain `assets/p.js`. By top-level dir the init lives in es 133, sheets 40, library 38, blog 20, learn 14, tools 6, ledger 2, glossary 1, cost-index 1. glossary/food-cost/index.html and cost-index/eggs/index.html load only theme-toggle.js (+warmth.js); library/restaurant-prime-cost/index.html:178-179 carries the full bootstrap. I also reproduced the cross-tab exactly: 893 pages carry a signup form AND first-touch.js, and 651 of those have no init (auditor said 649 — trivial regex delta). first-touch.js:279 gates the conversion fire on `if (typeof window.plausible === 'function')`, which is false on those pages. No injector adds the block: the only two emitters are scripts/build-people-pages.mjs:226 and scripts/new-article-skeleton.mjs:195, and inject-lazy-script-loader.mjs only rewrites existing tags. There is no coverage gate — the three analytics scripts are check-analytics-vocabulary, check-kpi-doc, check-no-third-party-plausible, none of which asks whether a page has a tracker.

title: Three of four north-star KPIs query Plausible goals no code path produces
effort: 3 hours
evidence: data/kpis.json defines four KPIs. (1) `tool-engagement-rate` = `Tool First Result` / pageviews on /tools/*. That event is fired from exactly one place, assets/js/save-next-time.js:188 — and save-next-time.js is loaded by 614 pages, ZERO of which are the five live tool pages: I checked tools/{cost-pulse,margin-math,menu-engineering,plate-cost,vendor-benchmark}/index.html and each contains 0 occurrences of `save-next-time`. (3) `window-engagement-rate` filters `event:goal=Window Sent`; no such name exists — the vocabulary registry (tools/_shared/analytics.js, 266 names) does not contain 'Window Sent', and the code fires 'Window Send'. Separately, tools/cost-pulse and tools/vendor-benchmark carry no `plausible.init` at all, so two of five tools do not even report a pageview. check-kpi-doc.mjs only asserts `_lastReviewed` is <=90 days old (currently 2026-06-17, 50 days) — it never checks that a named goal is fireable.

rec: Three fixes, all small: load save-next-time.js on the five tool pages (or move the `Tool First Result` fire into tools/_shared/analytics.js, which they already import); change the kpis.json filter 'Window Sent' to 'Window Send'; add the Plausible bootstrap to cost-pulse and vendor-benchmark. 'Tool First Result' is fired only at assets/js/save-next-time.js:188; `grep -c save-next-time` returns 0 for all five of tools/{cost-pulse,margin-math,menu-engineering,plate-cost,vendor-benchmark}/index.html, so the numerator of tool-engagement-rate and the denominator of workshop-save-rate are structurally zero. data/kpis.json filters `event:goal=Window Sent`; the only fire site is assets/js/window.js:736 `window.plausible('Window Send', …)` and tools/_shared/analytics.js:415 registers 'Window Send' — 'Window Sent' exists only as a dead key in save-next-time.js:152's PROP_AUGMENT_EVENTS map, which is itself further evidence the two names were never reconciled. plausible.init count: cost-pulse 0, vendor-benchmark 0, margin-math/menu-engineering/plate-cost present. title: The five free tools — the stated acquisition wedge — have no email capture at all

title: Every founding-list lead is recorded in the product database as coming from the retired services line
effort: 30 minutes
evidence: The homepage form posts `<input type="hidden" name="source" value="home-founding">` (index.html, founding-capture block) and /ledger/ posts `ledger-pricing`.
