title: The documented six-message drip has no implementation, and the one that ships is switched off in production
effort: 1 day to flip and verify; 3 days to rewrite the sequence
evidence: docs/email-drip/{01-welcome,02-audit-prompt,03-case-study,04-pricing,05-care-plan,06-direct-ask}.md describes a six-message operator sequence triggered by an `intent_source` field set to `tool-save`, `audit-pdf`, or `intake`, 'pasted into Buttondown one-by-one'. Grepping src/, scripts/, and data/ for 'buttondown' and 'intent_source' returns nothing — there is no implementation and no such field; the shipped subscriber record uses SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES = footer | article-end | workshop-empty-state | window | cost-index (src/worker.js:8745). Two of the three documented triggers (audit-pdf, intake) are retired-line events. The sequence that IS built — src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js welcome / 7-day nudge / 30-day digest — is gated at wrangler.jsonc:272 `"LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED": "false"`, and the weekly KPI email at :276 `"KPI_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED": "false"`. lifecycle-emails.js:42 returns {skipped:'flag-off'} on every cron tick.
impact: Someone who gives you their email today receives one double-opt-in confirmation and then silence until launch — which ADR-020 has now deferred to 2027. That is 18 months of a cooling list. The 613 footer forms are collecting addresses into a bucket with no outflow, and the drip the founder wrote is aimed at a business he no longer runs.
rec: Flip LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED to 'true' (the hard cap of 4/quarter is already enforced in the dispatcher) so the welcome/nudge/digest sequence starts working. Then rewrite docs/email-drip/* as a cost-line sequence — monthly Cost Index read, one tool, one library piece, the Ledger private-beta ask — and implement it against the existing lifecycle dispatcher rather than a Buttondown paste. Delete 02-audit-prompt.md and 05-care-plan.md; they sell the retired line.
note: Reproduced: wrangler.jsonc:272 LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED='false', :276 KPI_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED='false'; src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js:42 `isEnabled()` returns true only on the string 'true'. `grep -rn 'buttondown|intent_source' src/ scripts/ data/` returns nothing at all — the six docs/email-drip/*.md files describe a sequence with no implementation and no such field. src/worker.js:8746 SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES is the real record. I raise this to HIGH rather than medium because it compounds with the missed finding below: with lifecycle off AND the broadcast filter restricted to source='cost-index', there is currently NO recurring email path to any subscriber captured anywhere except the two Cost-Index hub pages. Every other address on the list is unreachable by design, not just un-nurtured.

title: The product's Spanish marketing surface is structurally invisible to search, while the storefront's 651 ES pages are done correctly
effort: 1 hour to drop the false hreflang; 1 week for prefixed ES routes
evidence: /home/user/Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/lib/canonical.ts:42-48 builds hreflang alternates where `es-MX` is assigned THE SAME URL as `en-US` and `x-default`. The docstring at :14-18 states the design plainly: 'The locale is cookie-based... we do NOT expose a /es/<route> URL prefix. The same canonical URL serves both EN and ES content via Accept-Language + cookie.' Googlebot sends no locale cookie and crawls with Accept-Language: en, so only the English render is ever seen; and hreflang annotations pointing multiple languages at one URL are discarded by Google rather than honored. By contrast the storefront does this correctly — distinct /es/ URLs, 1,318 pages carrying hreflang, verified triples with x-default on library/restaurant-prime-cost/index.html — across a genuinely substantive 651-page ES corpus (median body length: cost-index 1,702 words, glossary 758, library 577, blog 2,277; these are translations, not shells).
impact: The company is paying the ES maintenance tax twice and collecting on it once. The storefront's Spanish investment is real and indexable; the product's Spanish marketing pages — the pages that would actually convert a Spanish-speaking operator into a founding member — cannot be found in Spanish search at all. And because the storefront's ES pages are 518-of-651 untracked, there is currently no evidence either way about whether the ES bet is paying off.
rec: Cheapest honest fix today: stop emitting the `es-MX` hreflang until the URLs are distinct — it is a claim to Google that the code cannot honour. The real fix is /es/-prefixed routes on apps/web mirroring the storefront's pattern. Separately, and more importantly for the ES strategy question: get the tracker onto the 518 untracked ES pages so that six months from now there is data to decide whether 651 Spanish pages earn their keep. Right now that decision is unmakeable.
note: Reproduced at apps/web/lib/canonical.ts:41-48 — `languages` assigns en-US, x-default and (when hasES) es-MX all to the same `canonical` string. The docstring at :13-18 confirms the cookie-based design and then asserts something factually wrong about crawlers: 'The hreflang alternates tell crawlers that the SAME URL is the authoritative source for both locales; they pick the response based on Accept-Language.' Google discards hreflang sets that point multiple languages at one URL, and Googlebot does not send es-MX Accept-Language. The URL scheme is a deliberate tradeoff; the es-MX emission on top of it is the defect. Storefront ES side verified as correct by contrast (1,576 /es/ <loc> entries in sitemap.xml, 0 noindex, 0 missing on disk).

title: feed-llm.json violates its own spec on 46% of items and excludes the flagship asset entirely
effort: 4 hours
evidence: feed-llm.json declares JSON Feed 1.1, which requires RFC 3339 timestamps. 33 of its 72 items carry a bare date ('2026-05-31', '2026-04-20') and one — https://muntin.digital/library/ingredient-yields/ — has `date_published: null`. Coverage is thin against what llms.txt promises: 72 items total (39 en-US, 33 es-US) drawn only from library (17), blog (15), learn (7) and es (33) — zero of 171 glossary terms and zero of 101 Cost-Index pages, even though llms.txt files it under 'Full-body corpus (preferred for citation)' and content_text median length is 1,025 chars (min 416), i.e. summaries not bodies. llms.txt itself enumerates 153 URLs against 1,058 sitemap URLs and names no individual ingredient page — only the pattern `/cost-index/<ingredient>/`, which a model cannot expand. Related freshness signal gap: only 268 of 1,058 sitemap URLs carry <lastmod> — 0 of 172 glossary, 57 of 142 cost-index, 17 of 200 library.
impact: The AEO investment is the company's most differentiated discovery bet and the one most aligned with its actual asset (sourced, citable, CC0 data). Shipping a malformed feed means strict parsers drop nearly half the items, and omitting the Cost Index means the single thing most worth citing is the thing models are least able to enumerate. Meanwhile a crawler visiting 1,058 URLs with no freshness hints on the pages that change most often will re-crawl the wrong things.
rec: In build-llms-txt.mjs and the feed builder: emit full RFC 3339 timestamps with offset, drop or backfill the null, add the per-ingredient Cost-Index pages and glossary terms as items, and add <lastmod> for every sitemap URL from the page's dateModified. This is a half-day of builder work on a channel already half-built — the highest ratio of leverage to effort in this domain after the analytics fix.
note: The date defect reproduces exactly: parsing feed-llm.json gives 72 items, version jsonfeed.org/version/1.1, and 33 items whose date_published is a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' plus one null — I confirmed the null is on /library/ingredient-yields/. Section counts match (es 33, library 17, blog 15, learn 7; content_text median 1,025 chars, min 416). Sitemap lastmod reproduces: 268 of 1,058. But the headline 'excludes the flagship asset entirely' and 'summaries not bodies' mis-assigns the artifact. llms.txt:17 designates /llms-full.txt as 'every article, research note, and glossary term, EN, full body' — that file is 681KB across 562 documents and contains 1,590 glossary URL references, so 'zero of 171 glossary terms' is false at the corpus level; feed-llm.json is described at llms.txt:19 only as 'JSON Feed 1.1 with content_text per item' and never claims full body. The real, narrower gap — which I verified and the auditor did not — is that llms-full.txt contains just 14 cost-index references, so the Cost Index is thin in the FULL corpus too. 'Strict parsers drop nearly half the items' is unsupported: date_published is an optional JSON Feed field and mainstream parsers are lenient. Low.

title: A 'Free Website Audits for Small Businesses' tool is still indexed, in the sitemap, and linked from the tools hub
effort: 2 hours
evidence: tools/audits/index.html carries `<title>Free Website Audits for Small Businesses | Muntin Digital</title>`, contains 0 occurrences of 'noindex', appears in sitemap.xml, and is linked twice from tools/index.html; an ES mirror exists at es/tools/audits/. Its visible copy offers a 'Restaurant Website Audit — drop your restaurant URL and get a real mobile Lighthouse' run, and it is the only tool page on the site carrying an email capture form (3 occurrences of foot-newsletter-form) — so the one tool that collects emails sells the retired line. Corroborating residue: of the 266 names in the analytics registry (tools/_shared/analytics.js), 198 are not fired anywhere, and the overwhelming majority of those are Audit-* and GBP-* events ('Audit Started', 'Audit PDF Emailed', 'GBP Grader', 'Audit Weekend Mode Enter'...).
impact: It is the widest-aperture page on the site — 'small businesses', not restaurants, not cost — so it will attract exactly the wrong search intent and the wrong emails into the founding list, and it undercuts the positioning story to any operator or investor who clicks through the tools hub. Small in page count, disproportionate in what it says about what the company is.
rec: Freeze it (noindex, follow) or 301 it to /tools/, drop it from tools/index.html and the sitemap, and move its newsletter form to the five cost tools. Then trim the ~198 dead Audit/GBP names from the analytics registry so the vocabulary gate's output becomes readable again — right now its signal is buried under retired noise.
note: Reproduced: tools/audits/index.html:7 `<title>Free Website Audits for Small Businesses | Muntin Digital</title>`, 0 occurrences of 'noindex', 8 sitemap.xml matches for tools/audits (EN + ES), and it is the only tool page with a capture form (3 hits). One correction: it is linked ONCE from tools/index.html, not twice. tools/_shared/analytics.js is 448 lines; I did not re-derive the '198 dead names' figure, so treat that sub-claim as unverified.

title: The 162 Cost-Index ingredient pages promise a monthly email that the worker makes it impossible to send
evidence: scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:2898 stamps a signup band on every ingredient page with `source: 'cost-index-ingredient'` and this pitch: "Get the monthly read — the first Tuesday of each month, what moved and what to do. No filler, no funnels." (ES mirror identical). 162 built pages carry `name="source" value="cost-index-ingredient"`. src/worker.js:8746 `SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES = new Set(['footer','article-end','workshop-empty-state','window','cost-index'])` does NOT contain it, and :8863 `const source = SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES.has(body.source) ? body.source : 'footer'` silently rewrites it to 'footer'. The monthly broadcast then filters at src/worker.js:8793: `if (!sub || sub.status !== 'active' || sub.source !== 'cost-index') continue;`. `grep -rln 'name="source" value="cost-index"'` returns exactly two files: cost-index/index.html and es/cost-index/index.html. Corroborating rot in the same allowlist: three of its five entries — 'article-end', 'window', 'workshop-empty-state' — are emitted by ZERO pages on the site.
impact: Every subscriber acquired from the flagship acquisition asset — the 162 ingredient pages, the single highest-intent capture surface and the one the whole cost-intelligence funnel is built to feed — is filed as a generic footer subscriber and is permanently excluded from the newsletter they were explicitly promised. Combined with LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED='false', those addresses receive one double-opt-in confirmation and then nothing, ever. Only the two hub pages can produce a reachable Cost-Index subscriber. This is the domain's exact version of the 42-day-dormant market prior: a promise in prose, a form that posts, a worker that 200s, a broadcast that runs green with sent=0 and returns 'empty-audience' (worker.js:8817) rather than erroring — every shape present, the system ungrounded. And because the ingredient pages are 142-of-143 untracked, no signal would ever surface it.
rec: One-line fix first: add 'cost-index-ingredient' to SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES (worker.js:8746) and widen the broadcast filter at :8793 to `sub.source === 'cost-index' || sub.source === 'cost-index-ingredient'`. Then decide deliberately whether 'footer' subscribers should receive the monthly read at all — 613 pages capture into a bucket with no outflow. Delete the three dead allowlist entries. Finally add a gate that inverts the direction: enumerate every `name="source" value="…"` in built HTML and fail if a value is not in SUBSCRIBE_SOURCES/WAITLIST_SOURCES — the same inverse-index lesson check-claim-usage already taught this repo.

title: check-og-coverage runs green on 75 of 1,066 indexable pages while the product conversion page has no social card at all
evidence: I parsed og:image on every indexable (non-noindex) page: 1,066 scanned, 136 have NO og:image element whatsoever, and 185 have no twitter:card. Among the 136: /ledger/index.html and /es/ledger/index.html — the product page, the primary conversion surface, which carries og:locale, og:type, og:title, og:description and og:url (lines 19-27) and then simply stops — plus /cost-index/basket/, /studio/ (the company page), /trust/, /claims/, /methods/, /window/, /receipts/, /changelog/, /ai/, /never/ and 50 library pages including library/index.html. Both gates pass this: `node scripts/check-og-coverage.mjs --check` prints "OG coverage: clean. (75 pages checked.)" because its job (per its header, lines 8-25) is only to assert that certain enumerated page kinds use a specific card rather than a generic fallback — it never asks whether an og:image exists; and check-og-images.mjs only verifies that references which exist resolve (I confirmed 0 broken targets across 930 pages). A page with no reference passes both.
impact: Every share of the product page — the founder posting it, an operator pasting it into a Slack or a group chat, an AI assistant rendering a preview card — produces a bare text stub while the homepage renders a 1200x630 card. That is the conversion surface. More structurally, this is a second instance of the repo's own declared root-list rule being violated ('a script that scans the site walks everything and carries an explicit skip list, where every entry says why it is not reader-facing prose') by a gate whose green output actively conceals the gap it was written to protect.
rec: Add og:image + og:image:width/height + twitter:card to the shared head partial so absence is impossible, defaulting to /brand/og/home.png, and render a bespoke card for /ledger/ first. Then rewrite check-og-coverage.mjs to walk all 1,066 indexable pages with an explicit skip list and fail on a MISSING og:image, keeping the current 75-page specificity check as a second, narrower rule. Today the gate's scope is silent, which is the thing CLAUDE.md says is not allowed.

title: The RSS channel still calls the company a 'restaurant web library' — the one syndication artifact the repositioning pass never touched
evidence: feed.xml channel metadata: `<title>Muntin Digital — restaurant web library</title>` and `<description>Articles, glossary, and tools for independent restaurants — written and maintained by Don Goldstein.</description>`, emitted by scripts/build-rss.mjs:234. es/feed.xml is 'Muntin Digital — biblioteca para restaurantes'. Compare llms.txt, which the same repositioning pass DID rewrite and which now opens 'Muntin Digital is a restaurant cost-intelligence company' (llms.txt:3; the rewrite is recorded at docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md:292-295). Neither the word 'cost' nor 'price' nor 'index' appears in either feed's channel identity. check-positioning-drift.mjs scans HTML prose under content roots (SKIP_TOP at :63-67) and so structurally cannot see feed.xml, and no check-*.mjs reads the RSS channel block.
impact: The channel title is the company's name in every feed reader, every RSS-to-newsletter bridge, every aggregator index and every LLM crawl that ingests feeds rather than sitemaps — 50 items wide, updated on every deploy. It asserts the retired identity in the exact channel where identity is cheapest to assert and hardest to correct later. It is also a live counterexample to the audit's own conclusion that the freeze pass was 'roughly 70% done by page count': the residue is not only in page prose, it is in the machine-readable identity artifacts, which no gate covers.
rec: Change build-rss.mjs:234 and the ES equivalent to the llms.txt line ('Restaurant cost intelligence — the Cost Index, free operator tools, and a bilingual library on food cost'), rebuild both feeds, and extend check-positioning-drift.mjs (or a small sibling) to read feed.xml, es/feed.xml, feed-llm.json's `title`/`description`, and the homepage Organization `description` — the four machine-readable places the company states what it is.

title: The homepage's primary entity block is a LocalBusiness storefront that still advertises 'site audits'
evidence: index.html's first ld+json @graph node is `"@type": ["ProfessionalService", "LocalBusiness"]` with GeoCoordinates (38.9907, -77.0261), a PostalAddress, `priceRange: "$$"`, `openingHoursSpecification` Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, and areaServed = Silver Spring, Takoma Park, Bethesda, Washington + MD/DC — the full local-services scaffolding of the retired web studio. It is the only ProfessionalService node on the site (1 file), against 85 files carrying a plain Organization and 12 carrying SoftwareApplication. Inside it, `hasOfferCatalog.itemListElement[2]` reads: "Free operator tools — Plate cost, margin math, vendor benchmarks, **and site audits** — in the browser, no signup." `itemListElement[0]` points Muntin Ledger at https://ledger.muntin.digital/. Note `knowsAbout` WAS repositioned (board :285-291 records that fix) — the type, the local scaffolding and the offer catalog beneath it were not. I checked and refuted a fourth suspicion here: the Offer's 'refreshed Monday, Wednesday, and Friday' is TRUE (.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml:35 `cron: 0 13 * * 1,3,5`), though CLAUDE.md calls it 'daily 13:00 UTC'.
impact: This is the strongest single entity signal the site emits and it tells Google and every LLM crawler that Muntin is a Silver Spring local service business with office hours that sells website audits — for a company whose product is a national SaaS and whose flagship is an openly-licensed national dataset. The auditor counted 22 @types and 1,058 pages of valid JSON-LD and graded structured data a strength; validity was never the question. It also embeds the disputed ledger host in the entity graph, so the hostname problem propagates into the knowledge-graph layer where a 301 will not clean it up.
rec: Retype the root node Organization (+ SoftwareApplication for the Ledger offer, + the Dataset publisher relationship the Cost Index already emits on 193 pages), drop openingHoursSpecification / priceRange / geo, keep the address only if a real business address is required, and cut 'and site audits' from the tools offer in the same commit as the /tools/audits/ freeze. Then extend the existing JSON-LD gate from 'parses' to 'the root entity's type and offer catalog name only live surfaces' — validity gates are exactly the shape-not-grounding failure this audit round exists to catch.

title: The eight named AI-crawler stanzas in robots.txt each drop half the wildcard group's Disallow list
evidence: robots.txt's `User-agent: *` group disallows ten paths: /blog/drafts/, /workbench/, /es/workbench/, /account/, /es/account/, /api/auth/account-delete-confirm, /admin/, /sign-in/, /es/sign-in/, /es/blog/drafts/. Each of the eight per-agent stanzas that follow (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Bytespider, Applebot-Extended) re-lists only five: /blog/drafts/, /workbench/, /account/, /admin/, /sign-in/. Under REP group matching a crawler that matches a specific user-agent group ignores the wildcard group entirely, so all eight are permitted /es/workbench/, /es/account/, /es/sign-in/ (all three directories exist on disk) and /api/auth/account-delete-confirm. Separately, the stanza comment (robots.txt lines 27-36) frames this as the site's 'AI search posture', but names GPTBot — OpenAI's TRAINING crawler — while OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User, the agents that actually produce ChatGPT retrieval citations, appear nowhere.
impact: Small in blast radius and partly mitigated (the ES surfaces are server-404-gated per the file's own comments, and the unnamed retrieval bots still inherit the permissive wildcard), but it is a defense-in-depth control that silently does half its job, in the file the company points to as its AI-search posture. The pattern matters more than the paths: the disallow list was extended once for the wildcard group and never propagated, and nothing checks the two lists against each other.
rec: Make the per-agent stanzas a generated block from a single DISALLOW array so the lists cannot diverge, add OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User as named allows if the AEO bet is real, and add a five-line check that asserts every path in the wildcard group appears in every named group. There is currently no check-*.mjs that reads robots.txt at all.

title: The only edition published under the new monthly cadence is missing from the public archive and cites the wrong week's dataset
effort: 1 day
evidence: `blog/cost-index-2026-07/index.html` is the sole edition published since the 2026-07-09 founder call that made the dispatch monthly and hand-written (`article:published_time` = 2026-07-09). It is NOT in `data/cost-index-editions.json` — that append-only spine holds 4 editions ending at 2026-07-06. It is NOT in the public archive: `cost-index/weekly/index.html` lists only `cost-index-week-2026-06-05/-06-16/-06-18/-07-06`. It has no CC0 snapshot: `cost-index/` contains only `week-2026-06-18.{json,csv}` and `week-2026-07-06.{json,csv}`. Worst, its own citability block is misattributed — `grep '"contentUrl"' blog/cost-index-2026-07/index.html` returns `https://muntin.digital/cost-index/week-2026-07-06.json` and `.csv`, and the visible "Cite this edition" links resolve to the same 2026-07-06 files. Root cause is one line: `scripts/build-cost-index-archive.mjs:63` builds `const slug = \`cost-index-week-${e.asOf}\`` (also lines 120, 123), so the monthly slug family can never be rendered, and the builder reads only the spine the hand-written path never appends to. `scripts/check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` WAS taught the monthly slug family (`dispatchDate()`, lines 47–58) — the archive builder was not, so no gate notices the divergence.
impact: ADR-010's entire premise is that the Cost Index earns authority and inbound citation by being reproducible and addressable. Right now a researcher, journalist, or AI crawler landing on the July edition either (a) reads the archive and concludes the series died on 2026-07-06, or (b) follows the edition's own citation and downloads a different week's numbers under the July edition's name. That is a false public claim about a dataset, made by the company whose single differentiator is "we do not guess." It also poisons the exact channel — citation-driven discovery — that the whole content funnel exists to feed.
rec: Two fixes, same commit. (1) Teach `build-cost-index-archive.mjs` the monthly slug family: derive the slug from the edition record rather than hardcoding `cost-index-week-`, matching `dispatchDate()` in the freshness gate. (2) Make the hand-written path append to the spine and emit the CC0 snapshot — either a `node scripts/build-cost-index-dispatch.mjs --register-only <asOf>` step in the publish runbook, or move the spine append into `cost-index-refresh.yml` keyed on the newest `blog/cost-index-*` page meta. Then add a gate asserting every `blog/cost-index-*` edition has (a) a spine row, (b) an archive row, (c) a `week-<its own asOf>.json` that exists — the shape check that would have caught this.
note: The archive gap is real and the root cause is exactly where the auditor said: `scripts/build-cost-index-archive.mjs:63` hardcodes ``const slug = `cost-index-week-${e.asOf}` `` (also 120, 123), so `blog/cost-index-2026-07/` cannot render into `/cost-index/weekly/` — grep of that page returns only the four `cost-index-week-*` slugs. But the two claims that made it CRITICAL are false. (1) "cites the wrong week's dataset" — REFUTED: `blog/cost-index-2026-07/index.html:879` reads "Edition of 2026-07-09, **read as of 2026-07-06**; weighted basket −4.96%", and the spine's 2026-07-06 entry carries `basket.pct = -0.049648946840521666`, i.e. the identical read. `cost-index/week-2026-07-06.json` and `.csv` both exist on disk. The citation points at precisely the snapshot the edition read; a researcher following it gets the right data. (2) "absent from the append-only spine" — misleading: the data read IS in the spine; only an `editionDate`-keyed row is missing, and `build-cost-index-dispatch.mjs:392–424` already supports `editionDate` keying (`keyOf = (e) => e.editionDate || e.asOf`). (3) "a researcher concludes the series died 2026-07-06" — REFUTED: the July edition appears in `blog/index.html` (2 hits), `feed.xml` (2), `sitemap.xml` (3) and `llms.txt` (1). Only the archive page misses it, and its newest row is 3 days before the edition, not a dead series. Real severity: a discovery gap on one surface, not a false public data claim.

title: The Cost Index headline is anchored to 2026-06-01 prices while presenting a 2026-08-05 review date; the dead-feed roster doubled in seven days
effort: 3 days (triage) + 1 day (gate)
evidence: `data/cost-index.json` has `basket.asOf = 2026-06-01` (66 days old at 2026-08-06) against `_lastReviewed = 2026-08-05`. `node scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` reports 16 UNEXPECTED frozen feeds plus 10 known-latent — 26 of 100 — with `shrimp`, `vegetable-oil` and `salmon-fillet` explicitly tagged `[BASKET CONTRIBUTOR — dates the published headline]` at 67d, and seven produce series tagged `[STALE LEVEL ANCHOR — composite reads 2026-08-04, but the price behind it is from 2026-05-11]`. That gate's own header states "On 2026-07-30 there were 8" unexpected; the board (`docs/handoff/strategic-council-board.md`, OPEN item 1) says 18 total / 8 unexpected. Seven days later it is 26 total / 16 unexpected — the roster doubled and nothing was triaged. The gate is warn-only by design (`--strict` not promoted). `check-staleness-honesty.mjs` cannot see any of it: `tools/_shared/cost-staleness.js:70–80` computes `staleDays = point.asOf − freshestProvenance.date`, both frozen in the vendored record, so a feed that stops entirely reports staleness 0 — and it prints "0 overdue" across 93 shippable points. The 10 known-latent seafood series hit the 120-day cliff on 2026-09-29, at which point `build-cost-index.mjs` drops them.
impact: The Cost Index is the top of the funnel and the free proof that the paid product's numbers can be trusted. Publishing a basket headline whose anchor has not moved in 66 days, beside a fresh review date, is the precise failure the honesty contract was written to prevent — and it is invisible to every gate that claims to guard it. It is also a product dependency: `apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json` in the Ledger repo vendors from this, so a stale basket propagates into the inventory market prior.
rec: This is a founder decision that cannot be automated away. For each of the 16 unexpected feeds, choose within the week: re-source, or move to `KNOWN_SOURCE_LATENT` with a dated comment, or retire via the ADR-021 path. Then promote `check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs --strict`. Separately, add a `basketAnchorAgeDays` assertion so any edition whose `basket.asOf` is more than ~45 days behind `_lastReviewed` must either withhold the headline or state the anchor date in the H1 dek — `check-staleness-honesty.mjs` structurally cannot do this and should stop being counted as coverage.
note: The FEED COUNTS reproduce exactly: `node scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` → 16 unexpected + 10 known-latent = 26 of 100, with shrimp/vegetable-oil/salmon-fillet tagged BASKET CONTRIBUTOR at 67d; the gate header (lines 26–30) records 8 unexpected on 2026-07-30, so the unexpected roster did double. Sibling blindness also reproduces: `check-cost-index-freshness.mjs` → "freshest read as of 2026-08-04 (2d old) — fresh"; `check-staleness-honesty.mjs` → "93 shippable point(s) · max overdue ratio 0.00× · 0 overdue", and `tools/_shared/cost-staleness.js:68–76` confirms `staleDays = daysBetween(point.asOf, freshestLevelSource.date)` with both frozen. BUT the headline interpretation is REFUTED. `basket.asOf` is not an anchor and does not date the headline: `tools/_shared/cost-basket.js:45` — `if (r.asOf && (!asOf || r.asOf < asOf)) asOf = r.asOf; // oldest contributing date = honest "as of"` — it is a deliberately conservative freshness FLOOR across 16 contributors, and the file header at line 14 says so. The baseline anchor is a different value (the July edition prints "anchor 2026-05-01"). Also REFUTED: "invisible to every gate that claims to guard it" — `cost-index/index.html:677` already publishes, in reader prose, "**3** of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01." And `_lastReviewed` is never rendered on any cost-index page (`grep -rn '_lastReviewed' --include=*.html` returns only `admin/kpis/index.html`, for `data/kpis.json`), so the "fresh review date beside a stale anchor" juxtaposition the finding is built on does not exist on any published surface. title: /methods/ publicly describes a glossary verification cadence that exists nowhere in the codebase; the visible "Last verified" date is a git artifact
effort: 2 hours to correct the copy; 1 day for a real registry + gate
evidence: `methods/index.html:473` (indexed — no `noindex` meta) tells readers: "Glossary terms are stamped with a `verified` date… that re-asserts on the next quarterly review. The 22 most volatile terms (Google policy, Lighthouse versioning, GBP behavior) are date-checked on a 90-day cadence." The stamper is `scripts/inject-glossary-verified-stamp.mjs`. Its `gitMtime()` (lines 49–53) runs `git log --reverse --format=%cI -- "<dir>"` and takes the FIRST line — the OLDEST commit touching the directory — not a verification event; the file's own doc comment (line 9) says "git log -1", which the code does not do. This repo's history is shallow (`.git/shallow` present; first commit 2026-07-05), so all 11 stamped terms carry the identical date: `grep -rho 'datetime="[0-9-]*"'` over the stamped files returns `2026-07-11` × 11. Of the 23 slugs in `VOLATILE_SLUGS` (lines 30–41), 12 have no glossary directory at all — `doordash`, `ubereats`, `grubhub`, `opentable`, `resy`, `tock`, `schema-markup`, `menu-schema`, `aggregaterating`, `reservation-schema`, `google-business-profile`, `find-a-table`, `fid`. `ls scripts/ | grep gloss` shows 25 glossary scripts and no freshness checker; `grep -rln glossary .github/workflows/` returns only the dispatch and lighthouse workflows. Nothing implements a quarterly or 90-day review.
impact: This is a false process claim on the site's own trust-and-methods page — the page that also hosts the voice contract and the fact-gate narrative. It is the same class of failure as the fabrications the company built its whole gate stack to prevent, except it is a claim about the *company's* practice rather than about the world, which makes it worse: a reader who checks will find eleven terms all stamped the same day and twelve of the named "volatile" terms nonexistent. Also a live SEO liability — a dated freshness signal that is machine-generated from repo mechanics.
rec: Cheapest honest fix today: rewrite `methods/index.html:473` to describe what actually happens ("terms carry the date their entry last changed in the repository") and delete the "90-day cadence" and "22 most volatile" sentences. If the cadence is worth keeping, replace `gitMtime()` with a hand-maintained `data/glossary-verified.json` keyed by slug with a `date_verified`, prune `VOLATILE_SLUGS` to the 11 terms that exist, and add a gate that fails when any entry passes 90 days — a red CI line is the only thing that will make a monthly review happen.
note: The mechanism claim CONFIRMS precisely. `scripts/inject-glossary-verified-stamp.mjs:49–53` runs `git log --reverse --format=%cI -- "<dir>"` and takes `.split('\n')[0]` — the OLDEST commit — while the file's own doc comment at line 10 says "Date is derived from `git log -1 --format=%cI`". `.git/shallow` is present. All stamped files carry one date: `grep -rh -A5 'glossary-verified:start' glossary/ es/glossary/ | grep -o 'datetime="[0-9-]*"' | sort | uniq -c` → `22 datetime="2026-07-11"` (11 terms × EN/ES; the auditor wrote "11 stamped terms", correct at term level). Of the 24 entries in `VOLATILE_SLUGS` (lines 30–41 — the auditor said 23), 13 have no glossary directory: google-business-profile, find-a-table, fid, doordash, ubereats, grubhub, opentable, resy, tock, schema-markup, menu-schema, aggregaterating, reservation-schema. No freshness checker exists. `methods/index.html:473` is indexed (`noindex` count 0) and does claim the quarterly + 90-day cadence. HOWEVER the "live SEO liability" half is REFUTED: of the 11 stamped EN terms, 10 carry `noindex` — lighthouse, search-console, core-web-vitals, inp, apple-bing-maps, cls, pagespeed-insights, ttfb, opening-hours-specification, lcp. Only `glossary/gbp/` is indexed. The machine-generated freshness signal reaches search on exactly one page. Downgraded to medium: a false process claim on /methods/ (real) plus a stamper subsystem that is now almost entirely dead weight stamping frozen pages.

title: The monthly hand-written dispatch has exactly one instance, August is already 6 days late, and the reminder gate is silenced by the very data freeze it should escalate
effort: 2 hours (gate) + a founder call on cadence
evidence: `.github/workflows/cost-index-dispatch.yml` header records the 2026-07-09 founder call: monthly, hand-written, no publish cron, with `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` (38-day lag) as "the intended reminder." Exactly one edition has been published under that regime — `blog/cost-index-2026-07/`, 2026-07-09. Today is 2026-08-06; the gate currently passes: "✓ edition of 2026-07-09, data asOf 2026-08-05 (27d lag, ≤ 38)". Two structural problems. First, `MAX_LAG_DAYS = 38` measured from the *last edition* means a monthly publication can slip a full extra week before anything reds — the August reminder will not fire until ~2026-08-17. Second and worse, the gate computes `lag = dataAsOf − latestDispatch` where `dataAsOf` comes from `data/cost-index.js` `generatedAt` (lines 34–41); if the data pipeline freezes, `dataAsOf` freezes, the lag stops growing, and the editorial reminder goes green forever — the exact scenario now half-underway with 26 frozen series. Commit cadence corroborates the burstiness: 133 commits in the last 14 days but only 3 since 2026-08-01, against 57 on 2026-07-28 alone.
impact: The dispatch is the reason the newsletter exists, the reason the archive exists, and the only recurring reason a reader returns. A missed month is not a missed blog post — it breaks the of-record framing that ADR-010 spent the whole spec establishing, and it does so silently. With n=1 there is no evidence the cadence is sustainable for a full-time-employed founder, and the one mechanism meant to protect it can be silenced by an unrelated failure.
rec: Change the reminder to measure calendar months since the last edition, not data lag: fail when `today − latestDispatch > 38` regardless of `dataAsOf`, and drop the `if (!asOf) skip` early-exit that turns a data outage into an editorial pass. Separately, decide honestly whether monthly is the right cadence — quarterly, published reliably, is worth more of-record credibility than monthly published four times a year. Write that decision into an ADR the way ADR-020 handled the launch deferral.
note: All mechanics reproduce. `node scripts/check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` → "✓ edition of 2026-07-09, data asOf 2026-08-05 (27d lag, ≤ 38)". `MAX_LAG_DAYS = 38` at line 32; `dataAsOf()` at lines 34–41 reads `generatedAt` out of `data/cost-index.js`, so a frozen pipeline freezes the lag and the editorial reminder goes green — confirmed by inspection. `blog/cost-index-2026-07/` is the only edition under the new regime (`article:published_time` 2026-07-09) and `blog/drafts/` holds no August draft. One correction to the framing: the auditor treated the gate as the only cadence signal. It is not — the site makes a PUBLIC, dated promise ("monthly on the first Tuesday since August 2026") on the indexed EN and ES archive pages, and the first Tuesday of August was 2026-08-04. The promise is already broken in public, in two languages, which is stronger evidence than the internal gate lag and is the version worth acting on. See missed finding #3.

title: 758 MB and ~30–45 min/article of audio production, 7% complete, 40 manifest entries pointing at deleted pages, and not one KPI measuring whether anyone listens
effort: 2 hours to instrument; 1 day to prune; the decision is the deliverable
evidence: Assets: 114 MP3s totalling 758 MB in a 2.4 GB repo; 115 narration JSONs. Coverage from `data/article-audio.json`: 104 entries — 7 `rendered`, 48 `partial`, 47 `pending`, 2 `deferred`. `node scripts/check-audio-coverage.mjs` reports 57 issues including **MISSING-ARTICLE (40)** — every `course/*` and `es-course/*` entry still declared in the manifest though PR #530 deleted those pages on 2026-07-29 — and **NO-HASH (105)**, i.e. every narration file predates the `contentHash` field, so drift between an edited article and its spoken version is undetectable. The gate is wired warn-only (`scripts/check-all.mjs:790`, `'--warn'`), and its own remediation banner still prints the cut languages `--languages en,es,fr,it,pt,zh`. 108 pages mount a `#listen-btn`; 42 of them have no `audio.mp3` on disk (the large majority under `es/library/`), so those readers get browser speech synthesis via the `audioEl` error fallback at `assets/js/listen.js:1397–1399` rather than the promised studio edition. Cost per article is `docs/audio-pipeline.md:310`: "~30-45 minutes per article." Against all of that, `assets/js/listen.js` fires 15 distinct Plausible events (`Post Listened`, `Post Listened: Completed`, `Audio: Chapter Jump`, …) and `data/kpis.json` contains four KPIs — organic sessions, tool engagement, workshop save rate, window engagement — none of them audio.
impact: This is the clearest treadmill on the site: a differentiator that was built, instrumented, and then never measured, sitting at 7% completion with a 95-article backlog that would cost roughly 50–70 founder-hours to finish in EN+ES. It is also the surface that carries the $499 fabrication, because nobody re-renders. Meanwhile 42 pages advertise a studio audio edition the reader does not receive.
rec: Do not finish it — decide it. Add `Post Listened` and `Post Listened: Completed` to `data/kpis.json` today (the events already fire; you are one file from an answer). Give it 30 days. If listens are negligible: strip `#listen-btn` from the 42 pages with no MP3, delete the 40 dead course entries from the manifest, freeze the backlog at `deferred`, and keep only the ~60 rendered pairs. If listens are real: fix the manifest, add `contentHash` on the next render pass, and prioritise ES since that is where the gap and the fabrication both are.
note: Asset numbers verified independently: 114 `.mp3` files totalling 757.789 MB; 108 pages mount `id="listen-btn"`. `node scripts/check-audio-coverage.mjs` reports MISSING-ARTICLE and NO-HASH (105) as described — the manifest still declares 42 course entries (`course` 21 + `es-course` 21; the auditor said 40) though PR #530 deleted those pages, and the remediation banner still prints the cut `--languages en,es,fr,it,pt,zh`. Wired warn-only at `scripts/check-all.mjs:790` (`['Audio coverage (warn)', 'check-audio-coverage.mjs', '--warn']`). `data/kpis.json` contains no audio KPI. The analysis is sound and the recommendation (instrument, then decide) is the right shape. Severity corrected to medium: this is sunk cost and stale bookkeeping, not an active reader-facing falsehood — the one falsehood it carries ($499) is already counted under the ES-audio finding, and the 42 orphan manifest rows point at pages that 301 correctly via `src/worker.js:553–560`.

title: The company has publicly committed to at least eight recurring publishing cadences; four are currently overdue and one is 88 days and three cycles past due
effort: 1 day to triage + sign; then ~2 hours/month if the list is cut to canary + dispatch
evidence: Sum of standing public commitments, each verified: (1) **Warrant canary** — `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/warrant-canary.md`, "updated on the first day of each calendar month… next scheduled update is **2026-06-01**", last signed **2026-05-10** = 88 days, three cycles missed; the doc itself says "If the warrant canary disappears or stops being updated on schedule, draw your own conclusions," and it is referenced from the published threat model baked into `apps/web/lib/verify-content.generated.ts:306` which the `/verify/[slug]` route serves. (2) **Quarterly transparency report** — `docs/transparency-2026q2.md` headed "**Partial — final report at 2026-07-01**", still partial, **36 days overdue**. (3) **Monthly Cost Index dispatch** — one edition, August absent. (4) **Public changelog** — `changelog/index.html`'s newest section is "June 2026 · Trust", newest date 2026-06-27 = **40 days**, and it records neither the 2026-07-28 course/method retirement nor the 30 retired sheets — while `methods/index.html:470` tells readers "the change shows up in the /changelog/". (5) **Quarterly claim review** — asserted at `methods/index.html:431` and `about/index.html:912` ("reviewed quarterly"); no mechanism found. (6) **90-day glossary check** — `methods/index.html:473`; does not exist. (7) **21 manual `(idem)` builders**, 8 of them rendering operator-fetched data requiring the founder's Mac + API keys (`scripts/check-idem-coverage.mjs` MANUAL registry; `inject-knit-rail.mjs` flagged highest-churn). impact: Every one of these is a promise a reader or a prospective paying customer can check. Four are already checkable-and-false. For a privacy-positioned product, a warrant canary three cycles past its own stated schedule is the single most damaging of them — the document explicitly instructs readers to interpret silence as a signal. Cumulatively this is not a discipline problem; it is arithmetic. One person with a full-time restaurant job cannot service eight cadences plus a product, and the repos' own records show the pattern: 133 commits in fourteen days, then 3 in six.
rec: Cut the cadence list to what one employed person can defend, this week, in writing. Concretely: sign the canary today (it is a date and a signature, ~10 minutes, and it is the highest-liability item); either publish the Q2 transparency final or amend its header to a date you will meet; retire the two `/methods/` review claims that have no mechanism; and record the surviving list in an ADR with an owner and a red gate each — the company already proved with ADR-020 that binding a claim to a gate is the only thing that keeps it true. A published cadence with no gate behind it should be treated as a fabrication risk, not a nice-to-have.
note: Most items verify. Warrant canary: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/warrant-canary.md` header "Last updated and signed: 2026-05-10", cadence "first day of each calendar month… next scheduled update is 2026-06-01" — 88 days, 3 cycles. Transparency: `docs/transparency-2026q2.md` still headed "Partial — final report at 2026-07-01", and the route DOES exist (`apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/transparency/[quarter]/page.tsx` + the `transparency-<q>.md` branch at `apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:114–119`), so it is genuinely published and 36 days overdue — CONFIRMED. Changelog: newest section "June 2026 · Trust", newest date 2026-06-27 = 40 days, and it records neither the 2026-07-28 retirement nor the 30 retired sheets — CONFIRMED. Items 5–8 verify as described (no review mechanism in `ls scripts/ | grep -i 'claim\|verif'`; the MANUAL registry; the cross-repo re-vendor). But the canary sub-claim is REFUTED as stated: the auditor asserts it is "referenced from the published threat model baked into `apps/web/lib/verify-content.generated.ts:306` which the `/verify/[slug]` route serves" — the REFERENCE is served, the DOCUMENT is not. `apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:120–124` names `warrant-canary.md` as "Known filename shape but no public route… drop the link, keep the text" and returns `null`. There is no `/legal/warrant-canary` route. So the canary cannot signal anything to any reader whether it is signed or not; the real defect is non-publication, and with the launch deferred to 2027 and zero paying customers, three missed signatures are not the site's highest-liability item. See missed finding #4. The auditor also omitted a same-class item that HAS lapsed on an indexed page: `about/index.html:914`, "Sourcing standards last reviewed 2026-04-29" = 99 days against its own "reviewed quarterly."

title: 44% of the editorial corpus is noindex-frozen but still translated, gated, narrated, and hand-rebuilt
effort: 1 week
evidence: Counted directly: 262 of 1,368 HTML pages carry `noindex`. Within the editorial surfaces the ratio is far higher — `library` 21 of 40 frozen, `es/library` 21 of 40, `glossary` 73 of 171, `es/glossary` 73 of 171, `sheets` 18 of 33, `es/sheets` 18 of 33, `blog` 4 of 20, `es/blog` 3 of 12. `check-positioning-drift` confirms the shape: "1066 indexed article(s) scanned (260 frozen, skipped)". These pages are not dormant in cost: they remain in EN↔ES parity (`check-locale-parity`, `check-sheets-parity`), they carry audio (of the 42 Listen buttons without an MP3, most are frozen ES library pages), they are hubs' link targets by explicit design (`check-positioning-drift.mjs` ALLOW: "Glossary hub — lists all 171 terms including frozen ones"), and they are rebuilt by the 21 manual `(idem)` builders — `inject-knit-rail.mjs` is registered as the highest-churn one, run "after any article add, freeze, or retire." 645 of 1,368 pages are Spanish, so every editorial obligation is paid twice.

Freeze-don't-delete was the right call for link integrity, but it was implemented as "keep maintaining, just hide" rather than "stop spending." The founder is paying full editorial rent on assets earning zero.
rec: Separate "reachable" from "maintained." Add a `frozen: true` marker (a meta tag or a manifest) and teach the parity, audio-coverage, and knit-rail tooling to skip it — a frozen page keeps its URL and its inbound links but stops demanding an ES mirror, an MP3, or a rail rebuild. That is a one-week change that permanently halves the recurring editorial surface. Then decide separately whether the 18 frozen brand/design sheets (already named a prune candidate in CLAUDE.md) should 301 to `/sheets/` like the course pack did.
note: Per-surface ratios reproduce exactly: library 21/40, es/library 21/40, glossary 73/171, es/glossary 73/171, sheets 18/33, es/sheets 18/33, blog 4/20, es/blog 3/12. My whole-site count differs slightly from the auditor's (256 of 1,314 `index.html` files vs their 262 of 1,368 — they counted all `.html`, not just `index.html`); the shape is identical. `check-positioning-drift` confirms "1066 indexed article(s) scanned (260 frozen, skipped)". The cost argument holds: I verified the glossary hubs still link all 171 terms including frozen ones, that `check-locale-parity` still demands ES mirrors sitewide, and that `inject-knit-rail.mjs` is registered as the highest-churn manual `(idem)` builder run after any freeze. Severity medium is right — this is recurring cost, not a reader-facing falsehood — and the `frozen: true` marker recommendation is the correct shape.

title: The fact gate polices its own registry impeccably but nothing walks the prose asking whether a number is registered — and the registry's edges are quietly rotting
effort: 1 day
evidence: `scripts/check-fabrications.mjs` is explicitly a blocklist of five named May-2026 patterns (header, lines 25–46), and `data/sourced-claims.json` holds 47 claims — all with a `date_verified` inside 90 days, none stale. But the ratio to the corpus is the finding: 34 indexed EN library+blog pages contain 3,481 `$`/`%` tokens in prose against 106 `<details class="cite">` drawers and 47 registry entries. Nothing gates the gap; the three valid patterns in `docs/fact-check.md` are honour-system. The rot is already visible where the honour system is weakest: `check-claim-usage.mjs` reports 10 claims with an empty `used_in`, four of which — `fivestars_pricing`, `como_pricing`, `mailchimp_pricing`, `klaviyo_pricing` — are third-party SaaS prices that `methods/index.html:458` publicly states are "Used in the /library/loyalty-program-roi/" article. That article is indexed (`noindex` count 0), `dateModified` 2026-06-10, states "Toast Rewards is roughly $50/month; Square Loyalty starts at $25/month", renders no source URLs, and carries exactly 1 cite drawer. All 19 claims in the 2026-05-14 batch — nine of them volatile vendor pricing pages — are 84 days old. Because `used_in` is empty, the claim-usage gate can never report those edges as rotting; the registry does not know the article exists.
impact: The registry is the artifact the company points at to prove it does not invent. Its internal consistency is excellent and its external coverage is thin, and the thinnest part is the most perishable content on the site: competitor pricing, which changes without notice and which an operator will check. A wrong Toast or Square price on an indexed comparison article is a small credibility loss on its own and a large one for a company whose pitch is "we show what we measured."
rec: Two moves. (1) Backfill `used_in` for the four loyalty-pricing claims so the existing gate can see them, and add a `date_verified` age tier to `check-claim-usage.mjs`: warn at 180 days, fail at 365 for any claim whose `notes` or `source_name` indicates vendor pricing. (2) Accept that a full prose allowlist is not affordable, but narrow the honour system where it is cheapest: a gate that flags any indexed page containing a `$N/month`-shaped token with zero cite drawers and zero registry edges. That is a handful of pages, and it is where the falsifiable claims live.
note: The concrete rot verifies precisely, which is what carries this finding. `library/loyalty-program-roi/index.html` has `noindex` count 0, `dateModified": "2026-06-10"`, exactly 1 `details class="cite"` drawer, and prose reading "$50/month; Square Loyalty starts at $25/month". `methods/index.html:458` publicly states those vendor prices are "Used in the /library/loyalty-program-roi/ loyalty-program comparison" — while `node scripts/check-claim-usage.mjs` reports `fivestars_pricing, como_pricing, mailchimp_pricing, klaviyo_pricing` among 10 claims "registered but not cited anywhere", i.e. empty `used_in`, so the gate structurally cannot age them. I independently confirmed all 47 registry entries carry a `date_verified` and that the oldest is 84 days (the 2026-05-14 batch: toast_rewards_pricing, square_loyalty_pricing, uber_eats_published_rates, grubhub_published_rates, doordash_marketplace_tiers, klaviyo/mailchimp/fivestars pricing…). One correction to the auditor's own bookkeeping: they reported the gate as "149 edges resolving with 0 violations" in their STRENGTHS section and did not mention that the same run emits 23 warnings of the form "X exists but does not render <url>" — the registry's other soft edge, and the same honour-system gap they are describing here.

title: 313 shipped pages carry a legacy 4-hour reply promise the canon retired; the gate that should catch it is unwired and cannot match the entity actually shipped
effort: 1 day
evidence:
`grep -rc 'Mon–Fri'` matches **313** HTML files; the canonical form "Mondays through Fridays" appears on **3**. A representative footer, `library/restaurant-prime-cost/index.html:1236`: `

Reply: within 4 hours Mon–Fri; weekends by Monday.

` — and 315 files contain "within 4 hours". `scripts/check-reply-time-canon.mjs` FORBIDDEN list (lines 79–82) enumerates `'mon–fri'` (literal en-dash) and `'mon–fri'` (numeric entity) but **not** `mon–fri`, the named entity every one of those 313 pages uses. The gate is also one of the four in `check-gate-coverage.mjs`'s `UNWIRED` registry, whose justification states: "every shipped surface is already canonical — which is the useful finding." Whether or not it is met, it is a commitment nobody re-decided when the services line was retired — and the mechanism meant to keep footer copy honest cannot see the form the footer actually uses. rec: Add `'mon–fri'` and `'lun–vie'` to the FORBIDDEN list, then decide the copy question before wiring: either sweep the 313 footers to the canonical phrasing, or — better for a product-only company with no services line — replace the reply SLA with something you control, and delete the `methods/index.html:431` "Studio claims… reviewed quarterly" bullet with it. Only then wire the gate. Also extend `RETIRED_VOCAB` with services-line terms ("studio", "reply within", "audit", "capacity") so the drift gate covers the retirement it was named for.
note: Reproduced line for line. `grep -rlc 'Mon–Fri' --include=*.html .` → 313 files. `scripts/check-reply-time-canon.mjs` FORBIDDEN (lines 79–82) lists `'mon–fri'` (literal en-dash) and `'mon–fri'` (numeric entity) but not the named entity `mon–fri`, which is the form every one of those 313 pages ships; the script header (lines 8–14) states the canonical form is "Mondays through Fridays". Running it: 2 violations — `docs/editorial/the-hundred.md:2239` and `scripts/check-gate-coverage.mjs:73` — confirming both that the UNWIRED entry's recorded status ("FAILS — 1 violation") is stale and that the registry entry created the second violation it documents. The registry's justification at check-gate-coverage.mjs:69–76, "every shipped surface is already canonical — which is the useful finding", is false on 313 pages. Severity medium is right. The recommendation should be sequenced as written (fix copy, then extend FORBIDDEN, then wire) because the repo's own rule forbids wiring a failing gate.

title: The audio numeric-parity gate whitelists spoken numbers off audio TIMESTAMPS — an indexed page narrates the retired $499 offer in Spanish and the gate is green
evidence: `scripts/check-audio-fabrications.mjs` `sourceNumbers(dir)` reads the RAW BYTES of `index.html` and `audio.json` and feeds them to `extractNumbers()`, whose regex `/\d[\d.,   ]*\d|\d/g` then splits every match on `\D+` — so the float `499.57` yields the token `499`. `library/third-party-delivery-comparison/audio.es.json` speaks, verbatim: "Auditoría de 499 dólares — el diagnóstico escrito si prefieres ver tu mezcla de canales en papel". `grep -o '.\{0,40\}499.\{0,20\}' library/third-party-delivery-comparison/index.html` returns NOTHING (the article is clean) and the EN `audio.json` has no `499` in any chunk text — its only `499` is `': 499.57'`, an audio timing value. The gate therefore emits no warning for this file. The page carries `noindex` count 0 — it is INDEXED. `blog/instagram-as-restaurant-seo-strategy-2026/audio.es.json` speaks "499 dólares de auditoría — si quieres que reescriba los últimos 30 títulos" and is suppressed the same way (that page is frozen). Thirteen `audio.es.json` files contain the string `499`; the gate flags seven.
impact: The auditor reported 7 tracks speaking the retired $499 audit and called the detection "genuinely unusual… only the severity tier is wrong." The detection is in fact structurally leaky in exactly the direction that matters: any spoken figure that coincidentally appears as a timestamp fragment, a CSS pixel value, or an inline-style number anywhere in the page's raw bytes is silently accepted. On a 1,300-page site with second-resolution audio timings from 0 to ~1200s, essentially every 3-digit number under 1200 is pre-whitelisted. The largest single ES-narration false commercial claim on an INDEXED page is invisible to the gate the company treats as its narration fact gate.
rec: Change `sourceNumbers()` to extract from the article's PROSE and from `audio.json`'s `chunks[].text` only — never from raw file bytes, never from timing fields. Strip `<script>`, `<style>`, and all attribute values from `index.html` before extraction (the same discipline `check-article-graphics.mjs` rule 8 already enforces for autolink markers). Then re-run: the count of flagged ES tracks will rise from 7 to at least 9, including the indexed `library/third-party-delivery-comparison`. Only after that is the warn→fail promotion the auditor recommends meaningful.

title: Both glossary hubs — EN and ES, indexed, the entry point to 171 terms — advertise two retired tools in present-tense prose, and check-retired-links prints "chrome/funnel surfaces clean"
evidence: `glossary/index.html` body prose: "Brand Suite generates a palette + tokens to start" and "Brand Suite extracts a palette from an uploaded logo in the browser" and "The Menu Copy Inspector teaches how to read your own copy critically." `es/glossary/index.html` carries the ES mirrors. Both hubs have `noindex` count 0. Both tools are in `scripts/check-retired-links.mjs` `RETIRED` (lines 34–52) — they resolve only via the Worker 301 to `/tools/`, where they are not listed. Yet that gate's `CHROME` list (lines 58–70) enumerates `index.html`, `tools/index.html`, `cost-index/index.html`, `library/index.html`, `never/`, `security/`, `ai/`, `trust/`, `receipts/`, `methods/`, `ledger/` — and OMITS `glossary/index.html`, `es/glossary/index.html`, `sheets/index.html`, `blog/index.html`. The gate consequently reports: "check-retired-links: chrome/funnel surfaces clean. 193 in-content page(s) still 301-link a retired path (tracked roadmap debt)." I counted the warn bucket by index status: 73 INDEXED pages (EN + ES) hard-link a retired tool, including `library/ai-mode-reservation-strategy`, `library/commission-free-online-ordering-restaurants`, `library/toast-vs-square-vs-clover-for-restaurants`, and 8 indexed ES library/blog pages.
impact: This is the CLAUDE.md "root list" lesson recurring a fourth time, in the gate written specifically to stop a hub advertising a dead product — the gate's own header says the homepage CTA "Run free audit" pointing at the retired audit is the failure it exists to prevent. The glossary hub is the site's largest indexed hub. Its prose makes present-tense product claims ("generates", "extracts", "teaches") about tools that no longer exist, in two languages, to a reader who then 301s to a catalog that does not list them. `check-positioning-drift.mjs` cannot see it either: its `RETIRED_VOCAB` contains website-building words, not retired tool names.
rec: Add `glossary/index.html`, `es/glossary/index.html`, `sheets/index.html`, `es/sheets/index.html`, `blog/index.html`, `es/blog/index.html`, and `learn/index.html` to `CHROME` in `check-retired-links.mjs` — hubs are chrome by function, not by directory. Fix the four hub sentences first (the gate would red the deploy otherwise). Then, separately from the FAIL tier, promote the 73 INDEXED in-content pages out of "tracked roadmap debt": a warn bucket that mixes 131 frozen pages with 73 indexed ones hides the only half that can mislead a reader.

title: The site publicly promises the dispatch "monthly on the first Tuesday since August 2026" in EN and ES — the first Tuesday was 2026-08-04 and no edition exists
evidence: `cost-index/weekly/index.html` lede, verbatim: "The Restaurant Cost Index publishes a dated dispatch — monthly on the first Tuesday since August 2026, weekly before that." `es/cost-index/weekly/index.html`: "mensual el primer martes desde agosto de 2026, semanal antes de eso." Both pages have `noindex` count 0. The first Tuesday of August 2026 was 2026-08-04; today is 2026-08-06. `ls blog/ | grep cost-index` returns only `cost-index-2026-07` and the four `cost-index-week-*` slugs — no August edition, no draft (`ls blog/drafts/`). The reminder gate is green: `node scripts/check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` → "✓ edition of 2026-07-09, data asOf 2026-08-05 (27d lag, ≤ 38)".
impact: The auditor framed this as an internal cadence risk ("the August reminder will not fire until ~2026-08-17"). It is stronger than that: the company has published a specific, checkable, dated cadence promise on two indexed pages in two languages, and broke it two days ago. This is the same class as the /methods/ glossary claim the auditor rated high — a false process claim on the site's own surface — except it sits on the flagship publication's archive rather than a trust page, and the honesty of the whole Cost Index rests on it. It also means the archive page simultaneously promises a monthly first-Tuesday series and lists a newest row of 2026-07-06.
rec: Either publish the August edition this week, or amend both ledes today to a cadence the founder will actually hold — the ADR-020 precedent (defer publicly, in writing, with a date) is the house pattern. Then change `MAX_LAG_DAYS` to measure `today − latestDispatch` rather than `dataAsOf − latestDispatch` so the reminder tracks the promise that is published, not a data field that freezes when the pipeline does.

title: The warrant canary has no public route at all — apps/web deliberately drops every link to it while published legal and verify pages tell readers it exists
evidence: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/apps/web/lib/markdown.ts:120–124`: "// Known filename shape but no public route (warrant-canary.md, the runbooks/* files without a verify slug, community-templates.md, *-csv-export*, msa-template*, i18n-legal-docs.md): signal 'drop the link, keep the text'" — followed by `return null;`. Compare the branch immediately above it (lines 114–119), which DOES route `transparency-<q>.md` → `/legal/transparency/<q>`, and `apps/web/app/(marketing)/legal/transparency/[quarter]/page.tsx` exists. There is no analogous route for the canary: `find apps/web/app -path '*canary*'` returns nothing. Meanwhile `apps/web/lib/legal-content.generated.ts` references `docs/warrant-canary.md` at lines 143, 259–260, 281, 762, 892, 915 and 1560, and `apps/web/lib/verify-content.generated.ts:306` (served by `/verify/[slug]`) tells readers: "**Warrant canary** at `docs/warrant-canary.md` removes a sentence if any of the listed processes have been received, so customers can detect the gag-order case." The doc itself (`docs/warrant-canary.md`) is signed 2026-05-10 with "The next scheduled update is **2026-06-01**" and "If the warrant canary disappears or stops being updated on schedule, draw your own conclusions."
impact: The auditor called the 88-day staleness "the single most damaging" cadence miss. The actual defect is worse in kind and milder in blast radius: the canary is not published anywhere a reader can reach, so its "continued presence is itself a signal" mechanism cannot function at all — a customer cannot draw any conclusion because there is nothing to look at. What IS published is the residual-risk paragraph on `/verify/[slug]` claiming the canary lets customers detect the gag-order case. That is an unbacked security claim on an indexed marketing page. (Blast radius is currently bounded: pre-revenue, private beta, launch deferred to 2027 per ADR-020 — hence the staleness alone is not high-severity.)
rec: One decision, then one commit. If the canary is a real control: add `warrant-canary.md` to the routing branch beside `transparency-<q>` with a `/legal/warrant-canary` page, sign it today, and add a `check-*.mjs` that fails when the signature date is more than 45 days old — the repo's own rule is that a check script must be wired in the same commit. If it is not a real control at this stage: delete the sentence from `verify-content.generated.ts:306` and the seven `legal-content.generated.ts` references, and say in the threat model that the canary starts at GA. Do not leave a published claim pointing at an unroutable file.

title: /about/ publishes "Sourcing standards last reviewed April 29, 2026" — 99 days — beside its own "reviewed quarterly" claim, and /methods/ still describes the reply SLA as a live "Studio" commitment
evidence: `about/index.html:912` (indexed, `noindex` count 0): "…all benchmarks are dated in the tool footers and **reviewed quarterly**", and the section closes at line 914 with `Sourcing standards last reviewed <time datetime="2026-04-29">April 29, 2026</time>.` 2026-04-29 → 2026-08-06 is 99 days; a quarterly cadence lapsed on 2026-07-28. `methods/index.html:431`, in the numbered claim-types list: "**Studio claims** — 'Reply within 4 hours, Mon–Fri.' These describe **how the studio operates today**; they appear in the footer and on /about/, and they're **reviewed quarterly**." CLAUDE.md records the services line retired and `/studio/` repurposed as the company page. No script implements either review: `ls scripts/ | grep -i 'claim\|verif'` returns `build-claims-json`, `check-claim-usage`, `check-security-claims`, `check-tool-verified-stamp`, `inject-claims-rows`, `inject-glossary-verified-stamp`, `inject-tool-verified-stamp`, `verify-cost-index-sources` — none reads a review cadence.
impact: The auditor listed "quarterly claim review" as cadence item (5) with "no mechanism found" but never checked whether the visible date had already lapsed. It has, by 9 days, and it is stamped in a `<time>` element on the indexed /about/ page — a machine-readable, self-falsifying freshness signal, the same failure mode as the glossary stamp but on a higher-traffic trust page. The /methods/:431 wording additionally asserts, on the site's canon page, that a retired services line "operates today" — which is the positioning-drift failure the company built a gate for, in a vocabulary that gate cannot see (`RETIRED_VOCAB` is website-building words only).
rec: Delete the `<time>` stamp from about/index.html:914 rather than bumping it — an undated honest statement beats a dated one nobody can keep. Rewrite methods/index.html:431 to drop "Studio" and "how the studio operates today", and settle the 4-hour SLA question in the same edit as the `Mon–Fri` sweep (finding 10) so 313 footers and the canon page change together. Add "studio", "reply within", "capacity" to `RETIRED_VOCAB` in `check-positioning-drift.mjs` so the services retirement is covered by the gate named for retirements.

title: The indexed Spanish Cost-Index archive presents a complete Spanish edition series whose every dispatch link lands on English-only prose — and there is no Spanish dispatch at all
evidence: `es/cost-index/weekly/index.html` has `noindex` count 0 and its table's "Abrir despacho" column resolves to `/blog/cost-index-week-2026-06-05/`, `-06-16/`, `-06-18/`, `-07-06/` — all English. `ls -d es/blog/cost-index*` returns nothing: the Spanish blog has zero dispatch editions. The ES lede promises a Spanish-facing cadence ("El Índice de costos de restaurantes publica un despacho fechado — mensual el primer martes desde agosto de 2026") and the ES data note promises "Cada edición es un registro permanente y citable." `node scripts/check-locale-parity.mjs` passes for this surface (it compares page-for-page mirrors, and the archive PAGE has one); `node scripts/check-hreflang-orphans.mjs` reports "clean. (1326 HTML pages scanned)" because the EN dispatches correctly declare only `hreflang="en"` and `x-default`. CLAUDE.md records the design intent — driver `*_es` fields exist but "the dispatch is EN-only so they aren't rendered yet" — but that decision is not surfaced to the Spanish reader anywhere on the ES archive page.
impact: 645 of 1,368 pages are Spanish and every editorial obligation is paid twice — except on the flagship publication, where the ES surface is a shell that promises a series it does not have. A Spanish operator arriving at an indexed page that says "esta es la serie completa" clicks any row and gets English. Both parity gates pass, which is the domain's characteristic failure: they measure the PRESENCE of a mirrored page, not whether the mirror leads anywhere Spanish. It also means the auditor's "every editorial obligation is paid twice" framing is wrong in the one place it would have mattered most.
rec: Cheapest honest fix, today: add one sentence to the ES lede stating the dispatch is published in English only and linking `/es/cost-index/` for the Spanish data surfaces, and mark the "Abrir despacho" column header accordingly. Then make the choice explicitly — ES dispatch or no ES dispatch — and record it in an ADR beside ADR-010, because the `*_es` driver fields already carry the cost of the undecided version. Add an assertion to `check-locale-parity.mjs` (or a small sibling) that an ES page whose outbound content links are ≥80% EN is flagged: page-for-page mirroring is not locale parity.

title: The published headline basket number cannot be derived from the published data, and two live surfaces disagree by 10x
effort: 3 hours for the fix + gate; a founder call on the correction note
evidence: `scripts/build-cost-index.mjs:351` runs `out.basket = computeBasket(out)`; `computeBasket` (:83-89) reads `pts[0].trend.pct` for each ingredient and feeds `B.basketTrend` (`tools/_shared/cost-basket.js:34-74`, a weighted median). `.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml` then runs `scripts/reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs`, which at :60-66 rewrites `points[0].trend.pct` and `.dir` — and never recomputes the basket. I recomputed with the company's own library: committed `basket.pct` = −0.005322 (agreement 0.505); recomputed from the committed points = 0.000 flat (agreement 0.103). Committed contributor pcts match no vintage in the file — tomato is committed at −53.68% while its latest point reads +2.38%; eggs committed −14.36% vs +148.21% live. `cost-index/index.html:672-676` publishes '−0.5%', 'agreement 51%', teal 'down' band. `blog/cost-index-week-2026-07-06/index.html` publishes '−5.0%' and `cost-index/week-2026-07-06.json` `basket.pct: -0.0496` — both still live. `cost-index/methodology/index.html` claims 'the whole surface can be re-derived from the open data'; the CC0 export `cost-index/index.json` has fields `slug,name,unit,basis,currency,priceLowUsd,priceMedianUsd,priceHighUsd,spreadPct,pctInWindow,confidence,asOf,sources,url` — no trend field, so the basket is not reproducible from the open data at all. `scripts/check-cost-index-sync.mjs:177-190` validates only that `basket.pct` is a finite number and that contributors are vendored; its comment reads 'build-cost-index recomputes it from the vendored set' — it trusts the builder whose output is then overwritten.
impact: The single number the whole publication is named after is wrong, is published at two different values on two live pages, and is not checkable — against a positioning that is explicitly 'verification is the moat; opacity is the risk' and 'a number you can check, not a number you have to trust'. One informed reader (a journalist, an AI-answer citation, a competitor, an investor) recomputing the headline destroys the only asset that differentiates Muntin from a CSV of USDA data. This is not technical tidiness; it is the product claim being false.
rec: (1) Move the basket computation after reconciliation — either call `computeBasket` from `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs` or reorder so `build-cost-index.mjs` runs the curve reconciliation before line 351. (2) Add an invariant gate to `check-cost-index-sync.mjs`: `basket.pct` must equal `weightedMedian(points[0].trend.pct)` over the declared weights, and each `contributors[i].pct` must equal that ingredient's committed `points[0].trend.pct`, to 1e-9. (3) Add `trend.pct` + `trend.dir` + the frozen weights to `cost-index/index.json` so the reproducibility claim becomes true. (4) Decide explicitly what to do about the published 2026-07-06 edition — a dated correction note is more on-brand than a silent rewrite, and slugs are final-forever anyway.
note: Reproduced to the digit. `node -e` with the repo's own `tools/_shared/cost-basket.js` over `data/cost-index.json` points[0]: recomputed pct 0 / dir flat / agreement 0.103; committed basket.pct −0.005322241098086206 / agreement 0.505. Per-contributor divergence reproduced (chicken-breast −0.53 committed vs −29.07 live; eggs −14.36 vs +148.21; tomato −53.68 vs +2.38). `scripts/build-cost-index.mjs:351` `out.basket = computeBasket(out)` runs BEFORE `.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml:91` `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs`, which at :62-63 writes only `trend.pct`/`trend.dir`. `cost-index/index.html:673-677` renders −0.5%, agreement 51%, and the 5-above/8-below/3-flat spread — I hand-classified the 16 committed contributor pcts against cost-basket.js's ±0.5% FLAT band and got exactly 5/8/3, so the spread is derived from the same stale vintage. `es/cost-index/index.html` mirrors −0.5%. CC0 export confirmed trend-free: `build-cost-index-pages.mjs:1385` `pctInWindow` is median-position-within-range, not a trend. Methodology quote is verbatim real ('the whole surface can be re-derived from the open data'). ONE CORRECTION to the framing: the committed basket is not arbitrary — it is the pre-reconcile multi-source blend, and it matches every point's internal `label` string exactly (chicken-breast label 'down -0.5% over the window'). So the headline is internally consistent with a vintage that exists nowhere on the rendered site. 'Wrong' is less precise than 'orphaned'.

title: The refresh workflow rebuilds two derived artifacts then discards them, blocking the deploy and freezing the founder's public pledge
effort: 30 minutes for the fix; 3 hours for the anti-recurrence gate
evidence: At HEAD (`7808827cc data(cost-index): measured read 2026-08-05`), `node scripts/check-cost-index-picker.mjs` exits 1: '✗ grapefruit: dollarRef false != recomputed true'. That gate is wired at `scripts/check-all.mjs:492`, and `check-all.mjs` is in the Cloudflare `build.command` in `wrangler.jsonc` — so the deploy is blocked. Root cause: `.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml` runs `node scripts/build-cost-index-picker.mjs` (with a comment that literally predicts this bug: 'a refresh that … flips a firm-$ reference leaves it stale and trips check-cost-index-picker'), but `data/cost-index-picker.js` is absent from that step's `git add` list, and the following `git checkout -- .` discards it. `check-cost-index-picker` is also absent from the workflow's own gates step, so the refresh stays green while the deploy goes red. I bisected: green at 10f983843 (07-29), RED at bedc415f0 (07-31), green at 841222923 (08-03), RED at HEAD (08-05). The file has been hand-repaired twice already — `git log -- data/cost-index-picker.js` shows '2026-07-16 chore(cost-index): reconcile picker + revisions derived data to unblock deploy' and '2026-07-28 fix(ci): regenerate lockfloat + picker stale after the main merge'. Second casualty, same cause: `node scripts/inject-about-cost-read.mjs --check` exits 1 ('would update about/index.html, es/about/index.html'); `about/index.html` currently reads 'Muntin Restaurant Basket as of 2026-07-21' and 'Eggs ▲ +71.7%' while the live data is 2026-08-04 and eggs reads +148.21%. `about/` is likewise missing from the staging list, and `inject-about-cost-read` is not in `check-all.mjs`, so nothing outside the refresh ever notices.
impact: Measured reads are landing in git and stopping there. The site cannot deploy, so the fresh-data promise — the entire reason the Cost Index exists — dies at the repo boundary with no alarm anywhere. The /about/ page, the human trust surface that says 'the numbers I check on my shifts', is publishing a 16-day-old read under a pledge of currency. This is the third recurrence of the same staging-list omission; it will recur again.
rec: Add `data/cost-index-picker.js about/index.html es/about/index.html` to the `git add` list in the 'Commit the measured read' step, and add `node scripts/check-cost-index-picker.mjs` to the workflow's gates step so the refresh reds instead of the deploy. Then kill the class: write a gate that reads the workflow's build steps, collects every artifact path those builders write, and fails if any is not in the staging list — the staging list is exactly the hand-maintained root list this repo has already learned three times not to trust.
note: `node scripts/check-cost-index-picker.mjs` → EXIT=1, 'grapefruit: dollarRef false != recomputed true'. Wired at `scripts/check-all.mjs:492`. Running `node scripts/build-cost-index-picker.mjs` produces a 3-line diff to `data/cost-index-picker.js` and the gate then EXIT=0 — so the fix is exactly the omitted artifact. `node scripts/inject-about-cost-read.mjs --check` → EXIT=1 for `about/index.html` + `es/about/index.html`. Both paths are git-tracked (`git ls-files` confirms), so `git checkout -- .` at cost-index-refresh.yml:313 reverts them; neither is in the `git add` list at :302-312. ONE CORRECTION that strengthens the finding: `inject-about-cost-read.mjs --check` IS in the workflow's gates step (cost-index-refresh.yml:240) — the auditor said it wasn't. It passes only because the gates step runs before the commit step throws the file away. The gate verifies the builder ran; nothing verifies its output survived. That is a sharper statement of the defect than the one filed.

title: The of-record edition publishes a 'high confidence' rating the company's own calibration says has never been earned
effort: 3 hours
evidence: `blog/cost-index-week-2026-07-06/index.html`: 'the weighted basket reads -5.0% against its baseline at high confidence' and 'at high confidence across 16 contributing ingredients'. The citable CC0 dataset `cost-index/week-2026-07-06.json` carries `basket.confidence: "high"`. Against that: `data/cost-index-health.json` records `highEligible: 0` and `byConfidence {medium:20, low:62, directional:18}` — zero high across all 100 reads. `scripts/build-cost-index-dispatch.mjs:236-243` explicitly strips a high label with the comment 'the label has no realized track record anywhere … data/cost-confidence-calibration.json has zero high-tier rows', but that guard operates on the scaffold and cannot govern hand-written prose (ADR-012 made the dispatch manual) or a snapshot already written. `scripts/check-cost-index-confidence.mjs` passes — because its scope is '162 ingredient read(s) + hub composite (EN+ES) + /about/ read (EN+ES)'. The publication itself is not in the gate's root list, which is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md's 'declare roots, justify omissions' rule was written for.
