impact: The flagship publication asserts a confidence tier the company's own methodology page says it cannot reach, on a page under Don's byline, in a CC0 dataset built for citation. For a company whose differentiation is 'we label our limits', an overstated confidence on the of-record artifact is more damaging than a wrong number — it is the wrong number plus a claim of certainty about it.
rec: Widen `check-cost-index-confidence.mjs`'s root list to include `blog/cost-index-week-*/` (EN+ES) and the `cost-index/week-*.json` snapshots, asserting that no published confidence tier exceeds the max tier present in `data/cost-index-health.json` for that edition. Correct the 2026-07-06 post and snapshot in place with a dated note. Carry the same root-list widening into the basket-invariant gate from finding 1.
note: Strings reproduced: `blog/cost-index-week-2026-07-06/index.html` says 'at high confidence across 16 contributing ingredients'; `cost-index/week-2026-07-06.json` `basket.confidence:"high"`; `data/cost-index-health.json` summary `{total:100, byConfidence:{medium:20,low:62,directional:18}, highEligible:0}`. But the auditor conflates two different scales. `basket.confidence` is computed by `tools/_shared/cost-basket.js:64-66` from coverage≥0.6 ∧ n≥6 ∧ agreement≥0.6 — a documented basket-level formula the edition legitimately cleared. health.json's `highEligible:0` is a PER-INGREDIENT tier whose blocker is per-row 'add a 2nd independent-agency wholesale $ level on the same basis'. They are not the same tier and the report treats them as one. The honesty concern survives only because the company itself equates them at `build-cost-index-dispatch.mjs:236-243` — whose comment is dated 2026-07-06, i.e. the guard was written in response to this exact edition, so recurrence is already structurally blocked and live exposure is one dated post plus one snapshot. The recommendation is also wrong: `check-cost-index-confidence.mjs:15-19` states 'It does NOT invent or grade confidence — it only guards that the honest framing... cannot silently disappear.' Asking it to grade tiers is a new gate, not a root-list widening. Downgrade to medium.

title: NOAA has been dark 66 days across 15 seafood series; three basket contributors are frozen and date the headline
effort: 1 day for the diagnostic + triage; 1 week if re-sourcing seafood
evidence: Recomputed against 2026-08-06 from `data/cost-index.json`: 18 series ≥30 days stale, 17 of them last read 2026-06-01 (66d), plus ground-beef at 57d. Zero are past the 120-day cliff — the first is 2026-09-29, so the board's '~2026-08-29 squid cliff' has moved out. `scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` reports 16 unexpected + 10 known-latent (74 of 100 fresh within 45d). Three are basket contributors — shrimp (w 0.04), vegetable-oil (w 0.12), salmon-fillet (w 0.03) — 0.19 of the 1.07 declared weight, i.e. ~18% of the basket is priced off a 66-day-old read. Because `tools/_shared/cost-basket.js:45` sets `asOf` to the oldest contributing date, `basket.asOf` is 2026-06-01. `scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:791` then overrides it for display (`const asOf = newestAsOf`), so the hub chip reads 'as of 2026-08-04' with the lag disclosed only in prose ('3 of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01'). `scripts/fetch-cost-index-sources.mjs:126-142` documents the diagnosis — 'the NOAA family was 0-for-15 while AMS was 74-for-74 … NOAA is keyless, so no amount of secret configuration would have surfaced it' — and the reporting fix landed 2026-07-30, but the outage itself remains undiagnosed.
impact: A fifth of the headline basket has not moved since June while the page stamps an August date. The seafood category — the one an operator most wants a read on because it is the hardest to check — is dead across the board. Every day this sits, the terminal-retirement path (ADR-021, zero archive entries, never exercised on a real feed) gets closer to firing on 15 pages at once, untested in production.
rec: Run the one diagnostic the container cannot: `node scripts/fetch-cost-index-sources.mjs --live --out /tmp/ci.json` on the Mac and read the 'source family/families FAILED' block. Then make a per-feed call — re-source (the Census/USITC import unit value and state ex-vessel families in `docs/cost-index-sourcing-master.md` are named as rescues for squid/clams/trout and are simply unbuilt) or move to `KNOWN_SOURCE_LATENT` with a dated comment, and promote `--strict`. Separately: decide whether a basket contributor frozen >45 days should be dropped from the basket with stated coverage rather than carried, since `coverage` currently reads 1.0 while 18% of the weight is two months old.
note: Recomputed against 2026-08-06 over points[0].asOf: 18 series ≥30d, 17 at exactly 66d (2026-06-01), ground-beef 57d, 0 ≥120d. Basket weights sum 1.07 (16 declared); shrimp 0.04 + vegetable-oil 0.12 + salmon-fillet 0.03 = 0.19 = 17.8%. `basket.asOf` is 2026-06-01 in the file; the hub chip renders `data-asof="2026-08-04"`. Prose disclosure ('3 of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01') present. ONE CORRECTION: 2 of the 18 are not NOAA — vegetable-oil's provenance is bls/fred and pork-belly's is bls only. That matters operationally: the recommended NOAA-only live diagnostic will not surface either, and vegetable-oil is the single heaviest frozen basket weight (0.12).

title: The storefront's NOAA outage silently removed 8 of 32 market-prior slugs from the paid product, and no gate in either repo names the link
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/packages/cost-alerts/data/ingredient-aliases.json` declares 32 slugs the inventory market-prior can ever resolve. `apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json` contains 24. The missing 8 are pork-belly, salmon-fillet, whole-salmon, shrimp, tuna-loin, scallops, whole-lobster, vegetable-oil — precisely the storefront's frozen set (`vendor-cost-index.mjs` keeps the latest wholesale-basis point, and a frozen index-basis series produces none). The snapshot feeds five real call sites, not a dormant one: `apps/api/src/lib/queue.ts:56`, `cost-watch-scan.ts:31`, `plate-cost-tree.ts:34`, `routes/insights.ts:32`, `routes/inventory.ts:40`. `apps/api/scripts/vendor-cost-index.mjs` reports slug counts but nothing compares vendored-vs-registry, and `scripts/check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs` measures age, not coverage.
impact: 25% of the paid product's market-prior universe — and every seafood item, the highest-value category for an inventory count — silently returns null because of an upstream data outage in a different repository. An operator counting shrimp gets 'uncovered' with no explanation. This is the cross-repo coupling actually biting, and it is invisible in both repos' green CI.
rec: Extend `check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs` to assert vendored-slug coverage against the alias registry and print the missing list on every green run (the same pattern `check-pricing-consistency.mjs` uses to print 'NOT BILLABLE TODAY'). Make `vendor-cost-index.mjs` exit non-zero, or at minimum warn loudly, when coverage drops below the prior snapshot's.
note: Reproduced exactly. `packages/cost-alerts/data/ingredient-aliases.json` → 32 slugs under `.ingredients`; `apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json` → 24 under `.ingredients`; set difference is precisely [pork-belly, salmon-fillet, whole-salmon, shrimp, tuna-loin, scallops, whole-lobster, vegetable-oil], zero extras. Five import sites confirmed by grep: queue.ts:56, cost-watch-scan.ts:31, plate-cost-tree.ts:34, routes/insights.ts:32, routes/inventory.ts:40. Same correction as above: pork-belly and vegetable-oil are BLS/FRED gaps, not NOAA, so the causal sentence is 6-of-8 right.

title: The vendored market-prior snapshot goes dark again starting 2026-08-17; the permanent fix is approved but unminted
effort: 5 minutes now; 2 hours for the PAT automation
evidence: `apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json` `_asOfRange: "2026-07-18..2026-07-28"`. Ages as of today: freshest 9d, oldest 19d. `scripts/check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs:45` sets `WARN_AT_DAYS = 30 - 10 = 20`; the resolver's `STALE_AFTER_DAYS = 30` (`apps/api/src/lib/cost-index-valuation.ts:74`). Butter and cheddar-cheese (2026-07-18) cross the cliff on 2026-08-17; the chicken/egg group on 2026-08-19; all 24 by 2026-08-27. The gate does return 'dark' the moment any single slug crosses (:155-166), so it will alarm on the Monday 2026-08-17 `cost-index-snapshot-watch.yml` run — but the fix is a manual two-command chore requiring both repos checked out on one machine, and git history shows the cadence is audit-driven: `e3b7c07` (2026-07-30) followed `0f0c32d` (2026-06-21), a 39-day gap that produced the 42-day production dormancy. The storefront's data is fresh to 2026-08-04 today, so a re-vendor right now costs nothing and buys 30 days. Board item 9 (cross-repo PAT, `contents: write` scoped to Muntin-Invoice-Decoder) is approved and not minted.
impact: A recurring, calendared outage of a paid-product feature, on a founder who works full time elsewhere. The alarm is now real, which is the improvement; the mean-time-to-fix is still 'whenever Don next has both repos open'.
rec: Today: run `node apps/api/scripts/vendor-cost-index.mjs` and commit — 5 minutes, resets the clock to 2026-09-03. This week: mint the PAT and add a re-vendor step to the storefront's `cost-index-refresh.yml` so the snapshot tracks the Mon/Wed/Fri read automatically. That is the single highest-leverage automation left in the two repos.
note: Per-slug points[0].asOf in the vendored snapshot: 2026-07-18 (19d) butter+cheddar-cheese; 2026-07-20 (17d) chicken-breast/whole-chicken/chicken-thigh/eggs; 2026-07-28 (9d) the remaining 18. `_asOfRange 2026-07-18..2026-07-28` matches. `STALE_AFTER_DAYS = 30` at `apps/api/src/lib/cost-index-valuation.ts:72` (auditor cited :74 — trivial drift). `node scripts/check-cost-index-snapshot-fresh.mjs` → 'OK — fresh — freshest 9d, oldest 19d; 24 slugs, 0 dark', wired in ci.yml:204-205 and cost-index-snapshot-watch.yml:77-89. Cliff dates 2026-08-17 / 08-19 / 08-27 all check out.

title: Eight published price levels blend market observations up to 85 days apart under a single fresh date
effort: 4 hours
evidence: Computed over `points[0].level.provenance` in `data/cost-index.json`: 8 of 93 dollar-level ingredients carry observations more than 30 days apart, 7 of them more than 60. yellow-squash publishes `asOf: 2026-08-04` over a provenance set spanning 2026-05-11..2026-08-04 (85 days); cherry-tomato spans 81 days and blends a Baltimore quote of 4800¢ dated 2026-05-15 with an Atlanta quote of 1725¢ dated 2026-08-04 into a published band of $20.13–$25.25. Also collard-greens (77d), napa-cabbage (77d), artichoke (75d), butter-lettuce (74d), green-beans (69d), acorn-squash (57d). `scripts/check-cost-index-series-freshness.mjs` surfaces these as 'STALE LEVEL ANCHOR' but is warn-only and is not the gate that governs the published date.
impact: The published band's width is partly cross-time dispersion masquerading as cross-market dispersion, under a date the reader will take as the date of measurement. It is a narrower version of the same defect as finding 1 — an honest-looking date over a number that is not from that date — and it undercuts the methodology page's 'geographic basis … whether the range spans market families or a single source is recorded' claim.
rec: In the composer, drop level observations older than N days from the median and the range (N = the point staleness window, not 120), or publish `level.asOfRange` and render it. Then promote the STALE LEVEL ANCHOR class from warn to fail once the roster is clean.
note: Computed over points[0].level.provenance: 93 ingredients carry level provenance, 8 span >30d, 7 span >60d — the exact slugs and spans listed (yellow-squash 85, cherry-tomato 81, collard-greens 77, napa-cabbage 77, artichoke 75, butter-lettuce 74, green-beans 69, acorn-squash 57). cherry-tomato's usda-ams-baltimore 4800¢@2026-05-15 is in the 8-obs set under asOf 2026-08-04. IMPACT IS OVERSTATED: `rangeBasis:"markets"` and the published band 2013–2525 is a trimmed p25–p75 that excludes both the stale 4800 and the fresh 1725, so the stale point does not widen the band at all — it only shifts the median by one rank position (2175 with it, 2100 without: 3.6%). The report's claim that 'the published band's width is partly cross-time dispersion' is not what the data does. Downgrade to low.

title: The archive that is supposed to be the moat has four editions, none in 31 days, and the deep history is manual-only and 36 days stale
effort: 1 day for the edition; 4 hours for the spine automation
evidence: `data/cost-index-editions.json` holds 4 editions (2026-06-05, 06-16, 06-18, 07-06); per CLAUDE.md two of those are reconstructed seeds that can never anchor a week-over-week. `blog/cost-index-week-*` and `cost-index/weekly/` agree: 4 posts, last 2026-07-06 — 31 days ago. Only 2 CC0 per-week snapshots exist (`cost-index/week-2026-06-18.json`, `week-2026-07-06.json`). `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` passes at 27d lag against a 38d threshold, so it reds on ~2026-08-13. Appending the spine happens only in `cost-index-dispatch.yml`, which is `workflow_dispatch`-only and defaults to `dry-run=true`, so the longitudinal series accrues only when the founder remembers to run it non-dry. Separately `data/cost-index-history.json` — 86,996 observations across 102 series back to 2001-03-01, which feeds seasonality, event detection, the anomaly log, confidence calibration, the forecast backtest and the Vendor Benchmark context — tops out at 2026-07-01 and is written only by a manual `fetch-cost-index-sources.mjs --history-out` run on the Mac, registered nowhere in `check-idem-coverage.mjs`'s MANUAL registry. The public CC0 descriptor `cost-index/index.json` also still declares `"refresh": "daily"` against the Mon/Wed/Fri cadence adopted 2026-07-06.
impact: The defensible part of a public-data product is the time series nobody else bothered to keep and the of-record publication cadence that makes it citable. Four editions in two months, a month of silence, and a backfill store that only one laptop can extend is not yet a moat — it is a promising start with a single point of failure. The 'refresh: daily' line is a small false claim sitting inside the artifact designed to be cited.
rec: Write the August edition this week (it is due, and `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh` reds on 2026-08-13 by design). Move the spine append + per-week CC0 snapshot out of the dispatch workflow and into `cost-index-refresh.yml` so the archive accrues on the data cadence rather than the writing cadence — the DATA being automated and the PUBLICATION being manual is the stated policy, and the archive is data. Register the deep-history refresh in `check-idem-coverage.mjs` MANUAL with who runs it and when it drifts. Fix `refresh` to 'Mon/Wed/Fri' in the export builder.
note: Archive numbers reproduce: `data/cost-index-editions.json` = 4 (06-05 high, 06-16 medium, 06-18 medium, 07-06 high); 4 `blog/cost-index-week-*` dirs; 2 CC0 week snapshots; `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh` → '27d lag, ≤ 38'. `refresh: 'daily'` is hardcoded at `build-cost-index-pages.mjs:1401` — confirmed. BUT the deep-history statistics do not reproduce: walking `data/cost-index-history.json` (keys `_doc/generatedAt/ingredients/drivers`) I get 108 series and 89,749 observations spanning 2001-02-01..2026-07-01, not '86,996 observations across 102 series back to 2001-03-01'. `generatedAt` is 2026-06-27T21:42Z = 40 days stale, not 36 (36 is the last observation, a different quantity). In a domain whose whole thesis is 'verification is the moat', shipping counts an auditor cannot reproduce is a self-inflicted wound. Also unremarked: the 2026-07-06 edition's frozen `basket.asOf` is 2026-05-01 — a 66-day-old basket published as the July edition.

title: The moat is the verification apparatus, not the data — and it is currently the thing that is broken
effort: 1 week, mostly overlapping findings 1 and 8
evidence: Every input is free and public: `docs/cost-index-sourcing-master.md` enumerates seven families (USDA AMS/LMR, NASS QuickStats, BLS PPI, Census/Comtrade, NOAA FOSS, World Bank/IMF via FRED, state ex-vessel), all keyless or free-key. `docs/cost-index-value-strategy.md` §0-1 states the thesis correctly — 'Don't out-quote Urner Barry — out-explain it' and 'verification is the moat; opacity is fatal'. What is genuinely hard to copy is the apparatus, not the feed: 100 series with per-point provenance, the fact gate, `check-cost-index-basis-leak` (verified holding), `check-cost-index-independence` (verified holding), the honest-absence pages (`cost-index/shrimp/index.html` publishes no number and explains why), the CC0/CC-BY split, and 86,996 archived observations. A competent competitor could rebuild the raw feed in ~2 weeks; rebuilding the honesty apparatus and the 40-article + 171-term content graph around it is 6-12 months. But findings 1 and 3 mean the apparatus currently fails at its own headline — and the apparatus IS the product.
impact: The company is one credible external recomputation away from having its differentiator inverted: 'the honest index whose headline number is wrong' is a worse position than 'another USDA scraper'. Conversely, fixing findings 1-3 restores an asset that is genuinely hard to copy and that no incumbent (MarginEdge, R365, Toast — all closed, all customer-data-fed) can match without giving up their own data model.
rec: Treat the reproducibility claim as a product feature and ship it: publish trend + weights in the CC0 export, publish a one-file recompute script alongside it, and add the basket invariant gate. That converts the strongest sentence on the methodology page from an assertion into something a skeptic can execute — which is the only version of this moat that survives contact with a skeptic.
note: The underlying claims check out (`docs/cost-index-sourcing-master.md` seven families all free/keyless; `docs/cost-index-value-strategy.md` §0-1 states the thesis; `check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs` and `check-cost-index-independence.mjs` both pass; `cost-index/shrimp/index.html` publishes no number). But this is an essay restating strategy documents, not a finding: it names no defect the other findings don't already carry, cites no file:line for anything new, and carries a severity for prose. It inflates the finding count.

title: Driver-catalog provenance is 27-47 days stale with a 365-day warn threshold that will never fire in time
effort: 1 hour
evidence: `data/cost-index-drivers.json` holds 6 standing drivers; `retrievedAt` values are 2026-06-20 (four of them: hpai-poultry-eggs, leafy-greens-weather, field-produce-weather, imports-logistics), 2026-07-05 (feed-grain-livestock), 2026-07-10 (energy-oils) — 27 to 47 days old. Per CLAUDE.md the gate only warns past 365 days, and `check-cost-index-drivers.mjs` passes clean. HPAI and weather backdrops are live conditions that can reverse inside a month; a 'standing correlation' attached to a flagged mover on 47-day-old provenance is attributing current movement to a backdrop nobody has re-checked. The `*_es` fields exist but the dispatch is EN-only, so the Spanish half is unexercised.
impact: Low today — the drivers are direction-gated (only spoken when the measured read agrees with `directionExpected`) and framed as association-not-cause, which is the right guardrail. But 'standing' plus a 365-day warn means the catalog can drift a full year behind the world while CI reads green, in exactly the register where a wrong attribution is quotable.
rec: Drop the warn threshold to 90 days and add the re-check to the monthly dispatch writing ritual — the founder is already reading the market to write the edition; confirming six backdrops is a 15-minute add to work already happening.
note: `data/cost-index-drivers.json` — 6 drivers, retrievedAt 2026-06-20 ×4 (47d), 2026-07-05 (32d), 2026-07-10 (27d). `node scripts/check-cost-index-drivers.mjs` → 'clean. 6 driver(s), 4 dispatch(es) scanned.' Severity low is right, and the 15-minute-add recommendation is sound.

title: Every published per-ingredient trend % is a two-endpoint delta over an unbounded, per-ingredient-variable window — and it silently replaced the multi-source blend the methodology page and the JSON-LD advertise
evidence: `scripts/reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs:38-44` defines `curveChange(history)` as `C.windowChange(vals)` = `(last − first)/first` over the ENTIRE `ingredients[k].history` array, and :62-63 writes `trend.pct`/`trend.dir` from it. That array has no fixed span. Measured across the 81 shippable `ci-read` pages: history spans run 36 days / 26 points (ribeye, onion, cherry-tomato) to 105 days / 16 points (chicken-breast, chicken-thigh) to 120 days / 5 points (ground-beef, and the 17 frozen NOAA series). So `cost-index/onion/index.html` renders 'flat +0%' measured over 36 days directly comparable-looking to `cost-index/chicken-breast/index.html` 'down -29.1%' measured over 105 days, and `cost-index/eggs/` trend is +148.2% because its history begins at a single 56¢ print on 2026-06-08 and ends at 139¢. Both endpoints are single daily observations with no robustness. What it replaced: `tools/_shared/composite-price.js:164-186` `blendTrend` collapses sources into families, takes a weighted median, and reports agreement/nSources/nTypes/noise. For chicken-breast the blend produced −0.53%; the endpoint estimator produces −29.07%. AND the metadata was not recomputed: chicken-breast's committed trend object still reads `{pct:-0.2907, agreement:0.667, nSources:3, nFamilies:3, nTypes:3, noise:0.0095}` and `confidence:'medium'` — every one of those fields describes the discarded −0.53% blend. `cost-index/methodology/index.html` JSON-LD `variableMeasured` states 'Trend direction: Measured direction of change (up, down, or flat) blended across sources so one feed cannot swing it', and its prose states 'a jagged, noisy path is capped at low no matter how the endpoints line up' — after reconcile the published number IS the endpoints. `scripts/check-all.mjs:424` wires `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs --check`, so the deploy actively enforces the endpoint estimator.
impact: This is the number on 81 EN + 81 ES ingredient pages, the hub's up/down/flat spread, the 'moving now' ranking, and — via `apps/api/scripts/vendor-cost-index.mjs`, which carries `{pct, agreement}` into `apps/api/src/data/cost-index-snapshot.json` — the paid product's Plate vendor-vs-market read at `apps/api/src/lib/plate-cost-tree.ts:85-89`, which pairs the reconciled pct with the pre-reconcile agreement as if they described the same estimate. The domain audit filed this in 'unknowns' as 'one defensible definition among several' and moved on. It is not defensible: it is a different estimator than the one the citable methodology sells, carrying confidence metadata that rates a number that no longer exists, on a page whose entire promise is 'a number you can check'. Fixing the basket (finding 1) without fixing this republishes a headline built on 162 pages of two-point deltas.
rec: (1) Give the trend an explicit, declared, fixed window (e.g. trailing 30 or 60 days) and compute it over that window on every ingredient, so cross-ingredient comparison and the hub ranking mean something. (2) Recompute agreement/nSources/nTypes/noise and the trend-confidence tier from whatever estimator actually ships — never carry blend metadata onto an endpoint number. (3) Publish the window length on the page next to the percentage ('down 6.6% over the last 36 days'), which the surfaces currently elide as 'over the recent window'. (4) Land the estimator choice in an ADR before any republish — this is the same methodology fork finding 1 defers, and they must be decided together.

title: 13 EN + 13 ES ingredient pages publish a falling price directly above a hardcoded 'Up on paper' verdict
evidence: `tools/_shared/cost-verdict.js:38` sets `note_en: 'Up on paper, but for this item the move is not yet distinguishable from its own week-to-week noise…'` for the `flag.gated === false` branch with no direction switch; the identical string is duplicated at `tools/_shared/cost-index-format.js:108` (the server renderer) and `tools/_shared/cost-index-ui.js:718` (the browser tool). Rendered result on `cost-index/chicken-breast/index.html`: 'Trend: down -29.1% over the recent window.' immediately followed by 'Watch — Up on paper, but for this item the move is not yet distinguishable…'. I scanned all `cost-index/*/index.html` and found 13 pages where the rendered trend word contradicts the verdict word, all in the down/Up direction: acorn-squash (−12.5%), brussels-sprouts (−15.9%), cheddar-cheese (−7.9%), cherry-tomato (−25%), chicken-breast (−29.1%), chicken-thigh (−5.4%), corn-on-the-cob (−2%), green-beans (−26.1%), lime (−10%), okra (−11.8%), serrano-pepper (−14.5%), spinach (−3%), watermelon (−28.9%). 31 ES pages carry the Spanish 'Sube sobre el papel'; the same 13 slugs pair it with a negative number. No gate catches it: `check-cost-index-confidence.mjs` asserts the framing phrases are PRESENT, never that they are consistent with the number they sit beside.
impact: A self-contradicting sentence in one screenful, on the flagship surface, on 26 live pages including chicken-breast — the heaviest basket weight (0.17) and the most-searched ingredient in the index. This is the cheapest possible way for a skeptical reader to conclude the index is not read by anyone. It is also the exact class of defect `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs` was written to eliminate ('the headline change and the curve never tell different stories'), reintroduced on the axis that script explicitly declined to touch ('the verdict flag is already correct and stays put', :17).
rec: Make the gated-out note direction-aware — take `dir` from the same point the number came from, in all three copies of the string, and consider collapsing the triplicate into one shared constant. Then add a gate that, for every page carrying `class="ci-read"`, asserts the rendered direction word and the verdict note's direction word agree. Both are ~1 hour.

title: Every vendored point carries a second, contradictory trend number in a `label` string that nothing renders — and it is the only artifact the company's strongest honesty gate inspects
evidence: `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs:18-19` explicitly declines to update the label ('the internal label string is not a user surface'). Result in `data/cost-index.json` today: onion `label: 'About $24.88–$29.81 (wholesale reference), up +34.4% over the window'` while its published `trend.pct` is 0.0 flat; russet-potato label 'up +28.3%' vs 0.0; chicken-breast label 'down -0.5%' vs −29.1%. I checked all 94 labelled ingredients against their rendered pages: 0 of 94 label strings appear in any `cost-index/<slug>/index.html`. Those stale label percentages are numerically identical to the committed `basket.contributors[].pct` values — so the orphaned −0.53% headline family traces to exactly this dead-string vintage. Meanwhile `scripts/check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs` — the gate the audit correctly calls the rarest thing in the two repos — operates on these labels ('10 basis-bound source-level latent item(s) … suppressed from every rendered surface'), i.e. it is guarding dollar figures inside strings no surface reads.
impact: Two consequences. First, the company's best-designed honesty gate is protecting a dead artifact, which means it would pass unchanged on the day someone starts rendering labels — and the label would then ship a trend % contradicting the one two lines above it. Second, it explains finding 1: the basket is not 'wrong', it is pinned to a vintage that survives only in unrendered strings, which is why no auditor can reconcile it against anything published. Any fix to the basket that does not also delete or recompute the labels leaves the trap armed.
rec: Either recompute `label` inside `reconcile-cost-index-trends.mjs` (cheap — it already holds the new pct) or strip the trend clause from the label entirely so it carries only the level, which is the part `check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs` actually needs. Then re-point the basis-leak gate at the rendered pages as well as the labels, so it is verifying suppression rather than string contents.

title: The `_includes` footer template is 3 counts stale, and cost-index-refresh.yml runs `sync-includes.mjs` 3×/week against CLAUDE.md's explicit prohibition — the same staging-list omission that loses the picker is the only thing stopping a 332-page regression
evidence: CLAUDE.md: 'Do NOT run `sync-includes` in these flows — the `_includes` footer template drifts vs live count sentinels and would regress them.' `.github/workflows/cost-index-refresh.yml:159` runs `node scripts/sync-includes.mjs` anyway, with a comment justifying it ('Restore canonical nav — the page builders emit skeleton include sentinels'). I ran it at HEAD: 332 files changed, 4,313 insertions, and the injected footer carries `<!-- count:articles.library -->24`, `<!-- count:tools.live -->12`, `<!-- count:glossary.terms -->149` — against `data/site-counts.json` which is the declared source of truth at `{articles:{library:38}, tools:{live:5}, glossary:{terms:171}}`. `about/index.html` today correctly carries 38 / 5 / 171. The regression does not currently ship for exactly one reason: none of those 332 paths are in the workflow's `git add` list, so `git checkout -- .` at :313 discards them (I verified 0 of the 332 fall under `cost-index/` or `es/cost-index/`, the staged roots).
impact: The staging-list omission the audit correctly identifies as a recurring bug is simultaneously the only safety net preventing a 332-page count regression three times a week. Whoever fixes finding 2 by broadening the `git add` list — the obvious fix, and the one the report recommends — ships the regression unless they refresh `_includes` first. That is a booby trap sitting directly on the recommended remediation path, and neither the report nor any gate names it. Independently: a documented prohibition in CLAUDE.md that the live workflow contradicts with a counter-argument in a comment is two sources of truth disagreeing about a build step, with no ADR resolving it.
rec: Before touching the staging list: run `node scripts/build-site-counts.mjs && node scripts/inject-site-counts.mjs` and refresh the `_includes` footer template so it carries the live counts. Then either add `node scripts/inject-site-counts.mjs` immediately after the `sync-includes` call in cost-index-refresh.yml, or resolve the CLAUDE.md contradiction with a one-line ADR saying which is authoritative. Then broaden the `git add` list.

title: The CC0 export's freshness metadata is a build stamp and a false cadence, on the artifact designed to be machine-cited
evidence: `scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:1401-1402` hardcodes `refresh: 'daily'` and sets `lastRefreshed: CI._lastReviewed`. In the live `cost-index/index.json` that renders as `refresh:'daily', lastRefreshed:'2026-08-05', count:81`. `_lastReviewed` in `data/cost-index.json` is the BUILD date (set at `build-cost-index.mjs:71` from `--date`/today), not a data date: the newest observation anywhere in the file is 2026-08-04, and 18 tracked series — including 3 basket contributors carrying 17.8% of the weight — last printed 2026-06-01. The actual cadence has been Mon/Wed/Fri since 2026-07-06. There is no `asOfRange` or per-file staleness field; per-row `asOf` is present but a consumer keying on the document-level `lastRefreshed` will never see it.
impact: Small in dollars, precisely on-target in reputation. This is the file the company built for AI answer engines, journalists and researchers to cite; it is the one artifact where a machine reads the metadata and not the prose disclosure. 'Refreshed daily, last refreshed yesterday' over a 66-day-old seafood block is the kind of claim that, once quoted back, costs more than the basket error — because it is in a CC0 dataset with the company's name on it. The report caught `refresh:'daily'` but filed it as a clause inside finding 8 and did not notice `lastRefreshed` is a build stamp.
rec: Set `refresh` from a single declared constant shared with the workflow schedule ('Mon/Wed/Fri'), replace `lastRefreshed` with `dataAsOfMax` + `dataAsOfMin` computed from the rows actually in the export, and add a `staleSeries` count. Fold into the same pass that adds `trend.pct`/weights for finding 1's reproducibility fix. ~1 hour.

title: The storefront's public accessibility statement makes a WCAG AA contrast claim its own gate already disproves 58 times
effort: 1 day
evidence: `/accessibility.html` is live and INDEXED (no noindex robots tag; verified) and states flatly: "Color Contrast: Text meets WCAG AA standards for color contrast." It is stamped "Last reviewed 2026-05-01" — 97 days ago. Its "Known Limitations" section names ZERO actual limitations. Against that: `assets/site.css` uses `color: var(--stone-2)` (#9AA0AB) for real text in **58 declarations** — `.listen-source-note`, `.learn-topic-count`, `.research-index-uses`, `.search-loading`, `.viz-gauge__ends .mid`, `.mtn-breadcrumb__sep`, and more. I computed the ratio: **2.45:1 on --cream (#F6F7F8), 2.63:1 on white** — a hard AA failure (needs 4.5:1) that fails even the 3:1 large-text/non-text floor. The gate that finds it, `scripts/check-stone-2-usage.mjs`, is `REPORT_ONLY = true` (line 40) by policy, and its own header understates the severity: "it FAILS AAA as body text on the cream surface" — it fails AA. The gate that DOES block the deploy, `scripts/check-contrast.mjs`, hardcodes four text tokens (ink, ink-soft, stone, teal) × three surfaces × two themes = 24 pairs and never looks at --stone-2, so it reports OK. Separately, the same page is retired-agency content: "This commitment applies to our website, **all client work we produce**, and the services we provide" and a whole section headed "What We Build for Clients" — on a company whose services line is retired. `check-positioning-drift.mjs` walks the file but its RETIRED_VOCAB (lines 76-83) matches 'web design'/'wordpress'/'wix', not agency-client language, so it scores 0 and passes.
impact: A published, indexed accessibility statement asserting AA conformance while the site fails AA is the single cheapest thing for an ADA/§508 demand-letter mill to find and act on — they scan for exactly this pairing. Beyond legal exposure it is the precise failure the founder's mandate cannot survive: a skeptical operator who wants to know whether this company is competent checks the boring pages, and finds a claim that is false and boilerplate written for a business Muntin no longer is.
rec: Three moves, one day. (1) Retokenize the 58 `color:var(--stone-2)` sites to `--stone` or a new `--hint` token at ≥4.5:1, then flip `REPORT_ONLY = false` and wire the gate into check-all. (2) Rewrite `/accessibility.html` + `/es/accessibility.html` using the product's `/accessibility` page as the template — real dated known-issues, no client/agency language, and a review date that is honest. (3) Add a gate binding the reviewed-date the way `check-launch-date-claims.mjs` binds launch dates; the pattern already exists in this codebase.
note:
Reproduced and it is worse than stated. accessibility.html:425 'Text meets WCAG AA standards for color contrast'; :410 'Last reviewed 2026-05-01' (97d); :418 'all client work we produce'; :433 '

What We Build for Clients

'. I also found :417, unmentioned by the auditor, claiming conformance with the NEW WCAG 2.2 criteria by name ('focus appearance, dragging movements, target size, accessible authentication ... this site meets them too') — four claims with no corresponding gate anywhere. And the callout at :413 says 'known gaps are listed below' while the Known Limitations section (:436-438) lists ZERO gaps. No robots noindex (only max-image-preview), footer-linked at _includes/footer.html:169, so indexable — though NOT in sitemap.xml, contra the auditor's 'INDEXED (verified)'. Contrast math reproduced exactly: #9AA0AB on #F6F7F8 = 2.45:1, on #FFF = 2.63:1. Two count corrections: the 58 figure is the gate's total across THREE files, not 'assets/site.css uses ... in 58 declarations' — site.css has 29, the rest are in site-article.css and site-core.css. And site.css:229 and :172 already document --stone-2 as 'DECORATIVE ONLY ... dividers/icons ONLY, never text', so the codebase knows; the defect is the published claim, not ignorance. check-stone-2-usage.mjs:41 REPORT_ONLY=true confirmed; check-contrast.mjs:50 TEXTS=[ink,ink-soft,stone,teal] confirmed to never see --stone-2.

title: The founder's emotional pivot exists only in the plan; the shipped homepage still leads with the self-defending band the pivot retired
effort: 2 days
evidence: `docs/handoff/founder-vision.md:67-94` (2026-07-11) is unambiguous: "stop making the site defend itself"; "Trust goes AMBIENT: stated once, quietly… **never a headline, never a self-defending section**"; the site must move through their world → you can see it coming → who you become. The shipped `index.html` first section after the hero is `<h2 id="stances-heading">` "Every claim on this site carries its own receipt" under the eyebrow "Receipts, not promises", with three numbered panels: 01 The fact gate / 02 The network tab / 03 The public scorecard. I measured it: **199 words of a 1,805-word body — 11%, in the most valuable non-hero real estate on the site.** `git log -S 'Receipts, not promises' -- index.html` shows it entered in `87205e1fd` (2026-07-11, the v3 propagation), and `index.html` has been edited four times since (`3077d83a6`, `ba313d694`, `d33433f03`, `2ae8c69c6`, all 2026-07-28) without touching it. I then grepped the homepage for the vocabulary the vision's arc requires — "month-end", "P&L", "already bled", "a week ahead", "in command", "exhaust", "surprise", "walk in knowing" — **all eight return 0 hits.** What DID ship in the 26 days after the pivot was the "warmth" thread (Golden Hour washes, uppercase nav tabs, breadcrumb parity, theme cross-fade — commits 2026-07-17/18): real polish, none of it the arc. Note the ES homepage (`es/index.html`) has no stances band at all — 0 hits for `stances-heading` — so EN and ES diverge structurally on the flagship page.
impact: This is the founder's own #1 directive, and the thing the whole reinvention was convened to deliver, unbuilt after 26 days of design work that went elsewhere. Concretely: the second thing a restaurant owner reads on muntin.digital is an argument about Muntin's virtue rather than a sentence about their month. That is the exact posture the founder identified as making the site feel emotionless, and it is still the highest-value pixels on the property.
rec: Delete the `stances-heading` band from `index.html` and redistribute its three proofs as ambient one-liners (a single trust strip near the footer, plus the existing per-tool 'inspect this' drawers, which already carry the proof where it belongs). Replace it with the recognition beat the vision specifies — the month-end P&L that already bled, the price that crept up — and a 'who you become' beat before the founding CTA. Then mirror to `es/index.html`. This is a copy-and-section-order change on one file, not a rebuild.
note: Facts all reproduce: index.html:557 is the first <section> after :468 hero, id at :561 'Every claim on this site carries its own receipt' under eyebrow :560 'Receipts, not promises'; es/index.html has 0 hits for stances-heading and jumps hero(:522) → tool-cta(:600). founder-vision.md:67-94 says what is quoted. Severity is inflated to critical, though. This is an unexecuted PLAN, not a broken system: founder-vision.md is a proposal doc, the board's own CURRENT STATE block (strategic-council-board.md, updated 2026-07-30) has moved the active directive to eval-engineering, and launch is deferred to 2027 (ADR-020). A homepage section-order preference on a pre-revenue side venture is not the same class of defect as a false public conformance claim. The auditor also overstates the ES gap as 'EN and ES diverge structurally' — I diffed the section lists and the only other difference is EN carrying class 'below-fold-island', which has ZERO CSS rules in any stylesheet in the repo (see missed findings), i.e. a no-op.

title: The flagship data surface — 101 Cost Index pages — draws no price history at all
effort: 1 week
evidence: I parsed `cost-index/asparagus/index.html`: 11 `<svg>` elements, **every one of them chrome** (logo mark, theme-toggle sun/moon, nav icons). Across the tree: 101 ingredient directories; 79 render a `ci-season-curve` SVG (a 12-point seasonal-norm line); exactly **1 of 101** (`cost-index/menu-pricing/`) carries a `viz-figure`/`article-figure`. The measured price history — the actual product — is delivered as a sentence: "Indexed to 100 on 2026-06-29 · ~113 on 2026-08-04 — rose over the tracked window." The same page tells the reader "Across the ~25.2 years of public data we track…" and draws none of it. `check-article-graphics.mjs` is silent here by design: `GENERATED_ROOTS` scans cost-index pages for figure QUALITY only (rules 3,4,6,8,9) and skips figureless pages — so the gate is correct and the gap is invisible to CI. The strategic board's own directive (2026-07-28) says the Cost Index "is not a funnel for a product, it IS the company for the next year."
impact: MarginEdge, Restaurant365 and Toast sell on charts; their screenshots ARE their marketing. Muntin's equivalent surface is prose and tables. The founder's mandate is to beat them on perceived technical craft with no brand legacy to lean on — and the single artifact a prospect would judge that on does not exist. It also costs the Cost Index its shareability: a chart gets screenshotted into an operator Facebook group, a paragraph does not.
rec: Build one generated sparkline/area chart of the measured `points[]` series into the `ci-read` block in `scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs`, with the baseline window shaded and the current read marked — the season-curve SVG generator already in that builder is the pattern to copy, so this is extension, not new machinery. Ship it to all 101 EN + ES pages in one build. Then extend `check-article-graphics`'s GENERATED_ROOTS to require the figure rather than merely tolerate its absence.
note: This is the report's central failure and it is not reproducible. cost-index/asparagus/index.html ships TWO measured-price charts: (1) inside <div class="ci-read__spark">, an <svg class="mtn-spark" width=248 height=46 role="img"> plotting the 26-point measured series with a dashed baseline line and a marked current point, aria-label 'Price rose over the tracked window. Recent range $47.13-$51.81, right now $50.50...'; (2) <figure class="ci-index"> with an <svg class="mtn-spark" width=460 height=128> area chart of the indexed measured window, aria-label 'Indexed to 100 on 2026-06-29 · ~113 on 2026-08-04'. Coverage: 97 of 101 EN cost-index dirs and 97 ES carry mtn-spark. The generator is scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:908 `function sparkBlock(r, locale)`, with layout CSS at :1682/:1797/:1972. The auditor's claim '11 <svg> elements, every one of them chrome (logo mark, theme-toggle sun/moon, nav icons)' cannot be produced from this file — two of the eleven are the charts. Their recommendation ('Build one generated sparkline/area chart of the measured points[] series into the ci-read block ... copy the season-curve SVG generator') asks for code that already exists in that exact block. The grep behind the finding was for viz-figure|article-figure class names, and the conclusion 'no chart' was drawn from a class-name absence, not from parsing SVGs as claimed. A real residual exists (the charts are unlabeled by axis and carry no y-scale) but that is a low craft note, not 'the flagship data surface draws no price history at all'.

title: 69 live public pages print "fresh fruits & vegetables moved -49.4%" — an implausible figure the driver gate cannot see
effort: 1 day for the gate + suppression; the data fix needs a keyed live run on the operator's Mac
evidence: Every produce ingredient page renders: "For category context: fresh fruits & vegetables *as a whole* moved **-49.4%** over the window (BLS PPI, fresh fruits & vegetables)." I counted the occurrences across the tree: **69 pages, all the identical -49.4%.** Source is `data/cost-index.json` → `drivers['fresh-produce']`: `trend.pct: -0.4940611528457355`, `nSources: 1`, `nFamilies: 1`, and a `history` of exactly two points — `54977` (2026-03-01) → `27815` (2026-06-01), both `basis: "index"`. A produce PPI index halving in one quarter is not a market event; it is a series-alignment or rebasing artifact. The render site is `scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:2232-2242`. `scripts/check-cost-index-drivers.mjs` passes clean ("6 driver(s), 4 dispatch(es) scanned") because it validates schema, source presence and `retrievedAt` freshness — presence of shape — and never tests magnitude plausibility.
impact: This is the exact failure mode the honesty brand cannot absorb. One produce-literate operator or one competitor reads that line and the "every number sourced, zero inventions" positioning is gone — and it is on 69 indexed pages, so it is what a search engine surfaces. The fact gate protects hand-written prose; generated prose walked straight past it.
rec: Add a plausibility band to `check-cost-index-drivers.mjs`: fail (or suppress the render) when a category trend exceeds a stated magnitude, or when it rests on <3 points or a single source. Then suppress the category-context paragraph in the builder unless the driver has ≥3 points from ≥1 confirmed continuous series. Re-run the page build. Investigate the two BLS points separately — they are almost certainly two different series IDs.
note: Reproduced and undercounted. data/cost-index.json drivers['fresh-produce'] = trend.pct -0.4940611528457355, nSources 1, nFamilies 1, history exactly two points 2026-03-01:54977 -> 2026-06-01:27815, both basis 'index'. Render confirmed in prose: 'For category context: fresh fruits & vegetables as a whole moved -49.4% over the window (BLS PPI...)'. The auditor says 69 pages; the real count is 138 (grep -rl across cost-index/ AND es/cost-index/) — they counted EN only, so the Spanish mirror of the same false number went unreported. I also profiled the other five drivers, which the auditor did not: corn -3.2% (5 pts), soybeans +0.7% (5), diesel -5.1% (18), electricity -0.7% (5), seafood-import +1.9% (5). fresh-produce is the sole 2-point series and the sole outlier by two orders of magnitude, which strengthens the series-alignment diagnosis. Raising to critical: this is a fabricated-in-effect number on 138 indexed pages of the surface the board calls 'the company for the next year', published under a zero-inventions fact gate.

title: Every storefront gate that requires rendering a page is advisory; the 320 that block the deploy are all static analysis
effort: 3 days
evidence: `scripts/check-all.mjs` wires 320 entries and blocks the Cloudflare deploy — and every one is static file analysis. The four workflows that actually open a browser have no teeth: `.github/workflows/lighthouse-ci.yml` sets `continue-on-error: true` on the job AND deliberately comments out `LHCI_GITHUB_TOKEN` with a note explaining that setting it would let per-URL statuses block merges ("which, while the perf baseline is shaking out, has been every PR") — so no status check can ever land. `.github/workflows/window-a11y.yml` is `continue-on-error: true` at the job level AND on all four of its steps, and its axe-core run covers exactly `/window/` and `/es/window/` — 2 of ~1,368 pages. `.github/workflows/playwright.yml` is `continue-on-error: true`. And the only visual-regression test on the property, `tests/hub-baseline.spec.mjs:128`, is `test.fixme('hub visual snapshot — desktop', …)` — permanently skipped, with its three baseline PNGs sitting committed in `tests/hub-baseline.spec.mjs-snapshots/`. Both the lhci and a11y workflows carry the same note — "Promote to required-check once three consecutive PRs land green" — and were created 2026-07-05/06, i.e. 32 days ago, still provisional. Meanwhile `check-css-drift.mjs` (504 hardcoded-hex issues across 7 tool pages) is on the documented UNWIRED list, and `check-stone-2-usage.mjs` is REPORT_ONLY.
impact: This is the audit's own lesson applied to design: the storefront can regress its rendered appearance, its keyboard path, its contrast, and its load time without a single red check anywhere. The 2026-07-30 audit found three dead systems behind ~160 green gates; the design surface has the same structure, and nobody has looked yet.
rec: Do not promote them all — promote one and mean it. Pick `window-a11y.yml`: remove the four step-level `continue-on-error`s, keep the job-level one for one week, fix whatever it names, then remove that too and add `/`, `/cost-index/`, `/tools/margin-math/` to its URL list. Separately, either un-fixme the hub snapshot with a sane threshold or delete the test and its three PNGs — a permanently skipped test with committed baselines is worse than no test because it reads as coverage.
note: All specifics reproduce. lighthouse-ci.yml:41 job-level continue-on-error with the LHCI_GITHUB_TOKEN commented out at :161; window-a11y.yml:56 job-level plus step-level at :124/:131/:138, axe scoped to http://localhost:8788/window/ and /es/window/ only; playwright.yml:48 continue-on-error; tests/hub-baseline.spec.mjs:128 test.fixme with three committed PNGs in tests/hub-baseline.spec.mjs-snapshots/. check-all.mjs has 320 entries and is the wrangler.jsonc build.command's last gate before the tar. One correction the auditor should have made and did not: `node scripts/check-all.mjs` exits 1 TODAY (312/320). Six of the eight reds are '(idem)' regeneration builders that the deploy chain re-runs before check-all — that is documented and structurally enforced in scripts/check-all-baseline.json's two-layer safety gate, so it is a deliberate design, not rot. The two non-idem reds (Cost-index picker, Ingredient state record) are also explicitly named in that file as intentionally NOT baselined. The auditor asserted 'Both green this run' for the token gates without ever running check-all end to end.

title: Measured mobile performance is roughly half the stated bar, and the config that records this cannot fail a build
effort: 3 days
evidence: `lighthouserc.js` records the real numbers in its own comments: "Today's baseline (from PR #243's lhci run, median of 3): perf: 0.73 – 0.79 · LCP: 4.4s – 6.0s · CLS: 0.00 – 0.07 · render-blocking: 1 (the single site.css)" — measured on the launch plan's mobile / Slow-4G / 4× CPU scenario, dated 2026-05-03 (95 days ago). The launch-plan targets are sitting commented out at lines ~166-174: `performance ≥ 0.90`, `largest-contentful-paint ≤ 2000`, `total-blocking-time ≤ 200`, `render-blocking-resources maxLength 0`. The live assertions are a don't-regress floor — perf ≥0.70, LCP ≤6500ms, TBT ≤800ms — on a workflow that is `continue-on-error`. `assets/site.css` is **9,147 lines** shipped as one render-blocking stylesheet; the config's own note says the fix is "CSS shell split" and the repo does have `scripts/build-css-shells.mjs`, so the machinery exists and the homepage still loads the monolith. `errors-in-console` was downgraded to `warn` on 2026-07-28 with an honest explanation (the anonymous `/api/auth/me` 401 in `_includes/nav.html`).
impact: A ~6-second hero on a phone over 4G is the first impression a restaurant operator gets — very likely standing in a walk-in or a stockroom on bad signal. It is the direct opposite of the "sharper, calmer, in command" feeling the vision is engineering, and it is a ranking input on the surface the whole SEO corpus feeds. Nothing in CI will ever make this better because nothing in CI can make it worse.
rec: Two concrete things, in order. (1) Split `site.css`: inline the ~2KB of above-fold hero/nav critical CSS on `index.html` and load the rest with `media="print" onload`. `build-css-shells.mjs` already exists — wire it for the homepage first and re-measure. (2) Fix the console-error root cause named in the config: make anonymous `/api/auth/me` return 200 + `{signedIn:false}` and have nav.html read the flag, which restores `errors-in-response` to error and removes a first-paint 401 on every page. Then re-baseline lhci with a real number, not a 95-day-old one.
note: The measurements and the toothlessness are real; the DIAGNOSIS and the recommendation are refuted. Confirmed verbatim in lighthouserc.js: comments at :96-97 'perf: 0.73 - 0.79 / LCP: 4.4s - 6.0s', first measured run 2026-05-03 (:80); live assertions :108 minScore 0.70, :118 LCP 6500, :120 TBT 800; launch targets commented out at :167-169. But: 'assets/site.css is 9,147 lines shipped as one render-blocking stylesheet' and 'the homepage still loads the monolith' are both false. Only 16 pages in the whole repo carry a real <link href="/assets/site.css"> and they are workbench/ and admin/ pages. index.html loads /assets/site-core.css + /assets/site-article.css as `rel=preload as=style onload="this.rel='stylesheet'"`, with the blocking <link rel=stylesheet> present ONLY inside a <noscript> fallback, preceded by inlined critical CSS — exactly the pattern the auditor recommends building. build-css-shells.mjs + inject-css-shells.mjs already run twice in wrangler.jsonc's build.command, and check-css-shells.mjs proves the shells are a sound round-trip partition of site.css. The auditor's day-of-work recommendation #1 is finished work. What survives: a 95-day-old baseline nobody has refreshed, on a workflow that structurally cannot fail. That is medium.

title: The "two design languages" fork is 93% closed, but the record still says it is open — and the one token left behind is the AA-floor one
effort: 2 hours
evidence: I diffed the two token systems directly. 13 of 14 mapped spine tokens are byte-identical between `assets/site.css` `:root` and `packages/ui/tokens.css`. The single mismatch is `--stone: #6B7280` (storefront) vs `--mun-text-tertiary: #5f6670` (product) — and the product's tokens.css carries the reason inline: "UR3-4: bumped from #6b7280 (**4.51:1, right on the AA floor**) to #5f6670 (5.41:1 on canvas) so tertiary/caption ink clears AA with margin instead of teetering on it." The storefront never got the fix, and it cannot: the shared spec's `legacyVarMap` in `data/muntin.tokens.json` binds `--stone` → `core.slate.500 (#6b7280)` — a *neutral ramp step* — rather than `core.text.tertiary (#5f6670)`, the *text* token that exists in the same spec for exactly this job. So `check-tokens-sync.mjs` is green while the semantics are wrong. Meanwhile `docs/handoff/founder-vision.md:96-113` and `docs/handoff/reinvention-master-plan.md:§III` still describe an unresolved fork — "Warm editorial (cream/ink + teal #2A50C8 + Fraunces) — the entire marketing site" needing re-pigment — when `--cream` IS #F6F7F8 (the app's bg) and `--teal` IS #2A50C8 (the app's accent-text). The genuinely remaining divergences are narrow and deliberate per `docs/handoff/redesign-v3-system.md`: Fraunces on all storefront h1–h4 vs Inter-only product chrome (`apps/web/app/layout.tsx:9-10`, "the serif is retired from product chrome"), and the Golden-Hour marigold/coral layer, which is declared in `:root` on every page but applied on exactly 4 (`index.html`, `ledger/index.html`, and their ES twins).
impact: A fresh session — which this codebase explicitly designs for, since the container is ephemeral — reads founder-vision.md and re-does a re-pigment that shipped on 2026-07-11. That is the most expensive kind of stale doc in a one-person shop. And the --stone mis-binding means the marketing site's low-emphasis text will sit permanently at the AA floor while the product's clears it, with a green gate attesting to the alignment.
rec: Two lines and a paragraph. (1) Repoint `--stone` → `core.text.tertiary` in `data/muntin.tokens.json`'s legacyVarMap and in the product's `packages/ui/muntin.tokens.json`, set `--stone: #5F6670` in site.css, re-run `check-tokens-sync`. (2) Add a dated "SUPERSEDED 2026-07-11 — the re-pigment shipped; 13/14 tokens now identical, see redesign-v3-system.md" block to the top of founder-vision.md §'The design-language fork' and to reinvention-master-plan.md §III. Leave the Fraunces split alone — it is a defensible register decision, documented, and it gives the editorial surfaces a voice the product does not need.
note: The --stone sub-finding is a genuinely good catch and reproduces: data/muntin.tokens.json:159 binds '--stone' to 'core.slate.500 (#6b7280)' while the same spec carries core.text.tertiary '#5f6670' at :39, and packages/ui/tokens.css:52-55 documents the reason ('UR3-4: bumped from #6b7280 (4.51:1, right on the AA floor) to #5f6670'). I confirmed #6B7280 on #F6F7F8 = 4.51:1. But the HEADLINE is a misreading of the document it calls stale. founder-vision.md's own design-language-fork section already states 'the neutral ramp already matches; only accent (teal->electric-blue) and type (Fraunces->Inter) change, via scoped token overrides.' The auditor measured the neutral ramp, found it matches, and concluded the doc is obsolete — while the fork the doc actually describes is still fully OPEN on both axes it names: the storefront's --teal #2A50C8 is the product's --mun-accent-text (tokens.css:76), not its fill accent --mun-accent #3b68f5 (:70), and the storefront still ships Fraunces on h1-h4 against Inter-only product chrome. Nothing is 93% closed; the auditor closed the one dimension that was never in dispute. Downgrading to low and keeping only the --stone repoint.

title: The inbox says "Inbox is clear" when it does not know — a guess, from the product whose doctrine is never to guess
effort: 4 hours
evidence: `apps/web/app/(product)/inbox/page.tsx` `loadInboxRows()` wraps the fetch to `/v1/extractions?status=needs_review` in a try/catch that returns `[]` on both a non-ok response (`if (!r.ok) return [];`) and any thrown error, with a comment stating the intent: "Quiet failure: render the empty state… we deliberately do not throw so the inbox CTA stays reachable when the Worker is briefly unavailable." `inbox-client.tsx:937` branches on `rows.length === 0`, and lines 1211-1219 then render `<EmptyState>` with `copy.emptyStates.inbox.titleCleared` ("Inbox is clear.") or `.title` ("Drop your first invoice here."). There is no third state. A Worker blip, an expired session, or a 5xx therefore presents to the operator as a confident all-clear on their primary screen. This sits directly against the company's own honesty line, which shipped to the storefront homepage in EN + ES: the product "holds a number back rather than print a guess" — and against ADR-009's fail-closed valuation discipline, which the same team got right on the money path.
impact: The single behaviour that would lose an operator's trust fastest in an invoice product is being told there is nothing to review when there is. It is also silent: nothing logs, nothing alerts, and the operator has no reason to suspect it. Low frequency, high consequence — and the fix is small enough that the asymmetry is indefensible.
rec: Have `loadInboxRows` return a discriminated result (`{ok:true, rows}` / `{ok:false, reason}`) and add a third render branch: "We could not reach your ledger just now" + a Check-now action. Reuse the stalled-state pattern ADR-008 already built for the pending-docs poller — it is the same problem, already solved once in this codebase.
note: Reproduced exactly. apps/web/app/(product)/inbox/page.tsx:76-87: try { fetch(`${API_BASE}/v1/extractions?status=needs_review`) ; if (!r.ok) return []; if (!Array.isArray(body.items)) return []; } — three distinct paths that return an empty array indistinguishable from a genuinely empty inbox, and the catch below does the same. loadInboxRows() feeds initialRows into <InboxClient> at :174-179, so a 5xx, an expired session, or a Worker blip all render as 'Inbox is clear.' The comment naming this a deliberate 'quiet failure' makes it a knowingly-accepted tradeoff, but it is the wrong one for a product whose shipped positioning line is 'holds a number back rather than print a guess'. Medium is correct; the ADR-008 stalled-state pattern in use-pending-docs.ts is the right template for the fix.

title: The product publicly lists three screen readers it was "tested with"; every ADR walk receipt says no screen-reader walk has ever happened
effort: 1 day (3h walk + fixes + the gate)
evidence: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/accessibility/page.tsx` renders a "Tested with" list, inlined in JSX: "NVDA + Firefox on Windows", "VoiceOver + Safari on macOS", "VoiceOver + Safari on iOS". `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3835` publishes `lastAuditDate: "2026-05-21"` — **77 days ago** — under `cadenceBody`: "Before each release. After every change to a public route." Since that date, `git log` shows **12 commits touching `apps/web/app/(marketing)`**. All three known issues are stamped "Logged 2026-05-21" and none has moved. Against that, ten walk receipts across `docs/ux/decisions/` state the opposite in the company's own honest voice: ADR-002 "a live device walk (the container has no browser / screen reader / installed deps)"; ADR-006:78 "verified by code reasoning + tsc + the API/unit test suites, **NOT a live device walk**"; ADR-006:91 "**Still owed**… a keyboard-only + VoiceOver/NVDA walk of `/count` at 360px." ADR-001/002/004/005 are dated 2026-06-08 — **59 days** owed; ADR-006 2026-06-18 — 49 days. Nothing binds `lastAuditDate` to anything: grepping `scripts/*.mjs` and `.github/workflows/` for it returns only a string in `check-launch-date-claims.mjs`'s own self-test fixture — meaning the company built exactly this binding pattern for launch dates and did not apply it here.
impact: A dated "tested with NVDA/VoiceOver" claim that the engineering record contradicts is the same class of false public statement as finding #1, on a page whose entire credibility rests on being the honest one. Second-order: nobody knows whether `/count`'s per-row unit toggle, the reconciliation-flag card, or the "Reading…" status card actually announce usefully — the gates prove the ARIA wiring exists, not that the experience works.
rec: Book one three-hour session on the founder's own Mac: VoiceOver + Safari through sign-in → upload → inbox → review → `/count` at 360px, keyboard-only, with reduced-motion on. Write what you find into each ADR's walk receipt, update `lastAuditDate` and the known-issues list to what is true, and drop the two screen readers you did not actually use from the tested-with list. Then add a gate that fails when `lastAuditDate` is >90 days old — the `check-launch-date-claims.mjs` pattern ports in an hour.
note: Reproduced. apps/web/app/(marketing)/accessibility/page.tsx:94 'NVDA + Firefox on Windows', :98 'VoiceOver + Safari on macOS', :102 'VoiceOver + Safari on iOS'; apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3835 lastAuditDate: '2026-05-21' = 77 days at 2026-08-06; :3849 testedWithHeading 'Tested with'. The ADR walk receipts do say the opposite (this repo's own CLAUDE.md 'Environment honesty' section states flatly that verification here is code reasoning plus gates, 'NOT a live device/browser walk ... never claim a device walk you did not perform'). This is the same class of defect as finding #1 and the auditor is right to pair them. Note the mitigating fact they buried: this page's SHAPE is the honest one (dated, specific known-issues), which is why they also recommend it as the storefront's template — those two positions sit awkwardly together and should have been reconciled.

title: 504 tokenization violations frozen on the tool pages, and the demo built to showcase the product's craft uses an accent that fails AA
effort: 1 hour for the demo; 2 weeks at one tool/week for the drift
evidence: `node scripts/check-css-drift.mjs` reports **504 drift issues across 7 files** — `tools/index.html`, `tools/audits/`, `tools/cost-pulse/`, `tools/margin-math/`, `tools/plate-cost/`, `tools/start/`, `tools/vendor-benchmark/` — hardcoded hex (#1B1E24, #2C3038, #21262E, #F1EDE5, #1F6B3A, and #9AA0AB again) where tokens exist. It is honestly documented on `check-gate-coverage.mjs`'s UNWIRED list since 2026-07-28 with a real reason (retokenizing by hand risks regressions unverifiable without a browser). The free tools are the vision's designated "everyday, event-triggered return engine" — the surfaces an operator hits most — and they are the least token-governed on the site. Separately: `ledger/demo/index.html` and `es/ledger/demo/index.html` scope `--teal` to the app fill blue `#3b68f5` inside `.container.ld-wrap`, and use it as `color:` on `.ld-rail a[aria-current="step"]`. I computed #3b68f5 on #f6f7f8 = **4.37:1**, below AA. The reinvention plan flags this exact hazard in its own words (`reinvention-master-plan.md` §III: "Contrast fix (mandatory): links use --accent-text #2a50c8 on light (#3b68f5 fails AA)"), and the wired `check-contrast.mjs` hardcodes `teal: "#2A50C8"` so it structurally cannot see a scoped override.
impact: The tools drift is contained debt, not damage — but it is the reason the vision's "cutting-edge craft on every touchpoint" cannot be honestly claimed, since seven of the most-visited touchpoints are outside the system. The demo accent is small but pointed: the one page built to prove Muntin's design competence to a prospect ships a link colour below the accessibility floor that its own plan named.
rec: Demo first, it is one line: change the text uses inside `.ld-wrap` to `#2a50c8` (or the dark `#5b82ff` where already applied) and keep `#3b68f5` for fills and focus rings only — this is exactly the split the app's own tokens make (`--mun-accent` for fill, `--mun-accent-text` for text). For the drift, pick one tool per week rather than a sweep; `margin-math` and `plate-cost` are the highest-traffic, so retokenize those two and re-run the gate to watch the 504 fall before deciding whether to wire it.
note: The contrast defect is real but the cited selector is wrong. ledger/demo/index.html does scope `.ld-wrap{--font-display:var(--font-body);--teal:#3b68f5` and I confirm #3b68f5 on #F6F7F8 = 4.37:1, below AA. But the auditor's evidence — '.ld-rail a[aria-current="step"]' using it as color: — does not exist: that selector sets `border-color:var(--ink);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ink)` and its scoped twin sets `background:var(--teal-tint);border-color:var(--teal)`, i.e. fill and border, which is exactly the correct split they recommend. The finding survives on four DIFFERENT sites I located by offset inside the .ld-wrap element (opens at byte 107166): two breadcrumb links at 107419/107528, the AI-policy link at 114016, and the founding-rate exit CTA at 140230, all `style="color:var(--teal)"` and therefore all 4.37:1. The check-css-drift 504-issues-across-7-files claim and its documented UNWIRED status I did not independently re-run, but it is honestly labeled as documented debt in the report itself, which is the right call.

title: All 200 Cost-Index pages share one OG card — a TOOL's card — and the OG gate's root list cannot see them (75 of 1,363 pages checked)
evidence: Every ingredient page on both locales emits the identical social card: `grep -ho 'og:image" content="[^"]*"' cost-index/*/index.html | sort | uniq -c` returns `100 https://muntin.digital/brand/og/tool-cost-pulse.png`, and the ES run returns the same 100. That is the Cost Pulse TOOL's artwork on 200 ingredient pages. The machinery to fix it exists and was simply never pointed here: brand/og/ holds per-page cards for library (library-what-beef-prices.png, …), sheets (sheet-waste-log.png, …), blog and glossary, all rendered by scripts/build-og-cards.mjs — which contains zero occurrences of 'cost-index'. The gate is blind by construction: scripts/check-og-coverage.mjs walks the whole tree (SKIP_DIRS at :99) but only enforces via `requiresOwnCard(rel)` at :76-96, an allowlist of blog/, tools/, tools/audits/, learn/research/, learn/topics/ — cost-index/ appears nowhere in it. `node scripts/check-og-coverage.mjs` prints 'OG coverage: clean. (75 pages checked.)' against 1,363 HTML pages. tool-cost-pulse.png is not in GENERIC_FALLBACKS (:42-54) either, so even if the route were added the card would read as legitimately specific.
impact: This is the exact failure the auditor argued for and then attributed to the wrong artifact: they claimed the Cost Index is unshareable because it has no chart. It has two charts on 194 pages. What it has no share card for is every one of its 200 pages. Any asparagus, beef or egg link pasted into an operator Facebook group, a Slack, or an iMessage renders identical unrelated tool artwork with no ingredient name and no price — on the surface the strategic board calls 'the company for the next year'. It is also a textbook repeat of the storefront's own written lesson ('a scanner is only as good as its root list — declare roots, justify omissions'), this time on a gate the lesson never got applied to.
rec: Add a cost-index card family to build-og-cards.mjs reusing the existing 1200x630 template, stamping ingredient name + unit + the current read range + as-of date (all values already on the page). Then add `/^(es\/)?cost-index\/[^/]+\/index\.html$/` to requiresOwnCard() in check-og-coverage.mjs so the gate can never lose the surface again — and while in that function, audit it against the surface map: library/ and sheets/ are also absent from the allowlist and pass only because the builder happens to cover them.

title: Every email Muntin sends is rendered in the RETIRED brand palette — the site's own token spec calls those values 'a migration remnant to purge'
evidence: src/lib/templates.js and src/lib/templates.es.js — the live production templates, imported at src/worker.js:216 and by src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js:28 — contain 52 occurrences of #1F4E5B, 10 of #FAF7F2, 6 of #F3EEE3 and 4 of #B8541A, and ZERO occurrences of #2A50C8 or #F6F7F8. Cross-reference data/muntin.tokens.json:173-180, the shared cross-repo spec: `"retiredWarmPalette": { "_note": "Pre-Wave-8b editorial values. Any live occurrence (outside docs) is a migration remnant to purge, NOT a value to honor.", "cream": "#faf7f2", "cream-2": "#f3eee3", "teal": "#1f4e5b", "rust": "#b8541a" }` — an exact, four-for-four match with what the emails ship. The migration tool that was supposed to catch this, scripts/migrate-warm-palette.mjs, maps `rgba(31,78,91,` -> `rgba(42,80,200,` at :86-87 and runs in wrangler.jsonc's build.command, but it only rewrites the tarred site tree; src/ is Worker code, explicitly excluded from the tar. And scripts/check-tokens-sync.mjs reads exactly one file — `const SITE_CSS = path.join(REPO, "assets/site.css")` at :30 — so the cross-repo token contract the audit praised as 'gated on both ends' structurally cannot see the email surface at all.
impact: founder-vision.md names the emailed monthly edition as 'the anchor + the email re-engagement hook' and re-weights the entire return-visitor strategy onto it, because monthly is a weak habit loop. That hook arrives in an inbox wearing a teal-and-warm-cream identity the site retired, then lands the reader on a cool blue-and-grey site. For a company whose only differentiator is that it looks more competent than MarginEdge, a brand discontinuity at the single highest-intent click in the funnel is expensive — and it is invisible to every gate because the token spine ends at assets/site.css.
rec: Re-pigment src/lib/templates.js and templates.es.js to the spine (#1F4E5B -> #2A50C8, #FAF7F2 -> #F6F7F8, #F3EEE3 -> #EDEEF1, #B8541A -> #C42E2E), verifying against the two files' shared function-pair convention so EN and ES move together. Then widen check-tokens-sync.mjs from a single SITE_CSS constant to a root list that includes src/lib/templates*.js and brand/og/, with an explicit skip list — and add the four retiredWarmPalette hexes as a hard denylist so any reintroduction reds CI. This is the cheapest of the missed findings and the one with the clearest funnel consequence.

title: The Cost-Index price chart hardcodes its colors inline and has no dark variant — 2.45:1 in dark mode, below the 3:1 graphical-object floor — while its sibling chart on the same page themes correctly
evidence: The mtn-spark SVGs are emitted with literal hex in presentation attributes: `stroke="#2A50C8"` on the trend path, the baseline <line> and the current-point <circle> (2 charts per page). The pages ship real dark-mode support — 18 `prefers-color-scheme: dark` / `[data-theme='dark']` blocks in cost-index/asparagus/index.html, plus /assets/theme-toggle.js — and I searched every one of them: none touches .mtn-spark, and grep for 'mtn-spark' across assets/site-core.css and assets/site-article.css returns nothing. The site's own dark palette flips teal to #7AA7FF (scripts/check-contrast.mjs:32, T.dark), which would give 7.44:1. The frozen #2A50C8 gives 2.60:1 on dark section-base #16181D and 2.45:1 on dark raised #1B1E24 — under WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11's 3:1 requirement for graphical objects needed to understand content, which a price line unambiguously is. The contrast is with the season curve immediately above it in the same builder output, which does it right: `.ci-season-curve .sc-band{fill:var(--season);fill-opacity:.15}` and classed .sc-line/.sc-dot/.sc-lab, all theme-aware. Same file, same generator (scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs), two different standards. Neither wired contrast gate can see it: check-contrast.mjs enumerates four hardcoded token names, and check-dark-contrast.mjs likewise never parses SVG presentation attributes.
impact: 194 pages of the flagship surface render their primary data instrument at roughly half the legal contrast floor for any reader on dark mode — which on mobile is a large and growing default, and which this site actively offers with a toggle. It also means the one visual asset the auditor said didn't exist does exist but is invisible to a meaningful share of readers, and the same accessibility statement audited in finding #1 asserts AA conformance over it.
rec: Replace the inline hex in sparkBlock() (scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs:908) with `stroke="currentColor"` plus a `.mtn-spark{color:var(--teal)}` rule and a dark override, mirroring exactly what .sc-band/.sc-line already do fifty lines away. Rebuild all 194 pages. Then extend check-dark-contrast.mjs to parse stroke=/fill= presentation attributes on inline SVG — a literal hex inside an SVG is the one place a token-based contrast gate is guaranteed to miss, and this repo now has a worked example proving it.

title: The small Cost-Index sparkline fills with the retired teal-GREEN under a blue stroke, on 162 pages, because the palette migrator's map has a hole
evidence: The 248x46 sparkline in the ci-read block fills `rgba(31,111,106,0.12)` — that is #1F6F6A, a teal-green — beneath a #2A50C8 (blue) stroke and a #2A50C8 dot. The larger index chart on the same page gets it right: `rgba(42,80,200,0.10)`, which is #2A50C8. So one page ships a green-filled and a blue-filled chart of the same series, ten lines apart. Count: `grep -rl 'rgba(31,111,106' cost-index/ es/cost-index/` returns 162 files. The cause is a gap in the migrator: scripts/migrate-warm-palette.mjs:86-93 maps `rgba(31, 78, 91,`/`rgba(31,78,91,` and `rgba(20,54,64,` but has no entry for `rgba(31,111,106,`, and assets/site-core.css:189 shows the codebase knows this value exists ('even expects a teal-green #1f6f6a'). migrate-warm-palette.mjs runs in the deploy build.command, so it has had every opportunity to fix this and cannot.
impact: Two charts of the same data in two different brand colors, on 162 indexed pages, is the kind of detail a design-literate prospect notices instantly — and 'perceived technical craft against incumbents with no brand legacy' is the founder's stated basis for competing. Second-order, it is evidence that the warm-palette migration is not actually complete despite a deploy-time migrator that reports success, which is worth knowing before anyone certifies the re-pigment as done.
rec: Add `"rgba(31,111,106,": "rgba(42,80,200,"` (and the spaced variant) to migrate-warm-palette.mjs's map, and fix the literal at its source in sparkBlock(). Better: fold this into the currentColor fix above, which removes the hardcoded fill entirely. Then grep the tree for the other retiredWarmPalette values in rgba() form — the map covers two of five and nothing proves the other three are absent.

title: The article-graphics gate's clean run is purchased by 14 active waivers, all Spanish, all 70 days stale — the audit reported the opposite as a headline strength
evidence: The report's third strength claims the gate 'reports 105 articles + 2 generated data pages, 0 violations, with 0 active entries in HISTORICAL_WAIVERS' and calls it 'genuinely unusual' that it accumulated no allowlist debt. The first half reproduces (`node scripts/check-article-graphics.mjs` -> '105 article(s) + 2 generated data page(s) with figures scanned, 0 violations'). The second half is false: HISTORICAL_WAIVERS begins at scripts/check-article-graphics.mjs:194 and holds 14 live entries, every single one dated 2026-05-28 (70 days ago) and every single one an `es/` path — 8 es/library articles waived for rules 1 and 2 ('figures stripped in translation', 'viz-* class missing on figures') plus 6 legacy es/blog slugs. A separate DEDUP_ALLOW list sits alongside it. So the gate is clean because 14 Spanish pages are exempted from the requirement to carry figures at all.
impact: Two harms. First, the audit's single most confident craft compliment is factually inverted, and a future session reading it will believe the design gate carries no debt when it carries 70-day-old debt that is 100% Spanish. Second, and larger: this is a third independent instance — alongside the -49.4% figure being reported at 69 pages instead of 138, and the ES homepage's missing band — of the Spanish surface (645 pages, 47% of the site) being where quality is quietly allowed to lapse. That is a pattern worth naming as a pattern, and no finding in the report does.
rec: Either restore the figures on the 8 es/library articles (the EN originals have them; the translation pipeline stripped them) and delete the waivers, or convert the waiver comments from 'ES translation sweep pending' — a promise now 70 days old — into a dated owner and deadline the way check-idem-coverage.mjs's MANUAL registry requires ('who runs it and when it drifts'). Separately, run a deliberate ES-parity pass across the design gates rather than the locale-existence check check-locale-parity.mjs performs today.

title: `below-fold-island` is on 378 pages and has zero CSS rules anywhere in the repository
evidence: `grep -rl below-fold-island --include=index.html .` returns 252 EN pages and 126 ES; on the homepage it decorates four sections (index.html:673, :851, :888, :912). Searching every stylesheet — `grep -rn below-fold-island --include=*.css .` — returns nothing, and so does the same search across assets/*.js and scripts/. It is a class name with no rule and no JS consumer. git log -S over assets/ finds no commit that ever removed a matching rule, so the styling appears never to have landed.
impact: Small on its own, but it is the reason the auditor's 'EN and ES diverge structurally on the flagship page' reading overstates: the ES homepage's only structural difference from EN, besides the stances band, is the absence of a class that does nothing.
