And because the per-account/per-location bases collide, a founding member with 3-5 locations may sit either above or below the tier they'd otherwise be on with no rule to decide it.
rec: Two founder calls, both cheap and both overdue. (1) Decide whether the founding cohort is bounded — by count, by date, or by neither — and register the answer in the sourced claim, because 'for as long as they stay' is already published and cannot be quietly narrowed. (2) Write the one rule that reconciles per-location founding with per-account tiers before billing is built, not after; add a `volumeBasis` reconciliation assertion to check-pricing-consistency so the two systems cannot drift further. Then redo the break-even at $19/location net $18.15, which is the number that will actually apply.

title: `/api/brand-dossier`: an unauthenticated public endpoint that bills Anthropic tokens per request, on a dead surface, with its cache binding unprovisioned
evidence: `src/worker.js:358` registers `/api/brand-dossier` → `handleBrandDossier`; `:632-634` routes it to the default POST-only branch with no session check, and unlike ~42 other handlers it never calls `isOriginAllowed`. `:4400-4402` gates only on `env.AI && env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. **`env.AI` is definitely bound** — `wrangler.jsonc:345` is `"ai": { "binding": "AI" }`, uncommented, with the comment 'the binding alone costs nothing; usage only accrues on env.AI.run()'. `:4487` is `await env.AI.run('@cf/anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5', {...max_tokens: 400})`. The 1-hour cache at `:4436` goes through `withAuditCache`, which `:4727-4743` no-ops when AUDIT_CACHE is absent — and it is absent (`wrangler.jsonc:322-325` binds only AUDIT_SNAPSHOTS and AUTH_SESSIONS). So every request is a fresh billed inference, capped only by the same 30/min/IP tier as the Places endpoints. The surface it serves is the retired web-studio audit line (CLAUDE.md: 'the web-studio services tiers … retired').
impact: Same exposure class as the Places finding the auditor did flag, but with a firmer trigger: the Places key is a secret whose state is unknown, whereas the AI binding is committed in wrangler.jsonc and provably live. 43,200 requests/day/IP of Haiku inference at 400 max_tokens is a real bill, and it is spent on a page nobody visits. It also quietly contradicts the company's loudest engineering claim — 'no LLM in the read path, build-gated' — by putting an LLM call on an unauthenticated public route of the storefront that markets that promise.
rec: Delete `/api/brand-dossier` from `API_ROUTES` at src/worker.js:358 along with the four Places/PSI entries; it serves a retired line and no live page calls it. If it is being kept for the workbench, put it behind the same session gate `/api/workbench/*` uses and require `AUDIT_CACHE` to be bound before the handler will run, so an unprovisioned cache fails closed instead of billing per call. Either way, check whether ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is still set on the Worker in the same pass as the Places key check.

title: The pricing gate the auditor praised does not verify billability — `basis: "per_seat"` is an unconditional pass and no Stripe configuration is checked at all
evidence: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:36-40` defines `billable` as 'a customer can actually be charged this today: a matching SKU in stripe-tiers.ts, a branch in priceIdForTier, and a STRIPE_PRICE_* env field.' The gate that enforces it, `scripts/check-pricing-consistency.mjs:308-317`, checks exactly one of those three: `const hasTier = Object.values(tiers).includes(price.cents) || price.basis === "per_seat"` — i.e. the dollar figure appears somewhere in the TIERS table, and any `per_seat` entry (accountantSeat) passes unconditionally with no check whatsoever. It never reads priceIdForTier, never asserts a STRIPE_PRICE_* field is populated, and never touches STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. The three-condition check does run — but only on the `billable: false` branch at `:326-329`, to catch a stale exemption. Runtime reality: `apps/api/wrangler.toml` contains no STRIPE_* entries, so `priceIdForTier` returns undefined and `apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:150-158` answers `tier_unconfigured` 500 for solo, team and accountant alike.
impact: The report holds this registry up as 'exactly the kind of gate that measures grounding rather than shape.' It is the opposite: it verifies that a number appears in a table. Its green run prints 'NOT BILLABLE TODAY — founding' while three other prices are equally uncollectable, which means the standing CI line the company is relying on to keep the billing gap visible is understating that gap by three quarters. That is precisely the 2026-07-30 lesson recurring inside the fix written for the 2026-07-30 lesson.
rec: Invert the asymmetry: run the same three-condition test on the `billable: true` branch that already runs on the false branch — require a priceIdForTier branch naming the tier and a `STRIPE_PRICE_*` field for it in env.ts — and delete the `|| price.basis === "per_seat"` escape. Then either flip solo/team/accountant to `billable: false` with a dated reason until Stripe is configured, or add the check that Stripe is configured. Today the registry's own definition of `billable` is false for all four entries.

title: The published per-invoice cost table bills a service with zero callers, and its printed total is below the sum of its own rows
evidence: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/about/cost/page.tsx:57-63` publishes an AWS KMS row — 'Locking your data, per invoice … ~$0.0003'. `apps/api/src/lib/kms-client.ts:1-8` says 'Status: PRE-FAB ONLY. This module is unused in production until the Phase 1 queue.ts wiring lands', and a grep for `kms-client` across `apps/api/src/` returns zero importers. Separately, the five published rows sum to $0.0048 (0.002 + 0.001 + 0.0003 + 0.001 + 0.0005) while `:177` hardcodes the total as `~$0.004`. The page's `lastReviewed` is 2026-06-11 (copy.ts:3246) — 57 days stale as of today — on a page whose own correction block (copy.ts:3268) states 'we will republish exact figures from the next billing cycle' and whose table note promises republication 'when drift passes 20%'.
impact: Small dollars, but this is the one page whose entire premise is that publishing the cost math honestly IS the brand — it carries a dated self-correction for exactly this class of error. It currently charges customers' mental model for a service that is not in the path, rounds its own total down, and has missed two billing cycles against its own republish promise. The auditor cited the KMS 'PRE-FAB ONLY' comment inside the break-even inputs but never noticed it contradicts the published table.
rec: Drop the KMS row until kms-client.ts has a caller (or relabel it as planned), fix the total to match the rows, and republish from the July bill in the same pass that reconciles the Fly figure. If the republish cadence cannot be met by hand, change the promise on the page rather than letting it go stale — a missed promise on the honesty page costs more than the $0.0003 the row describes.

title: Zero confirmed users after ~15 months of build — and no artifact in either repo names a single non-founder operator
effort: 2 weeks to set up; 60 days to read
evidence: `Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/transparency-2026q2.md:36-38` — 'The numbers below are illustrative for the first publication (private beta; no live customers as of 2026-05-11)', with ingest/extractions/operator-confirmations all 0. `services/extract/CONFIDENCE-CALIBRATION.md:149-151` (2026-06-18) — 'using reconciliation as the correctness label (the operator correction log is still empty pre-pilot)'. `docs/sub-processors.md:73-74` — 'no customer data has flowed yet because no customers have connected'. `potentially-profitable/data/article-fieldnotes.json` ships `"fieldnotes": {}` — zero reader submissions since the Field Notes subsystem (855-line `admin/submissions/index.html`, 251-line `src/lib/submissions.js`) went in. `runbooks/founder-todos.md` §4 F7/F8 still park the testimonial and the `/customers/[name]` story page on 'operator signs release'. Grepping both trees for design partner / beta operator / testimonial returns only proposal prose (`runbooks/proposals/landing-refresh/lens-12-social-proof.md:26` is literally titled 'The honest baseline — what we ship with zero customers').
impact: Every product decision, every one of the ~2,500 files, the entire retention architecture, and the $19 and $150 price points rest on an untested hypothesis about what a restaurant operator wants. The company has spent its scarcest resource — a full-time-employed founder's nights — on a machine no one has asked for in writing. This is the fact that makes every other finding in this domain secondary.
rec: Stop building for 30 days. Convert the single asset you already have into the first validated user: run Muntin Ledger on Tacombi Bethesda + Arlington yourself for 60 days (see the next finding), then hand-recruit 3 DMV operators you already know by name and put them on the SIGNIN_ALLOWLIST. Set one number as the company's north star — 'operators who uploaded an invoice in the last 14 days' — and put it on `/admin/kpis/` above everything else.
note: All three citations reproduced verbatim: Muntin-Invoice-Decoder/docs/transparency-2026q2.md:36-38 ("illustrative for the first publication (private beta; no live customers as of 2026-05-11)"), services/extract/CONFIDENCE-CALIBRATION.md:149-151 ("the operator correction log is still empty pre-pilot"), docs/sub-processors.md rows 7-8 ("no customer data has flowed yet because no customers have connected"). potentially-profitable/data/article-fieldnotes.json ships `"fieldnotes": {}`. Fair caveat the report does not make: zero self-serve users is partly DELIBERATE — apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:481,623 close sign-in to SIGNIN_ALLOWLIST pre-launch, and ADR-020 deferred the launch. The defect is not "no self-serve signups"; it is that in a deliberately-closed beta nobody was put ON the allowlist. Severity critical stands.

title: The founder dogfoods the extraction ENGINE on real Tacombi invoices but has never run the PRODUCT — the activation path is untested by anyone, including him
effort: 1 week to wire; 60 days to run
evidence: ~20 CLIs under `services/extract/cli/` all document `--buyer "Tacombi Bethesda" --buyer "Tacombi"` against `~/muntin-docling-json-new` (e.g. `corpus_seed.py:28`, `vendor_flywheel.py:65`, `total_gap.py:25`, `handoff_coverage.py:16`), and `services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/` holds 7 real docling dumps (baldor, chefs_warehouse, cintas, fresco, i_halper). That is the offline engine path. The product path is empty: `find . -name "fc_*.golden.json"` returns **0** despite `runbooks/founders-choice.md` documenting the `pnpm fc add` harness end-to-end; the operator correction log is empty (`CONFIDENCE-CALIBRATION.md:150`); transparency counts are 0. The three rows sitting in `needs_review` at 29-35% confidence (CLAUDE.md — ImperialDade, chefswarehouse, SOLD TO) are described as 'from before the current pipeline' with source PDFs unavailable — i.e. nobody has uploaded through the live app recently enough to matter.
impact: The upload → extract → review → confirm → ledger → insight loop — the entire thing the customer pays for — has never been walked by a real operator on real invoices, not even by the one person who has both the invoices and the restaurant. Every activation assumption (time-to-first-value, how many taps a review costs at 10pm, whether the inbox is legible after a shift) is unvalidated, and the corpus that could answer it is being consumed by CLIs that write nothing back into the product.
rec: Point the founder's own invoice flow at app.muntin.digital for 60 days: forward or upload every Tacombi invoice through the real product, review them in the real inbox, and let the templates promote through the real `record_confirmation` path. Log the honest numbers weekly — invoices uploaded, % landing in needs_review, minutes per review, invoices-until-first-auto-confirm per vendor. That log is simultaneously your activation dataset, your first-customer proof, and the input the correction-log-dependent work (`cli/calibration_replay.py`) has been parked on for two months.
note: Reproduced independently: `find . -name "fc_*.golden.json" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` returns 0; services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/ holds 7 real docling dumps (baldor_collapse, chefs_warehouse_stacked_header, cintas_fail_total, cintas_pricezero_2, fresco_lineitems, fresco_merged_header, ihalper_metadata_header). The engine-vs-product split is real and is the sharpest finding in the report.

title: Cold start: 3-4 manual confirmations per vendor per layout before any hands-off read, and all three mechanisms that could shortcut it are off or unsound
effort: 3 days for the vendor-trust flip + shadow read; 2-3 weeks for the community-pool fingerprint fix
evidence: `services/extract/drift.py:134-141` — an empty template (any brand-new vendor) returns `NEW_LAYOUT` with `miss_critical=True`. `engine_pkg/constants.py:104` puts `drift:new_layout` in `HARD_BLOCK_REASON_PREFIXES`, and `orchestrate.py:2242` sets `needs_review = any(_is_hard_block(r))`. Auto-confirm gate #2 (`engine_pkg/review.py:199-201`) requires `template.state == ACTIVE` (>=3 prior confirmations) AND gate #1 requires `extraction_method` in ('template','template_synonym') — so a first-touch synonym_only/generic_harvest read can never auto-confirm. `template_store.py:100` sets `LINE_ITEM_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD = 4` (3 with a catalog-matched vendor per `_promotion_threshold`, lines 137-180). Shortcut 1 — the vendor-trust OR-path — defaults to SHADOW: `services/extract/README.md:137` `EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE | off (shadow)`, and `main.py:119` only activates on the literal '1'. Shortcut 2 — the community pool — is dark and broken: `docs/plans/first-try-reliability-roadmap.md` §2 documents that a pooled line-item rule's `fingerprint_v2` folds `row_anchor_norm` (the row's SKU), so 'a pooled line-item rule matches at most the single fresh-org row whose SKU coincides with the reference row (≈ never)', supply side SEVERED, deployment DARK, and gate (a) real-invoice coverage still unmet. Shortcut 3 — the anonymous `/try` demo — is 'parked, per the operator's constraint' per the same roadmap.
impact: A restaurant with a dozen active vendors faces roughly 36-48 hand-confirmed invoices before the product runs itself, spread over weeks because most vendors deliver 1-3x/week. The buyer is a person who took this on precisely because they have no time. The measured ~75% first-sight to ~95%+ templated lift (`cli/seed_template.py` docstring, quoted in the roadmap §1) is real but holds PER-ORG ONLY — one operator's confirmations help nobody else, so every new customer pays the full tax from zero. This is the classic extraction-product churn mechanism and it is architecturally present, not hypothetical.
rec: Pick ONE shortcut and finish it rather than holding three at 80%. Cheapest with the most evidence behind it: flip `EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE=1` for the seven vendors `VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:213-224` measured above 83% reconcile (i_halper, chefs_warehouse, baldor, pat_lafrieda, edward_don, fresco_products, montgomery_county_dlc), after reading the shadow-agreement rate the flag was built to produce. Reconciliation stays the final gate, so the downside is bounded. Separately, instrument and publish 'invoices until first auto-confirm, per vendor' as a product KPI — it is the number that governs whether anyone stays.
note: Mechanism CONFIRMED: services/extract/template_store.py:100 `LINE_ITEM_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD: int = 4` (note the path is services/extract/template_store.py, NOT engine_pkg/ as cited — the auditor's file:line is wrong); services/extract/main.py:120 activates vendor-trust only on the literal "1"; README.md:137 confirms `off (shadow)` default. But SHORTCUT 3 IS REFUTED AS STATED. The auditor read docs/plans/first-try-reliability-roadmap.md prose and never opened the route table: /try is BUILT AND MOUNTED — apps/api/src/index.ts:310 `app.route("/v1/demo", demoExtract)`, and apps/api/src/env.ts:620-624 documents DEMO_ANONYMOUS_EXTRACT as an EMERGENCY KILL SWITCH whose default (unset) "keeps the route live"; apps/api/wrangler.toml sets no value. What the roadmap parks is the community-pool-backed first-try QUALITY gate, not the surface. So the report says a shipped, live-by-default acquisition surface is 'parked' — and misses the far worse fact that it is unlinked (see missed finding).

title: The two highest-ranked retention loops are a no-op scaffold aimed at the retired product line, and an unbuilt alert
effort: 2 weeks
evidence: `docs/handoff/retention-strategy.md` ranks the architecture: (2) 'Event-spike alerts — the real return engine for this audience', (3) 'Free tools — the everyday first-visit win … the *save* ("save this, we'll tell you when it moves")'. Loop 3's watch half is an explicit stub: `src/lib/watch-checks.js:9-17` — 'FIRST-PASS SCAFFOLD: every recheck function currently returns the score baked into the saved payload … the diff vs. lastScore will always be 0, so no email fires.' Worse, the watchable kinds are the RETIRED web-studio checks, not cost: `src/lib/workbench.js:111-113` — `WATCHABLE_KINDS = {'audit','seo','gbp','mobile','schema','speed'}`. Loop 2 does not exist on the public side at all: `src/lib/templates.js` has lifecycle + digest templates and no cost-movement alert; the only real one is the paid-Ledger ADR-010 digest (`apps/api/src/scheduled/cost-watch-digest.ts`, cron `0 15 * * 2`), which is opt-in default-off and requires `price_hike` verdicts, which require >=2 non-provisional observations of the same canonical item at >=8% AND >=$5 (`apps/api/src/lib/verdict-compute.ts:60-67`, `verdicts-store.ts:1492`). The one push producer in the whole system fires only when a QBO/Xero post is blocked by the anomaly gate (`apps/api/src/lib/anomaly-push-enqueue.ts`, called once from `routes/integrations/posting.ts:783`). `src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js:22` gates all lifecycle mail behind `LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED === 'true'`, default off, and still imports the retired course templates.
impact: The company's own strategy names event-driven reach as 'the real return engine for this audience' and 'more defensible + more honest than any calendar ritual' — and the free/public side has no reach channel whatsoever. A visitor who saves something is told, in effect, 'we'll tell you when it moves,' and the code guarantees they will never be told. The only working reach lives behind a paid account, an invoice history, and a default-off toggle — i.e. behind exactly the activation wall the previous finding describes.
rec: Build ONE public cost-movement alert against the Cost Index basket an anonymous visitor can save — threshold-gated, sometimes reassuring ('this barely moved your plate'), one email. That is loop 2, it needs no accounts, and the retention doc already specifies its honesty guards. In the same commit, either point `WATCHABLE_KINDS` at ingredient/basket watches or delete the watch surface entirely — a scaffold that silently promises notification is worse than no button.
note: src/lib/watch-checks.js:9-17 reproduced verbatim ("the diff vs. lastScore will always be 0, so no email fires"). src/lib/workbench.js:111-113 `WATCHABLE_KINDS = new Set(['audit','seo','gbp','mobile','schema','speed'])` — all retired-studio kinds, zero cost kinds. src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js:18-21 gates on LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED === 'true', default off. apps/api/wrangler.toml:260 confirms the `0 15 * * 2` digest cron exists. Severity high stands.

title: Nothing measures signup, activation, or retention — the KPI set has no customer metric, the dashboard is static, and the one live experiment cannot be read
effort: 1 week
evidence: `data/kpis.json` holds 4 KPIs — organic sessions, tool-engagement rate, workshop-save rate, window-engagement rate. Not one measures a signup, an activation, or a return. `admin/kpis/index.html` states in its own CSS comment: 'v1 is a static registry view — the live Plausible numbers are looked up by following the per-tile link'. The weekly KPI email prints, verbatim, 'Live values are not yet wired (Plausible Stats API requires a separate token). This email confirms the cron ran' (`src/worker.js:1419`), and only fires when `KPI_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED === 'true'` (`src/worker.js:1395`). `data/experiments.json` has one experiment (`window-cta-copy`) `"status":"running"` since 2026-06-17 — **50 days** — with `"concludedAt": null`, `minExposuresPerArm: 200`, and `_lastReviewed: "2026-04-30"` (**98 days** stale). Its gate, `scripts/check-experiments-parity.mjs`, verifies only that the experiment NAMES match between JSON and worker; it exits 0 today. On the product side `runbooks/funnel-events.md` defines ten `funnel.*` events that 'emit via the existing log() helper … and stream to the founder's log-drain', but `apps/api/wrangler.toml` declares no `tail_consumers` and no logpush, and `runbooks/founder-todos.md` F14 ('funnel.* events reaching log-drain — Provision the BetterStack drain destination') is still open.
impact: This is the audit's own lesson recurring inside the growth stack: `check-experiments-parity` and `check-kpi-doc` both pass green while measuring shape rather than grounding. If ten operators signed up tomorrow, nothing in either repo would tell the founder how many uploaded an invoice, how many came back in week 2, or which page converted them — and the one running experiment would keep splitting traffic forever because nothing enforces a conclusion date.
rec: Replace the 4 traffic KPIs with 4 funnel KPIs — waitlist signups/week, signups→first upload, first upload→3rd upload, 14-day active operators — and wire the Plausible Stats API token so `/admin/kpis/` shows numbers instead of links. Add a `concludeBy` field to `data/experiments.json` and make the gate fail past it. Provision the log drain (F14); until it exists, `funnel.*` is instrumentation that writes to nowhere.
note: Ran the gate myself: `node scripts/check-experiments-parity.mjs` → exit 0, output "Experiments parity: 1 experiment(s) match across data/experiments.json + src/worker.js" — it asserts name parity only, nothing about concludedAt. data/kpis.json holds exactly the 4 traffic KPIs claimed. src/worker.js:1394 `KPI_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED !== 'true'` and the verbatim "Live values are not yet wired" string reproduced. `grep -n "tail_consumers|logpush" apps/api/wrangler.toml` returns NOTHING — the funnel.* log-drain claim is confirmed dead. Staleness recomputed for 2026-08-07: experiment running 51 days, _lastReviewed 99 days.

title: The one retention anchor that exists has published once in 62 days, and the public index still opens on a 66-day-old price
effort: 3 days for the edition; 1 week for the frozen-series treatment
evidence: `data/cost-index-editions.json` contains **4 editions ever** — 2026-06-05, 2026-06-16, 2026-06-18, 2026-07-06. Three fall inside a 13-day window in June; the latest is **31 days** old today (2026-08-06). `blog/` confirms: `cost-index-week-2026-07-06` is the last dispatch directory. Computed from `data/cost-index.json`: **18 of 100** ingredients are >30 days stale and **17 sit at exactly 66 days** (salmon-fillet, shrimp, vegetable-oil, tuna-loin, whole-lobster, scallops, clams, squid, octopus…, all NOAA), against a median age of 2 days. `cost-index/index.html:677` says it out loud to every visitor: '3 of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01.' `scripts/check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` prints '✓ Cost Index dispatch is current' because 27d ≤ its 38-day allowance. `docs/handoff/retention-strategy.md` punch-list item **0** (written 2026-07-11) reads: 'Fix staleness + the cadence contradiction FIRST … it *opens on a 10-week-old anchor* — which literally teaches people not to return … precondition for everything.' 26 days later it is 9.4 weeks and unfixed.
impact: The Cost Index is the entire top of funnel and, under ADR-020, the product the company is now building first. A returning visitor's first impression is a seafood page frozen since June and a masthead admitting it. The company's own retention analysis identifies this as the mechanism that trains people not to come back, ranks it as the thing to fix before anything else, and it has not been fixed. Meanwhile the monthly publication — the deliberate, founder-chosen habit anchor — has effectively skipped a month and the freshness gate is calibrated loosely enough not to say so.
rec: Two moves this week. (1) Write the August edition; the gate is designed to remind, not to publish, and a 4-edition-total 'monthly publication' with a 31-day gap has no habit to anchor. (2) Give the 17 NOAA-frozen series a terminal treatment — either substitute a live source, or render them explicitly retired per ADR-021 rather than as live prices holding last-good. A visitor should never see a two-month-old number presented in the same visual register as a two-day-old one.
note: Numbers reproduced and slightly corrected. data/cost-index-editions.json holds exactly 4 asOf values (2026-06-05, 06-16, 06-18, 07-06); latest is 32 days old today. Recomputed from data/cost-index.json across all 100 ingredients: 18 are >30d stale, 17 sit at exactly 67 days, median age 3 days. cost-index/index.html:677 reproduced verbatim: "3 of 16 staples are holding last-good since 2026-06-01." WHERE IT IS WRONG: the auditor calls the 17 frozen series "all NOAA". They are not — the 67-day cohort includes `vegetable-oil` and `pork-belly`, neither a NOAA series, and `ground-beef` sits at 58 days. Attributing the whole freeze to one upstream outage under-describes it: at least two frozen series have a different, unexplained cause the founder would not go looking for.

title: The accountant tier is marked billable at $150/mo + $30/seat but its multi-client surface has no web UI — the cheapest expansion lever is an API half
effort: 1 week for the cockpit; 1 hour for the honest registry entry
evidence: `apps/web/lib/pricing-constants.ts:49-50` declares `accountant: { cents: 15000, basis: "per_account", billable: true }` and `accountantSeat: { cents: 3000, basis: "per_seat", billable: true }`. The API half exists: `apps/api/src/routes/cockpit.ts:11-17` ships `GET /v1/cockpit/workspaces` returning the caller's memberships, with `POST /switch` noted as 'D.4'. The web half does not: grepping `apps/web` for 'cockpit' returns exactly two hits — an error-code string in `settings/members/members-client.tsx:35` and a comment in a generated file. `find apps/web/app -ipath "*cockpit*"` returns nothing. `STATUS-v6.md` listed this as ranked launch-blocker #5 ('Accountant tier sells a UI that doesn't exist — invite/switcher/cockpit absent') and it remains true. The one accountant-facing thing that does work is a one-time, single-use, 7-day export token (`apps/api/src/routes/accountant-handoffs.ts:26-38`) — and even there `csv | pdfs | accountant` shapes return 503.
impact: An accountant who serves 8 restaurants is the single cheapest acquisition path this company has: one sale, eight orgs, and a buyer who reads invoices for a living and will actually value determinism. That lever is priced, declared billable, and has no product behind it — so it cannot be sold, and worse, if it were sold the customer would find nothing there.
rec: Ship the smallest honest cockpit: a workspace list + switcher page in `apps/web/app/(product)/cockpit/` over the existing `GET /v1/cockpit/workspaces`, plus `POST /switch`. That is days of work against an API that already exists and is already tenant-safe. Until it ships, mark `accountant` and `accountantSeat` `billable: false` in `pricing-constants.ts` with a dated reason — the registry's entire purpose is to stop a posted price from describing a business that does not exist, and right now it is doing that for $19 while missing it for $150.
note: Web half CONFIRMED: `find apps/web/app -ipath "*cockpit*"` returns nothing; the only apps/web hits are an error-code string (settings/members/members-client.tsx:35,80) and a comment in verify-content.generated.ts:3660. pricing-constants.ts:49-50 confirmed billable:true for accountant + accountantSeat. BUT the API claim is WRONG: the auditor reports POST /switch as merely "noted as 'D.4'" — it is SHIPPED. cockpit.ts:67 `cockpit.get("/workspaces")` AND cockpit.ts:100 `cockpit.post("/switch")`, both mounted at apps/api/src/index.ts:302 `app.route("/v1/cockpit", cockpit)`. The auditor read the file's header docstring (which still says "D.4 adds POST /switch") instead of the route registrations 60 lines below — the exact stale-doc failure mode this audit was commissioned to avoid. This makes the recommendation cheaper, not weaker, so severity high stands.

title: Every storefront waitlist signup is relabeled 'studio' before it reaches the product, and the form promises a confirmation step that does not exist
effort: 2 hours
evidence: `index.html:828` posts `source="home-founding"`; `ledger/index.html:673` and `es/ledger/index.html:615` post `source="ledger-pricing"`; `es/index.html:835` posts `home-founding`. But `src/worker.js:8921` defines `WAITLIST_SOURCES = new Set(['studio','studio-hero','studio-product','studio-banner'])` and line 8943 clamps: `const source = WAITLIST_SOURCES.has(body.source) ? body.source : 'studio'`. Neither real value is in the set, so all four live capture points arrive at `apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts` tagged `studio` — the label for the retired web-studio line. Separately, `index.html:837` reads 'Thanks — check your inbox to confirm your spot', but the product route persists immediately and `apps/api/src/lib/email.ts:591 sendWaitlistConfirmationEmail` sends a receipt with no confirm token (unlike `/api/subscribe`, which does mint a `sub-confirm:` token at `src/worker.js:8878`).
impact: When founding members do start arriving, the founder cannot tell whether the homepage, the /ledger/ pricing block, or the Spanish surfaces converted them — the single most useful thing a pre-revenue funnel can learn, discarded in one line. The copy issue is smaller but corrosive on a brand built on precision: a signup who never sees the receipt (spam filter) reasonably concludes they are not on the list, and one who does gets told to confirm something with no link to click.
rec: Add `home-founding`, `ledger-pricing` (and any future capture surface) to both `WAITLIST_SOURCES` in `src/worker.js` and `ALLOWED_SOURCES` in `apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts` — they must be changed together, so add a gate that asserts every `name="source"` value in the HTML appears in both sets. Then change the inline copy to 'Thanks — you're on the list. A confirmation is on its way.'
note: Fully reproduced. src/worker.js:8921 `WAITLIST_SOURCES = new Set(['studio','studio-hero','studio-product','studio-banner'])`; :8943 `const source = WAITLIST_SOURCES.has(body.source) ? body.source : 'studio'`. The four live capture points post values not in that set: index.html:828 + es/index.html:835 = `home-founding`; ledger/index.html:673 + es/ledger/index.html:615 = `ledger-pricing`. apps/api/src/routes/waitlist.ts ALLOWED_SOURCES likewise lacks both. STRENGTHENED: the forms also carry `data-surface="home-founding"` / `"ledger-pricing"`, but `grep -rn "data-surface" assets/ src/` returns ZERO JS hits — nothing reads it, so Plausible does not recover the attribution either. Both recovery paths are dead, and this is the ONLY conversion event a pre-revenue company can capture. Raising medium → high.

title: Onboarding puts the paywall and two crypto chores ahead of first value, and the engine's easy one-tap confirm has no inbox surface
effort: 3 days
evidence: `apps/api/src/routes/onboarding.ts:36-40` fixes the step order as passkey → recovery_phrase → subscription → first_extraction → first_posting — three steps before the operator ever sees an invoice read, and the docstring calls it 'the natural setup sequence'. `/today` renders it (`apps/web/app/(product)/today/page.tsx:99`). Separately: `orchestrate.py:1618-1636` deliberately demotes a reconciling new-layout invoice from a hard block to `confirm_new_layout:reconciled` — 'an easy ONE-TAP confirm rather than a hard dead-end review' — which is a SOFT reason, so `needs_review` stays False (`orchestrate.py:2242`). But the inbox fetches only `?status=needs_review` (`apps/web/app/(product)/inbox/page.tsx:81`). The one-tap the engine engineered lands on a document that is not in the review queue.
impact: Time-to-first-value is the whole ballgame for a product whose buyer is exhausted, and the checklist spends the operator's first three units of patience on a passkey, a recovery phrase, and a plan choice — none of which show them a single number about their own costs. The orphaned soft-confirm compounds it: on the corpus's own numbers a large share of first-touch invoices reconcile, so the most common day-one outcome is a document that quietly needs a confirmation the operator is never shown, which then never promotes a template, which extends the cold-start tax indefinitely.
rec: Reorder the checklist to first_extraction → passkey → recovery_phrase → subscription → first_posting; nothing in the API forces the current order beyond the docstring. Add a `?severity=soft_flag` (or `status=ready&has_reasons=true`) lane to the inbox so `confirm_new_layout:reconciled` documents surface as a one-tap queue — that queue is simultaneously the fastest path to template promotion and the least painful work you can ask a new operator to do.
note: Both halves reproduced and the second is worse than rated. onboarding.ts:34-40 fixes passkey → recovery_phrase → subscription → first_extraction → first_posting. orchestrate.py:1618-1636 emits `confirm_new_layout:reconciled`; engine_pkg/constants.py:252 lists `confirm_new_layout:` in the SOFT set with an explicit comment "still surfaces to the operator"; orchestrate.py:2242 `needs_review = any(_is_hard_block(r))` → False; apps/api/src/lib/queue.ts:1066-1068 therefore writes status `"ready"`; and apps/web/app/(product)/inbox/page.tsx:81 fetches only `?status=needs_review`. The engine's own comment promises a surface the web app does not implement — a documented intent with no caller. This is the mechanical CAUSE of the high-rated cold-start tax (no confirm → no template promotion → tax never ends), so it is not a medium.

title: There is no referral, share, or expansion mechanic anywhere in either repo
effort: 1 week, after the cockpit
evidence: Grepping `apps/`, `docs/`, and `runbooks/` for referral / refer-a-friend / invite-a-friend / share-link returns only proposal prose (`runbooks/proposals/landing-refresh/lens-12-social-proof.md`, `lens-13`, `runbooks/plausible-ce-activation.md`) — no route, no store, no migration, no UI. The only fan-out primitives that exist are `members.post("/invite")` (`apps/api/src/routes/members.ts:175`, staff INTO your own org, tier-gated and volume-capped) and the single-use 7-day accountant handoff token (`apps/api/src/routes/accountant-handoffs.ts`). On the storefront, `data/experiments.json` shows the only growth experiment is CTA copy, and `src/lib/share-snapshots.js` (92 lines) shares a tool result, with no attribution back to a signup.
impact: A one-person company with no marketing budget and a full-time job cannot buy growth; it has to be built into the product or it does not happen. Right now every new operator is a fresh act of founder effort, which caps the business at whatever Don can personally recruit on his days off. The strongest natural loop — an accountant carrying the product into their client book — is blocked by the missing cockpit (see that finding), and the second-strongest — an operator forwarding a genuinely surprising cost read to a peer — has no share affordance on the paid surfaces at all.
rec: Do not build a referral program with rewards; build the one honest share. When the cost-watch digest or an invoice alert produces a real finding, offer 'send this read to someone' — a single link with a source tag that lands on the waitlist form. That is one route, one tagged param, and it rides value that already exists. Sequence it after the accountant cockpit, which is the higher-leverage version of the same lever.
note: The greps hold — members.ts:175 invite and accountant-handoffs.ts are the only fan-out primitives, and there is no referral route/store/migration. But the finding is an absence-of-feature complaint against a pre-launch product whose sign-in is deliberately closed (auth.ts:481), and it misses that a genuine acquisition surface already exists and is live: /try captures the founding list at the success peak (apps/web/app/(marketing)/try/page.tsx:22-26). Recommending a share loop that rides value 'when the cost-watch digest produces a real finding' sequences a growth mechanic behind two other unbuilt things. Weakest finding in the report; medium → low.

title: Every product CTA on the storefront — 496 links across 405 pages — points at ledger.muntin.digital, a hostname neither repo routes
evidence: `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc:26-31` declares exactly ONE route for the product Worker: `{"pattern": "app.muntin.digital/*", "zone_name": "muntin.digital"}`. There is no ledger.muntin.digital route in apps/web/wrangler.jsonc, apps/api/wrangler.toml, or potentially-profitable/wrangler.jsonc. Yet on the storefront `grep -rl "ledger.muntin.digital" --include=*.html` = 405 files and `grep -rho "https://ledger.muntin.digital[^\"']*"` = 496 hits on `/` plus 10 on `/promises`, 4 on `/#app`, 2 on `/legal/terms`. It is generated, not incidental: `scripts/inject-ledger-cta.mjs:51 const LEDGER_URL = 'https://ledger.muntin.digital/'`, plus build-cuisine-landing-pages.mjs:447, build-ingredient-yield-pages.mjs:773, build-theme-story-pages.mjs:222, build-themes-review-board.mjs:297. Simultaneously the product app's own identity defaults to that same unrouted host: `apps/web/app/robots.ts:16`, `sitemap.ts:27`, `layout.tsx:51,258,263,351,371`, `(marketing)/verify/page.tsx:121`, `.well-known/security.txt/route.ts:14` all read `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "https://ledger.muntin.digital"` — while `wrangler.jsonc:52` sets `APP_ORIGIN: "https://app.muntin.digital"`. The only deploy guard, `scripts/guard-web-deploy-env.mjs:40`, validates `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` and nothing else — SITE_URL is unguarded, so the fallback ships unless someone remembers to set it. No gate in either repo asserts the CTA host, and the storefront's link checkers (check-blog-index-links.mjs, check-retired-links.mjs) do not resolve external hosts.
impact: This is the single seam between the entire top of funnel and the product, and the repos disagree with themselves about where it lands. Two possibilities, both bad: (a) ledger.muntin.digital is unrouted, and every 'See Muntin Ledger' button on 405 pages — the payoff of every article, every tool, the whole Cost Index funnel — is a dead link, in which case the funnel has a 100% leak at the handoff and nothing would tell the founder; or (b) it is routed out-of-repo in the Cloudflare dashboard, in which case the product Worker serves identical marketing pages on two hosts while canonical/sitemap/robots point at one and the deploy route points at the other — duplicate content plus a canonical chain Google has to guess at, on the pages that are supposed to rank. This is precisely the 2026-07-30 lesson recurring: ~170 green gates across both repos and not one asserts that the funnel's exit door has a building behind it.
rec: Resolve the host FIRST (one `curl -I https://ledger.muntin.digital/` from the Mac answers it). Then pick one canonical product host and make the repo say so in one place: add the chosen hostname to `apps/web/wrangler.jsonc` routes, set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` explicitly in the deploy env, extend `guard-web-deploy-env.mjs` to require it and to assert it equals a routed pattern, and add a storefront gate that asserts every `https://<host>` product CTA in HTML matches a single constant that also appears in the product repo's route list. Until that gate exists, the CTA host is an eleven-hand-restated-constant of exactly the kind ADR-020's launch-date fix already eliminated once.

title: /try — the shipped, live-by-default 'read your own invoice' surface with founding-list capture — has ZERO inbound links from the 1,368-page storefront
evidence: The surface is real and un-gated: `apps/web/app/(marketing)/try/page.tsx` with TryItClient.tsx, base-from-invoice.ts, downscale.ts; API mounted at `apps/api/src/index.ts:310`; `apps/api/src/env.ts:620-624` documents DEMO_ANONYMOUS_EXTRACT as a kill switch whose unset default "keeps the route live"; apps/api/wrangler.toml sets no value. Its docstring (try/page.tsx:19-26) states it "reads the visitor's OWN file live via POST /v1/demo/extract, with the founding-list capture at the success peak and on every off-ramp." Now the funnel: `grep -rn "ledger.muntin.digital/try" --include=*.html --include=*.mjs .` across the storefront returns NOTHING. Zero. All 496 product CTAs land on `/` . What the storefront does link is its own static mockup: `index.html:840` — "Want to see it first? Walk the mockup demo →" pointing at `/ledger/demo/`, a 2,518-line hand-authored page whose outbound hrefs are `/ledger/` (5), `/window/` (4), `/cost-index/` (4), `/tools/`, `/studio/`, `/library/` — it never once reaches the product.
impact: The auditor's own headline finding is that the product front-loads work and back-loads payoff, and that nothing lets an operator see value before the cold-start tax. The answer to that already exists, is built, hardened (Turnstile, phone-photo downscale, per-IP/ASN budget breakers), live by default, and captures the founding list at the moment of delight — and the 1,368-page content engine that is the company's entire acquisition strategy does not point a single link at it. The visitor most likely to convert (someone reading a cost article with an invoice on their desk) is instead routed to a static mockup that dead-ends back into the storefront. This is a one-line fix sitting on top of the most expensive asset the company owns.
rec: Change `scripts/inject-ledger-cta.mjs:51` to point the article CTA at `/try` rather than `/` (after resolving the host question above), and change `index.html:840` + `es/index.html` to offer 'read your own invoice' ahead of the mockup. Tag it (`plausible-event-source`) so the one experiment the company runs finally measures something that matters. Before flipping, confirm `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is set on the API Worker — see the next finding.

title: If TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is unset, the anonymous demo silently hard-caps at ONE run per IP per day — every restaurant on shared wifi gets a 429 on their second invoice
evidence: `apps/api/src/env.ts:625-628`, verbatim: "TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY — Cloudflare Turnstile secret. Required from the second run per IP per day... **When unset, the route degrades to a 1/day-per-IP hard cap (no challenge — just 429 from run 2 onward).** Document the degraded posture in p1-done.md and provision before GA." Defaults if unset are documented at :629-635 (DEMO_DAILY_PER_IP 5/day, DEMO_PER_ASN_PER_MINUTE 200/min) — but the per-IP default only applies once Turnstile exists. On the storefront side the same secret is optional and the failure is silent: `src/worker.js` handleWaitlist calls `checkTurnstile(body, env, request)` and proceeds when `turnstile.skipped` is true, so the anti-spam layer on the founding form is also off by default. No gate in either repo asserts the secret is provisioned; the auditor listed it only as an unknown in a bundled env-flag list, without reading what the degraded posture actually does.
impact: A restaurant is exactly the environment where several people share one NAT'd IP. Under the degraded posture, the second person to try the demo from the same restaurant — or the same person trying a second invoice — gets a 429 with no explanation and no challenge to solve. That is a worse first impression than no demo at all, and it is invisible: it produces no error, no gate failure, and no log the founder reads (there is no log drain — apps/api/wrangler.toml has no tail_consumers). The company's flagship activation asset can be silently throttled to one impression per restaurant per day by an unset secret.
rec: Run `wrangler secret list` on both Workers today and record the result in-repo. Then add a startup/deploy assertion: if the demo route is live (DEMO_ANONYMOUS_EXTRACT not 'off') and TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is unset, fail the deploy guard rather than degrade silently — a fail-closed posture is the same discipline cost-index-valuation.ts already applies to stale snapshots. Same for the storefront waitlist's skipped-Turnstile path.

title: Two disconnected identity systems, and the only 'bottom-of-funnel intent' KPI measures the population that cannot become a customer
evidence: The storefront runs its OWN auth: `src/worker.js:365-368` mounts `/api/auth/magic-link`, `/api/auth/verify`, `/api/auth/me`, `/api/auth/signout` against the `AUTH_SESSIONS` KV, with an `/account/` surface. The product runs a separate one (passkey/password/reset, `apps/web/app/sign-in`, `apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`) on a different host, gated by SIGNIN_ALLOWLIST. Nothing joins them — there is no shared subject, no SSO hand-off, no `waitlist_signups` → storefront-account key. Then `data/kpis.json`, the `window-engagement-rate` KPI: metric = "ratio: distinct visitors with Window Sent ÷ distinct authenticated", described as "Bottom-of-funnel intent." 'Authenticated' there means authenticated on the STOREFRONT. The same file's other three KPIs measure tool runs and Workshop saves — and `src/lib/workbench.js:111-113` shows the Workshop's watchable kinds are all retired web-studio checks.
impact: The company's four north-star KPIs measure a storefront account system that leads nowhere: a visitor can sign in, save Workshop items, and write to Don through /window/ without ever touching an identity the product recognises. 'Bottom-of-funnel intent' is measuring the bottom of a funnel that terminates in a different building. When the founder finally wires the Plausible token (the auditor's fix), he will get precise numbers for a population that must re-register on another host to buy anything — which is worse than no numbers, because it looks like measurement.
rec: Decide whether the storefront account survives at all. If it does, make the join explicit: a storefront-authenticated visitor hitting the product CTA should carry a signed hand-off token so `waitlist_signups` and the product org can be reconciled later. If it does not, retire /account/ and /window/'s auth requirement with the same discipline applied to the course subsystem, and replace `window-engagement-rate` with a metric whose denominator is people who can actually buy. Either way, no KPI should count a storefront session as funnel progress until a join key exists.

title: The only lifecycle-email dispatcher — the storefront's sole owned reach channel — still imports the retired course subsystem at module scope
evidence: `potentially-profitable/src/lib/lifecycle-emails.js:22-27` imports `lifecycleCourseStartedEmail` and `lifecycleCourseCompletedEmail` from `./templates.js`, and `readProgress as readCourseProgress` from `./course.js`. Per potentially-profitable/CLAUDE.md, the entire 'Open the Doors' course subsystem was retired 2026-07-28 — every `/course/` page 301s to `/cost-index/`, the CI gates and injectors were torn out, and `src/lib/course.js` plus the `/api/course/*` KV runtime were explicitly left DORMANT 'with no course pages to feed them'. The dispatcher is gated off (`LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED === 'true'`, default off, :18-21), so nobody has noticed. `docs/handoff/retention-strategy.md` ranks event-driven reach as 'the real return engine for this audience'.
impact: The company's own retention doc names lifecycle mail as a return engine, and the one dispatcher that would carry it is wired half to a product line that no longer exists. Flipping LIFECYCLE_EMAILS_ENABLED — the obvious move the day someone decides to activate retention — runs code paths that read course progress for a course with zero pages. Retirement cleanup stopped at the pages and the gates and did not reach the one subsystem whose whole job is to reach customers; the retirement was verified by gates that check page presence, not by asking which callers survived.
rec: Before any retention work, walk `lifecycle-emails.js` end to end: delete the two course template imports and the `readCourseProgress` path, and replace `lifecycleSavedNoReturnEmail`'s trigger (which currently rides the dead Workshop watch scaffold at `src/lib/watch-checks.js:9-17`) with the Cost-Index-basket save the retention doc actually specifies. Then flip the flag on a list of one — the founder — and confirm a real send before it touches a signup.
